docs.title: Exact chemistry search, proved
docs.text:
SMSD Pro finds substructures, maximum common substructures and similar molecules in C++, Java and Python. Every result states whether the search completed and whether its answer is proved optimal, so you always know what you can rely on.

Get started Try the notebooks GitHub

docs.title: Start in a minute
docs.text:
pippip with NVIDIA GPUDockerJava (Maven) 
python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0"

docker load -i smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-amd64.tar.xz
docker run --rm smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 --help

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.bioinceptionlabs</groupId>
  <artifactId>smsd</artifactId>
  <version>8.0.3</version>
</dependency>

import smsd

# Is benzoic acid inside aspirin?
hit = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1C(=O)O").match("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O")
print(hit.found)                               # True

# What do two molecules share, and is that proved maximal?
mcs = smsd.MCS.find("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O").match("OC(=O)c1ccccc1O")
print(mcs.matches[0].atom_count, mcs.optimal)  # 10 True

# How similar are they?
a = smsd.fingerprint_from_smiles("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", radius=2, fp_size=2048)
b = smsd.fingerprint_from_smiles("OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", radius=2, fp_size=2048)
print(round(smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(a, b), 3))  # 0.185

docs.title: Connecting AI assistants
docs.text:
SMSD lets an AI assistant run molecular comparisons on your machine: maximum common substructure, substructure and SMARTS matching, fingerprints, similarity, screening, standardisation and MCS depiction. Each search result reports its status and whether it is optimal and complete, so the assistant can tell a proven answer from a search that stopped at its limit.

You can use a hosted assistant or an open model that runs on your own machine. Connect SMSD through its local MCP server, smsd-mcp, or pass its tool definitions to a model API from your own Python code. SMSD itself sends nothing over the network. A hosted assistant sends your prompts, tool arguments and results, including any structures, to its model provider.

The eight tools and their results are described in Molecular tools and MCP.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install "smsd[mcp]>=8.1.0"
which smsd-mcp    # Windows: where.exe smsd-mcp

The MCP server and the tool definitions need SMSD 8.1.0 or later and Python 3.12 or later. The [mcp] extra adds the MCP SDK that smsd-mcp needs. The Python loops below need smsd without the extra, plus the client package that each section installs.

smsd-mcp (or python -m smsd.mcp_server) starts the server over standard input and output. It takes no arguments, opens no network port and writes diagnostics to standard error. Assistants start it themselves when they need the tools. Use the path that which or where.exe prints wherever a client needs an absolute path.

To check the server without an assistant, run python/examples/mcp_stdio_client.py; it lists the tools and runs one search over standard input and output.

docs.title: Connect the MCP server
docs.text: Clients are listed in alphabetical order. Each block follows the syntax in that product's documentation as of 29 October 2026. Each result carries engine_version; use it to confirm the SMSD version, because some clients show the MCP SDK's version for the server.

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
claude mcp add --transport stdio smsd -- smsd-mcp
claude mcp get smsd

The server is added to the current project for you only. Add --scope user before -- to use it in all your projects, or --scope project to share it with your team through .mcp.json. Inside a session, /mcp shows its status. Reference: Claude Code MCP.

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Add the server to claude_desktop_config.json:

  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
  • Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "smsd": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/smsd-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}

Replace the command with the absolute path printed by which smsd-mcp or where.exe smsd-mcp, because Claude Desktop may not find commands on your shell's PATH. In JSON, write Windows paths with doubled backslashes or forward slashes. Quit Claude Desktop fully and restart it. The server then appears under Connectors in the chat + menu. Server output is logged to mcp-server-smsd.log in ~/Library/Logs/Claude (macOS) or %APPDATA%\Claude\logs (Windows). Reference: Connect to local MCP servers.

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
codex mcp add smsd -- smsd-mcp
codex mcp list

The command writes an [mcp_servers.smsd] table to ~/.codex/config.toml. The Codex CLI, the Codex IDE extension and the ChatGPT desktop app share this file, so the server appears in all three. To add it from the IDE extension instead, open the gear menu, choose MCP servers, then Add server; enter smsd, choose STDIO, enter smsd-mcp as the command, save and select Restart extension. In the terminal interface, /mcp lists active servers.

Codex waits a short time for optional servers when it builds the first tool list. To wait for each server's startup_timeout_sec instead, set mcp_optional_startup_grace_ms = 0 at the top level of config.toml. To make start-up fail when the SMSD server cannot start, add required = true to the [mcp_servers.smsd] table. References: Codex MCP, configuration reference.

docs.title: Gemini CLI and Antigravity CLI
docs.text:
gemini mcp add --scope user smsd smsd-mcp
gemini mcp list

Without --scope user, the server is added to .gemini/settings.json in the current folder. Gemini CLI connects stdio servers only in trusted folders; run gemini trust in a folder to trust it. Google moved some account types from Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI (agy) on 18 June 2026; Google's announcement lists which. Antigravity CLI reads servers from ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json, or you can add them with its /mcp manager:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "smsd": {
      "command": "smsd-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}

References: Gemini CLI MCP, Antigravity MCP.

docs.title: Goose with a local model
docs.text:
Goose is an open-source agent that can use a model served by Ollama. Run goose configure, choose Ollama as the provider, confirm the API host http://localhost:11434 and choose a model with tool support, such as qwen3 (models with tools). On machines with less than 24 GiB of VRAM, Ollama's default context is 4k, which is small for eight tool definitions; start Ollama with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve. Then add SMSD under extensions: in ~/.config/goose/config.yaml (Windows: %APPDATA%\Block\goose\config\config.yaml):

extensions:
  smsd:
    type: stdio
    name: smsd
    enabled: true
    cmd: smsd-mcp
    args: []
    env_keys: []
    envs: {}
    timeout: 300

References: Goose configuration files, Ollama context length. Other local MCP clients are listed under Open models.

docs.title: Use the tool definitions from Python
docs.text:
smsd.tool_definitions.get_tool_definitions(provider) returns the eight tools in the shape a model API expects. Pass one of the four values below as provider; the default is mcp. call_tool(name, arguments) runs a tool locally and returns its JSON-compatible result. It rejects unknown tools, unknown or missing arguments, wrong JSON types and out-of-range values with a ValueError; the loops below return that message to the model so that it can correct the call. python/examples/agent_workflow.py runs the same tools in a fixed sequence (screening, MCS and depiction) without a model.

Value Shape Use with mcp name, description, inputSchema MCP tool lists input-schema name, description, input_schema Claude Messages API function flat: type: "function", name, description, parameters OpenAI Responses API; Gemini API after the change shown below chat-function nested: type: "function", function: {name, description, parameters} Chat Completions API, DeepSeek API, llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama, vLLM

The function and chat-function values set strict: false, so the model can leave out optional arguments and SMSD applies its defaults. Each loop below reads any API key it needs from the environment and sends every tool result back to the model in full, including status, optimal and complete. The APIs are listed in alphabetical order of vendor.

docs.title: Claude Messages API
docs.text:
python -m pip install anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...    # your own key

import json

import anthropic
from smsd.tool_definitions import call_tool, get_tool_definitions


def run_tool(name, arguments):
    """Run one SMSD tool locally and return (text, is_error)."""
    try:
        return json.dumps(call_tool(name, arguments)), False
    except (ValueError, ImportError) as error:
        return str(error), True


client = anthropic.Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
tools = get_tool_definitions("input-schema")
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Find the maximum common substructure of "
             "c1ccccc1O and c1ccccc1N. Is the result proven optimal?"}]

while True:
    response = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-opus-5-5", max_tokens=4096, tools=tools, messages=messages)
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
    if response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
        break
    results = []
    for block in response.content:
        if block.type == "tool_use":
            text, is_error = run_tool(block.name, block.input)
            results.append({"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": block.id,
                            "content": text, "is_error": is_error})
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": results})

print("".join(block.text for block in response.content if block.type == "text"))

claude-opus-5-5 was a current model on 29 October 2026; the models overview lists current IDs. Reference: Claude tool use.

docs.title: Gemini API
docs.text:
python -m pip install google-genai
export GEMINI_API_KEY=...    # your own key

from google import genai
from google.genai import types
from smsd.tool_definitions import call_tool, get_tool_definitions


def run_tool(name, arguments):
    """Run one SMSD tool locally; errors go back to the model."""
    try:
        return {"result": call_tool(name, arguments)}
    except (ValueError, ImportError) as error:
        return {"error": str(error)}


# Gemini's parameters schema has no additionalProperties field, so drop it.
# call_tool still rejects unknown arguments.
declarations = [
    {"name": tool["name"], "description": tool["description"],
     "parameters": {key: value for key, value in tool["parameters"].items()
                    if key != "additionalProperties"}}
    for tool in get_tool_definitions("function")
]
client = genai.Client()  # reads GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY
config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
    tools=[types.Tool(function_declarations=declarations)], store=False)
contents = [types.Content(role="user", parts=[types.Part(
    text="Find the maximum common substructure of c1ccccc1O and c1ccccc1N. "
         "Is the result proven optimal?")])]

while True:
    response = client.models.generate_content(
        model="gemini-3.8-flash", contents=contents, config=config)
    if not response.function_calls:
        break
    contents.append(response.candidates[0].content)
    parts = [types.Part(function_response=types.FunctionResponse(
        id=call.id, name=call.name, response=run_tool(call.name, call.args or {})))
        for call in response.function_calls]
    contents.append(types.Content(role="user", parts=parts))

print(response.text)

Gemini accepts default without applying it and may not enforce every limit in the schema; call_tool checks every argument itself. store=False opts the request out of storage, which is on by default for new paid projects from 26 October 2026; it needs google-genai 2.33.0 or later. gemini-3.8-flash was a current model on 29 October 2026; see Gemini models. Google recommends its Interactions API for new projects (Generate Content); its function tools use the flat type, name, description and parameters shape of the function value. References: function calling with generateContent, function calling with Interactions.

docs.title: OpenAI Responses API
docs.text:
python -m pip install openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...    # your own key

import json

from openai import OpenAI
from smsd.tool_definitions import call_tool, get_tool_definitions


def run_tool(name, arguments):
    """Run one SMSD tool locally; errors go back to the model as text."""
    try:
        return json.dumps(call_tool(name, json.loads(arguments)))
    except (ValueError, ImportError) as error:
        return f"Error: {error}"


client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY
tools = get_tool_definitions("function")
input_list = [{"role": "user", "content": "Find the maximum common substructure of "
               "c1ccccc1O and c1ccccc1N. Is the result proven optimal?"}]

while True:
    response = client.responses.create(model="gpt-6-astra", tools=tools, input=input_list)
    input_list += response.output
    calls = [item for item in response.output if item.type == "function_call"]
    if not calls:
        break
    for item in calls:
        input_list.append({"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": item.call_id,
                           "output": run_tool(item.name, item.arguments)})

print(response.output_text)

gpt-6-astra was a current model on 29 October 2026; see OpenAI models. OpenAI recommends the Responses API for new projects (migration guide). Reference: Function calling.

docs.title: Chat Completions API
docs.text:
import json

from openai import OpenAI
from smsd.tool_definitions import call_tool, get_tool_definitions


def run_tool(name, arguments):
    """Run one SMSD tool locally; errors go back to the model as text."""
    try:
        return json.dumps(call_tool(name, json.loads(arguments)))
    except (ValueError, ImportError) as error:
        return f"Error: {error}"


client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY
tools = get_tool_definitions("chat-function")
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Find the maximum common substructure of "
             "c1ccccc1O and c1ccccc1N. Is the result proven optimal?"}]

while True:
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-5.6-terra", reasoning_effort="none", messages=messages, tools=tools)
    message = response.choices[0].message
    messages.append(message)
    if not message.tool_calls:
        break
    for tool_call in message.tool_calls:
        messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tool_call.id,
                         "content": run_tool(tool_call.function.name,
                                             tool_call.function.arguments)})

print(message.content)

On 29 October 2026, OpenAI's migration guide stated that, from GPT-5.4 onwards, Chat Completions supports tool calls only with reasoning_effort="none". gpt-5.6-terra was available on that date and supports this setting. GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra need the Responses API for tool calls; see OpenAI models. The same loop works with other Chat Completions services; see Open models.

docs.title: One loop for DeepSeek and local runtimes
docs.text:
The hosted DeepSeek API and the local runtimes below accept tools in the chat-function shape through Chat Completions-compatible endpoints. This loop works with each of them; change only BASE_URL and MODEL. Runtimes are listed in alphabetical order.

python -m pip install openai
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=...    # DeepSeek only; local runtimes need no key

import json
import os
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from openai import OpenAI
from smsd.tool_definitions import call_tool, get_tool_definitions

# Change only these two values; the table below lists each runtime.
BASE_URL = "https://api.deepseek.com"
MODEL = "deepseek-flash"


def run_tool(name, arguments):
    """Run one SMSD tool locally; errors go back to the model as text."""
    try:
        return json.dumps(call_tool(name, json.loads(arguments)))
    except (ValueError, ImportError) as error:
        return f"Error: {error}"


# Local runtimes need no key, but the client needs a value.
# The DeepSeek key is sent only to the DeepSeek API.
if urlparse(BASE_URL).hostname == "api.deepseek.com":
    api_key = os.environ["DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"]
else:
    api_key = "local"
client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE_URL, api_key=api_key)
tools = get_tool_definitions("chat-function")
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Find the maximum common substructure of "
             "c1ccccc1O and c1ccccc1N. Is the result proven optimal?"}]

while True:
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=MODEL, messages=messages, tools=tools)
    message = response.choices[0].message
    messages.append(message)
    if not message.tool_calls:
        break
    for tool_call in message.tool_calls:
        messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tool_call.id,
                         "content": run_tool(tool_call.function.name,
                                             tool_call.function.arguments)})

print(message.content)
Runtime Start command BASE_URL MODEL DeepSeek API none: set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY https://api.deepseek.com deepseek-flash or deepseek-v4-pro llama.cpp llama-server --jinja -hf bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M --port 9931 http://localhost:9931/v1 the model name listed at http://localhost:9931/v1/models LM Studio lms server start http://localhost:1234/v1 a model identifier listed at http://localhost:1234/v1/models Ollama ollama pull qwen3, then ollama serve http://localhost:11434/v1/ qwen3 vLLM vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --host 127.0.0.1 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1 http://localhost:8000/v1 Qwen/Qwen3-8B

Notes on each runtime, as of 29 October 2026:

  • DeepSeek API: thinking mode is on by default and supports tool calls. The loop appends each assistant message whole, which passes back its reasoning_content as DeepSeek requires. Current model IDs: Models and pricing. DeepSeek also publishes open weights, such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (763B parameters; model card).
  • llama.cpp: native tool-call formats include Hermes 2 and 3, Llama 3.1 to 3.3, Mistral Nemo and Qwen 2.5. DeepSeek R1 is listed as work in progress. Other models use a generic format. The default port changed from 8080 to 9931, so the commands on this page set it. Reference: function calling.
  • LM Studio: Qwen, Llama 3.1, Llama 3.2 and Mistral models have native tool use; other models use LM Studio's default tool format. Reference: LM Studio tool use.
  • Ollama: models with tool support in its library include gemma4, gpt-oss, llama3.1, mistral-small3.2, muse-glimmer, qwen3 and qwen3.8. Some entries, such as deepseek-v4.1-flash, have only cloud tags; choose a local tag to keep data on your machine. Ollama sets its default context from the available VRAM: 4k below 24 GiB, 32k from 24 to 48 GiB and 256k from 48 GiB. A 4k context is small for eight tool definitions; on such machines start the server with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve. Ollama does not support tool_choice, and the loop does not send it. References: tools listing, context length.
  • vLLM: tool calls need --enable-auto-tool-choice and a --tool-call-parser that matches the model. The command above follows Qwen's vLLM instructions; vLLM's own reasoning page gives --reasoning-parser qwen3 for the Qwen3 series. vLLM's tool-calling page gives the parser for other families, including DeepSeek, Llama and Mistral. For Gemma 4, the Gemma 4 recipe gives --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4, together with a chat template.

docs.title: MCP with a local model
docs.text:
Goose connects smsd-mcp to a model served by Ollama. llama.cpp's llama-server can also start stdio MCP servers itself. Save this as mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "smsd": { "command": "smsd-mcp", "args": [], "timeout_ms": 60000 }
  }
}

llama-server --jinja -hf bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M --port 9931 --mcp-servers-config mcp.json

llama.cpp stops each tool call after 30 s unless the entry sets timeout_ms. The value above leaves room for an SMSD search at its 30,000 ms maximum. The SMSD tools then appear as smsd_find_mcs and so on in the built-in web interface at http://127.0.0.1:9931. This option is experimental. The server starts smsd-mcp with its own privileges, and the llama.cpp documentation advises against enabling it in untrusted environments. Reference: llama.cpp server.

LM Studio (version 0.3.17 or later) reads MCP servers from its mcp.json file: on the Program tab, choose Install > Edit mcp.json. The file is ~/.lmstudio/mcp.json on macOS and Linux and %USERPROFILE%/.lmstudio/mcp.json on Windows (LM Studio MCP, LM Studio 0.3.17). Jan adds MCP servers under Settings > MCP Servers (Jan MCP). In either, enter the absolute path to smsd-mcp as the command.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• The tools run on your machine and contact no network service. Molecular arguments are SMILES or SMARTS text, never paths, URLs or commands.
  • Limits are fixed: 16,384 characters per text argument and 1,024 atoms per molecule (256 for depiction and 128 for standardisation). A similarity or screening call takes at most 4,096 atoms in total, and a screen at most 64 targets and 65,536 characters. search_smarts returns at most 32 matches, and screen_molecules at most 32 hits per page. A search stops at timeout_ms (default 1,000, at most 30,000) or node_limit (default 100,000, at most 1,000,000). These budgets cover the search, not the whole call. Standardisation has no time budget. Use process or container limits for a hard deadline. The container recipe runs the server with no network access.
  • smsd-mcp and call_tool check every argument themselves, so a client that drops schema keywords cannot widen these limits.
  • Ask the assistant to report status, optimal and complete with each answer. A search that stopped early may not be maximum, and found: false from an unfinished search does not prove absence.
  • A hosted assistant sends your prompts, tool arguments and results, including any structures, to its provider. Use a local runtime when structures must stay on your machine.
  • API keys come from environment variables such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. Do not write keys into code or committed configuration files. smsd-mcp needs no key, so its client entries need no environment settings.
  • Keep your assistant's tool approval prompts on unless you trust every tool it can call.

docs.title: SMSD search algorithms
docs.text: The C++, Java and Python libraries share one search model: a prepared query owns a copy of its graph, chemistry and resource options, and each match, matchAll or matchMany call runs an independent search against one target. The Python package calls the native search. The Python, C++ and Java guides document the API; this page states what each search guarantees, what a result means and how the languages differ. The supported-platforms table lists the release packages. Matching runs on the CPU; optional CUDA screening does not perform the MCS search.

docs.title: What each search guarantees
docs.text:
• Substructure finds embeddings of the whole query in the target. Non-induced matching requires every query bond in the target; induced matching also forbids extra target bonds between mapped atoms. Enumeration returns every embedding up to the requested limit, symmetric self-mappings included.
  • MCIS (maximum common induced subgraph) maximises mapped atoms, then bonds, or the supplied query atom weights, and preserves both edges and non-edges between mapped atoms.
  • MCES (maximum common edge subgraph) maximises common bonds, then the atoms they touch.
  • Every reported mapping satisfies the chemistry options, and connectivity and fragment limits apply to the reported components.
  • Canonical mapping selection returns one representative mapping under the symmetries of both molecules, or raises an error when it cannot.

docs.title: Results and budgets
docs.text:
• Every search reports status, optimal and complete separately from its matches. Completed means the search ran to its end. TimedOut and Cancelled mean the time limit or a cancellation stopped it. LimitReached means the node limit stopped it, an enumeration reached its match limit, or an MCES pair beyond the size limits below was declined before any search; a declined pair returns no match and proves nothing.
  • Complete-ring matching uses full relevant-cycle perception. Strict ring fusion compares per-atom ring counts. If the perception required by either option is incomplete in either input, MCS retains its selected mappings but reports LimitReached, with optimal and complete both false. TimedOut and Cancelled take precedence. Consensus applies the same status rule when any input has truncated ring perception, keeping its fragment and supporting mappings. A valid mapping's maximality cannot be proved in this case, so the check raises its existing proof-unavailable exception.
  • Positive numeric SMARTS R<n> (n > 0) uses one deterministic minimum cycle basis, the same in C++ and Java. When a molecule has more than one minimum cycle basis, R<n> and per-atom ring counts can depend on the input atom order. If ring perception cannot complete the basis, a search that cannot be decided without it returns LimitReached without matches, including for negated, combined and recursive predicates; the empty result does not prove absence. Literal R and R0 remain independent of that basis. Other functions that need the basis raise an error naming the cause; computeSSSR and computeRings may return incomplete rings with truncation flags. relevantCyclesTruncated alone does not make the basis incomplete.
  • Ring perception works within one fixed, deterministic work limit, the same in C++, Java and Python and independent of time, thread count and hardware. Very large fused-ring systems, such as synthetic cages, can reach it. When it is reached, ringsTruncated reports it. A refusal it causes recurs on every run, so a longer timeout will not help. Values computed without the missing ring information are still returned exactly; searches that need it report LimitReached, and other ring-dependent results raise RingBasisUnavailable (Java RingBasisUnavailableException) naming the cause, with the zero-based input index in C++ and Python batch calls.
  • Progressive consensus is an approximation. Its optimal flag is always false, including empty and single-input calls. complete records whether the progressive pass finished. Neither it nor Completed proves a global optimum or absence of a qualifying common graph. Its threshold, budget, selected fragment and supporting mappings retain their existing meanings.
  • A stopped search may return a valid mapping without proving the optimum, and a capped enumeration may prove the objective while leaving the enumeration incomplete. An empty incomplete result does not prove absence.
  • A negative timeout selects the default budget: 10 s for a substructure search and, for an MCS, 500 ms plus 2 ms per atom pair (query atoms × target atoms), at most 30 s. That is 1.3 s for two 20-atom molecules, 5.5 s for two 50-atom molecules and 30 s from 122 atoms each. Zero stops immediately, and a node limit of zero leaves the node count unlimited.
  • Batch results do not depend on the thread count unless a search reaches its time limit.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text: An MCES search declines a pair, with LimitReached and no match, when query atoms × target atoms exceed 2³⁰, as for two molecules of more than 32,768 atoms each; when the two molecules are too large in bonds, as for two molecules of more than 16,384 bonds each; or, rarely, when a molecule has an atom with 512 or more bonds and the two molecules share many kinds of bond. MCIS searches are never declined. The three libraries share these limits.

docs.title: Stereochemistry
docs.text: With chirality or double-bond stereochemistry enabled, a mapped centre or double bond is compared by the parity of its mapped neighbours, not by CIP labels, whose priorities depend on atoms outside the mapping. The comparison is a hard constraint. MCIS returns the largest common subgraph whose mapped stereochemistry agrees, which can be smaller than the MCIS without it: for the alanine enantiomers N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O and N[C@H](C)C(=O)O it keeps five of the six atoms. MCES instead leaves out the fewest common bonds that resolve each disagreement: for C[C@@H]1CCCO1 and C[C@H]1CCCO1 it keeps all six atoms and five of the six bonds, where MCIS keeps five atoms.

docs.title: Cross-language differences
docs.text:
These differences are deliberate; most follow the conventions of each language.

docs.title: SMSD Pro 8.1.0 API reference
docs.text:
This reference describes the 8.1.0 source API. Use a matching wheel or build; an earlier installed native extension cannot provide new Python APIs.

The Python package provides molecular graphs, exact searches, fingerprints, screening, depiction and optional data adapters. Java and C++ expose related graph operations; their names and available options are documented in the Java guide and C++ guide. Identical fingerprint parameters do not establish bit identity across toolkits.

docs.title: MCS and substructure searches
docs.text:
import smsd

options = smsd.MCS.Options()
options.timeout_ms = 1000
options.node_limit = 100000
result = smsd.MCS.find("CCO").with_options(options).match("CCN")
assert result.found and result.best.atom_count == 2
assert smsd.MCS.validate_mapping("CCO", "CCN", result.best, options) == []

MCS.Objective.MCIS maximises common atoms while preserving edges and non-edges. MCES maximises selected common bonds; its witness includes the chosen bonds as well as atoms. The objectives are different and should not be compared as interchangeable scores. MCS.Connectivity.CONNECTED requires a connected common graph; FRAGMENTS permits disconnected selected components. with_fragments(min_atoms=..., max_fragments=...) selects the latter mode. with_atom_weights assigns weights to query atoms in MCIS; weighted scores are not atom counts. Use the matching options when validating a witness.

Prepared searches copy options and support match, match_all(limit=...) and match_many(num_threads=...). A prepared query can be reused; avoid mutating its source molecule or shared mutable inputs during calls. Options are copied, but a shared cancellation token intentionally remains a signal to all searches using it. num_threads=0 selects the native OpenMP default; set an explicit positive thread count for a controlled batch.

SearchResult contains matches, status, optimal, complete, score, nodes_visited and elapsed_ms; found and best are convenience properties. best is None when there is no witness. Match contains atom_mapping, selected bond_mapping and fragments, with atom_count and bond_count. For SMILES inputs, atom indices are zero-based in parsing order. Foreign molecule inputs retain their caller-visible numbering through conversion.

Inspect found, status, optimal and complete separately. A time-, node- or cancellation-stopped call can retain a useful witness without proving an optimum. An unfinished result with no witness does not prove absence. complete also records enumeration completeness; a requested result limit can stop enumeration after an optimum is found. Ring-perception work limits can prevent a proof even when a mapping is feasible. Preserve stopped cases when analysing outcomes; stopped latency is not completed-work throughput.

Search budgets apply after input parsing and preparation. General API options permit native defaults and unlimited node settings; set explicit finite limits when accepting untrusted or interactive requests. The MCP tools impose their own stricter limits. timeout_ms=0 requests an immediate timeout. A CancellationToken is one-way: call cancel() and create a fresh token for a later independent request.

ChemOptions controls atom type, charge, isotope, bond order, aromatic compatibility, stereo, ring and optional tautomer handling. The default profile does not require matching formal charges or isotopes. Use explicit options or ChemOptions.profile("strict") when those restrictions matter; do not infer them from a tool or method name. complete_rings_only, ring_matches_ring_only and ring_fusion_mode impose different restrictions. The graph aromaticity model is a preparation choice, selected through perceive_aromaticity or the builder. The deprecated chemistry aromaticity_model field is not read by search.

query = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[OX2H]")
assert query.match("CCO").found
assert not query.match("CCN").found

embeddings = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[#8]").match_all("OCCO", limit=8)
assert len(embeddings.matches) == 2

Substructure.find takes a molecule query; Substructure.smarts compiles a predicate query. with_induced(True) additionally requires query non-bonds to remain non-bonds. SMARTS predicates can specify hydrogen, isotope, charge, aromaticity and topology directly. A parsed SMARTS string and a proved search result are separate facts.

MCS.match_constrained processes queries in order while excluding already used target atoms. MCS.consensus builds a progressive common graph with a support threshold and supporting mappings. It is an approximation and always reports optimal=False, including empty and single-input calls. complete reports whether the progressive pass finished. Neither it nor COMPLETED proves a global multi-molecule optimum or absence of a qualifying common graph. is_mapping_maximal tests extendibility of a given valid mapping, which is different from proving a maximum. Symmetry canonicalisation and tautomer-confidence helpers also have separate contracts; confidence is a heuristic, not a search proof or stability prediction.

docs.title: Result graphs, SMARTS and images
docs.text:
Match.to_graph(query) and Match.to_smiles(query) extract selected atoms and bonds. A partial selected graph can have capped valences and should not be mistaken for an unchanged fragment of the original complete molecule. Match.to_smarts(query, chemistry) and MCS.match_with_smarts(target) export portable predicates for represented selected graphs. Unsupported stereo, tautomer and ring-export constraints raise rather than being silently dropped. A SMARTS predicate does not carry an optimum proof, enumeration status or all induced non-edge requirements; retain the associated SearchResult.

exported = smsd.MCS.find("CCO").match_with_smarts("CCN")
assert exported.result.found
assert smsd.Substructure.smarts(exported.smarts).match("CCN").found

from smsd.highlight import mcs_svg
svg = mcs_svg("CCO", "CCN", exported.result)
assert '<svg' in svg and 'data-search-status=' in svg

Native depict_svg, depict_mapping and depict_pair return SVG strings and use DepictOptions. The pair renderer highlights mapped atoms and input bonds between them. smsd.highlight.mcs_svg carries search flags in the SVG and rejects selected-edge witnesses that this renderer would over-highlight; render best.to_graph(query) separately in that case. The MCP depiction tool instead labels this highlighting scope and returns the selected bond mapping alongside the image.

The older depict_mcs, depict_substructure and deprecated to_svg helpers use the optional RDKit drawing dependency. Their convenience images do not replace the proof-bearing result. The native SVG functions need no external drawing toolkit. save_svg writes only when explicitly called.

docs.title: Molecule I/O and chemistry
docs.text:
parse_smiles accepts OpenSMILES text; an empty string constructs an empty graph. lenient=True explicitly requests recovery from malformed input. to_smiles writes the native canonical representation, including supported stereo and atom maps. Canonical ordering can differ between language ports. canonical_hash and graph canonical hashes are compact screening keys, not proofs of molecular identity or difference. same_canonical_graph compares native canonical outputs; use a validated mapping when exact identity is required by an application.

read_mol_block, read_mol_file, write_mol_block, write_mol_block_v3000 and write_molfile cover MOL V2000/V3000 text or files. read_sdf, write_sdf and write_sdf_record cover SDF records. read_sdf loads the whole file and represents malformed records as empty graphs; inspect them rather than counting every record as accepted chemistry.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    destination = Path(directory) / "molecules.sdf"
    smsd.write_sdf(["CCO", "CCN"], destination)
    assert [graph.n for graph in smsd.read_sdf(destination)] == [3, 3]

MolGraphBuilder takes explicit atom properties, adjacency and parallel bond properties. Its build can run aromaticity perception; select that behaviour deliberately when carrying an externally prepared representation. MolGraph exposes atom and bond properties and lazy invariant getters. prewarm prepares common invariants; perceive_aromaticity and kekulize explicitly change a graph. Do not mutate it concurrently with reads/searches. Molecule names, comments, program lines and SDF properties are ordinary metadata.

compute_sssr, rings_truncated, relevant_cycles_truncated and graph ring-system methods expose ring perception. rings_truncated keeps its 8.0.x meaning: the ring search behind compute_sssr stopped before finding a complete set of rings. That search works within one fixed, deterministic work limit; see Results and budgets. relevant_cycles_truncated separately reports incomplete relevant-cycle enumeration. Strict ring fusion compares per-atom ring counts; complete-ring matching uses relevant cycles. Each checks completeness of the perception it uses. assign_cip, assign_rs and assign_ez expose represented stereo descriptors, including unresolved cases; missing annotations are not inferred experimental configurations. count_components, split_components, extract_subgraph and murcko_scaffold return graph topology or transformed graph objects, rather than implicitly standardising every input.

compute_relevant_cycle_families groups the relevant cycles into families, each with one member and its exact number of members as a Python integer, so they can be counted without listing them; truncated reports an incomplete enumeration. relevant_cycle_family_of finds the family of a ring and relevant_cycle_family_members lists members up to a limit. When the enumeration is complete, the relevant cycles and their number do not depend on the input atom order; the grouping into families can.

from_rdkit/to_rdkit and from_openbabel/to_openbabel use optional toolkit bindings. They pass through molecular text and are not unrestricted object serialisation. get_index_map and translate_mapping preserve RDKit atom numbering. Cache clearing releases reusable conversions without invalidating index maps retained by live graphs. translate_to_atom_ids uses explicitly supplied external graph atom IDs. Keep toolkit versions and conversion choices with cross-tool results.

docs.title: Fingerprints and coefficients
docs.text:
fingerprint and fingerprints accept molecules or SMILES and return sorted set-bit positions, or non-zero (position, count) pairs when counts are requested. fingerprint_from_smiles is a text convenience helper. Families include MCS-aware paths, element paths, ECFP/circular, FCFP and topological torsions; FingerprintOptions adds configurable invariants, fragment/scaffold choices, stereo and SMARTS keys. FingerprintOptions.maccs() supplies 166 MACCS keys, with key number k at position k - 1. Fingerprint family names and options are not guarantees of cross-tool bit identity.

specification = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
first, second = smsd.fingerprints(["CCO", "CCN"], options=specification, num_threads=1)
assert 0 <= smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(first, second) <= 1

counted = smsd.FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", size=128, counts=True)
counts = smsd.fingerprint("CCCCCC", options=counted)
assert any(count > 1 for position, count in counts)

Bit Tanimoto is intersection over union; bit Dice and cosine use bit counts. Count Tanimoto uses sum(min)/sum(max), count Dice uses 2*sum(min)/(sum(a)+sum(b)), and count cosine uses the dot product and L2 norms. These are different definitions. Use the count-specific helpers when retaining multiplicity. Empty-input conventions are documented on individual functions. Pass the actual fingerprint width to bit Dice/cosine/distance helpers whose default is 2,048 bits. to_hex, from_hex, to_binary_string and counts_to_array provide explicit serialisation forms. Fingerprint quality estimates concern hashed-vector density/collisions, not biological accuracy.

batch_similarity ranks by ECFP Tanimoto with stable input-order ties. similarity_upper_bound, its similarity alias and screen_targets are graph-label bounds used for screening; they are neither the same coefficient nor an exact MCS search. TargetCorpus captures molecules once for repeated graph-bound or ECFP screens and exact prepared-query batches.

docs.title: Corpus search decisions
docs.text:
Substructure.match_corpus(corpus, *, gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0) decides for each target whether it contains the query, and MCS.match_corpus(corpus, minimum_atoms, *, gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0) whether its unweighted MCIS with the query has at least minimum_atoms atoms. A conservative pre-screen rules out targets that cannot qualify; the CPU searches the rest, including targets whose bound equals the threshold. Existing match_many is unchanged.

Each CorpusSearchResult has target_index, atom_upper_bound (integer or None), proven_below_threshold, threshold_reached and result (the actual SearchResult, or None for a target ruled out by the pre-screen). Both decision flags false means unknown; a search stopped below the threshold proves nothing. Substructure has no atom bound. MCES and weighted searches return CPU results, but their scores never prove that a target falls below the atom threshold.

gpu_prefilter=False runs the pre-screen on the CPU. True asks the optional GPU provider to run it and falls back to the CPU when the device cannot. The GPU is never selected automatically, and graph matching always runs on the CPU. With unsupported query options, node caps, immediate timeouts or cancellation tokens, every target is searched. Original target order and atom numbering are retained. See the Python examples and budget scope.

docs.title: Packed corpora, clustering and optional data adapters
docs.text:
FingerprintCorpus is a read-only memory-mapped packed-bit file with explicit fingerprint width and row count. create/from_smiles construct it; fingerprint, iter_packed_chunks, screen_many, similarities, threshold_pairs and top_k_pairs read it. Use its context manager or close. The underlying file must remain unchanged while open. Chunk bounds limit working arrays, not returned-hit storage, mapped pages or total comparison work. Counts of representable rows are not throughput or memory measurements.

stream_screen_smiles and stream_screen_many_smiles process target iterables in chunks. butina clusters by similarity to a chosen centre; members need not be mutually close. maxmin makes a greedy diverse selection with deterministic input-index ties. Full threshold pair/clustering work can be quadratic even when it avoids a dense distance matrix.

The smsd.adapters module imports optional dependencies only when requested:

API Output and dependency to_numpy, fingerprints_numpy Dense binary/count arrays; NumPy. to_scipy, fingerprints_scipy Sparse matrices; SciPy and NumPy. molecules_pandas, molecules_polars Molecule/fingerprint columns; pandas or Polars. to_arrow Fixed-size-list fingerprint table; PyArrow and NumPy. to_torch, fingerprints_torch Tensors; PyTorch and NumPy. to_pyg Molecular graph Data; PyTorch Geometric and PyTorch. FingerprintTransformer, SimilarityTransformer Fit/transform estimators for scikit-learn pipelines.

Arrow can share a native-endian, C-contiguous 2-D integer NumPy buffer and retains its owner. Shared input must not be mutated. Other inputs/layouts can require copies; zero_copy_only=True rejects those cases and table metadata records the ownership/copy result. A tensor/graph adapter's device argument does not itself establish a GPU chemistry kernel.

docs.title: Accelerators and molecular tools
docs.text:
Exact MCS/substructure proof remains on the CPU. GPU support is operation-, build-, device- and package-dependent; availability alone does not prove a particular call dispatched to a device. gpu_is_available and gpu_device_info describe discovery. warm_start explicitly prepares a reusable corpus/query path. Packed corpus APIs expose explicit backends and retain deterministic CPU-defined score/hit semantics. Native Metal packed fingerprint screening is available only in C++ and runs only when requested explicitly; Python screening and search never run on Metal. See CUDA operation scope, native Metal scope and the optional smsd-cuda package for build and device requirements; the supported-platforms table lists the GPU that automatic screening uses by default.

The eight MCP tools expose finite text, atom, target, result and search limits plus status/proof/timing metadata. Native default standardisation changes representation only; opt-in chemical transformations record their optional backend. The tool registry also exports local function definitions in the input-schema, function and chat-function formats, and LangChain and LlamaIndex tools, without creating a model client.

docs.title: Compatibility names
docs.text: The 8.x API retains deprecated names such as canonical_smiles, prewarm_graph, read_molfile, export_sdf, dearomatize, overlapCoefficient, count_overlapCoefficient, to_svg and chem=. Use their documented replacements. Retaining these names is not permission to remove or reinterpret them in a minor release; warnings and old return values remain part of the compatibility behaviour.

docs.title: Native graph and option objects
docs.text:
Object Public operations MolGraph bonds(), has_bond(i, j), bond_order(i, j), bond_in_ring(i, j), bond_aromatic(i, j) read represented topology. prewarm(), ensure_canonical() and ensure_ring_counts() prepare lazy invariants. get_canonical_hash(), get_automorphism_generators() and automorphism_generators_truncated() expose bounded canonical/symmetry results. num_rings(), ring_system_of(atom), ring_system_sig(rs_id) and ring_system_count() describe perceived rings. perceive_aromaticity(model), kekulize() and dearomatize() explicitly mutate representation. MolGraphBuilder atom_count, atomic_numbers, formal_charges, mass_numbers, hydrogen_counts, ring_flags, aromatic_flags, neighbors, bond_orders, bond_ring_flags, bond_aromatic_flags, atom_ids, name, program_line, comment and properties set builder data and return the builder. build(perceive_aromaticity=True, aromaticity_model=DAYLIGHT_LIKE) constructs the graph. Bond-property rows run parallel to neighbour rows. ChemOptions profile(name) selects a named profile and tautomer_profile() selects the tautomer-aware profile. Fluent setters with_match_isotope, with_complete_rings_only, with_tautomer_aware, with_solvent, with_bond_order_mode, with_aromaticity_mode, with_ph and with_ring_fusion_mode change and return that options object. Constructing ChemOptions(existing) copies it. MCS.Options Search chemistry, timeout_ms, node_limit, cancellation, objective, connectivity, min_fragment_atoms, max_fragments, atom_weights and excluded_target_atoms. Substructure.Options Search chemistry, timeout_ms, node_limit, cancellation and induced. CancellationToken cancel() sets the one-way signal; is_cancelled reads it. FingerprintOptions Constructor keyword options and mutable fields describe fingerprint terms. copy() makes an independent copy; factories ecfp(radius=2, size=2048), fcfp(radius=2, size=2048), path(path_length=7, size=2048), torsion(size=2048) and maccs() select classic configurations. maccs_keys() returns the key definitions. FingerprintKey FingerprintKey(smarts, minimum=1) defines a SMARTS occurrence key; read-only smarts, minimum and kind describe it. CIPDescriptors rs_labels is a label per atom; ez_bonds contains (atom1, atom2, label) entries. Produced by assign_cip. RelevantCycleFamilies Read-only families, relevant_cycle_count (the exact number of members of the families listed) and truncated. Produced by compute_relevant_cycle_families. RelevantCycleFamily Read-only size, root, first, second, opposite, prototype (one member as atom indices) and the exact member_count. Point2D, Point3D Empty or coordinate constructors, with writable x, y and, for 3-D, z. DepictOptions Native SVG dimensions, bond lengths/widths/spacing, atom labels, map/index visibility, highlight styling, padding and font family.

Native enums are SearchStatus, BondOrderMode, AromaticityMode, AromaticityModel, RingFusionMode, Solvent, FingerprintFamily, FragmentMode, ScaffoldMode, RSLabel, EZLabel, and the nested MCS.Objective/MCS.Connectivity. Use their named values rather than numeric ordinals. Graph atom arrays are in graph index order; canonical_label and orbit are derived data and are not permission to replace caller numbering. properties supports ordinary string-key/value mapping operations.

smsd.RingBasisUnavailable is the native RuntimeError subclass raised when a result needs the minimum cycle basis and ring perception reached its work limit before completing it; batch calls add the zero-based input index.

docs.title: Callable index
docs.text: The source-linked index below includes the top-level purpose modules, their public prepared-search/corpus methods, the separate adapters/highlight modules and molecular tool functions. Native graph/options fields and builder methods are grouped above and in their runtime docstrings. Optional dependencies are required only for the corresponding call.

docs.title: Molecules and I/O
docs.text:
Source: _molecule.py.

Callable Contract smsd.canonical_hash(mol) The canonical hash of a molecule as a Python int. smsd.canonical_smiles(mol) Deprecated alias of :func:to_smiles. smsd.count_components(mol) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.export_sdf(molecules, filename) Deprecated alias of :func:write_sdf. smsd.clear_cache() Clear reusable toolkit conversions; live graphs keep their atom correspondence. smsd.extract_subgraph(mol, atom_indices) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.murcko_scaffold(mol) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.parse_mapped_smiles(smiles) Parse a SMILES string that contains atom map numbers. smsd.parse_smiles(smiles, *, lenient=False) Parse a SMILES string into a MolGraph. smsd.prewarm(mol) Compute and cache the common lazy invariants of a molecule once; returns its graph. smsd.prewarm_graph(mol) Deprecated alias of :func:prewarm that returns None. smsd.read_mol_block(mol_block) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.read_mol_file(filename) Read a MOL file (V2000 or V3000) into a MolGraph; one that cannot be opened or read raises ValueError. smsd.read_molfile(filename) Deprecated alias of :func:read_mol_file that reads the file as UTF-8 text. smsd.read_sdf(filename) Read every record of an SDF file at once; malformed records become empty graphs. smsd.same_canonical_graph(mol1, mol2) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.split_components(mol) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.strip_atom_maps(smiles) Remove atom map numbers from a SMILES string. smsd.to_smarts(mol, include_aromaticity=True, include_charge=True, include_ring_member=False, include_h_count=False, include_isotope=False) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.to_smiles(mol) Canonical SMILES of a MolGraph, SMILES string or RDKit Mol. smsd.translate_to_atom_ids(mapping, g1, g2) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.write_mol_block(mol) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.write_mol_block_v3000(mol) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example. smsd.write_molfile(mol, filename, *, v3000=False, sdf=False) Write a molecule to disk as MOL V2000, MOL V3000 or a single SDF record. smsd.write_sdf(molecules, filename) Write molecules as SDF records, each a V2000 MOL block followed by $$$$. smsd.write_sdf_record(mol) Native callable; its runtime docstring includes an ordinary example.

docs.text:
Source: _chemistry.py.

docs.title: SMSD Pro C++ guide
docs.text: A header-only C++17 library in namespace smsd for substructure search, maximum common substructure (MCS) search and related chemistry. Atom indices are zero-based. Each example is a complete program; build it as in the C++ quick start. See also the installation guide, the Java and Python guides and the changelog.

docs.title: SMARTS export in 8.1.0
docs.text: MCS::matchWithSmarts(target) returns MCS::SmartsResult, whose result retains the ordinary search status and whose smarts uses the prepared chemistry. Match::toSmarts(query, chemistry) exports an existing selected match. See SMARTS export for portable query semantics and a library-search example. Unsupported stereo, tautomer-aware, complete-ring and strict ring-fusion rules raise instead of weakening the query. The output does not encode induced MCIS or establish an optimality proof.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
Include smsd/smsd.hpp, which includes every header below except depictor.hpp, bond_energies.hpp, color_palette.hpp and rdkit_adapter.hpp, or only the headers you need: each compiles on its own. Headers under smsd/detail/ and namespaces ending in detail are implementation code.

Area Headers under smsd/ Search mcs.hpp (MCS, mapping utilities); substructure.hpp (Substructure, RGroupResult); search_types.hpp (SearchOptions, MCSOptions, SubstructureOptions, Match, SearchResult, SearchStatus, CancellationToken); chem_options.hpp (ChemOptions) Molecules mol_graph.hpp (MolGraph, MolGraph::Builder); smiles_parser.hpp (parseSMILES, toSMILES, toSMARTS); smarts_parser.hpp (parseSMARTS, SmartsPredicateRegistry); parser_utils.hpp (input limits); mol_reader.hpp (MOL and SDF) Fingerprints and screening batch.hpp (fingerprints, similarity, TargetCorpus) and fingerprint_options.hpp (FingerprintOptions), in smsd::batch; similarity_screen.hpp (similarityUpperBound, screenTargets); gpu.hpp (optional CUDA or Metal screening with a CPU fallback, in smsd::gpu) Rings, stereo and drawing ring_finder.hpp (computeSSSR, computeRelevantCycles, computeURFs, computeRings, ringsTruncated when the ring search stops before finding a complete set of rings, relevantCyclesTruncated for incomplete relevant-cycle enumeration, and RingBasisUnavailable, thrown where an exact ring basis is required but unavailable); relevant_cycle_families.hpp (computeRelevantCycleFamilies, relevantCycleFamilyOf, relevantCycleFamilyMembers: relevant cycles grouped into families with exact member counts); cip.hpp (smsd::cip); layout.hpp (2D and 3D coordinates, transform); depict.hpp (SVG); depictor.hpp (2D coordinates constrained to fixed atoms or a reference) Data and utilities hungarian.hpp (optimalAssign); periodic_table.hpp (getElement, atomicWeight, paulingElectronegativity and more); scaffold_library.hpp (reference ring systems, scaffolds, pharmacophore and functional-group SMARTS, drug-likeness limits); bond_energies.hpp (bondDissociationEnergy, mappingBondChangeCost, in kJ/mol); color_palette.hpp (mapNumberToPaletteColor, a fixed 20-colour cycle for atom-map numbers); rdkit_adapter.hpp (optional)

docs.title: Prepared queries
docs.text:
MCS::find and Substructure::find take a MolGraph or SMILES; Substructure::smarts takes SMARTS text or a SmartsQuery. A prepared query owns copies of its query and options and may be shared between threads. withOptions(options) and withTimeout(milliseconds) return new queries; MCS::withOptions throws std::invalid_argument for invalid fragment limits or atom weights. match and matchAll take a MolGraph or SMILES target, which must not change during a search.

  • match(target): one best common subgraph (MCS) or the first embedding (Substructure).
  • matchAll(target, limit = 1000): up to limit optimal mappings or embeddings, symmetric ones included; zero throws std::invalid_argument.
  • matchMany(targets, numThreads = 0): one match result per target, in order, each with its own budget; 0 means the hardware concurrency, 1 the calling thread, and a negative count throws std::invalid_argument. The exception of the lowest failing index is rethrown.
  • resultsTimeMillis(target): when, in milliseconds from the search start, matches found within the timeout are assembled (the effective timeout plus one eighth).
  • cancellation(): the token of the options, or null.
#include <cassert>
#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    const auto query = smsd::parseSMILES("CC(=O)NC");   // N-methylacetamide
    const auto target = smsd::parseSMILES("CCC(=O)N");  // propanamide
    const auto result = smsd::MCS::find(query).withTimeout(1000).match(target);
    assert(result.status == smsd::SearchStatus::Completed && result.optimal && result.complete);
    assert(result.matches.size() == 1 && result.matches.front().atomMapping.size() == 4);
    assert(smsd::MCS::validateMapping(query, target, result.matches.front()).empty());
    const auto phenol = smsd::parseSMILES("c1ccc(O)cc1");
    assert(!smsd::Substructure::find("c1ccccc1").match(phenol).matches.empty());
    assert(!smsd::Substructure::smarts("[OH]").match(phenol).matches.empty());
    const auto all = smsd::Substructure::find("CO").matchAll("OCO", 10);
    assert(all.complete && all.matches.size() == 2);
}

docs.title: SMARTS
docs.text:
SMARTS follows Daylight semantics, as in Java: [H], [2H] and [H+] are hydrogen atoms, [CH] and [H1] count hydrogens, r<n> is the smallest ring size, (C.C) requires one target component and (C).(C) different ones. / and \ are single, non-aromatic bonds; a double bond between them must have the written configuration unless one is /? or \?, and an unpaired one matches either way.

parseSMARTS(text, maxRecursionDepth = 20) throws std::invalid_argument for malformed SMARTS, including a pattern that ends with a bond such as CC-, and for input over the parser_utils.hpp limits MAX_SMARTS_LENGTH, MAX_ATOMS (also applied by parseSMILES), MAX_SMARTS_EXPRESSION_NODES and MAX_SMARTS_NODES_PER_EXPRESSION. A SmartsPredicateRegistry expands $name tokens into recursive SMARTS with expandPredicates(text); the static builtinRegistry() supplies the ten predicates listed in the Java guide, with the same definitions, and registerPredicate(name, smarts) adds more.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
SearchResult holds matches, status, optimal, complete, score, nodesVisited and elapsedMillis. status is Completed when the search ran to its end, TimedOut or Cancelled when the time limit or the cancellation token stopped it, and LimitReached when the node limit stopped it, an enumeration reached its match limit, or an MCES pair beyond the size limits was declined before any search; a declined pair returns no match and proves nothing. A stopped search may return an unproved mapping, and a capped enumeration may be optimal yet incomplete, so check both flags, and check matches before front(). A stopped MCIS search can return a result or atom mapping that differs from 8.0.3 or Java (see the upgrade notes). score counts mapped atoms for the maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS), selected bonds for the maximum common edge subgraph (MCES), the summed weight for weighted MCIS, and query atoms for a Substructure match (zero without one).

completeRingsOnly requires complete relevant-cycle perception; RingFusionMode::STRICT requires complete perception for its per-atom ring counts. If that perception is incomplete in either input, the selected mappings remain, but the result is LimitReached, with optimal and complete both false; TimedOut and Cancelled take precedence. Positive numeric SMARTS R<n> (n > 0) uses one deterministic minimum cycle basis, the same in C++ and Java. If ring perception cannot complete it, a search that cannot be decided without it returns LimitReached without matches, including for negated, combined and recursive predicates; the empty matches then proves nothing. Literal R and R0 remain independent of that basis. Other functions that need the basis throw smsd::RingBasisUnavailable, a std::runtime_error, naming the cause; computeSSSR and computeRings may return incomplete rings with truncation flags. relevantCyclesTruncated alone does not make the basis incomplete. Ring perception works within one fixed, deterministic work limit; see Results and budgets.

A Match holds atomMapping (a std::map<int, int> from query to target atom), bondMapping (a std::array<int, 4> per selected bond: two query atoms, then two target atoms; keep it with MCES results, as atom pairs do not show which bonds were left out) and fragments (the components of the selected bonds, as query atoms). Explicit hydrogen atoms are vertices; bracket hydrogen counts are not. Match::toSmiles(query) writes the selection with valences capped at cut bonds; Match::toGraph(query) returns it, compactly renumbered, with its original chemical context.

docs.title: Corpus threshold decisions
docs.text:
Substructure::matchCorpus(corpus, gpuPrefilter, numThreads) and MCS::matchCorpus(corpus, minimumAtoms, gpuPrefilter, numThreads) return one CorpusSearchResult per original target slot. targetIndex is that slot; result contains the ordinary CPU SearchResult when searched. It is absent only when a conservative filter proves rejection. thresholdReached needs a real witness; provenBelowThreshold needs a bound or completed CPU proof. Both false means unknown, including a stopped search below the threshold.

#include <smsd/mcs.hpp>
#include <smsd/substructure.hpp>
#include <cassert>
int main() {
    smsd::batch::TargetCorpus corpus;
    corpus.addTargets({smsd::parseSMILES("CCO"), smsd::parseSMILES("N")});
    auto embeddings = smsd::Substructure::find("CO").matchCorpus(corpus, false, 1);
    assert(embeddings[0].thresholdReached && embeddings[0].result);
    assert(embeddings[1].provenBelowThreshold && !embeddings[1].result);
    auto decisions = smsd::MCS::find("CC").matchCorpus(corpus, 2, false, 1);
    assert(decisions[0].thresholdReached && decisions[1].atomUpperBound == 0);
}

gpuPrefilter=false, the default, runs the same conservative filter on the CPU. true attempts the optional provider and falls back to the CPU filter. There is no automatic GPU selection for these new methods. For unweighted MCIS, atomUpperBound is an upper bound on the MCS atom count, and a target whose bound equals minimumAtoms is searched. When no bound is available, atomUpperBound is -1. With unsupported query chemistry, SMARTS, caps, immediate timeouts, cancellation tokens, MCS weights, MCES or exclusions, every target is searched on the CPU. A weighted or MCES result does not prove an atom-threshold negative. Existing matchMany is unchanged.

Searches retain original target order and atom numbering, and each call searches the targets the corpus held when it started, even if targets are added meanwhile. numThreads has the ordinary batch meaning. Each target's search budget excludes the pre-screen, and these methods do not promise a whole-corpus wall-time limit.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
An MCES search declines a pair before searching it, with LimitReached, no match, and optimal and complete both false, when:

  • query atoms × target atoms exceed 2³⁰ (1,073,741,824), as for two molecules of more than 32,768 atoms each;
  • the two molecules are too large in bonds, as for two molecules of more than 16,384 bonds each;
  • rarely, a molecule has an atom with 512 or more bonds and the two molecules share many kinds of bond.

MCIS searches are never declined; the time and node limits bound them. Java and Python use the same limits.

docs.title: Objectives and fragments
docs.text:
MCIS, the default, maximises mapped atoms, then common bonds, and preserves edges and non-edges between mapped atoms. MCES maximises selected common bonds, then their atoms; isolated atoms do not count. Connectivity and fragment limits apply to the selected bonds.

MCS::Options fields, with defaults:

  • objective (Objective::MCIS): MCIS or MCES.
  • connectivity (Connectivity::Connected): Fragments allows a disconnected result.
  • minFragmentAtoms (1) and maxFragments (INT_MAX): positive limits on fragment size and count.
  • excludedTargetAtoms (empty): target atoms the search may not use.
  • atomWeights (empty): MCIS only, one finite, signed weight per query atom.

With atomWeights, MCIS maximises the summed weight, then atoms, then bonds, comparing whole thousandths truncated towards zero. Weights with MCES, or whose positive or negative sum in thousandths exceeds the 32-bit range, throw std::invalid_argument.

#include <cassert>
#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    const auto query = smsd::parseSMILES("C1CC1");    // cyclopropane
    const auto target = smsd::parseSMILES("CC(C)C");  // isobutane
    const auto induced = smsd::MCS::find(query).match(target);
    assert(induced.matches.front().atomMapping.size() == 2);

    smsd::MCS::Options options;
    options.objective = smsd::MCS::Objective::MCES;
    const auto edges = smsd::MCS::find(query).withOptions(options).match(target);
    const auto& match = edges.matches.front();
    assert(match.atomMapping.size() == 3 && match.bondMapping.size() == 2);
    const auto output = smsd::parseSMILES(match.toSmiles(query));
    std::size_t degreeSum = 0;
    for (const auto& neighbors : output.neighbors) degreeSum += neighbors.size();
    assert(output.n == 3 && degreeSum == 4);
    assert(smsd::MCS::validateMapping(query, target, match, options).empty());

    options.objective = smsd::MCS::Objective::MCIS;
    options.connectivity = smsd::MCS::Connectivity::Fragments;
    const auto fragments = smsd::MCS::find("CCOCC").withOptions(options).match("CCNCC");
    assert(fragments.matches.front().fragments.size() == 2);
}

docs.title: Search options
docs.text:
MCS::Options and Substructure::Options share the SearchOptions fields:

  • chemistry (ChemOptions{}): atom and bond compatibility rules.
  • timeoutMs (-1): milliseconds; negative selects the default, min(30000, 500 + 2 × query atoms × target atoms) for MCS (1,300 for two 20-atom molecules, 5,500 for two 50-atom molecules, 30,000 from 122 atoms each) and 10,000 for Substructure, and zero stops at once.
  • nodeLimit (0): most search nodes; zero is unlimited.
  • cancellation (null): a std::shared_ptr<CancellationToken>; cancel() stops the search.
  • induced (false, Substructure::Options only): also preserve non-edges.

The budget starts once the query is built and string inputs are parsed, and one step can overrun it.

#include <cassert>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>
#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    const auto query = smsd::Substructure::smarts("[#6]-[#8]");
    const std::vector<smsd::MolGraph> targets = {
        smsd::parseSMILES("CO"), smsd::parseSMILES("CC")
    };
    const auto results = query.withTimeout(1000).matchMany(targets, 2);
    assert(results.size() == 2);
    assert(results[0].complete && results[0].matches.size() == 1);
    assert(results[1].complete && results[1].matches.empty());

    auto token = std::make_shared<smsd::CancellationToken>();
    smsd::Substructure::Options options;
    options.cancellation = token;
    token->cancel();
    const auto stopped = query.withOptions(options).match(targets.front());
    assert(stopped.status == smsd::SearchStatus::Cancelled);
    assert(stopped.matches.empty() && !stopped.optimal && !stopped.complete);

    const auto immediate = smsd::MCS::find("CC").withTimeout(0).match("CCC");
    assert(immediate.status == smsd::SearchStatus::TimedOut);
    assert(immediate.matches.empty() && !immediate.optimal && !immediate.complete);
}

docs.title: Chemistry options
docs.text:
ChemOptions fields, with defaults:

  • matchAtomType (true), matchFormalCharge (false) and matchIsotope (false): mapped atoms share their element, their formal charge, or, when both specify one, their mass number.
  • matchBondOrder (BondOrderMode::STRICT): LOOSE and ANY ignore bond-order differences.
  • aromaticityMode (AromaticityMode::FLEXIBLE): aromatic bonds may match single or double bonds; STRICT requires equal aromatic flags.
  • ringMatchesRingOnly (false): ring atoms and bonds map only to ring atoms and bonds.
  • completeRingsOnly (false): retained ring atoms and bonds lie in fully selected relevant rings of their own input; a fusion atom needs only one.
  • ringFusionMode (RingFusionMode::IGNORE): STRICT requires mapped ring atoms to have the same per-atom ring count; PERMISSIVE adds no constraint, like IGNORE.
  • useChirality and useBondStereo (false): mapped tetrahedral centres and double bonds must agree in configuration, compared by the parity of their mapped neighbours, not by CIP labels (R/S, E/Z).
  • tautomerAware (false): relax bond orders where tautomer rules apply.
  • pH (7.4) and solvent (Solvent::AQUEOUS): the tautomer confidence context.

The fluent setters are withBondOrderMode, withAromaticityMode, withCompleteRingsOnly, withMatchIsotope, withRingFusionMode, withTautomerAware, withPH (clamped to 0–14; throws std::invalid_argument if not finite) and withSolvent. ChemOptions::profile(name), ignoring case, returns default, strict (strict aromaticity), pharma (charge, ring-only and complete-ring matching), compat-fmcs, compat-substruct or reaction (loose bond orders), and throws std::invalid_argument otherwise; ChemOptions::tautomerProfile() adds tautomer-aware matching with loose bond orders. Deprecated: ChemOptions::fmcsProfile() (use profile("compat-fmcs")) and the unread aromaticityModel field (MolGraph::Builder::build() and perceiveAromaticity() take the model).

Stereo: tetrahedral centres have four neighbours, or three plus an implicit hydrogen or, for N, P, S, As, Se, Sb and Te, a lone pair; the SMILES parser drops other tags, and MolGraph::Builder tags on other atoms are compared as given. A Builder tag (1 for @, 2 for @@) winds the stored neighbours, the implicit hydrogen or lone pair coming second if the first neighbour's index is below the atom's and first otherwise, as in Java. Substructure requires tagged query stereo to recur in the target, and untagged query stereo matches anything; MCS compares the stereo the mapping fixes, treating unspecified target stereo as a wildcard. The comparison uses the parity of the mapped neighbours, not CIP labels, whose priorities depend on atoms outside the mapping. In MCS it is a hard constraint: an MCIS is the largest common subgraph whose mapped stereo agrees, so it can be smaller than the MCIS found without these options, and an MCES leaves out the fewest common bonds that resolve each disagreement.

docs.title: Mapping utilities
docs.text:
• MCS::validateMapping(query, target, match, options = {}): a message per rule a Match or atom map violates; empty when valid.
  • MCS::mappingMatch(query, target, atoms, options = {}): a Match from an atom map, with the compatible bonds between mapped atoms.
  • MCS::isMappingMaximal(query, target, match, options = {}): whether the mapping is valid with no valid strict extension, which is weaker than optimal; throws std::runtime_error if it cannot decide, including when required ring perception was truncated.
  • MCS::canonicalizeMapping(query, target, mapping): one representative under the symmetry of both molecules; throws if the symmetry cannot be resolved.
  • smsd::validateTautomerConsistency(query, target, atomMapping): whether mobile N–H, O–H and S–H protons are conserved in each mapped tautomeric group.
  • MCS::computeTautomerConfidence(query, target, match, chemistry): a heuristic confidence, not a probability, in the selected tautomeric relaxations at the solvent and pH of chemistry; identical chemistry scores 1.

Per atom, MolGraph exposes tautomerClass (from 0, independent of atom order except among symmetric classes; −1 outside every class), tautomerWeight (for water at pH 7.4 unless MolGraph::Builder::solvent and pH set another context), tautomerSite (TAUTOMER_SITE_ACID, TAUTOMER_SITE_BASE or TAUTOMER_SITE_NONE) and tautomerPKa; the MolGraph::TW_* and TPKA_* constants hold the motif weights and pKa values. Java MolGraph.tautomerWeight is unscaled, so the arrays can differ, but the confidences agree to within rounding.

docs.title: Several molecules
docs.text:
• MCS::matchConstrained(queries, target, options = {}) runs the queries in order against one target, one result each; atoms used by an earlier query are unavailable to later ones, and indices refer to the original target.
  • MCS::consensus(molecules, options = {}, threshold = 1.0) returns a ConsensusResult: a common graph (graph, fragment, sourceIndex, toSmiles()) in at least the fraction threshold of the inputs, with supportCount and verified mappings keyed by input index; found is false when none qualifies. threshold must lie in (0, 1]; atom weights and excluded target atoms are rejected. Consensus is heuristic, shares one budget and always reports optimal == false, including empty and single-input calls. complete reports whether the progressive pass finished. Neither it nor Completed proves a global optimum or absence of a qualifying common graph. With complete rings or strict ring fusion, truncated ring perception in any input makes it LimitReached and incomplete, unless it is already TimedOut or Cancelled; its fragment and supporting mappings are retained.
  • Substructure::decomposeRGroups(core, molecules, options = {}) returns an RGroupResult per molecule: the matched core, substituents in rgroups (R1, R2, …) and the search result.

docs.title: Graphs, SMILES, MOL and SDF
docs.text:
parseSMILES(text) throws std::invalid_argument for malformed SMILES, including bracket atoms beyond the OpenSMILES limits; parseSMILES(text, options) with ParseOptions::lenient = true recovers where it can, such as from unclosed rings or unknown elements. toSMILES(graph) writes canonical SMILES, with / and \ on single bonds wherever a configured double bond has one at an end; an end with only aromatic ring bonds, as at an exocyclic C=N on an aromatic ring, carries them on an aromatic bond, as RDKit writes it, which strict OpenSMILES readers take as a single bond. toSMARTS(graph, options) writes canonical SMARTS; SmartsWriteOptions writes aromaticity and charge by default, and ring membership, hydrogen count and isotope on request. Both writers reject a graph that needs more than 99 ring closures open at once. For a graph of more than 5,000 atoms, or when canonical labelling reaches its search limit, canonical output can depend on the input atom order; automorphismGeneratorsTruncated() is then true.

MolGraph::Builder sets atoms (atomCount, atomicNumbers, formalCharges, massNumbers, hydrogenCounts, atomClasses, ringFlags, aromaticFlags), bonds (setNeighbors, setBondOrders, bondRingFlags, bondAromaticFlags), stereo (tetrahedralChirality, doubleBondStereo, doubleBondStereoSparse) and metadata (atomIds, name, programLine, comment, properties, solvent, pH). build() perceives aromaticity, giving supplied aromatic systems a Kekulé structure and perceiving them again, and build(false) keeps the supplied flags. When perception cannot read every candidate cycle of a molecule, as with a large bowl-shaped polyarene, the aromatic systems supplied on its fused ring systems keep their flags.

MolGraph::ringCountsTruncated() reports whether the per-atom ring counts may be incomplete because ring perception reached its work limit before the minimum cycle basis was complete; it computes the counts first if needed. MolGraph::computeRelevantCyclesFromBasis(basis, truncated) returns the relevant cycles found from a given set of the graph's cycles, normally a minimum cycle basis, and sets truncated to whether the result may lack relevant cycles: the basis has fewer cycles than the cycle rank, or the enumeration reached one of its limits. With its optional third argument set to false, a basis with fewer cycles than the cycle rank no longer sets truncated and the work limit no longer stops the enumeration, which can then take much longer.

computeRelevantCycleFamilies(graph) groups the relevant cycles into families and caches the result on the graph. Each RelevantCycleFamily gives the ring size, the root (the highest-numbered atom of every member), first, second and opposite, which locate the bond or atom opposite the root, one member as prototype and the exact memberCount as a decimal string, because counts can exceed 64 bits. RelevantCycleFamilies::relevantCycleCount is the exact number of members of the families listed, so the relevant cycles can be counted without listing them; truncated reports an incomplete enumeration, whose families are relevant but may not be all of them. relevantCycleFamilyOf(graph, families, ring) returns the index of the family that has ring as a member, or -1, and relevantCycleFamilyMembers(graph, family, limit) returns up to limit members, starting with the prototype. When the enumeration is complete, the relevant cycles and their number do not depend on the input atom order; the grouping into families can.

  • extractSubgraph(graph, atoms): the induced subgraph, in the given order, keeping a stereocentre whose neighbours all stay and the E/Z configuration of a double bond whose ends keep the neighbours that define it.
  • murckoScaffold(graph): the Bemis–Murcko scaffold (ring atoms, linkers and atoms double- or triple-bonded to them), capped with hydrogen, keeping surviving stereo; a molecule without rings is unchanged.
  • translateToAtomIds(mapping, query, target): a mapping in external atom IDs.
  • readMolBlock(text) and readMolFile(path) read V2000 or V3000 and throw std::invalid_argument for a block they cannot read, such as one with a bond to a missing atom, a V3000 integer field outside its range, a V3000 coordinate that is not a decimal number in the range of a double or more than MAX_ATOMS atoms; V2000 numeric fields are read leniently. Coordinates are read by one rule whatever the locale or platform, and one below 1e-307 in magnitude reads as zero. readSDF(path) reads every record, a malformed one giving an empty graph.
  • writeMolBlock(graph) writes V2000, or V3000 above 999 atoms or bonds; writeMolBlockV3000(graph) writes V3000; writeSDFRecord(graph) writes one record ending in $$$$, and writeSDF(graphs, path) a file.

MOL round trips do not imply support for MDL query features.

#include <cassert>
#include <string>
#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    const auto query = smsd::MolGraph::Builder().atomCount(4)
        .atomicNumbers({7, 6, 6, 8})
        .setNeighbors({{1}, {0, 2}, {1, 3}, {2}})
        .setBondOrders({{1}, {1, 1}, {1, 1}, {1}}).build();
    assert(smsd::MCS::find(query).match("CC(O)CN").matches.front().atomMapping.size() == 4);
    const auto text = smsd::writeMolBlockV3000(query);
    const auto restored = smsd::readMolBlock(text);
    assert(!smsd::Substructure::find(query).match(restored).matches.empty());
    assert(smsd::writeSDFRecord(query).find("$$$$") != std::string::npos);
}
