docs.title: Optional native adapter
docs.text: Configure with SMSD_WITH_RDKIT=ON and include smsd/rdkit_adapter.hpp; the static library is exported as smsd::smsd_rdkit and needs an RDKit development installation and C++20. smsd::fromRDKit(molecule, removeHs = true) removes explicit hydrogens by default, which can change atom indices, and copies element, charge, isotope, ring, aromaticity and tetrahedral data, but not hydrogen counts or double-bond stereo. smsd::fromSmiles(text) parses with RDKit and removes hydrogens likewise; smsd::parseSMILES(text) is the native parser.

docs.title: Fingerprints, screening and assignment
docs.text:
#include <cassert>
#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    const auto fingerprint = smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("c1ccc(O)cc1", 2, 2048);
    assert(fingerprint.size() == 32);
    assert(smsd::batch::fingerprintTanimoto(fingerprint, fingerprint) == 1.0);
    const auto assignment = smsd::optimalAssign({{1.0, 3.0}, {4.0, 2.0}});
    assert(assignment.totalCost == 3.0);
}

Packed fingerprints are vectors of 64-bit words, count fingerprints vectors of integer bins; compare only fingerprints of the same family, radius and size. In smsd::batch:

  • fingerprintFromSmiles(smiles, radius = 2, fpSize = 2048): ECFP; radius 2 is ECFP4.
  • batchFingerprint(molecules, pathLength = 7, fpSize = 1024, numThreads = 0): path fingerprints over all atoms, explicit hydrogens included, fpSize rounded up to a multiple of 64; Python path_fingerprint uses heavy atoms only and differs.
  • fingerprintTanimoto, fingerprintOverlap, fingerprintDice, fingerprintCosine and fingerprintSoergel compare packed fingerprints; for two empty ones, Tanimoto and overlap give 1 and the others 0, as in Java and Python. countTanimoto, countDice and countCosine compare equal-length count vectors, giving 0 for empty or unequal ones.
  • fingerprintSubset(query, target) tests whether every query bit is set in the target; batchFingerprintScreen(query, targets, numThreads = 0) returns the passing target indices.
  • fingerprintQuality(fingerprint, fpSize), for packed words or set positions, returns a FingerprintQuality with setBits, fpSize, density, expectedCollisionRate and saturated (density over FINGERPRINT_SATURATION_DENSITY, 0.75), as Python analyze_fp_quality and Java analyzeFpQuality report them.
  • toHex, fromHex, toBinaryString and countsToArray convert formats.
  • TargetCorpus holds reusable targets: addTarget, addTargets, prewarm(numThreads = 0), size, isPrewarmed, targets, screen(query, threshold, numThreads = 0), which returns the indices of the targets with ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity of at least threshold, and none before prewarm, and screenTargets(query, threshold, chemistry, numThreads = 0), the bound screen below for the held targets, which needs no prewarm.
  • TargetCorpus::screenMany(queries, threshold, numThreads = 0) and screenTargetsMany(queries, threshold, chemistry, numThreads = 0) return one hit-index vector per query, in query order. Each vector keeps target order. screenMany needs prewarmed ECFP4 fingerprints; screenTargetsMany uses the atom-count MCS similarity bound and needs no prewarm.
  • Errors in prewarm and in CPU screening reach the caller; when several targets fail, the error of the first in target order is raised, whatever the thread count.

similarityUpperBound(query, target, chemistry) bounds the atom-count Tanimoto similarity of the MCS from above; screenTargets(query, targets, threshold, chemistry) returns the indices of the targets whose bound reaches threshold, on the calling thread, or with a fifth argument on up to numThreads threads (0 = the OpenMP thread limit), giving the same indices. gpu::batchSimilarityScreenAuto is a separate native CUDA or Metal source-build interface with a CPU fallback, returning a ScreenHit{index, score} per passing target. The optional Python smsd-cuda package uses the corpus screening interface described in the Python guide. gpu::isAvailable() and gpu::deviceInfo() report the backend; a non-empty SMSD_DISABLE_GPU other than 0 makes isAvailable() false. Batch fingerprints, screens and TargetCorpus run in parallel when compiled with OpenMP.

optimalAssign(cost, penalty = 1.0) solves rectangular minimum-cost assignment over every row or column of the smaller side, returning the (row, column) pairs and totalCost, which excludes unmatched penalties; ragged or non-finite input throws std::invalid_argument.

docs.title: Optional Metal fingerprint screening
docs.text:
On macOS, the native source build compiles the smsd_metal library by default when Metal is available; -DSMSD_BUILD_METAL=OFF leaves it out and -DSMSD_BUILD_METAL=ON makes it required. A program uses Metal only when it links that library from the same source build, for example with target_link_libraries(my_target PRIVATE smsd smsd_metal); the installed header-only package does not include smsd_metal. In a program linked with smsd_metal, gpu::batchSimilarityScreenAuto runs on a Metal GPU when one is available, unless SMSD_DISABLE_GPU disables it, and on the CPU otherwise. For fingerprint screening, include smsd/metal_gpu.hpp and smsd/screen_accelerator.hpp.

metal::fingerprintAccelerator() supplies a resident packed-fingerprint provider. Pass it explicitly as the final argument of screen_accelerator::fingerprintScreens(queries, targets, threshold, cache, score, provider). Automatic selection is disabled: its minimum_targets returns UINT64_MAX, so attaching the provider alone does not enable it.

Use equal, non-zero word lengths and the same fingerprint settings for all queries and targets. Keep target fingerprints unchanged while reusing a screen_accelerator::ResidentCache. The score(commonBits, queryBits, targetBits) callback must use the CPU score expression and be non-decreasing in commonBits. The result keeps query and target order and matches the CPU screen exactly.

A declined screen or reported provider failure returns std::nullopt; the caller must then run its CPU screen. Provider errors are recorded by screen_accelerator::failureCount() and latestFailure(). A non-empty SMSD_DISABLE_GPU other than 0 disables GPU use.

This provider supports packed fingerprints only and has no Python export. The separate float-valued metal::batchSimilarityScreen and graph-kernel APIs are outside this integer fingerprint contract. MCS and substructure search remain on the CPU.

The Metal screening example screens a few molecules this way, falls back to the CPU screen when the provider declines or fails, and reports which path ran; configure with -DSMSD_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON to build it. Without smsd_metal it builds and runs on the CPU alone.

docs.title: Configurable fingerprints
docs.text:
FingerprintOptions gives the same bits in C++, Java and Python for computeFingerprint(graph, options) (packed bits), computeFingerprintCounts(graph, options) (count bins), fingerprintFromSmiles and batchFingerprint(molecules, options, numThreads = 0), which reads any sequence of graphs and throws the exception of the first molecule that fails. An smsd::RingBasisUnavailable error, or the error of a key left undecided by its time or embedding limit, keeps its type and adds the zero-based input index to its message. FingerprintOptions::ecfp(radius = 2, size = 2048), fcfp(radius = 2, size = 2048), path(pathLength = 7, size = 2048) and torsion(size = 2048) reproduce computeCircularFingerprintECFP, computeCircularFingerprintFCFP, Python path_fingerprint and computeTopologicalTorsion; a default-constructed FingerprintOptions is ECFP4. Turning on another switch adds terms, which can change the classic bits, so compare only fingerprints built with the same options.

#include <cassert>
#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    using smsd::batch::FingerprintOptions;
    auto options = FingerprintOptions::ecfp(2, 2048);
    options.cipAtoms = true;   // adds CIP R/S terms
    options.ringSize = true;   // adds smallest-ring-size terms
    const auto l = smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("C[C@H](N)C(=O)O", options);
    const auto d = smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("C[C@@H](N)C(=O)O", options);
    assert(l != d);
    assert(smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("C[C@H](N)C(=O)O", FingerprintOptions::ecfp())
           == smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("C[C@@H](N)C(=O)O", FingerprintOptions::ecfp()));

    auto framework = FingerprintOptions::ecfp();
    framework.scaffold = smsd::batch::ScaffoldMode::MURCKO;
    assert(smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("Cc1ccccc1", framework)
           == smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("c1ccccc1", FingerprintOptions::ecfp()));

    const auto keys = smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", FingerprintOptions::maccs());
    const auto set = smsd::bitPositions(keys, 166);
    assert(std::find(set.begin(), set.end(), 162) != set.end());   // MACCS key 163, a six-membered ring
}

FingerprintOptions members:

  • family (ECFP, FCFP, PATH, TORSION or KEYS), radius (2, or −1 for the whole component), pathLength in bonds (7) and size in bits or bins (2048).
  • Atom terms: element, degree (explicit neighbours), valence (bond order sum; pi electrons for TORSION), formalCharge, isotope, hydrogenCount, tautomerClass, aromaticity, ringMembership, and ringSize, the smallest SSSR ring, with rings of ringSizeCap (8) atoms or more sharing a class. Bond terms: bondOrder, aromaticBond and ringBond.
  • cipAtoms and cipBonds: CIP R/S (and r/s) and E/Z from smsd/cip.hpp. Circular families separate stereoisomers from radius 1; double bonds in rings under eight atoms have no E/Z term.
  • fragments: WHOLE (default), LARGEST (most heavy atoms) or PER_FRAGMENT (each atom term carries its component). scaffold: NONE (default) or MURCKO, the murckoScaffold scaffold, applied first.
  • keys: the FingerprintKey(smarts, minimum = 1) entries of a KEYS family; a key is set when at least minimum distinct atom sets match. FingerprintOptions::maccs() gives the 166 MACCS keys, key k at bit k − 1, listed by maccsKeys(); FingerprintOptions::withKeys(keys) builds a custom family.

Defaults: ECFP sets every atom term except ringSize, and bondOrder; FCFP sets degree, ringMembership and bondOrder and always adds the pharmacophore class; PATH sets element; TORSION sets element, degree, valence and ringMembership. Other switches are off. Inconsistent options and unparsable SMARTS keys throw std::invalid_argument; a key count that cannot be settled within its budget throws std::runtime_error. These options do not configure the MCS screening fingerprint.

A key whose minimum number of matches is found before the embedding limit is set; a key search that runs out of time throws, as in 8.0.3. Ring-size terms, double-bond stereo terms, aromatic-ring keys and SMARTS keys whose search needs the minimum cycle basis throw smsd::RingBasisUnavailable naming the cause if ring perception cannot complete that basis; a separate relevant-cycle truncation does not prevent their use. The ring refusals replace values that 8.0.3 could compute from incomplete rings.

docs.title: Stereochemistry and depiction
docs.text:
• cip::assignAll(graph) returns CIPDescriptors, with per-atom R/S labels in rsLabels and E/Z labels in ezBonds; cip::assignRS and cip::assignEZ label one centre or bond, cip::assignFromSMILES takes SMILES and cip::to_string formats a label. IUPAC 2013 Rule 1a applies literally to duplicate atoms, so phosphinates and phosphonates may get the opposite descriptor from software that ranks the oxo oxygen lower.
  • generateCoords2D(graph, targetBondLength = 1.5) and generateCoords3D(graph, targetBondLength = 1.5) generate coordinates; layoutQuality scores a 2D layout; transform translates, rotates, scales, mirrors and aligns coordinates.
  • depict(graph, options) returns SVG; depictWithMapping(graph, atomMapping, options) highlights mapped atoms; depictPair(query, target, mapping, options) draws a mapped pair; depictSMILES and depictMCS take SMILES; DepictOptions sets the style.
  • depictor.hpp provides compute2DCoords(graph, options), an overload keeping the atoms of a CoordMap2D fixed, and generateDepictionMatching2DStructure, which aligns a molecule to a reference by matched atom pairs.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text:
• smsd::computeTautomerConfidence(query, target, mapping): use MCS::computeTautomerConfidence(query, target, match, chemistry); the old form selects every mapped bond in both molecules and assumes water at pH 7.4.
  • smsd::implicitHydrogens(z, bondOrderSum, charge): use MolGraph::implicitHydrogenCount(atom).
  • smsd::ChemOps: use MCS::validateMapping.
  • Static MolGraph::refinePartition, comparePerm and computeCanonicalLabeling: use MolGraph::getCanonicalLabeling().
  • MolGraph::TW_NITRO_ACI_NITRO: use MolGraph::TW_NITRO_ACI.
  • hungarianSolve and HungarianResult: use optimalAssign and AssignmentResult.
  • runHortonPipeline: use computeRings or computeRelevantCycles.

Deprecated with no replacement: MolGraph::ensurePatternFP(), getNeighborsByDegDesc(), getNLF1(), getNLF2(), getNLF3(), nlfCheckOk, TW_SULFOXIDE and TW_NITRILE_ISONITRILE; popcountAnd, popcountN, anyBitAnd and popcountAndNot; and transform::translate3D, rotate3DX, rotate3DY, rotate3DZ, scale3D, center3D and rmsd2D.

docs.title: SMSD Pro Python examples
docs.text: Runnable examples for the smsd Python package beyond molecule search. Each block is self-contained, and blocks that write files create them in the current directory. Searches, options and the full API reference are in the Python guide. Interpreter and platform requirements are in the supported-platforms table.

docs.title: Circular and torsion fingerprints
docs.text:
import smsd

mol = smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccc(O)cc1")
fp = smsd.circular_fingerprint(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048)  # ECFP4
counts = smsd.circular_fingerprint_counts(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048)
fcfp = smsd.circular_fingerprint(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="fcfp")
torsion = smsd.topological_torsion(mol, fp_size=2048)
assert fp and counts and fcfp and torsion

ECFP describes structural environments and FCFP functional classes (Rogers and Hahn, 2010). Binary fingerprints hold set bit positions; count fingerprints hold (position, count) pairs. Choose the fingerprint and threshold on your own data.

docs.title: Binary and count metrics
docs.text:
import smsd

mol1 = smsd.parse_smiles("CCO")
mol2 = smsd.parse_smiles("CCCO")
fp1 = smsd.circular_fingerprint(mol1, radius=2)
fp2 = smsd.circular_fingerprint(mol2, radius=2)
scores = [smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(fp1, fp2), smsd.dice(fp1, fp2),
          smsd.cosine(fp1, fp2)]
assert all(0.0 <= score <= 1.0 for score in scores)

c1 = smsd.circular_fingerprint_counts(mol1, radius=2)
c2 = smsd.circular_fingerprint_counts(mol2, radius=2)
count_tanimoto = smsd.count_tanimoto_coefficient(c1, c2)
dense1 = smsd.counts_to_array(c1, 2048)
dense2 = smsd.counts_to_array(c2, 2048)
count_dice = smsd.count_dice(dense1, dense2)
assert 0.0 <= count_tanimoto <= 1.0 and 0.0 <= count_dice <= 1.0

# Hexadecimal storage for a binary fingerprint.
hex_string = smsd.to_hex(fp1, fp_size=2048)
assert set(smsd.from_hex(hex_string)) == set(fp1)

count_dice() and count_cosine() accept dense vectors, (position, count) pairs or dictionaries; count_tanimoto_coefficient() and count_overlap_coefficient() take pairs. Binary tanimoto_coefficient() compares set positions only, even for count input. Two empty fingerprints score 1.0 with tanimoto_coefficient() and overlap_coefficient().

docs.title: Configurable fingerprints
docs.text:
import smsd

aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"
# ECFP4 with ring-size and stereo terms; the default ECFP options give the
# same bits as circular_fingerprint().
options = smsd.FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", ring_size=True, cip_atoms=True, cip_bonds=True)
fp = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=options)
keys = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs())  # 166 MACCS keys
assert fp and keys

The same FingerprintOptions give the same bits in C++ and Java.

docs.title: Rank a small set by similarity
docs.text:
import smsd

query = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"                    # aspirin
library = ["OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1"]
ranked = smsd.batch_similarity(query, library)    # (index, Tanimoto), most similar first
assert library[ranked[0][0]] == "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1"
for index, score in ranked:
    print(f"{score:.2f}  {library[index]}")

docs.title: Screen a large library, then confirm by substructure
docs.text:
import itertools
import smsd

groups = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "Br", "C#N", "C(F)(F)F",
          "C(=O)O", "C(=O)N", "S(=O)(=O)N", "OCC"]
library = [f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}" for a, b, c in itertools.product(groups, repeat=3)]
assert len(library) == 2744

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library)   # parse once, search many times
corpus.prewarm()

query = "c1c(C)cc(O)cc1C(=O)O"
nearest = smsd.batch_similarity(query, library)[:10]

acid = smsd.Substructure.smarts("C(=O)[OX2H1]")
results = acid.match_many(corpus, num_threads=0)  # every processor core
hits = [library[i] for i, result in enumerate(results) if result.found]
assert library[nearest[0][0]] == query and query in hits

With OpenMP, as in the published wheels, num_threads=0 uses every core unless OMP_NUM_THREADS sets fewer; results keep the order of the targets.

docs.title: Screen by MCS similarity, then compute the MCS
docs.text:
import itertools
import smsd

groups = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = [f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}" for a, b, c in itertools.product(groups, repeat=3)]

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library)   # prepared once for repeated screens

query = "c1c(C)cc(O)cc1C(=O)O"
candidates = smsd.screen_targets(query, corpus, 0.8)   # targets that can reach 0.8
results = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_timeout(1000).match_many([library[i] for i in candidates])
assert candidates and all(result.found for result in results)

screen_targets bounds the atom-count Tanimoto similarity of the MCS from above, so under the same chemistry options it never rejects a target able to reach the threshold, and the MCS runs only where it can matter. For repeated screens of the same library, a prepared TargetCorpus such as this one saves converting the targets on every call; a list of molecules or SMILES gives the same indices.

This threshold applies to atom-count Tanimoto, not bond Tanimoto or weighted MCS scores. MCS.match_many itself searches every supplied target without a similarity threshold.

With smsd-cuda and an NVIDIA GPU, gpu_screening.py runs packed and corpus screens on the device and checks every result against the CPU; without them it runs on the CPU.

docs.title: SVG drawing
docs.text:
The native SVG renderer needs no RDKit. Check each drawing before publishing it, as fonts depend on the viewer.

import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import smsd

svg = smsd.depict_svg("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O")
assert ET.fromstring(svg).tag.endswith("svg")
smsd.save_svg(svg, "aspirin.svg")

query = smsd.parse_smiles("CC(=O)NC")   # N-methylacetamide
target = smsd.parse_smiles("CCC(=O)N")  # propanamide
result = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_timeout(1000).match(target)
mapping = dict(result.best.atom_mapping)
assert mapping == {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 4}
smsd.save_svg(smsd.depict_pair(query, target, mapping), "mcs_pair.svg")

# Highlight target atoms: keys must be indices in the rendered molecule.
target_mapping = {b: a for a, b in mapping.items()}
smsd.save_svg(smsd.depict_mapping(target, target_mapping), "target.svg")

docs.title: Styling
docs.text:
import smsd

options = smsd.DepictOptions()
options.bond_length = 35
options.show_map_numbers = False
options.font_family = "Arial, sans-serif"
for index, smiles in enumerate(["CCO", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)O"]):
    smsd.save_svg(smsd.depict_svg(smiles, opts=options), f"molecule_{index}.svg")

svg = smsd.depict_svg("c1ccc2c(c1)cc1ccccc1c2", bond_length=50,
                      width=800, height=400, padding=40, show_atom_indices=True)
smsd.save_svg(svg, "large.svg")

Keyword arguments such as bond_length=50 set DepictOptions attributes, on opts when it is passed.

docs.title: Optional conversion to PNG
docs.text:
Convert aspirin.svg from above with Inkscape or CairoSVG, installed separately:

inkscape aspirin.svg --export-type=png --export-filename=aspirin.png --export-dpi=600
python -c "import cairosvg; cairosvg.svg2png(url='aspirin.svg', write_to='aspirin.png', dpi=600)"

docs.title: Two and three dimensions
docs.text:
import smsd

mol = smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccccc1")
coords = smsd.generate_coords_2d(mol, target_bond_length=1.5)
assert len(coords) == len(mol) and all(len(point) == 2 for point in coords)
quality = smsd.layout_quality(mol, coords)
assert quality >= 0.0
coords_3d = smsd.generate_coords_3d(mol, target_bond_length=1.5)
assert len(coords_3d) == len(mol) and all(len(point) == 3 for point in coords_3d)

A layout_quality() score of 0.0 is ideal. Three-dimensional coordinates are a starting geometry, not a validated conformer or energy minimum.

docs.title: Refinement
docs.text:
import smsd

mol = smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccccc1")
coords = smsd.generate_coords_2d(mol)
_, coords = smsd.force_directed_layout(mol, coords, max_iter=100)
_, coords = smsd.stress_majorisation(mol, coords, max_iter=100)
crossings, coords = smsd.reduce_crossings(mol, coords, max_iter=100)
assert len(coords) == len(mol)

Refinement does not improve every layout; compare layout_quality() and inspect the drawing.

docs.title: Transforms
docs.text:
import math
import smsd

mol = smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccccc1")
coords = smsd.generate_coords_2d(mol)
coords = smsd.translate_2d(coords, dx=10.0, dy=5.0)
coords = smsd.rotate_2d(coords, angle=math.radians(45))
coords = smsd.scale_2d(coords, factor=2.0)
coords = smsd.mirror_x(coords)
coords = smsd.mirror_y(coords)
coords = smsd.center_2d(coords)
coords = smsd.normalise_bond_length(mol, coords, target=1.5)
coords = smsd.canonical_orientation(mol, coords)
reference = smsd.generate_coords_2d(mol)
rmsd, aligned = smsd.align_2d(coords, reference)
box = smsd.bounding_box_2d(aligned)
assert len(aligned) == len(mol) and len(box) == 4 and rmsd >= 0.0

Angles are in radians. Save coordinates when exact reproducibility matters.

docs.title: Stereo assignment
docs.text:
import smsd

alanine = smsd.parse_smiles("N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O")
assert smsd.assign_rs(alanine) == {1: "S"}
butene = smsd.parse_smiles("C/C=C/C")
assert smsd.assign_ez(butene) == {(1, 2): "E"}
descriptors = smsd.assign_cip(alanine)
assert descriptors.rs_labels[1] == smsd.RSLabel.S

Write explicit stereo markers in the SMILES; unspecified stereo is not assigned.

docs.title: MOL and SDF files
docs.text:
Each example creates its own input files.

import smsd

mol = smsd.parse_smiles("CCO")
smsd.write_molfile(mol, "molecule.mol")
loaded = smsd.read_mol_file("molecule.mol")
assert len(loaded) == 3
block = smsd.write_mol_block(loaded)
block_v3000 = smsd.write_mol_block_v3000(loaded)
assert len(smsd.read_mol_block(block)) == 3
assert len(smsd.read_mol_block(block_v3000)) == 3

import smsd

molecules = [smsd.parse_smiles(s) for s in ["CCO", "c1ccccc1"]]
smsd.write_sdf(molecules, "compounds.sdf")
loaded = smsd.read_sdf("compounds.sdf")
assert [len(mol) for mol in loaded] == [3, 6]
smsd.write_sdf(loaded, "output.sdf")

read_sdf() loads the whole file and turns malformed records into empty graphs, so check each record. For large files, pass records one at a time to read_mol_block(). write_mol_block() and the SDF writers switch to V3000 above 999 atoms or bonds.

docs.title: R-group decomposition
docs.text:
import smsd

options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.timeout_ms = 1000
results = smsd.Substructure.decompose_r_groups("c1ccccc1", ["Oc1ccccc1", "Nc1ccccc1", "CCO"], options)
assert [result["search"].found for result in results] == [True, True, False]
assert results[0]["core"].n == 6 and results[0]["rgroups"]["R1"].n == 1

Each entry holds the core graph, the substituent graphs and the core's search result, which shows whether a missing core was proved absent.

docs.title: Scaffolds
docs.text:
import smsd

parent = smsd.parse_smiles("Cc1ccccc1")
scaffold = smsd.murcko_scaffold(parent)
assert scaffold.n == 6
assert smsd.Substructure.find(scaffold).match(parent).found
result = smsd.MCS.find(scaffold).match("Oc1ccccc1")
assert result.best.atom_count == 6

The Bemis–Murcko scaffold keeps ring systems, their linkers and atoms double- or triple-bonded to them, such as carbonyl oxygens. An acyclic input is returned unchanged.

docs.title: Graph utilities
docs.text:
import smsd

mol = smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccccc1.CCO")
assert smsd.count_components(mol) == 2
components = smsd.split_components(mol)
assert sorted(len(part) for part in components) == [3, 6]
assert smsd.same_canonical_graph(smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccccc1"),
                                 smsd.parse_smiles("C1=CC=CC=C1"))

To compare stereoisomers in a search, enable the stereo chemistry options.

docs.title: Atom maps
docs.text:
import smsd

mapped = "[CH3:1][C:2](=[O:3])[OH:4]"
clean = smsd.strip_atom_maps(mapped)
assert clean == "[CH3][C](=[O])[OH]"
assert len(smsd.parse_smiles(clean)) == 4

Use strip_atom_maps() rather than a regular expression: outside brackets, a colon is an aromatic bond, so text replacement can alter the structure. parse_mapped_smiles() strips and parses in one call.

docs.title: AI assistants
docs.text: An AI assistant can call the molecular tools through the local MCP server (smsd-mcp) or through tool definitions in your own Python loop. The tools run on your machine. Each search result reports its status and whether it is optimal and complete. See Connecting AI assistants for set-up steps and worked examples. agent_workflow.py chains screening, MCS and depiction through call_tool without a model, and mcp_stdio_client.py checks the MCP server from Python.

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text:
See the user guide, the Python guide, the installation guide, the C++ guide and the Java guide. Five notebooks work through the guide's topics: substructure and SMARTS search, maximum common substructure, fingerprints and similarity, library screening and CPU and GPU screening.

A C++ program that screens packed fingerprints on a Metal GPU, with the CPU screen as the fallback, is the Metal screening example.

docs.title: Installation and source builds
docs.text: This guide covers installing SMSD Pro 8.1.0 and building it from source. Release files are on the GitHub releases page; the README lists the Python and Maven packages and the conda recipes.

docs.title: Install SMSD Pro 8.1.0
docs.text:
Install the Python package from PyPI:

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"

For NVIDIA GPU screening on Linux x86_64, add the optional CUDA package of the same version: python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0". The Java library and command-line tool stay at 8.0.3 on Maven Central, as com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd:8.0.3 and com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli:8.0.3; the Java module README gives their Maven and Gradle dependencies. The CPU Docker images carry the 8.1.0 command-line tool, and a Java source build produces the 8.1.0 Java library and tool. The C++ headers need a C++17 compiler and no Python or Java runtime.

See Python adapters and MCP, packed corpora and clustering, and SMARTS export. PyTorch on macOS may require an OpenMP-free SMSD source build to avoid incompatible bundled runtimes. Portable SMARTS rejects unsupported matching constraints instead of silently dropping them.

The conda guide describes the recipes that build smsd and, on Linux x86_64, smsd-cuda for NVIDIA GPU screening. It also covers the conda, mamba and Pixi install routes.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
Package Platform Interpreter or runtime Compute smsd wheel Windows 10 or later, x86_64 (AMD64) CPython 3.12–3.15 CPU/OpenMP smsd wheel Linux with glibc 2.28 or later, x86_64 or aarch64 CPython 3.12–3.15 CPU/OpenMP smsd wheel macOS 14 or later, arm64 (Apple silicon) CPython 3.12–3.15 CPU/OpenMP smsd-cuda wheel Linux with glibc 2.34 or later, x86_64 CPython 3.12–3.15; matching smsd; NVIDIA driver compatible with the installed CUDA 12 runtime Automatic ECFP4 screening on Tesla T4 (compute capability 7.5) Java library, CLI JAR and portable CLI Windows, macOS or Linux Java 8 or later; Java 25 LTS preferred CPU Java CLI installers (8.0.3 release) Windows x86_64 (MSI), macOS arm64 (DMG), Linux amd64 (DEB) Bundled Java 25 runtime CPU Python source build A platform with a C++17 compiler Python 3.12 or later; CMake 3.18 or later CPU; optional CUDA package built separately C++ headers A platform with a C++17 compiler No Python or Java runtime needed CPU; native CUDA or macOS Metal source build optional

Minimum operating-system versions are build targets. The standard wheel matrix has four CPython versions on four platforms. Free-threaded CPython and Intel macOS need source builds. Python wheels do not include macOS GPU support or native Windows CUDA. Native C++ source builds on macOS include optional Metal support, which a program uses only when it links smsd_metal; Metal fingerprint screening runs only when requested explicitly. Search matching runs on the CPU in every package. By default, automatic ECFP4 screening of a prepared TargetCorpus uses the GPU only on a Tesla T4 and only for a corpus of at least 100,000 targets; the CUDA screening section gives the explicit routes for other devices.

docs.title: Verify downloads
docs.text:
Each GitHub release includes a SHA256SUMS file. Download it into the same directory as the release files, then check each file you use.

macOS or Linux:

grep ' smsd-cpp-8.1.0-headers.tar.gz$' SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c

Windows PowerShell (prints True when the checksum matches):

$entry = Select-String -Path SHA256SUMS -SimpleMatch ' smsd-cpp-8.1.0-headers.tar.gz'
(Get-FileHash .\smsd-cpp-8.1.0-headers.tar.gz -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq $entry.Line.Split(' ')[0]

Replace the file name to check another download.

docs.title: Portable Java CLI
docs.text:
The standalone Java command-line tool stays at 8.0.3 in this release, so this section uses the files of the 8.0.3 release; the CPU Docker images carry the 8.1.0 tool, and a Java source build produces it.

smsd-cli-8.0.3-jar-with-dependencies.jar contains the SMSD library, CDK 2.13 and the other CLI dependencies, and runs on Java 8 or later. From its directory:

java -jar smsd-cli-8.0.3-jar-with-dependencies.jar --version
java -jar smsd-cli-8.0.3-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --Q SMI --q "CCN" --T SMI --t "CCCNC" -m --json -

The second command runs a substructure search and writes every mapping as JSON to standard output. The same JAR is on Maven Central as com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli:8.0.3 with the classifier jar-with-dependencies.

smsd-8.0.3-cli.tar.gz holds Unix and Windows launchers. Extract it into one directory so that bin and repo stay together:

mkdir smsd-cli
tar -xzf smsd-8.0.3-cli.tar.gz -C smsd-cli
./smsd-cli/bin/smsd --version

On Windows, run smsd-cli\bin\smsd.bat. Neither package includes a Java runtime.

The 8.0.3 MSI, DMG and DEB installers include Java 25. Their architectures are listed in the supported-platforms table.

docs.title: Java source build
docs.text:
Use a JDK (Java 25 LTS preferred) and Maven 3.9 or later. From the repository root:

mvn -f java/pom.xml clean package
java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar --version

The build runs the default tests, writes the library JAR to java/core/target, and writes the CLI JARs and the portable launchers to java/cli/target. mvn -f java/pom.xml install also installs com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd:8.1.0 and com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli:8.1.0 in the local Maven repository. To use them, set version 8.1.0 in the Maven or Gradle dependencies of the Java module README; Gradle also needs mavenLocal() in its repositories.

To run the slow tests as well:

mvn -f java/pom.xml -Dslow.tests.exclude=nothing clean verify

The code is compiled for Java 8 (--release 8). To run the tests on a Java 8 runtime, set SMSD_JAVA8_HOME to a Java 8 JDK:

mvn -f java/pom.xml -Dslow.tests.exclude=nothing \
  "-Djvm=$SMSD_JAVA8_HOME/bin/java" test

See the Java guide for the API and CLI reference.

docs.title: C++ source build
docs.text:
The C++ library is header-only: use cpp/include, or the release archive smsd-cpp-8.1.0-headers.tar.gz. The CMake build needs CMake 3.18 or later, and ctest --test-dir needs CMake 3.20 or later. On Windows, use Developer PowerShell for Visual Studio with the Desktop development with C++ workload. From the repository root:

cmake -S cpp -B build/cpu -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DSMSD_BUILD_TESTS=ON -DSMSD_BUILD_PYTHON=OFF -DSMSD_BUILD_METAL=OFF -DSMSD_BUILD_CUDA=OFF
cmake --build build/cpu --config Debug --parallel 4
ctest --test-dir build/cpu --build-config Debug --output-on-failure

Batch operations use OpenMP when CMake finds it; on macOS, install libomp (for example with Homebrew) and add its prefix to CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH. -DSMSD_WITH_RDKIT=ON builds the optional RDKit adapter, which needs the RDKit development files and C++20. The C++ module README shows how to install the package and use it from CMake; the C++ guide is the API reference.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
Install the release wheel for your platform from PyPI or the GitHub release:

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"
python -c "import smsd; print(smsd.__version__); assert smsd.parse_smiles('CC').n == 2"

Wheels are built for standard CPython 3.12–3.15 (cp312 through cp315), not the free-threaded builds. Other interpreters and platforms need a source build, with Python 3.12 or later, a C++17 compiler, CMake and the Python development headers.

Linux or macOS, from the repository root:

python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
.venv/bin/python -m build --wheel

Windows, from Developer PowerShell:

py -3 -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip build
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m build --wheel

Source builds leave Metal and CUDA out by default. Python screening and search do not run on them, so -Ccmake.define.SMSD_BUILD_METAL=ON or -Ccmake.define.SMSD_BUILD_CUDA=ON (or AUTO, which includes each one when it is available) changes only what gpu_is_available() and gpu_device_info() report. NVIDIA screening comes from the separate smsd-cuda package. The wheel is written to dist/; install it with the same environment's Python. For development, install the checkout in editable mode with the test dependencies, then run the tests:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -c "import smsd; assert smsd.Substructure.find('CC').match('CCC').found"
python -m pytest python/tests -q

The standard wheels use CPU/OpenMP. For optional NVIDIA CUDA screening on a supported Linux system, install the matching package:

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0"

The CUDA runtime is installed as a package dependency; the host still needs a compatible NVIDIA driver. See CUDA screening for dispatch and CPU fallback behaviour. RDKit is needed only for RDKit molecule conversion and RDKit depiction (python -m pip install "smsd[rdkit]==8.1.0"). See the Python guide for examples and build options.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The CPU images include the 8.1.0 Java CLI and the Python package. The default command is the Java CLI; use --entrypoint python for Python. After loading the image archive from the release:

docker load --input smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-amd64.tar.xz
docker run --rm smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 \
  --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "c1ccc(O)cc1" --json -
docker run --rm --entrypoint python smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 \
  -c "import smsd; assert smsd.Substructure.find('CC').match('CCC').found"

On an arm64 host, load smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-arm64.tar.xz and use smsd:8.1.0-cpu-arm64. The GPU image includes the Python package, matching smsd-cuda and CUDA runtime, with Python as its entry point:

docker load --input smsd-8.1.0-cuda-linux-amd64.tar.xz
docker run --rm --gpus all smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8 \
  -c "import smsd; print(smsd.__version__); print(smsd.gpu_device_info())"

It needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and a compatible host driver, including when used through WSL2 on Windows. The final image contains no CUDA toolkit. Backend availability does not prove that a screening call used the GPU.

Source builds use a prepared context containing the matching release wheels and their checksums. Given a completed release directory with its source and wheel manifests, prepare a fresh context and use the source_commit recorded in SOURCE_MANIFEST.json as the revision:

python scripts/prepare_docker_context.py \
  --release-dir release --output docker-context --architecture amd64
docker buildx build --load --platform linux/amd64 \
  --build-arg SMSD_REVISION=SOURCE_COMMIT \
  -f docker-context/Dockerfile -t smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 docker-context

Replace SOURCE_COMMIT with that recorded value. For arm64, use a separate context with --architecture arm64, platform linux/arm64 and tag smsd:8.1.0-cpu-arm64. To prepare the GPU context, add --cuda-wheel, --cuda-provenance and --runtime-wheel with the matching smsd-cuda wheel, its provenance record and the pinned runtime wheel. Build that context with Dockerfile.cuda, platform linux/amd64 and tag smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8. The GPU Dockerfile needs BuildKit with its bundled Dockerfile frontend 1.2 or later. Its wheel inputs are mounted for installation rather than copied into final image layers; the same installed-file and runtime checks still run. python scripts/prepare_docker_context.py --help lists the required inputs. The CPU images hold LICENSE, NOTICE and the CLI dependency licence files in /usr/share/doc/smsd; every image retains the notices of its bundled runtimes.

To save a built image as a release archive:

python scripts/archive_docker_image.py --image smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8 \
  --revision SOURCE_COMMIT --architecture amd64 \
  --output smsd-8.1.0-cuda-linux-amd64.tar.xz
docker load --input smsd-8.1.0-cuda-linux-amd64.tar.xz

If the Docker engine has no xz decompressor, decompress on the host before loading:

xz --decompress --stdout smsd-8.1.0-cuda-linux-amd64.tar.xz | docker load

For a CPU image, use --image smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 and output smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-amd64.tar.xz; replace both architecture values with arm64 for that platform. The helper saves the documented tag and checks that its image identity, revision label and platform stay unchanged during export. It requires the xz archive to be smaller than 2,000,000,000 bytes. An existing output is never overwritten. Failed exports retain the partial archive, stderr log and a JSON record with accepted=false.

docs.title: Check the documented examples
docs.text:
After a source build, this runs every Python, Java and C++ code block in the main guides; examples that need RDKit are skipped when it is absent:

python scripts/check_examples.py \
  --jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --report build/example-check.json

Add --languages python (or java, cpp) to check one language.

docs.title: SMSD Pro Java guide
docs.text:
Java prepared queries retain their CPU matchMany API. The optional native corpus prefilters exposed in C++ and Python do not add a Java GPU search API.

The package com.bioinception.smsd.core (artefact com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd) provides substructure, maximum common substructure (MCS) and SMARTS search, fingerprints, stereo descriptors, standardisation and R-group decomposition for CDK 2.13 IAtomContainer molecules and MolGraph graphs. The command-line interface (CLI) is com.bioinception.smsd.cli.SMSDcli (com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli). The Javadoc lists every public member.

In this release the Java library and command-line tool stay at 8.0.3 on Maven Central. This guide covers the Java code in the 8.1.0 source, which a Java source build turns into the library and command-line tool; the 8.0.3 artefacts do not have its 8.1.0 changes. The CPU Docker images also carry the 8.1.0 command-line tool.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
The JARs run on Java 8 and later; Java 25 LTS is recommended. See the supported-platforms table for the CLI installers. Maven:

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.bioinceptionlabs</groupId>
  <artifactId>smsd</artifactId>
  <version>8.0.3</version>
</dependency>

Gradle (Kotlin DSL):

repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    implementation("com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd:8.0.3")
}

To parse SMILES, as the examples do, add org.openscience.cdk:cdk-smiles:2.13. The Java module README lists the other optional dependencies, such as jackson-databind for Standardiser.PredicateRegistry.loadJsonFile, and covers building from source and a quick start. To run an example, save it under its class name and compile it from the repository root against the self-contained JAR of the source build:

javac --release 8 -cp java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar PreparedSearchExample.java
java -cp "java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar:." PreparedSearchExample

With a Java 8 compiler, omit --release 8; on Windows, separate the classpath entries with a semicolon.

docs.title: SMARTS export in 8.1.0
docs.text: MCS.matchWithSmarts(target) returns MCS.SmartsResult; result() retains the ordinary search status and mappings, and smarts() is the best match's portable pattern under the prepared chemistry. SearchResult.Match.toSmarts(query, chemistry) and SmartsWriter.toSmarts(graph, chemistry) provide explicit export. See SMARTS export for a library-search example, selected bond semantics and rejected options. Stereo, tautomer-aware, complete-ring and strict ring-fusion constraints cannot be silently discarded. Portable SMARTS does not encode the induced MCIS objective, a resource budget or an optimality proof.

docs.title: Input graphs
docs.text:
Searches accept an IAtomContainer or a MolGraph. new MolGraph(container) keeps the CDK atom order; mappings, atom weights and exclusions use these zero-based indices. Aromaticity, hydrogen counts and stereochemistry are used as given; Standardiser.standardise(container, Standardiser.TautomerMode.NONE) returns a copy with atom types, implicit hydrogens, rings and Daylight aromaticity. The CDK SmilesParser gives atoms written in capitals but joined by : ring bonds, as in C1:C:C:C:C:C:1, the hydrogens of single bonds; MolGraph and Standardiser.standardise read such a ring as aromatic, as the native reader does, but the CDK molecule does not record which nitrogen a bracket hydrogen was written on, so where several could carry it, one that gives a Kekulé structure does, whatever the atom order. The CLI reads such SMILES as written.

MolGraph.Builder builds a graph without CDK from atomCount, atomicNumbers and neighbors, optionally with formalCharges, massNumbers, hydrogenCounts, aromaticFlags, ringFlags, bondOrders, bondAromaticFlags, bondRingFlags, tetrahedralChirality, doubleBondStereo, atomIds, name, programLine, comment and properties; build() returns the graph. A graph exposes the per-atom arrays atomicNum, formalCharge, massNumber, label, tautomerClass and atomId, the methods atomCount(), hydrogenCount(atom) and hasBond(i, j), and the MOL header fields name, programLine, comment and properties.

Prepared queries copy their query and options, so they can be reused and shared between threads; do not modify a target during a search.

docs.title: Prepared searches
docs.text:
• MCS.find(query), Substructure.find(query): a prepared query with default options; Substructure.smarts(expression): a SMARTS query, including recursive and stereo predicates.
  • withOptions(options), withTimeout(milliseconds): a new prepared query with copied options.
  • match(target): a SearchResult with the best MCS or one embedding.
  • matchAll(target), matchAll(target, limit): all tied MCS optima, symmetric ones included, or all embeddings, up to a positive limit (default 1,000).
  • matchMany(targets), matchMany(targets, numThreads): one SearchResult per MolGraph target, in order, each with the full timeout; 0 threads uses every processor, 1 searches in turn.

Substructure.smarts follows Daylight SMARTS and aromaticity and raises IllegalArgumentException for invalid SMARTS or SMARTS beyond Substructure.MAX_SMARTS_LENGTH, MAX_SMARTS_ATOMS, MAX_SMARTS_EXPRESSION_NODES, MAX_SMARTS_NODES_PER_EXPRESSION or MAX_SMARTS_RECURSION_DEPTH.

Standardiser.expandNamedPredicates(smarts, registry) replaces $name tokens, where a name is ASCII letters, digits and underscores, inside recursive SMARTS as well, with SMARTS from a Standardiser.PredicateRegistry, which offers put(name, smarts), contains(name), get(name) and loadJsonFile(path) (a JSON object of names and SMARTS). A definition is expanded as recursive SMARTS, so it describes the atom written first. The registry starts with ten predicates, defined as in the native core:

  • isAmideN: N with three connections bonded to a carbonyl carbon (amides, lactams, imides, ureas and carbamates), aromatic rings such as uracil and 2-pyridone included.
  • isCarboxylC: carbonyl carbon bearing OH or O⁻ (carboxylic acids and carboxylates, carbamic acids, carbonic acid monoesters and bicarbonate).
  • isSulfonamideN: N with three connections bonded to a sulfonyl S.
  • isEster: carbonyl carbon of a carboxylic ester, formates and aromatic lactones such as coumarin included; anhydrides are excluded.
  • isKetone: carbonyl carbon bonded to two carbons, ring carbonyls such as chromone and 4-pyridone included.
  • isHalogen: F, Cl, Br or I.
  • isPositive, isNegative: a charge of +1 to +15, or −1 to −15.
  • isHBDonor: N, O or S bearing hydrogen, aromatic NH included.
  • isHBAcceptor: N, O or S of charge 0 to −3 with a free lone pair, aniline, nitrile, thioamide, amidine and sulfonamide N included; amide N, aromatic N with three connections (pyrrole type), N of valence 5 (nitro and N-oxide written without charges) and S of valence 4 or 6 (sulfoxides, sulfones) are excluded.

Standardiser.matchAll(smarts, target) is deprecated in favour of Substructure.smarts(smarts).matchAll(target).

docs.title: Search options
docs.text:
Set fields on MCS.Options or Substructure.Options and pass the object to withOptions; invalid values raise IllegalArgumentException. Defaults are in brackets.

  • chemistry (new ChemOptions()): see chemistry options.
  • MCS.Options.objective (MCS.Objective.MCIS): MCIS, the maximum common induced subgraph, maximises atoms, then bonds; MCES, the maximum common edge subgraph, maximises bonds, then atoms, with no isolated atoms.
  • MCS.Options.connectivity (MCS.Connectivity.Connected): one common fragment, or several with Fragments; minFragmentAtoms (1) and maxFragments (Integer.MAX_VALUE), both at least 1, bound their size and number.
  • MCS.Options.atomWeights (null): MCIS only; one finite weight per query atom, maximising the weight sum first. null or empty is unweighted.
  • MCS.Options.excludedTargetAtoms (empty): target atoms never mapped.
  • Substructure.Options.induced (false): unbonded query atom pairs must map to unbonded target atoms.
  • timeoutMillis (-1): negative selects the default, which for MCS is 500 ms plus 2 ms per atom pair (query atoms × target atoms), at most 30,000 ms: 1,300 ms for two 20-atom molecules, 5,500 ms for two 50-atom molecules and 30,000 ms from 122 atoms each. For substructure search it is 10,000 ms. 0 stops at once; positive is milliseconds.
  • nodeLimit (0, unlimited): the maximum number of search nodes.
  • cancellation (null): a BooleanSupplier; returning true cancels.

The timeout and node limit cover the search, not parsing or preparation; interrupting the calling thread also cancels it. Java uses atom weights unrounded, whereas C++ and Python score them in units of 0.001.

docs.title: Chemistry options
docs.text:
ChemOptions fields are public. withBondOrderMode, withAromaticityMode, withCompleteRingsOnly, withMatchIsotope, withRingFusionMode, withTautomerAware, withPH and withSolvent set a field and return the same instance; ChemOptions.copyOf(options) returns an independent copy.

  • matchAtomType (true), matchFormalCharge, matchIsotope (false): compare elements, formal charges and isotope labels.
  • matchBondOrder (BondOrderMode.STRICT): STRICT needs equal orders, LOOSE relaxes them within the aromaticity and ring settings, ANY accepts any.
  • aromaticityMode (AromaticityMode.FLEXIBLE): aromatic bonds also match single and double bonds; STRICT matches them only with aromatic bonds.
  • ringMatchesRingOnly (false): ring atoms and bonds match only ring atoms and bonds. completeRingsOnly (false): MCS keeps ring atoms and bonds only within relevant cycles selected whole in both molecules.
  • ringFusionMode (RingFusionMode.IGNORE): IGNORE, PERMISSIVE or STRICT; strict matching requires matched ring atoms to have the same per-atom ring count.
  • useChirality, useBondStereo (false): mapped tetrahedral centres and double bonds must agree in configuration, compared by the parity of their mapped neighbours, not by CIP labels (R/S, E/Z); see stereochemistry.
  • tautomerAware (false): treat tautomeric bonds as equivalent.
  • pH (7.4), solvent (Solvent.AQUEOUS; also DMSO, METHANOL, CHLOROFORM, ACETONITRILE, DIETHYL_ETHER): used only by MCS.computeTautomerConfidence.

The deprecated fields useTwoHopNLF, useThreeHopNLF and useBitParallelFeasibility, and their setters withTwoHopNLF, withThreeHopNLF and withBitParallelFeasibility, never change a result.

Profiles return new instances; ChemOptions.profile(name) ignores case and raises IllegalArgumentException for an unknown name:

  • new ChemOptions(), ChemOptions.profile("default"): the defaults above.
  • profile("strict"): strict bond order and aromaticity.
  • profile("compat-fmcs"), profile("compat-substruct"), profile("reaction"): loose bond order. The deprecated ChemOptions.fmcsProfile() returns profile("compat-fmcs").
  • profile("pharma"): formal-charge, ring-only and complete-ring matching.
  • ChemOptions.tautomerProfile(): tautomer-aware matching, loose bond order.

docs.title: Stereochemistry
docs.text:
With useChirality, a tetrahedral centre has four neighbours and no implicit hydrogen, or three neighbours and one implicit hydrogen or, for N, P, S, As, Se, Sb and Te, a lone pair. MolGraph.Builder.tetrahedralChirality takes 1 for @ and 2 for @@ over the listed neighbours, with the implicit hydrogen or lone pair second when the first neighbour's index is below the centre's, and first otherwise. A configured query centre or double bond needs the same configuration in the target (in MCS, once enough neighbours are mapped to define it); unconfigured query atoms and bonds, and in MCS unspecified target stereochemistry, match any. The test compares the parity of the mapped neighbours, the @ or @@ order around a centre and the cis or trans placement across a double bond, not CIP labels, whose priorities depend on atoms outside the mapping.

In MCS, stereochemistry is a hard constraint. An MCIS is the largest common subgraph whose mapped centres and double bonds agree, so it can be smaller than the MCIS found without these options; an MCES instead leaves out the fewest common bonds that resolve each disagreement.

docs.title: Tautomers
docs.text:
MCS.computeTautomerConfidence(query, target, match, chemistry) scores the tautomeric relaxations of a match found with ChemOptions.tautomerProfile(), at chemistry.pH (0 to 14) in chemistry.solvent: 1 when none is needed or tautomerAware is off, lower for less favoured ones. It is not a probability or an MCS score, changes neither graph and agrees across Java, C++ and Python. The deprecated three-argument form takes an atom mapping, selects every mapped bond common to both molecules and assumes water at pH 7.4. MCS.validateTautomerConsistency(query, target, mapping) checks that mobile N–H, O–H and S–H protons are conserved within each mapped tautomeric group.

Per atom, MolGraph.tautomerClass holds the tautomer class (from 0, independent of atom order except among symmetric classes; −1 outside every class), tautomerWeight its MolGraph.TW_* weight (1 outside every class), tautomerSite its ionisable site (TAUTOMER_SITE_ACID, TAUTOMER_SITE_BASE or TAUTOMER_SITE_NONE) and tautomerPKa its aqueous MolGraph.TPKA_* pKa.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A SearchResult reports:

  • status(): Completed (the search ran to its end), TimedOut (the time limit stopped it), Cancelled (cancellation or an interrupt stopped it) or LimitReached (the node limit stopped it, an enumeration reached its match limit, or an MCES pair beyond the size limits was declined before any search, which returns no match and proves nothing).
  • optimal(): the result is proved. complete(): the requested search finished. found(): a match was retained.
  • matches(), score(): the SearchResult.Match objects and the best score.
  • nodesVisited(), elapsedMillis(): search effort.

completeRingsOnly requires complete relevant-cycle perception; RingFusionMode.STRICT requires complete perception for its per-atom ring counts. If that perception is incomplete in either input, the selected mappings remain, but the result is LimitReached, with optimal() and complete() both false; TimedOut and Cancelled take precedence. Positive numeric SMARTS R<n> (n > 0) uses one deterministic minimum cycle basis, the same as C++ and Python, so a result that 8.0.3 computed from a different minimum basis of equal size can change. If ring perception cannot complete the basis, a search that cannot be decided without it returns LimitReached without matches, including for negated, combined and recursive predicates; found() is then false, which does not prove absence. Literal R and R0 remain independent of that basis. Other functions that need the basis throw RingBasisUnavailableException, an IllegalStateException, naming the cause; computeSSSR and computeRings may return incomplete rings with truncation flags. relevantCyclesTruncated alone does not make the basis incomplete. Ring perception works within one fixed, deterministic work limit; see Results and budgets.

A SearchResult.Match uses the original atom indices; pass it the query that prepared the search:

  • atomMapping(): query atom to target atom.
  • bondMapping(): query bond to target bond, as SearchResult.Bond pairs with the lower atom index in first() and the higher in second().
  • fragments(): sets of query atoms joined by selected bonds.
  • atomCount(), bondCount(), score(): the score is the atom count for MCIS, the weight sum for weighted MCIS and the bond count for MCES.
  • toMolecule(query), toSmiles(query), toGraph(query): the common fragment as a CDK molecule, as canonical SMILES (cut valences capped), or as a MolGraph with the original chemical properties.

A completed search proves its result, including absence, and a substructure match proves existence; a stopped search may return a valid but unproved match. A capped MCS enumeration can be optimal yet incomplete. The C++ and Python MCIS search changed in 8.1.0 and Java's did not, so a stopped search can return a different result in Java; see the upgrade notes. In rare cases Java reports Cancelled, with optimal() true and complete() false, for a search whose proof had already completed; the score and the proof are unaffected.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
An MCES search declines a pair before searching it, with LimitReached, no match, and optimal() and complete() both false, when:

  • query atoms × target atoms exceed 2³⁰ (1,073,741,824), as for two molecules of more than 32,768 atoms each;
  • the two molecules are too large in bonds, as for two molecules of more than 16,384 bonds each;
  • rarely, a molecule has an atom with 512 or more bonds and the two molecules share many kinds of bond.

MCIS searches are never declined; the time and node limits bound them. The C++ and Python libraries use the same limits.

docs.title: Example: prepared queries and fragments
docs.text:
PreparedSearchExample.java compares an MCIS with an MCES, finds common fragments, enumerates embeddings with and without a cap, searches a batch and matches SMARTS. Cyclopropane and isobutane share two atoms as an MCIS, as any three ring atoms form a triangle, but a two-bond path as an MCES; diethyl ether and diethylamine share two separate ethyl groups:

import com.bioinception.smsd.core.MCS;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.MolGraph;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.SearchResult;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.Substructure;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;
import org.openscience.cdk.silent.SilentChemObjectBuilder;
import org.openscience.cdk.smiles.SmilesParser;

public class PreparedSearchExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        SmilesParser parser = new SmilesParser(SilentChemObjectBuilder.getInstance());
        MolGraph ring = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("C1CC1"));       // cyclopropane
        MolGraph branched = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("CC(C)C"));  // isobutane
        SearchResult induced = MCS.find(ring).match(branched);
        MCS.Options options = new MCS.Options();
        options.objective = MCS.Objective.MCES;
        SearchResult edges = MCS.find(ring).withOptions(options).match(branched);
        if (!induced.optimal() || !induced.found()
                || induced.matches().get(0).atomCount() != 2
                || !edges.optimal() || !edges.found()
                || edges.matches().get(0).bondCount() != 2) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected a two-atom MCIS and a two-bond MCES");
        }

        options.connectivity = MCS.Connectivity.Fragments;
        options.minFragmentAtoms = 1;
        MolGraph ether = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("CCOCC"));
        MolGraph amine = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("CCNCC"));
        SearchResult fragments = MCS.find(ether).withOptions(options).match(amine);
        if (!fragments.optimal() || !fragments.found()
                || fragments.matches().get(0).fragments().size() != 2) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected two common ethyl fragments");
        }

        Substructure query = Substructure.find(new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("CO")));
        MolGraph target = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("OCO"));
        SearchResult all = query.matchAll(target, 10);
        List<SearchResult> batch = query.matchMany(Arrays.asList(target, branched));
        if (!all.complete() || all.matches().size() != 2
                || !batch.get(0).found() || batch.get(1).found()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected enumeration or batch result");
        }
        SearchResult capped = query.matchAll(target, 1);
        if (capped.status() != SearchResult.Status.LimitReached || capped.complete()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected an incomplete capped enumeration");
        }
        if (!Substructure.smarts("[OX2H]").match(
                parser.parseSmiles("CCO")).found()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected an alcohol SMARTS match");
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Mapping and consensus utilities
docs.text:
• MCS.matchConstrained(queries, target, options): one result per query, searched in turn with its own budget, avoiding target atoms that earlier matches claimed; Cancelled for the rest after cancellation.
  • MCS.consensus(molecules, options, threshold): a fragment shared by at least ceil(threshold × number of molecules) inputs, under one budget; threshold lies in (0, 1], and atom weights are rejected. Progressive reduction is an approximation; it does not prove a global multi-molecule optimum.
  • MCS.validateMapping(query, target, match, options): the ways a match violates the options, empty if valid. The atom-mapping overload checks the bonds mappingMatch selects; the ChemOptions overload is deprecated.
  • MCS.mappingMatch(query, target, mapping, options): an atom mapping as a match, with every compatible query bond between mapped atoms.
  • MCS.isMappingMaximal(query, target, match, options), also for an atom mapping: true if no valid extension exists, false for an invalid match, IllegalStateException if the budget runs out or required ring perception was truncated.
  • MCS.fragment(query, atoms, bonds): a Match from an atom mapping and query bonds.
  • MCS.canonicalizeMapping(query, target, mapping): the canonical form of an atom mapping under the symmetries of both graphs, ignoring bond selections; IllegalArgumentException for an atom outside either graph, IllegalStateException if a graph's symmetry cannot be fully determined.
  • MCS.similarityUpperBound(query, target, chemistry): an upper bound on atom-based MCS similarity from atom labels.
  • MCS.murckoScaffold(molecule): the Bemis-Murcko scaffold (ring systems, linkers and atoms double- or triple-bonded to them) as a new molecule, hydrogen-capped, keeping stereochemistry that stays defined.

MCS.ConsensusResult holds fragment() in the atom indices of input sourceIndex(), the same fragment as graph() and toSmiles(), and mappings() from graph() atoms to each supporting input; supportCount(), status(), complete(), nodesVisited() and elapsedMillis() describe the search. optimal() is always false, including empty and single-input calls. complete() reports whether the progressive pass finished. Neither it nor Completed proves a global optimum or absence of a qualifying common graph. With no result, sourceIndex() is -1 and the fragment, graph and SMILES are empty. With complete rings or strict ring fusion, truncated ring perception in any input also makes consensus LimitReached and incomplete, unless its status is already TimedOut or Cancelled. Its fragment and supporting mappings are retained.

docs.title: Fingerprints, stereo descriptors and R-groups
docs.text:
FeaturesExample.java compares fingerprints, assigns stereo descriptors and decomposes phenol and toluene against benzene:

import com.bioinception.smsd.core.ChemOptions;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.CIPAssigner;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.FingerprintEngine;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.MolGraph;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.Substructure;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.openscience.cdk.interfaces.IAtomContainer;
import org.openscience.cdk.silent.SilentChemObjectBuilder;
import org.openscience.cdk.smiles.SmilesParser;

public class FeaturesExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        SmilesParser parser = new SmilesParser(SilentChemObjectBuilder.getInstance());
        IAtomContainer phenol = parser.parseSmiles("c1ccc(O)cc1");
        long[] path = FingerprintEngine.pathFingerprint(phenol, 7, 2048);
        long[] common = FingerprintEngine.mcsFingerprint(phenol, new ChemOptions(), 7, 2048);
        long[] circular = FingerprintEngine.ecfp(phenol, 2, 2048);
        if (!FingerprintEngine.fingerprintSubset(path, path)
                || FingerprintEngine.tanimoto(common, common) != 1.0
                || FingerprintEngine.tanimoto(circular, circular) != 1.0) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected identical fingerprints to match");
        }

        MolGraph chiral = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O"));
        MolGraph alkene = new MolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("F/C=C/F"));
        Map<Integer, Character> rs = CIPAssigner.assignRS(chiral);
        Map<Long, Character> ez = CIPAssigner.assignEZ(alkene);
        if (rs.isEmpty() || ez.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected explicit stereo descriptors");
        }
        System.out.println("Atom descriptors: " + rs);
        System.out.println("Bond descriptors: " + ez);

        IAtomContainer core = parser.parseSmiles("c1ccccc1");
        List<IAtomContainer> molecules = Arrays.asList(
                phenol, parser.parseSmiles("Cc1ccccc1"));
        List<Substructure.Decomposition> groups =
                Substructure.decomposeRGroups(core, molecules, new ChemOptions(), 1000);
        if (groups.size() != 2) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Expected two decomposition rows");
        }
        for (Substructure.Decomposition row : groups) {
            if (!row.search().complete() || row.core() == null) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("Core search did not complete with a match");
            }
            System.out.println("Attached groups: " + row.rgroups().size());
        }
    }
}

FingerprintEngine methods are static; the IAtomContainer forms standardise a copy first, so for several fingerprints convert once with FingerprintEngine.toMolGraph(molecule):

  • pathFingerprint(molecule, pathLength, size); for MCS screening, mcsFingerprint(molecule, chemistry, pathLength, size), which honours tautomerAware.
  • ecfp, fcfp, circularFingerprint(..., Mode) (FingerprintEngine.Mode.ECFP or FCFP; radius 2 is ECFP4), ecfpCounts, fcfpCounts, circularFingerprintCounts, topologicalTorsion, topologicalTorsionCounts.
  • tanimoto, dice, cosine, soergel (1 − Tanimoto), overlapCoefficient, and for counts tanimotoCounts, diceCounts, cosineCounts. Two empty bit fingerprints give 1.0 from tanimoto and overlapCoefficient, 0.0 from dice and cosine.
  • fingerprintSubset(query, target): every query bit is set in the target; a screen, not a substitute for graph matching.
  • toHex, fromHex, toBitSet, fromBitSet, toBinaryString, countsToArray: conversion.
  • analyzeFpQuality(fp, size): set_bits, fp_size, density, expected_collision_rate and is_saturated (density over 0.75), with the definitions of Python analyze_fp_quality: s of N bits set suggest n = ln(1 − s/N) / ln(1 − 1/N) uniformly hashed features, of which the share 1 − s/n fell on a bit already set; path fingerprints of a power-of-two size collide more often than uniform hashing predicts. analyzeFingerprintQuality is deprecated.
  • suggestFingerprintSize(atoms, librarySize, rate): the path fingerprint size at which a path absent from a molecule finds its bit set with probability of about rate, allowing seven distinct paths per atom, more than most drug-like molecules have, and one bit per path: m = −n / ln(1 − rate), rounded up to a multiple of 64; atoms must be at least 1, rate must lie strictly between 0 and 1, and a size beyond the int range is rejected.

docs.title: Configurable fingerprints
docs.text:
FingerprintOptions gives the same bits in Java, C++ and Python. FingerprintEngine.fingerprint(graph, options) returns a long[] bitset and fingerprintCounts(graph, options) an int[] of bins. The factories FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius, size), fcfp(radius, size), path(pathLength, size) and torsion(size), and their no-argument forms, reproduce ecfp, fcfp, pathFingerprint and topologicalTorsion exactly; new FingerprintOptions() is ECFP4. Extra switches add terms without changing the default ones, as FingerprintOptionsExample.java shows:

import com.bioinception.smsd.core.FingerprintEngine;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.FingerprintOptions;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.MolGraph;
import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.BitSet;
import org.openscience.cdk.silent.SilentChemObjectBuilder;
import org.openscience.cdk.smiles.SmilesParser;

public class FingerprintOptionsExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        SmilesParser parser = new SmilesParser(SilentChemObjectBuilder.getInstance());
        FingerprintOptions options = FingerprintOptions.ecfp(2, 2048);
        options.cipAtoms = true;   // add the R/S descriptor of each centre
        options.ringSize = true;   // add the smallest ring size of each atom
        long[] left = FingerprintEngine.fingerprint(parser.parseSmiles("C[C@H](N)C(=O)O"), options);
        long[] right = FingerprintEngine.fingerprint(parser.parseSmiles("C[C@@H](N)C(=O)O"), options);
        if (Arrays.equals(left, right)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Enantiomers must differ with the CIP atom term");
        }

        FingerprintOptions framework = FingerprintOptions.ecfp();
        framework.scaffold = FingerprintOptions.Scaffold.MURCKO;
        long[] toluene = FingerprintEngine.fingerprint(parser.parseSmiles("Cc1ccccc1"), framework);
        long[] benzene = FingerprintEngine.fingerprint(parser.parseSmiles("c1ccccc1"), FingerprintOptions.ecfp());
        if (!Arrays.equals(toluene, benzene)) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("The framework of toluene is benzene");
        }

        MolGraph aspirin = FingerprintEngine.toMolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"));
        BitSet keys = BitSet.valueOf(FingerprintEngine.fingerprint(aspirin, FingerprintOptions.maccs()));
        System.out.println("MACCS keys set: " + keys.cardinality() + ", six-membered ring: " + keys.get(162));
    }
}

Fields, with defaults and the families whose terms are on by default:

  • family: ECFP, FCFP, PATH, TORSION or KEYS; radius (2; −1 for the whole component), pathLength in bonds (7), size in bits or bins (2,048).
  • Atom terms: element (ECFP, PATH, TORSION), degree and ringMembership (ECFP, FCFP, TORSION), valence, the bond order sum or for TORSION the pi electrons (ECFP, TORSION), and formalCharge, isotope, hydrogenCount, tautomerClass and aromaticity (ECFP).
  • Bond terms: bondOrder (ECFP, FCFP); aromaticBond, ringBond (off).
  • ringSize (off): the smallest ring through each atom; rings of ringSizeCap (8) atoms or more share one class.
  • cipAtoms, cipBonds (off): R/S (and r/s) of centres and E/Z of double bonds, from CIPAssigner. Circular fingerprints of radius 0 do not separate stereoisomers, and double bonds in rings below eight atoms carry no E/Z term.
  • fragments: WHOLE (default), LARGEST (most heavy atoms) or PER_FRAGMENT (each component tagged). scaffold: NONE (default) or MURCKO (the scaffold of MCS.murckoScaffold; a molecule without rings is used whole).
  • keys: for KEYS, one bit per new FingerprintOptions.Key(smarts, minimum), set when at least minimum distinct atom sets match.

FingerprintOptions.maccs() gives the 166 MACCS keys, key k at bit k − 1; maccsKeys() lists them, withKeys(keys) builds a custom key family and copy() copies the options. Inconsistent options and unparsable SMARTS keys raise IllegalArgumentException, and a key count not settled within its budget raises IllegalStateException. mcsFingerprint ignores these options.

Ring-size terms, double-bond stereo terms and aromatic-ring keys use the same minimum cycle basis as C++ and Python, so a Java value that came from a different minimum basis of equal size can change. They throw RingBasisUnavailableException naming the cause if ring perception cannot complete that basis, as do SMARTS keys whose search needs it; a separate relevant-cycle truncation does not prevent their use. The ring refusals replace values that 8.0.3 could compute from incomplete rings. A key whose minimum number of matches is found before the embedding limit is set; a key search that runs out of time throws, as in 8.0.3.

CIPAssigner.assignRS(graph) returns R or S (r or s if pseudoasymmetric) by atom index, and CIPAssigner.assignEZ(graph) E or Z for each annotated double bond by a long bond key. Rule 1a of IUPAC 2013 is applied literally, so phosphinate and phosphonate centres may differ from some toolkits. Ranking is bounded by CIPAssigner.MAX_DEPTH, so check which centres were assigned.

Substructure.decomposeRGroups(core, molecules, options), or decomposeRGroups(core, molecules, chemistry, timeoutMillis), returns one Substructure.Decomposition per molecule. Check search() before using core() (the matched atoms and query-bond images; null without a match) or rgroups() (attached groups keyed R1, R2 and so on).

docs.title: Graph utilities
docs.text:
• toCanonicalSmiles(), toCanonicalSmiles(atomMaps): canonical SMILES with the supplied stereochemistry; the overload adds positive atom-map labels, keyed by atom index, without changing the ranking or the graph. / and \ go on single bonds wherever a configured double bond has one at an end; an end with only aromatic ring bonds carries them on an aromatic bond, as RDKit writes it, which strict OpenSMILES readers take as a single bond; the CDK 2.13 SmilesParser does not keep that configuration. For a graph of more than 200 atoms, or when canonical labelling reaches its search limit, the output can depend on the input atom order; automorphismGeneratorsTruncated() is then true.
  • computeRings(), numRings(), MolGraph.computeSSSR(graph), MolGraph.layoutSSSR(graph): the smallest set of smallest rings, also ordered for layout. computeRelevantCycles(), computeURFs(): relevant cycles and unique ring families. ringsTruncated(): whether the ring search stopped before finding a complete set of rings. relevantCyclesTruncated(): whether full relevant-cycle enumeration was incomplete. ensureRingCounts(), getRingCounts(): per-atom ring counts, computed on first use; they can depend on the input atom order.
  • computeRelevantCycleFamilies(): the relevant cycles grouped into families, as RelevantCycleFamilies with families(), relevantCycleCount() and truncated(). Each RelevantCycleFamily gives the ring size(), the root() (the highest-numbered atom of every member), first(), second() and opposite(), which locate the bond or atom opposite the root, one member as prototype() and the exact memberCount(), so the relevant cycles can be counted without listing them; counts are BigInteger values. truncated() reports an incomplete enumeration, whose families are relevant but may not be all of them. relevantCycleFamilyOf(families, ring) returns the index of the family that has the ring as a member, or -1, and relevantCycleFamilyMembers(family, limit) returns up to limit members, starting with the prototype. When the enumeration is complete, the relevant cycles and their number do not depend on the input atom order; the grouping into families can.
  • ringSystemOf(atom), ringSystemCount(), ringSystemSig(id): ring systems and their signatures.
  • MolGraph.sanitizeSmiles(smiles): balances parentheses and removes unclosed ring openings before CDK parsing.
  • getCanonicalLabeling(), getCanonicalHash(), getOrbit(): canonical labelling, graph hash and symmetry classes, each a copy (getOrbits() is deprecated). getAutomorphismGenerators(), automorphismGeneratorsTruncated(): symmetry generators, and whether they are incomplete.
  • MolGraph.matchTemplate, MolGraph.forceDirectedLayout, MolGraph.stressMajorisation, MolGraph.reduceCrossings: two-dimensional layout with MolGraph.Point2D coordinates.
  • MolGraph.translateToAtomIds(mapping, query, target): a mapping in the atom IDs set with Builder.atomIds.

docs.title: Command-line interface
docs.text:
A source build of the module com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli writes the self-contained smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar; the Java module README shows how to obtain the 8.0.3 JAR or depend on SMSDcli. From the repository root, after a source build, print the version and help, test whether benzene is a substructure of phenol, and find the MCS of N-methylacetamide and propanamide (mcs_size is 4):

java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar --version
java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar --help
java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "c1ccc(O)cc1" --json -
java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --Q SMI --q "CC(=O)NC" --T SMI --t "CCC(=O)N" --mode mcs --json -

MCS mode defaults to a connected MCIS; request MCES and fragments explicitly, here for the two ethyl groups of diethyl ether and diethylamine:

java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --Q SMI --q "CCOCC" --T SMI --t "CCNCC" \
  --mode mcs --objective MCES --fragments --timeout 1000 --json -

SMARTS queries use the type SIG in substructure mode; here the first search reports "exists": true (exit status 0) and the second "exists": false (1):

java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --Q SIG --q "C=O" --T SMI --t "CC(=O)O" --json -
java -jar java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar \
  --Q SIG --q "C=O" --T SMI --t "CCO" --json -

Options:

  • --Q, --q: query type and value: SMI or SIG with the string, or MOL, ML2 (MOL2), CML or PDB with a file path.
  • --T, --t: target type and value: SMI, MOL, ML2, CML, PDB, or SDF for a batch.
  • --mode: sub (default) or mcs, with --objective MCIS (default) or MCES and --fragments for disconnected fragments.
  • --induced: require an induced embedding. -m, --mappings: enumerate up to 10,000 embeddings.
  • --timeout: milliseconds per pair (default 10,000). --threads: SDF batch threads (default 0, every processor).
  • -a, --add-hydrogens; -r, --remove-hydrogens: add or remove explicit hydrogens first.
  • --json, --json-pretty: (pretty-printed) JSON to a file, or standard output with -. -o, --output: the MCS fragment as SMILES, likewise.
  • --map-out, --map-format, --map-pretty: mapping export, below.
  • --benchmark: time substructure and MCS search on one pair and print the averages.

Each molecule is standardised (atom typing, implicit hydrogens, rings and Daylight aromaticity) first. CML and PDB files must hold one molecule or model, empty inputs are rejected, and an SDF batch may hold up to 100,000 molecules.

JSON output (UTF-8) includes status, optimal, complete, score, nodes_visited, elapsed_ms and the first match's bonds and fragments; substructure mode adds exists (with --mappings, mappings instead), MCS mode mcs_size, pairs and, with a match, mcs_smiles. An SDF batch has one row per target under results.

--map-out writes the mappings of a single-pair search (in substructure mode, with --mappings) to a file or standard output. --map-format is json (default), smiles (query and target with matching atom maps and stereochemistry), smarts or mdl (in MCS mode, the common atoms and bonds of the first match as a MOL block).

Exit status 0 means a completed search with a match (SDF: at least one match, every search completed), 1 a completed search without one (SDF: no match, every search completed), and 2 invalid input, an unknown mode, an error or an incomplete search (SDF: any target failed or incomplete).
