docs.title: Molecular tools and MCP
docs.text:
SMSD provides eight local molecular tools through the official Model Context Protocol Python SDK. The same registry exports function definitions for model clients and optional LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters. Exporting a definition or calling a tool does not make a model request, need an API key or contact a network service.

Install SMSD 8.1.0 with the optional MCP SDK, then start the server:

python -m pip install 'smsd[mcp]==8.1.0'
smsd-mcp
# Equivalent: python -m smsd.mcp_server

From a source checkout, install with python -m pip install '.[mcp]'. Releases before 8.1.0 do not include these tools.

Configure an MCP client to start smsd-mcp with no arguments. The server has no HTTP listener. Molecular arguments are SMILES or SMARTS text, never paths, URLs, Python expressions or commands. Client configuration, logging and any model connection belong to the client.

See Connecting AI assistants for client set-up.

Tool Operation find_mcs One common graph: atom-maximising MCIS or bond-maximising MCES; connected or fragmented. find_substructure One molecular or SMARTS embedding, with optional induced matching. search_smarts Bounded SMARTS embedding enumeration. molecular_fingerprint Set-bit positions or sparse position/count pairs. molecular_similarity Tanimoto, Dice or cosine on native fingerprints. screen_molecules Tanimoto screening of a small in-memory target list, with stable ties and explicit pages. standardise_molecule Native representation canonicalisation; explicitly requested optional chemical transformations. depict_mcs Native mapping-highlight SVG together with the MCS result and proof flags.

docs.title: Search results and limits
docs.text:
Every result is JSON-compatible and includes the engine version, limits and wall elapsed time. Search results additionally retain the native status, optimal, complete, score, nodes_visited, elapsed_ms, chemistry options, budgets and mappings. proof describes these engine flags; it is not an independent chemical validation certificate. Atom indices are zero-based in the parsed inputs. wall_elapsed_ms ends before the JSON size/serialisation check and SDK/transport handling; wall_scope records that boundary.

Inspect proof and stopping status separately from found. An unfinished match need not be maximum; an unfinished found: false does not prove absence. complete also describes whether requested enumeration finished. A result limit can leave enumeration incomplete even when an optimum is known. Fingerprint and representation operations mark search proof as inapplicable. A fingerprint coefficient is not an MCS proof or a biological-accuracy score.

Search defaults are 1,000 ms and 100,000 nodes per call. The permitted maxima are 30,000 ms and 1,000,000 nodes; zero time requests an immediate stop. A zero node cap is rejected rather than selecting an unlimited search. These budgets cover native search, after parsing and SMARTS compilation. Wall time also includes preparation and any depiction, but excludes JSON serialisation and SDK/transport handling; it is not a hard wall deadline for the whole Python call. Use process/container limits for that.

Molecular text is limited to 16,384 characters and parsed molecules to 1,024 atoms. SMARTS has the text limit; its compiled predicate size is not a molecule atom count. Enumeration and returned screening pages have at most 32 matches. Fingerprint limits are 65,536 positions, radius 8 and path length 8, with at most 2,000,000 estimated path walks. Search chemistry switches expose stereo, complete-ring and ring-to-ring restrictions; unsupported options are not silently inferred from natural language.

Screening accepts at most 64 targets, 65,536 combined text characters and 4,096 combined query/target atoms. It scores all supplied targets, sorts by descending score and then input index, and returns total_hits, offset, next_offset and truncated. A page is incomplete when it does not contain the whole hit list; next_offset: null means there is no later page. This small-list tool does not promise a GPU path or an exact structure search.

from smsd.tool_definitions import call_tool

result = call_tool("find_mcs", {
    "query_smiles": "CCO", "target_smiles": "CCN", "timeout_ms": 1000,
})
assert result["found"] and result["matches"][0]["atom_count"] == 2

hits = call_tool("screen_molecules", {
    "query_smiles": "CCO", "targets_smiles": ["CCO", "CCN", "CCO"],
    "threshold": 1.0, "max_hits": 1,
})
assert hits["hits"][0]["target_index"] == 0 and hits["next_offset"] == 1

docs.title: Standardisation and depiction
docs.text:
The default standardise_molecule parses and writes native canonical SMILES. It preserves the represented charge, fragments, isotope, atom maps and stereo; it does not neutralise, remove salts or choose a tautomer. remove_atom_maps is a separate explicit representation option. Whatever options are set, standardise_molecule accepts at most 128 atoms, and each result's limits reports this as standardise_atoms.

The optional smsd[rdkit] dependency is required only when cleanup, largest_fragment, neutralise or canonical_tautomer is explicitly true. The result records the backend/version and operation sequence; there is no automatic fallback. These operations change chemical graphs and can change charge, fragments or stereo. Canonical tautomer selection is a representation choice, not a prediction of stability. Tautomer enumeration is limited to 128 tautomers and 256 transformations. If that enumeration stops, the result reports LIMIT_REACHED, complete: false and a canonical choice from the partial set.

depict_mcs accepts at most 256 atoms per input and returns at most 1 MiB of SVG, with dimensions bounded to 200–1,600 by 150–1,200. Its native SVG is checked for executable elements, external references and document entities. The drawing highlights mapped atoms and input bonds between them. For MCES, the returned bond_mapping is the selected-edge witness; the drawing can also show other input bonds between highlighted atoms. No match gives svg: null. A stopped search remains stopped when depicted. Each result is limited to 2 MiB as JSON text, measured before the MCP SDK encodes it.

docs.title: Function definitions and framework adapters
docs.text:
from smsd.tool_definitions import get_tool_definitions, langchain_tools, llamaindex_tools

input_schema_tools = get_tool_definitions("input-schema")
function_tools = get_tool_definitions("function")
chat_function_tools = get_tool_definitions("chat-function")
mcp_tools = get_tool_definitions("mcp")

Every definition carries the tool's name and description. mcp gives the argument schema as inputSchema, and input-schema gives it as input_schema. function gives flat definitions with type: "function" and parameters; chat-function nests name, description and parameters in a function object beside type: "function". Both function formats put strict: false beside parameters, because omitted optional arguments keep their Python defaults; the schemas do not use strict mode. All exports reject additional fields and include finite single-argument bounds; combined work/atom limits are also checked by the functions. Both call_tool and the MCP server check the original JSON object before SDK normalisation, rejecting unknown fields and type coercions. The server advertises the registry's additionalProperties: false schema.

Install langchain-core or llama-index-core separately when needed; the adapters require their Pydantic 2 interfaces. They load lazily and create only local tools, not clients, models or indexes:

from smsd.tool_definitions import langchain_tools, llamaindex_tools

tools = langchain_tools()  # optional langchain-core dependency
assert tools[0].invoke({"query_smiles": "CCO", "target_smiles": "CCN"})["found"]

tools = llamaindex_tools()  # optional llama-index-core dependency
assert tools[0].call(query_smiles="CCO", target_smiles="CCN").raw_output["found"]

See the container recipe and the Hugging Face demonstration source. Neither deploys a service. The official protocol reference is the MCP Python SDK.

docs.title: Packed fingerprint corpora
docs.text:
smsd.corpus.FingerprintCorpus stores binary fingerprints as fixed-width packed rows in a read-only, memory-mapped file. NumPy is required for this API and for smsd.clustering; importing the modules does not import NumPy.

For a task-based walk-through of building, reopening and searching an index, see the packed fingerprint index chapter of the user guide.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus
from smsd.clustering import butina, maxmin

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    with FingerprintCorpus.create(path, [[1], [1], [2]], fp_size=8) as corpus:
        assert len(corpus) == 3
        assert corpus.fingerprint(0) == [1]
        assert list(corpus.similarities([1], threshold=1.0)) == [(0, 1.0), (1, 1.0)]
        assert list(corpus.screen_many([[1], [2]], threshold=1.0)) == [
            (0, 0, 1.0), (0, 1, 1.0), (1, 2, 1.0)
        ]
        assert list(corpus.threshold_pairs(1.0)) == [(0, 1, 1.0)]
        assert list(corpus.top_k_pairs(1)) == [
            (0, 1, 1.0), (1, 0, 1.0), (2, 0, 0.0)
        ]
        assert butina(corpus, threshold=1.0) == [(0, 1), (2,)]
        assert maxmin(corpus, count=3, seed=0) == [0, 2, 1]
        chunks = list(corpus.iter_packed_chunks(chunk_size=2))
        assert chunks[0][0] == 0
        assert chunks[0][1].tolist() == [[2], [2]]
        assert corpus.cuda_calls == 0  # The default backend is CPU.
    # Chunk arrays own their data and remain usable after the mapping is closed.
    assert chunks[1][1].tolist() == [[4]]
    with FingerprintCorpus(path) as reopened:
        assert reopened.fingerprint(2) == [2]

from_fingerprints is an alias for create. The fingerprint input can be a generator. Construction publishes a complete file atomically, preserves an existing destination by default and removes its temporary file after an input failure. Use overwrite=True for replacement. The containing filesystem must support hard links for the default create mode.

To create packed rows directly from molecule inputs, use from_smiles. Queries must use the same fingerprint specification:

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import smsd
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus

molecules = ["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)O"]
options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    with FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(
        Path(directory) / "molecules.fp", iter(molecules), options=options,
        chunk_size=1024
    ) as corpus:
        query = smsd.fingerprint("CCO", options=options)
        for index, score in corpus.similarities(query, threshold=0.3):
            print(index, score)

The file stores its bit width and row count, rather than the chemistry specification. Keep that specification with the application. Count fingerprints are rejected; duplicate binary positions are folded. Two empty fingerprints score 1, and an empty fingerprint compared with a non-empty one scores 0, as with smsd.tanimoto_coefficient. Thresholds are inclusive and must be finite values from 0 to 1.

docs.title: CPU and CUDA backends
docs.text:
screen_many, similarities, threshold_pairs, top_k_pairs, butina and maxmin accept the same explicit backend argument:

Backend Behaviour "cpu" Default. NumPy computes packed intersections; no CUDA provider is requested. "cuda" Requires a compatible smsd-cuda package and device. Unavailable providers or unsupported widths raise. "auto" Uses the CUDA provider when available and supported; otherwise uses CPU comparisons.

The core and CUDA package versions must match. Packed CUDA supports fingerprint widths up to 65,536 bits and a little-endian host. Wider packed fingerprints remain supported on the CPU; auto uses that CPU path. Errors during a device call, result validation or resident cleanup propagate. They do not silently retry the operation on the CPU. These packed operations do not use the native TargetCorpus operation crossovers.

A CUDA-capable installation can request the device explicitly:

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus
from smsd.clustering import butina, maxmin

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    with FingerprintCorpus.create(
        Path(directory) / "bits.fp", [[1], [1, 2], [3]], fp_size=8
    ) as corpus:
        before = corpus.cuda_calls
        hits = list(corpus.screen_many([[1], [3]], threshold=0.5, backend="cuda"))
        assert hits == [(0, 0, 1.0), (0, 1, 0.5), (1, 2, 1.0)]
        assert corpus.cuda_calls > before
        pairs = list(corpus.threshold_pairs(0.5, backend="cuda"))
        neighbours = list(corpus.top_k_pairs(1, backend="cuda"))
        clusters = butina(corpus, threshold=0.5, backend="cuda")
        selected = maxmin(corpus, count=2, backend="cuda")

CUDA computes exact integer intersections. screen_many applies integer cutoff tables on device, chosen to reproduce the CPU's binary64 threshold comparison; the host forms the returned Tanimoto scores from integer counts. top_k_pairs performs threshold selection and per-tile top-k on device, then merges those lists on the CPU with the same descending score and ascending target-index tie break. Pair searches and clustering use the same exact scores. GPU acceleration does not make those algorithms approximate.

Butina centre selection, count updates and assignment bookkeeping remain on the CPU. MaxMin's minimum-distance updates and next-row choice also remain on the CPU. Both have deterministic lower-index tie breaks. The cuda_calls property is a cumulative count of completed packed CUDA calls, including clustering passes. A positive increase is evidence that this adapter completed CUDA work; it is not a count of queries, hits or GPU kernels, and does not establish a speedup or the fraction of an application executed on the GPU.

docs.title: Ordering, work and memory
docs.text:
screen_many accepts at most 32 packed queries and consumes at most one extra query input to detect an excess before reading targets. It yields target-chunk order, then query index and target index. This is not a global query-major or similarity ranking. similarities yields target input order for one query.

CUDA tiles contain at most 1,048,576 query/target pairs. A conservative 64 MiB host-work estimate also limits each tile, so the effective target chunk can be smaller than the requested chunk_size. CPU packed comparison temporaries are similarly bounded to approximately 64 MiB; chunk_size can lower the bound. These are array/work estimates, not hard caps on process memory. Mapped pages, query storage, Python objects and application results are additional costs. Molecule construction and parsing memory are also input-dependent.

The native resident workspace separately retains at most 256 MiB of device scratch. That cap is not a total GPU-memory limit: resident target fingerprints, other temporary allocations, CUDA runtime resources and host pinned staging are separate. The packed adapter creates and releases a target resident handle for each tile; an open memory-mapped file does not imply that the entire corpus is resident on the GPU or that targets persist on device between calls. The native TargetCorpus API has its own retained-library lifetime.

top_k_pairs yields directed neighbours, ordered by descending similarity and then target index, with at most k heap entries in the global merge. threshold_pairs yields each undirected pair once in index order. Both exclude self pairs by default. Neither creates a dense all-against-all matrix. Retaining every yielded threshold pair can nevertheless require quadratic application memory, and retaining all top-k results can require O(n * k) memory.

The exact all-against-all scans take quadratic comparison work. Butina keeps linear auxiliary arrays and returns tuples with the centre first. Its default uses initial neighbour counts; reordering=True updates those counts after each cluster. A member must meet the similarity threshold with its centre, but need not meet it with every other member. MaxMin keeps a linear array of minimum Tanimoto distances and uses a deterministic starting row; comparison work is O(n * selected_count).

The format has a 24-byte little-endian header and ceil(fp_size / 8) bytes per row. The supported width is 1 to 16,777,216 bits. A 2048-bit corpus requires 256 bytes per row plus the header. The format and bounded tiles do not establish validation at a particular corpus size or any throughput result.

Keep an open corpus file unchanged, and close it with a context manager. Concurrent reads copy their mapped rows under a shared lifetime lock. close() waits for an active copy before unmapping; repeated closes are harmless. Computation on copied rows and already yielded results remains valid. A running iterator raises ValueError when it next requests a mapped row after close. Closing does not cancel a whole search. Explicit lifecycle calls are available when a context manager is unsuitable:

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    corpus = FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "bits.fp", [[1]], fp_size=8)
    try:
        assert corpus.fingerprint(0) == [1]
    finally:
        corpus.close()
    corpus.close()

docs.title: Streamed native screening
docs.text:
stream_screen_smiles screens a target iterable with the public native corpus API and releases each target chunk before loading the next. It uses the fixed ECFP radius 2, 2048-bit specification of TargetCorpus.screen. It requires no NumPy installation. This native graph path is separate from the packed backend choices above.

from smsd.corpus import stream_screen_smiles

targets = iter(["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1", "CCO"])
for index in stream_screen_smiles("CCO", targets, 0.5, chunk_size=4096):
    print(index)

Each chunk holds at most chunk_size target inputs, their prepared native graphs and one chunk's hit indices; the maximum accepted chunk is 1,048,576 targets. Graph memory depends on the input molecules. Hit indices retain their global input offsets. An invalid later molecule raises after any earlier chunks' hits have been yielded.

The native screen uses the optional smsd-cuda backend when eligible and retains its ordinary CPU fallback. The operation's crossover applies to each chunk: a small chunk may run on the CPU even when a GPU is available. This wrapper does not force GPU execution. For repeated queries over one retained library, use TargetCorpus directly so its resident device allocation can be reused.

For several query inputs, stream_screen_many_smiles uses bounded query and target tiles through the same native operation:

from smsd.corpus import stream_screen_many_smiles

molecules = ["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1", "CC(=O)O"]
for query_index, target_index in stream_screen_many_smiles(
    iter(["CCO", "CCN"]), iter(molecules), 0.5,
    query_chunk_size=64, target_chunk_size=4096, max_queries=4096
):
    print(query_index, target_index)

The query inventory is limited by max_queries; one extra query input may be consumed to reject an excess before reading targets. Queries are prepared once, and the target iterable is consumed once. Native result storage covers at most one query tile by one target tile. All three controls must be positive and at most 1,048,576, and the query/target tile product cannot exceed 1,048,576. These are bounds on molecule counts and result pairs; graph memory depends on the input molecules. Hits follow target-tile order, then query index, then target index. They are not globally query-major or ranked by similarity. The packed corpus's 32-query limit does not apply to this native tiled wrapper. Empty queries yield no hits without consuming targets. Invalid later targets can raise after earlier tiles have yielded hits.

smsd.warm_start(corpus, query, threshold=0.5) discovers available accelerators, prewarms that real corpus if needed and returns its ordinary screen hit indices. The corpus retains any prepared fingerprints and resident device allocation. The same dispatch rules apply; a successful call alone does not establish that a GPU kernel ran.

docs.title: SMSD Pro Python guide
docs.text: Reference for the smsd Python package, version 8.1.0. The Python examples cover fingerprints, drawing, layout, stereo, files, R-groups and scaffolds.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"

The CPU/OpenMP wheels cover CPython 3.12–3.15; the supported-platforms table lists the operating systems and architectures. smsd.__version__ gives the installed version. Core matching needs no other toolkit. RDKit is needed only for RDKit molecules, to_rdkit, to_svg, depict_mcs and depict_substructure (python -m pip install "rdkit<2027"); Open Babel only for from_openbabel and to_openbabel.

Deprecated compatibility aliases remain available in 8.1. Prefer their current replacement names in new code.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
With Python 3.12 or later, a C++17 compiler and CMake 3.18 or later, from the repository root:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"

This builds the CPU/OpenMP package. Metal and CUDA are left out unless -Ccmake.define.SMSD_BUILD_METAL=ON or -Ccmake.define.SMSD_BUILD_CUDA=ON is added (AUTO includes each one when it is available); Python screening and search do not run on them, so they change only what gpu_is_available() and gpu_device_info() report. Without OpenMP, batch calls run sequentially.

docs.title: Optional CUDA screening
docs.text:
smsd-cuda provides optional NVIDIA CUDA screening on Linux x86_64 and needs the same version of smsd:

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0"

The GPU computes integer overlaps; scores use the CPU expressions and hits keep target order. Matching runs on the CPU. The backend keeps prepared corpus fingerprints on the device for reuse. ECFP4 Tanimoto screening and the atom-count MCS similarity bound are distinct operations.

Automatic ECFP4 screening of a prepared TargetCorpus uses CUDA on a Tesla T4 with compute capability 7.5 when the corpus has at least 100,000 targets. Smaller corpora and other devices use the CPU. Setting SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS to a positive integer N makes this automatic screening use any NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 7.5 or later for corpora of at least N targets; on a Tesla T4, N replaces 100,000. Other values are ignored, and SMSD_DISABLE_GPU still overrides the setting. These rules do not cover the packed FingerprintCorpus backend "auto", described under CPU and CUDA backends. A device below compute capability 7.5 is reported as unavailable, with the reason given by smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason(); automatic screening and the packed backend "auto" then use the CPU, and an explicit packed backend="cuda" call raises an error that gives the reason. Automatic similarity-bound screening (screen_targets) and substructure pre-screening use the CPU; the explicit match_corpus(..., gpu_prefilter=True) methods can ask an optional GPU provider to run their pre-screen. gpu_is_available() and gpu_device_info() report backend availability, not whether a call used the device. Missing devices, allocation failure and device loss use the CPU. Setting SMSD_DISABLE_GPU to anything but an empty string or 0 disables the GPU at run time; an explicit packed backend="cuda" call then raises RuntimeError. macOS uses the CPU; the supported-platforms table gives the CUDA package requirements.

docs.title: Additions in 8.1.0
docs.text:
• Python adapters and MCP: NumPy/PyTorch arrays, scikit-learn transformers, bounded search tools and MCS SVG highlighting. Known bundled OpenMP conflicts are rejected before the PyTorch adapter runs; use a shared runtime or an OpenMP-free SMSD build.
  • Packed corpora: streamed construction, memory-mapped binary fingerprints, chunked threshold/top-k scans, Butina and MaxMin. All-against-all comparisons remain quadratic, without a dense result matrix.
  • SMARTS export: Match.to_smarts(query, chemistry) and MCS.match_with_smarts(target) retain selected common bonds. The latter uses the prepared chemistry and returns a SmartsResult with result and smarts. Stereo, tautomer-aware, complete-ring and strict ring-fusion export are rejected, together with unsupported conditional resonance cases. The pattern does not encode induced MCIS or establish that a search completed.
  • stream_screen_smiles consumes target chunks through the public native corpus screen. warm_start(corpus, query, threshold=...) prepares and screens a retained corpus. Both keep ordinary device crossovers and CPU fallback.

The macOS wheels need macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon and include their OpenMP runtime.

docs.title: Searches
docs.text:
A molecule is a SMILES string, MolGraph or RDKit molecule; a graph is a MolGraph (parse SMILES with parse_smiles). Prepare a query once:

  • Substructure.find(query): a molecule to embed whole in each target.
  • Substructure.smarts(query): a SMARTS pattern; an empty or non-string pattern raises ValueError.
  • MCS.find(query): a molecule for a maximum common substructure (MCS) with each target.

A prepared query provides:

Method Returns match(target) A SearchResult with at most one match match_all(target, limit=1000) Up to limit matches: all optimal MCS mappings or all Substructure embeddings, symmetry-related ones included match_many(targets, *, num_threads=0) One SearchResult per target, in order, each with its own budget; 0 uses the OpenMP default (OMP_NUM_THREADS) with_options(options), with_timeout(milliseconds) A new query with a copy of the options MCS.with_objective(objective), MCS.with_fragments(*, min_atoms=1, max_fragments=2147483647), MCS.with_atom_weights(weights) A new MCS query with that setting Substructure.with_induced(enabled=True) A new Substructure query with induced matching

limit must be a positive integer and num_threads a non-negative integer, or ValueError is raised. Searches release the global interpreter lock, so a prepared query can serve several threads; do not modify a target during a call.

import smsd

query = smsd.Substructure.find("CO")
assert query.match("CCO").found
assert not query.match("CCN").found
embeddings = query.match_all("OCO", limit=10)
assert len(embeddings.matches) == 2 and embeddings.complete

result = smsd.MCS.find("c1ccc(O)cc1").with_timeout(1000).match("c1ccc(N)cc1")
assert result.best.atom_count == 6 and result.optimal
print(result.best.atom_mapping)

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
SearchResult field Meaning matches, best, found Tuple of Match objects; the first or None; whether any exists status SearchStatus.COMPLETED, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED or LIMIT_REACHED optimal The MCS optimum, or the substructure answer, is proved complete The search or enumeration finished score Objective value, in weight units with atom weights nodes_visited, elapsed_ms Search effort and elapsed milliseconds

COMPLETED means the search ran to its end; TIMED_OUT and CANCELLED mean the time limit or the cancellation token stopped it. LIMIT_REACHED means the node limit stopped it, an enumeration reached its match limit, or an MCES pair beyond the size limits was declined before any search; a declined pair returns no match and proves nothing.

With complete_rings_only or RingFusionMode.STRICT, truncated ring perception in either input leaves the mappings selected using the perceived rings, but cannot prove the result. The status is LIMIT_REACHED, with optimal and complete both False; TIMED_OUT and CANCELLED take precedence.

A stopped search can return a valid but unproved match, and an empty incomplete result does not prove absence, so check status, optimal and complete. An enumeration limit can leave optimal=True with complete=False. Tied matches are not ranked chemically. A stopped MCIS search can return a result or atom mapping that differs from 8.0.3 or Java; see the upgrade notes.

import smsd

result = smsd.Substructure.find("CC").match_all("CCC", limit=1)
assert len(result.matches) == 1 and result.optimal and not result.complete
assert result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.LIMIT_REACHED

Each Match has:

  • atom_mapping: a read-only, one-to-one map from query to target atom index;
  • bond_mapping: (query_first, query_second, target_first, target_second) for each selected bond;
  • fragments: the components of the selected bonds, as query atom indices;
  • atom_count and bond_count of the selected graph;
  • to_smiles(query) and to_graph(query): the selection as SMILES with cut valences capped, or as a MolGraph with the original chemistry and hydrogen counts.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
An MCES search declines a pair before searching it, with LIMIT_REACHED, no match, and optimal and complete both False, when:

  • query atoms × target atoms exceed 2³⁰ (1,073,741,824), as for two molecules of more than 32,768 atoms each;
  • the two molecules are too large in bonds, as for two molecules of more than 16,384 bonds each;
  • rarely, a molecule has an atom with 512 or more bonds and the two molecules share many kinds of bond.

MCIS searches are never declined; the time and node limits bound them. C++ and Java use the same limits.

docs.title: MCIS, MCES and fragments
docs.text:
import smsd

query, target = "C1CC1", "CC(C)C"  # cyclopropane, isobutane
induced = smsd.MCS.find(query).match(target)
edges = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_objective(smsd.MCS.Objective.MCES).match(target)
assert (induced.best.atom_count, induced.best.bond_count) == (2, 1)
assert (edges.best.atom_count, edges.best.bond_count) == (3, 2)
assert len(smsd.parse_smiles(edges.best.to_smiles(query)).bonds()) == 2
fragments = smsd.MCS.find("CCOCC").with_fragments().match("CCNCC")
assert fragments.best.atom_count == 4 and len(fragments.best.fragments) == 2
all_matches = smsd.MCS.find(query).match_all(target, limit=100)
assert all_matches.optimal and all_matches.complete
  • MCS defaults to a connected maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS): most atoms, then most bonds, keeping bonds and non-bonds between mapped atoms.
  • MCS.Objective.MCES, the maximum common edge subgraph, maximises common bonds, then their atoms; it may omit input bonds and adds no isolated atoms.
  • with_fragments() allows several components of at least min_atoms atoms each, so MCIS may include isolated atoms when min_atoms=1. Limits below one raise ValueError.
  • Substructure is non-induced unless with_induced() or Substructure.Options.induced is set.

docs.title: Chemistry options
docs.text:
import smsd

options = smsd.MCS.Options()
options.chemistry.match_formal_charge = True
options.chemistry.use_chirality = True
options.chemistry.use_bond_stereo = True
options.chemistry.complete_rings_only = True
options.timeout_ms = 1000
search = smsd.MCS.find("c1ccccc1").with_options(options)
assert search.match("Cc1ccccc1").best.atom_count == 6

sub_options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
sub_options.induced = True
assert not smsd.Substructure.find("CCC").with_options(sub_options).match("C1CC1").found

ChemOptions, as options.chemistry, decides which atoms and bonds match:

Attribute Default Effect match_atom_type True Same element match_bond_order BondOrderMode.STRICT Equal orders, subject to aromaticity_mode; LOOSE and ANY relax this aromaticity_mode AromaticityMode.FLEXIBLE Aromatic bonds also match single or double bonds; STRICT needs agreement aromaticity_model AromaticityModel.DAYLIGHT_LIKE Deprecated; no search reads it match_formal_charge False Same formal charge match_isotope False Same mass number where both atoms give one use_chirality, use_bond_stereo False Mapped tetrahedral centres or double bonds agree in configuration, by the parity of their mapped neighbours, not CIP labels ring_matches_ring_only False Ring atoms and bonds match only ring atoms and bonds complete_rings_only False Retained ring atoms and bonds lie in fully selected relevant cycles of each input ring_fusion_mode RingFusionMode.IGNORE STRICT: matched ring atoms have the same per-atom ring count; PERMISSIVE adds no constraint, like IGNORE tautomer_aware False Allow recognised tautomeric relaxations; match_bond_order is unchanged pH, solvent 7.4, Solvent.AQUEOUS Context for MCS.compute_tautomer_confidence only

Stereo is checked only where the mapping determines it. In Substructure, a tagged query centre or double bond needs the same configuration in the target, and an untagged one matches any; in MCS, an unspecified target atom or bond matches either configuration. The comparison uses the parity of the mapped neighbours, not CIP labels, whose priorities depend on atoms outside the mapping. In MCS it is a hard constraint: an MCIS is the largest common subgraph whose mapped stereo agrees, so it can be smaller than the MCIS found without these options, and an MCES leaves out the fewest common bonds that resolve each disagreement.

Tautomer matching usually also needs a relaxed bond order:

import smsd

options = smsd.MCS.Options()
options.chemistry.tautomer_aware = True
options.chemistry.match_bond_order = smsd.BondOrderMode.ANY
options.timeout_ms = 1000
result = smsd.MCS.find("CC(=O)C").with_options(options).match("CC(O)=C")
assert result.best.atom_count == 4
options.chemistry.match_bond_order = smsd.BondOrderMode.STRICT
strict = smsd.MCS.find("CC(=O)C").with_options(options).match("CC(O)=C")
assert strict.best.atom_count == 2

ChemOptions.profile(name="default") returns a preset; names are not case-sensitive, and an unknown name raises ValueError:

Preset Differs from the defaults default No differences strict aromaticity_mode=STRICT pharma match_formal_charge, ring_matches_ring_only, complete_rings_only reaction, compat-fmcs, compat-substruct match_bond_order=LOOSE ChemOptions.tautomer_profile() tautomer_aware=True, match_bond_order=LOOSE

ChemOptions(options), copy.copy and copy.deepcopy copy options. The setters with_bond_order_mode, with_aromaticity_mode, with_complete_rings_only, with_match_isotope, with_ring_fusion_mode, with_tautomer_aware, with_solvent and with_ph set one field and return the same object; with_ph clamps a finite pH to [0, 14].

docs.title: Timeouts, node limits and cancellation
docs.text:
• timeout_ms, default -1: a negative value selects 10 s for Substructure and 500 + 2 × (query atoms × target atoms) ms, at most 30 s, for MCS: 1.3 s for two 20-atom molecules, 5.5 s for two 50-atom molecules and 30 s from 122 atoms each; 0 stops at once; a positive value applies to each query–target pair.
  • node_limit, default 0 (none): reaching it reports LIMIT_REACHED.
  • cancellation, default None: a CancellationToken; cancel() from any thread stops the search with CANCELLED. Tokens stay cancelled, so use a new one per search.

Parsing and preparation can take the total time past the deadline. Converting matches to Python objects counts towards it in match and match_all, which then return the matches converted so far with TIMED_OUT or CANCELLED and complete=False; match_many stops conversion only on cancellation.

docs.title: Atom weights
docs.text: with_atom_weights(weights), for MCIS only, ranks results by the sum of query atom weights before atom and bond counts; negative weights can favour a smaller result. Give one finite weight per query atom, in input order. Weights are compared to 0.001; result.score is in the supplied units. Non-finite weights, totals beyond about ±2.1 million, a list missing a query atom, and use with MCES raise ValueError.

docs.title: Tautomer confidence
docs.text:
MCS.compute_tautomer_confidence(query, target, match, chemistry) scores the tautomeric relaxations a Match uses, in the pH and solvent of chemistry; identical selected chemistry scores 1. The score is a heuristic, not a probability, and changes neither molecules nor search. A plain atom mapping raises TypeError.

import smsd

query, target = smsd.parse_smiles("ONC(C)=O"), smsd.parse_smiles("ON=C(C)O")
options = smsd.MCS.Options()
options.chemistry = smsd.ChemOptions.tautomer_profile()
match = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_options(options).match(target).best
for pH in (2.0, 7.4, 9.0, 12.0):
    chemistry = smsd.ChemOptions.tautomer_profile().with_ph(pH)
    print(pH, round(smsd.MCS.compute_tautomer_confidence(query, target, match, chemistry), 3))

MCS.validate_tautomer_consistency(query, target, match) reports whether a Match or atom mapping conserves the mobile N–H, O–H and S–H protons of each mapped tautomeric group.

docs.title: SMARTS and target collections
docs.text:
import smsd

query = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[#6]-[#8]")
assert [result.found for result in query.match_many(["CCO", "CCN"])] == [True, False]
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(["CCO", "CCN"])
corpus.prewarm(num_threads=1)
assert [result.found for result in query.match_many(corpus, num_threads=2)] == [True, False]

SMARTS queries follow the result, timeout and enumeration rules of molecule queries. TargetCorpus holds targets for repeated queries:

  • TargetCorpus(), TargetCorpus.from_smiles(targets), add_target(target), add_targets(targets): capture molecules and their atom numbering, unaffected by later changes to the inputs; len(corpus) counts them.
  • prewarm(*, num_threads=0) computes invariants and ECFP4 fingerprints; is_prewarmed says whether they cover every target.
  • screen(query, threshold, *, num_threads=0): indices of targets with ECFP4 Tanimoto of at least threshold, empty until prewarm() follows the last addition. ECFP similarity is not a substructure test.
  • screen_many(queries, threshold, *, num_threads=0): the same ECFP4 screen for each query, returning a list of hit-index lists in query order. Each hit list keeps target order and needs the same prewarm().
  • Errors in prewarm() and in CPU screening reach the caller; when several targets fail, the error of the first in target order is raised, whatever the thread count.
  • screen_targets_many(queries, threshold, chemistry=None, *, num_threads=0): the atom-count MCS similarity-bound screen for each query, with one chemistry setting for the batch. No prewarm() is needed. Each hit list keeps target order, as screen_targets(query, corpus, threshold, chemistry) does.
import smsd

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(["CCO", "CCN", "CCC"])
corpus.prewarm(num_threads=1)
assert corpus.screen_many(["CCO", "CCN"], 1.0, num_threads=1) == [[0], [1]]
assert corpus.screen_targets_many(["CCO", "CCN"], 1.0, num_threads=1) == [[0], [1]]

docs.title: Explicit corpus prefilters
docs.text:
The additive Substructure.match_corpus(corpus, *, gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0) and MCS.match_corpus(corpus, minimum_atoms, *, gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0) return CorpusSearchResult objects in original target order, preserving each target's input atom numbers.

import smsd
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(["CCO", "N"])
embeddings = smsd.Substructure.find("CO").match_corpus(corpus, num_threads=1)
assert embeddings[0].threshold_reached and embeddings[0].result.found
decisions = smsd.MCS.find("CC").match_corpus(corpus, 2, num_threads=1)
assert decisions[1].atom_upper_bound == 0
assert decisions[1].proven_below_threshold and decisions[1].result is None

result is an actual CPU search result, or None only for a proved filter rejection. threshold_reached requires a real witness. Both decision flags being false means unknown, including stopped searches without a sufficient witness. For eligible unweighted MCIS, atom_upper_bound is an upper bound on the MCS atom count; a target whose bound equals minimum_atoms is searched. Substructure decisions report no bound, so the field is None.

The default runs the same pre-screen on the CPU. gpu_prefilter=True explicitly asks the optional GPU provider to run it; unavailable or failed GPU work falls back to the CPU. Availability does not prove device use. No prewarm is required. With SMARTS, unsupported queries, node caps, immediate timeouts, cancellation tokens, MCS weights, MCES or excluded atoms, every target is searched on the CPU. MCES or weighted scores cannot prove an atom-count negative. match_many remains unchanged. Each target's search budget excludes the pre-screen; there is no whole-corpus timeout. Java retains its ordinary CPU batch API.

Corpus substructure searches can rule out targets that cannot contain the query before CPU matching. With SMARTS queries, untyped queries or a finite node limit, every target is searched. Target results keep their original slots, atom numbering and search status.

docs.title: Constrained and consensus searches
docs.text:
import smsd

results = smsd.MCS.match_constrained(["CO", "CN"], "CO.CN")
assert [result.best.atom_count for result in results] == [2, 2]
assert set(results[0].best.atom_mapping.values()).isdisjoint(
    results[1].best.atom_mapping.values()
)

consensus = smsd.MCS.consensus(["CCO", "CCN", "O"], threshold=2 / 3)
assert consensus.found and consensus.support_count == 2
assert consensus.graph.n == 2 and not consensus.optimal
assert consensus.to_smiles() == "CC"
  • MCS.match_constrained(queries, target, options=None): one SearchResult per query, in order, each excluding target atoms claimed earlier; the joint mapping is not proved optimal.
  • MCS.Options.excluded_target_atoms reserves further target atoms without changing the target.
  • MCS.consensus(molecules, options=None, threshold=1.0): a common graph in at least ceil(threshold * len(molecules)) inputs, threshold in (0, 1], under one budget; always optimal=False, including empty and single-input calls. complete reports whether the progressive pass finished. Neither it nor COMPLETED proves a global optimum or absence of a qualifying common graph. Atom weights and exclusions raise ValueError. With complete rings or strict ring fusion, truncated ring perception in any input makes it LIMIT_REACHED and incomplete, unless it is already TIMED_OUT or CANCELLED; its fragment and supporting mappings are retained.
  • ConsensusResult has graph, to_smiles(), support_count, mappings (supporting input index to a Match from graph), fragment and source_index (the graph in its source), found, status, optimal, complete, nodes_visited and elapsed_ms.

docs.title: Validation and symmetry
docs.text:
import smsd

query, target = "c1ccc(O)cc1", "c1ccc(N)cc1"
result = smsd.MCS.find(query).match(target)
assert result.best.atom_count == 6
assert result.best.bond_count == 6
assert smsd.MCS.validate_mapping(query, target, result.best) == []
fragment = result.best.to_smiles(query)
assert smsd.parse_smiles(fragment).n == 6
  • MCS.validate_mapping(query, target, match, options=None): a list of errors, empty when valid. A plain atom mapping selects every compatible mapped bond, so pass a Match for MCES.
  • MCS.is_mapping_maximal(query, target, match, options=None): whether no compatible extension exists, which is weaker than optimality. An invalid mapping gives False; a valid mapping raises RuntimeError if the proof cannot finish or required ring perception was truncated.
  • MCS.canonicalize_mapping(query, target, atom_mapping): the lexicographically smallest equivalent mapping under both molecules' symmetries; raises if it cannot finish.

docs.title: R-group decomposition
docs.text: Substructure.decompose_r_groups(core, targets, options=None) returns, per target, a dictionary with core (a MolGraph), rgroups (labels such as "R1" mapped to graphs) and search (the core's SearchResult, to check first); see the R-group example.

docs.title: Input atom numbering
docs.text:
SMILES use parser order, MolGraph objects graph order and RDKit molecules their own order, separately on each side; search results and atom weights use these indices. Other functions number an RDKit molecule as from_rdkit does; get_index_map(from_rdkit(mol)) gives the RDKit index of each atom. Explicit hydrogen atoms are vertices; bracket hydrogen counts are not.

from rdkit import Chem
import smsd

query = Chem.RenumberAtoms(Chem.MolFromSmiles("NCCO"), [3, 1, 0, 2])
target = Chem.MolFromSmiles("CC(O)CN")
result = smsd.MCS.find(query).match(target)
assert result.best.atom_count == 4
for first, second in result.best.atom_mapping.items():
    assert query.GetAtomWithIdx(first).GetAtomicNum() == target.GetAtomWithIdx(second).GetAtomicNum()

Conversion passes through SMILES, so coordinates, data fields and query predicates are lost. For C++, see the optional native adapter.

  • from_rdkit(mol, use_cache=True): a graph with the atom correspondence, reused while the molecule is unchanged; empty or hydrogen-only molecules raise ValueError.
  • to_rdkit(mol_or_smiles): an RDKit molecule in canonical SMILES order.
  • get_index_map(g): a copy of result[smsd_index] = rdkit_index for a from_rdkit graph, else None.
  • translate_mapping(mapping, g_query=None, g_target=None): a mapping between from_rdkit graphs in RDKit indices; an out-of-range index raises IndexError.
  • clear_cache(): clears reusable conversions; live graphs keep their correspondence.
  • from_openbabel(mol), to_openbabel(mol): Pybel molecule or OBMol to graph, and back to Pybel, without the Open Babel numbering.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: Every name in smsd.__all__ appears in this guide.

docs.text:
Name Members MCS.Objective, MCS.Connectivity MCIS (default), MCES; CONNECTED (default), FRAGMENTS SearchStatus COMPLETED, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED, LIMIT_REACHED BondOrderMode, AromaticityMode, AromaticityModel STRICT, LOOSE, ANY; STRICT, FLEXIBLE; DAYLIGHT_LIKE RingFusionMode IGNORE, PERMISSIVE, STRICT Solvent AQUEOUS, DMSO, METHANOL, CHLOROFORM, ACETONITRILE, DIETHYL_ETHER CancellationToken cancel(), is_cancelled
