docs.title: Molecules and SMILES
docs.text:
• parse_smiles(smiles, *, lenient=False): a graph; "" gives an empty one. Malformed text raises ValueError unless lenient=True recovers it; bracket atoms beyond the OpenSMILES limits (one-digit hydrogen count, charge within ±15, three-digit isotope) always raise it.
  • parse_mapped_smiles(smiles): parse without atom maps; strip_atom_maps(smiles) removes them from the text, keeping ring closures and aromatic bonds.
  • to_smiles(mol): canonical SMILES, whose order may differ between languages; canonical_smiles is a deprecated alias. / and \ go on single bonds wherever a configured double bond has one at an end; an end with only aromatic ring bonds carries them on an aromatic bond, as RDKit writes it, which strict OpenSMILES readers take as a single bond. For a molecule of more than 5,000 atoms, or when canonical labelling reaches its search limit, the output can depend on the input atom order; the graph's automorphism_generators_truncated() is then True. A graph that needs more than 99 ring closures open at once is rejected.
  • to_smarts(mol, include_aromaticity=True, include_charge=True, include_ring_member=False, include_h_count=False, include_isotope=False): SMARTS for a molecule with the selected predicates; a graph that needs more than 99 ring closures open at once is rejected.
  • canonical_hash(mol): a hash of connectivity, bond orders, aromaticity, rings, charges, mass numbers and stereo; a screening key, not proof of identity. same_canonical_graph(mol1, mol2) compares atom count, canonical hash and canonical SMILES.
  • prewarm(mol): caches invariants and returns the graph; prewarm_graph is a deprecated alias returning None.
  • extract_subgraph(mol, atom_indices): the induced subgraph, numbered in the supplied order, keeping a stereocentre whose neighbours all stay and the E/Z configuration of a double bond whose ends keep the neighbours that define it.
  • murcko_scaffold(mol): the Bemis–Murcko scaffold (ring systems, linkers and atoms double- or triple-bonded to them), other substituents replaced by hydrogen and stereo kept where defined; acyclic graphs are returned unchanged.
  • count_components(mol), split_components(mol): the number of connected components, or one graph for each.
  • translate_to_atom_ids(mapping, g1, g2): a mapping in the IDs set by MolGraphBuilder.atom_ids; unchanged without IDs.

MolGraph members:

  • n, len(graph): atom count.
  • atomic_num, formal_charge, mass_number, hydrogen_count, atom_class, aromatic, ring, degree, neighbors, label: per-atom values, adjacency lists and matching labels.
  • bonds() as (i, j, order) tuples; bond_order(i, j), has_bond(i, j), bond_in_ring(i, j), bond_aromatic(i, j), raising IndexError out of range.
  • name, program_line, comment, properties: writable MOL header lines and SDF data fields.
  • num_rings(), ensure_ring_counts(), ring_system_of(atom), ring_system_count(), ring_system_sig(rs_id): rings and ring systems.
  • get_canonical_hash(), ensure_canonical(), morgan_rank, canonical_label, orbit: canonical ranks, labels and symmetry classes, computed on first access.
  • get_automorphism_generators(), automorphism_generators_truncated(): automorphism generators, and whether they were capped.
  • tautomer_class: tautomer class per atom from 0, or −1; independent of atom order except between symmetric classes.
  • prewarm() caches invariants; perceive_aromaticity(model=AromaticityModel.DAYLIGHT_LIKE), kekulize() and dearomatize() change the graph in place.

MolGraphBuilder builds a MolGraph through chainable setters: atom_count(n), atomic_numbers(nums), formal_charges(charges), mass_numbers(masses), hydrogen_counts(counts), ring_flags(flags), aromatic_flags(flags), neighbors(adj), bond_orders(orders) (parallel to neighbors), bond_ring_flags(flags), bond_aromatic_flags(flags), atom_ids(ids), name(value), program_line(value), comment(value), properties(values), then build(perceive_aromaticity=True, aromaticity_model=AromaticityModel.DAYLIGHT_LIKE).

docs.title: Stereo, rings and atom chemistry
docs.text:
• assign_rs(mol), assign_ez(mol): {atom: "R" or "S"} and {(atom, atom): "E" or "Z"} where priorities resolve.
  • assign_cip(mol) returns CIPDescriptors with rs_labels, one RSLabel per atom (NONE, R, S, pseudoasymmetric r, s), and ez_bonds, (atom, atom, EZLabel) tuples (NONE, E, Z).
  • compute_sssr(mol): the smallest set of smallest rings, as atom lists by ascending size.
  • rings_truncated(mol): whether the ring search behind compute_sssr stopped before finding a complete set of rings, as for a very large ring system; its 8.0.x meaning is retained.
  • relevant_cycles_truncated(mol): whether full relevant-cycle enumeration was incomplete. It can be true with a complete minimum basis. Complete-ring matching checks this perception; strict ring fusion checks the perception that produced its per-atom ring counts.
  • compute_relevant_cycle_families(mol): the relevant cycles grouped into families, as RelevantCycleFamilies with families, relevant_cycle_count and truncated. Each RelevantCycleFamily gives the ring size, the root (the highest-numbered atom of every member), first, second and opposite, which locate the bond or atom opposite the root, one member as prototype and the exact member_count, so the relevant cycles can be counted without listing them; counts are Python integers of any size. truncated reports an incomplete enumeration, whose families are relevant but may not be all of them. When the enumeration is complete, the relevant cycles and their number do not depend on the input atom order; the grouping into families can.
  • relevant_cycle_family_of(mol, families, ring): the index in families.families of the family that has ring, a list of atom indices in ring order, as a member, or -1.
  • relevant_cycle_family_members(mol, family, limit): up to limit members of family as atom-index lists, starting with its prototype.
  • perceive_aromaticity(mol, *, model=AromaticityModel.DAYLIGHT_LIKE): recompute ring membership and aromaticity.
  • kekulize(mol): replace aromatic bonds with Kekulé bonds, or raise ValueError; dearomatize(mol) is a deprecated alias issuing a DeprecationWarning.
  • classify_pharmacophore(mol, atom_index): bit mask of a graph atom: 0 donor, 1 acceptor, 2 positive and 3 negative ionisable, 4 aromatic, 5 hydrophobic.
  • implicit_h(atomic_num, bond_order_sum, formal_charge, aromatic=False): implicit hydrogens by SMILES valence; 0 when none fits.

Positive numeric SMARTS R<n> (n > 0) uses one deterministic minimum cycle basis, the same as C++ and Java. If ring perception cannot complete it, a search that cannot be decided without it returns LIMIT_REACHED without matches, including for negated, combined and recursive predicates; found is then false, which does not prove absence. Literal R and R0 remain independent of that basis. Other functions that need the basis raise smsd.RingBasisUnavailable, a RuntimeError, naming the cause; compute_sssr may return incomplete rings, flagged by rings_truncated. relevant_cycles_truncated alone does not make the basis incomplete. Ring perception works within one fixed, deterministic work limit; see Results and budgets.

The other functions here accept a molecule; perceive_aromaticity, kekulize and dearomatize change a MolGraph in place and return it. CIP labels follow IUPAC 2013: at phosphorus, oxo outranks hydroxy and alkoxy oxygen, so phosphinates and phosphonates can differ from toolkits that rank it lower.

docs.title: Fingerprints
docs.text:
Binary fingerprints are sorted set positions; count fingerprints are (position, count) pairs.

  • fingerprint(mol, *, kind="mcs", path_length=7, fp_size=2048, radius=2, options=None): kind is "mcs", "path", "ecfp" or "circular" (ECFP4), "fcfp" (FCFP4) or "torsion"; options overrides it.
  • fingerprint_from_smiles(smiles, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="ecfp", *, path_length=7, options=None): mode takes the kind values above; options overrides it.
  • fingerprints(mols, *, kind="mcs", path_length=7, fp_size=2048, radius=2, options=None, num_threads=0): the fingerprint of every molecule, each as fingerprint gives it, in input order. SMILES strings are parsed and the fingerprints computed natively on num_threads threads (0 uses the OpenMP default); the first molecule that fails raises the error fingerprint gives for it. An smsd.RingBasisUnavailable error, or the error of a key left undecided by its time or embedding limit, keeps its type and adds the zero-based input index to its message.
  • circular_fingerprint(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="ecfp"), circular_fingerprint_counts(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="ecfp"): ECFP or FCFP of a graph; radius 2 is ECFP4.
  • path_fingerprint(mol, path_length=7, fp_size=2048): heavy-atom paths of up to path_length bonds in a graph.
  • mcs_fingerprint(mol, path_length=7, fp_size=2048, tautomer_aware=False): an MCS-aware path fingerprint of a graph.
  • topological_torsion(mol, fp_size=2048), topological_torsion_counts(mol, fp_size=2048): four-atom torsions (Nilakantan et al., 1987) of a molecule, or counts for a graph.
  • fingerprint_subset(fp1, fp2): whether every position of fp1 is in fp2; both sorted.
  • analyze_fp_quality(fp, fp_size=2048): set_bits (distinct positions), fp_size, density (set bits over fp_size), expected_collision_rate and is_saturated (density over 0.75); a position beyond fp_size raises ValueError. With s of N bits set, the fingerprint holds about n = ln(1 − s/N) / ln(1 − 1/N) uniformly hashed features, and the collision rate is the share 1 − s/n of them that fell on a bit already set: 0 for an empty fingerprint and 1 for a full one. Path fingerprints of a power-of-two size collide more often than uniform hashing predicts, so the rate understates their collisions. Java analyzeFpQuality uses the same definitions.

docs.title: Configurable fingerprints
docs.text:
FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", **switches) gives the same bits in Python, C++ and Java. Each family starts from the classic configuration that reproduces circular_fingerprint, path_fingerprint and topological_torsion; FingerprintOptions() is ECFP4. The class methods ecfp(radius=2, size=2048), fcfp(radius=2, size=2048), path(path_length=7, size=2048), torsion(size=2048) and maccs() build the same configurations. Pass the value as options to fingerprint, fingerprints or fingerprint_from_smiles.

import smsd

chiral = smsd.FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", radius=2, size=2048, cip_atoms=True, ring_size=True)
left = smsd.fingerprint("C[C@H](N)C(=O)O", options=chiral)
right = smsd.fingerprint("C[C@@H](N)C(=O)O", options=chiral)
assert left != right
assert smsd.fingerprint("C[C@H](N)C(=O)O", options=smsd.FingerprintOptions()) == smsd.fingerprint(
    "C[C@@H](N)C(=O)O", options=smsd.FingerprintOptions())

framework = smsd.FingerprintOptions(scaffold="murcko")
assert smsd.fingerprint("Cc1ccccc1", options=framework) == smsd.fingerprint("c1ccccc1", options=smsd.FingerprintOptions())

keys = smsd.fingerprint_from_smiles("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs())
assert 162 in keys  # MACCS key 163, a six-membered ring, is position 162
counts = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=smsd.FingerprintOptions("keys", keys=["[#8]", ("c1ccccc1", 1)], counts=True))
assert counts == [(0, 4), (1, 1)]

Keywords, with their defaults for ecfp, fcfp, path and torsion:

  • family: "ecfp" (default), "fcfp", "path", "torsion", "keys", or a FingerprintFamily (ECFP, FCFP, PATH, TORSION, KEYS).
  • radius (2, 2, –, –; −1 for the whole component), path_length in bonds (–, –, 7, –), size in bits or bins (2048), and counts to return (position, count) pairs (False).
  • Atom terms: element (on, off, on, on); degree, explicit neighbours (on, on, off, on); valence, the bond order sum or pi electrons for torsion (on, off, off, on); formal_charge, isotope, hydrogen_count, tautomer_class and aromaticity (on, off, off, off); ring_membership (on, on, off, on); ring_size, the smallest ring through the atom, with rings at or above ring_size_cap (8) sharing a class (off).
  • Bond terms: bond_order of neighbour or path bonds (on, on, off, off); aromatic_bond and ring_bond (off).
  • cip_atoms, cip_bonds: R/S (and r/s) and E/Z as from assign_rs and assign_ez (off).
  • fragments (ecfp, "whole"): "whole", "largest" (most heavy atoms, independent of atom order), "per_fragment" (terms carry the component), or a FragmentMode (WHOLE, LARGEST, PER_FRAGMENT).
  • scaffold (ecfp, "none"): "none", "murcko" (the Bemis–Murcko framework, taken before fragments; ring-free molecules stay whole), or a ScaffoldMode (NONE, MURCKO).
  • keys, for "keys": SMARTS strings, (smarts, minimum) pairs or FingerprintKey(smarts, minimum=1); a bit is set when at least minimum distinct atom sets match.

FCFP always includes the pharmacophore class. Stereo terms use whole-molecule CIP labels; radius 0 does not separate stereoisomers, and double bonds in rings under eight atoms carry no E/Z term. maccs() gives the 166 MACCS keys, key k at position k − 1; maccs_keys() lists them as FingerprintKey values with smarts, minimum and kind (what the key counts). Attributes are readable and writable, and copy() returns an independent copy. An unknown keyword raises TypeError; an unknown family, fragment or scaffold name raises ValueError, as do inconsistent options and unparsable keys when computing. A key search that runs out of time, or a key count that the embedding limit leaves undecided, raises RuntimeError; a key whose minimum number of matches is found before that limit is set. Ring-size terms, double-bond stereo terms, aromatic-ring keys and SMARTS keys whose search needs the minimum cycle basis raise smsd.RingBasisUnavailable naming the cause if ring perception cannot complete that basis; a separate relevant-cycle truncation does not prevent their use. The ring refusals replace values that 8.0.3 could compute from incomplete rings. mcs_fingerprint ignores these options.

docs.title: Similarity coefficients and encodings
docs.text:
• tanimoto_coefficient(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048): |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|; 1.0 for two empty fingerprints.
  • overlap_coefficient(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048): |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|); 1.0 for two empty, 0.0 for one. overlapCoefficient is a deprecated alias.
  • dice(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048), cosine(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048): 2|A ∩ B| / (|A| + |B|) and |A ∩ B| / √(|A| |B|).
  • soergel(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048): 1 − Tanimoto.
  • count_tanimoto_coefficient(fp1, fp2): Σ min(a, b) / Σ max(a, b).
  • count_overlap_coefficient(fp1, fp2): Σ min(a, b) / min(Σ a, Σ b); count_overlapCoefficient is a deprecated alias.
  • count_dice(fp1, fp2), count_cosine(fp1, fp2): Dice and cosine of dense count vectors of equal length, (position, count) pairs or dictionaries.
  • counts_to_array(counts_dict, fp_size): a dense list of length fp_size from a dictionary or pairs, ignoring positions outside it.
  • to_hex(fp, fp_size=2048), from_hex(hex_str): hexadecimal text and back; a non-hexadecimal character raises ValueError.
  • to_binary_string(fp, fp_size=2048): fp_size characters of 0 and 1.

tanimoto_coefficient and overlap_coefficient compare positions only, even for counts, and ignore fp_size. The two sparse count coefficients take pairs or position lists and return 0.0 when both are empty.

docs.title: Screening
docs.text:
• similarity(mol1, mol2): an upper bound in [0, 1] on MCS similarity, for screening; not a fingerprint metric.
  • similarity_upper_bound(g1, g2, chemistry=None): the same bound under chemistry; screen_targets(query, targets, threshold, chemistry=None, *, num_threads=0): indices of targets whose bound reaches threshold, in target order; 0 uses the OpenMP default (OMP_NUM_THREADS), as in match_many. For both, chem is a deprecated keyword. To screen the same targets repeatedly, pass a prepared TargetCorpus as targets, so that they are not converted again on each call.
  • batch_similarity(query, targets, fp_size=2048, radius=2): (index, Tanimoto) pairs on ECFP, most similar first.
  • gpu_is_available(), gpu_device_info(): whether a GPU backend is available, and a description of the run-time compute backend (the CPU when there is no GPU), not of the backend a call used.

docs.title: MOL and SDF
docs.text:
• read_mol_block(mol_block), read_mol_file(filename): V2000 or V3000 text or file; an unopenable file or a block that cannot be read, such as a V3000 block with more than 10,000 atoms, raises ValueError; V2000 numeric fields are read leniently. read_molfile is a deprecated alias.
  • read_sdf(filename): every record at once; malformed records become empty graphs.
  • write_mol_block(mol) (V2000, or V3000 above 999 atoms or bonds), write_mol_block_v3000(mol) and write_sdf_record(mol): MOL text or one SDF record.
  • write_molfile(mol, filename, *, v3000=False, sdf=False): write a MOL block, V3000 block or SDF record.
  • write_sdf(molecules, filename): write SDF records; export_sdf is a deprecated alias.

docs.title: Coordinates and layout
docs.text:
Coordinates are lists of (x, y) or (x, y, z) tuples, one per atom; [x, y] lists are accepted, and new lists are returned. Every function taking mol accepts a molecule.

  • generate_coords_2d(mol, target_bond_length=1.5), generate_coords_3d(mol, target_bond_length=1.5): 2D coordinates, or a 3D starting geometry that is not a validated conformer.
  • layout_quality(mol, coords, target_bond_length=1.5): a bond-length, overlap and crossing score; 0.0 is ideal.
  • count_crossings(mol, coords), is_degenerate_layout(coords): crossing bond pairs; whether width or height is zero.
  • layout_sssr(mol): the smallest set of smallest rings, ordered for layout.
  • match_template(mol, target_bond_length=1.5): coordinates for benzene, naphthalene, indole, purine, steroid, morphinan, quinoline, biphenyl, cyclohexane or piperidine, else [].
  • force_directed_layout(mol, coords, max_iter=500, target_bond_length=1.5), stress_majorisation(mol, coords, max_iter=300, target_bond_length=1.5): (stress, coords).
  • reduce_crossings(mol, coords, max_iter=1000): (crossings, coords) after flipping ring systems; resolve_overlaps(coords, threshold=0.3, max_iter=100): (remaining_overlaps, coords).
  • translate_2d(coords, dx, dy) translates; rotate_2d(coords, angle), in radians, and scale_2d(coords, factor) act about the centroid.
  • mirror_x(coords), mirror_y(coords): reflect in the x or y axis; center_2d(coords) centres on the origin.
  • align_2d(coords, reference): (rmsd, aligned); bounding_box_2d(coords): (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y).
  • normalise_bond_length(mol, coords, target=1.5) scales to the bond length; canonical_orientation(mol, coords) rotates onto a 30-degree grid.
  • Point2D(x, y), Point3D(x, y, z): value types with writable coordinates.

docs.title: Depiction
docs.text:
• depict_svg(mol_or_smiles, opts=None, **kwargs): SVG text.
  • depict_mapping(mol_or_smiles, mapping, opts=None, **kwargs): SVG highlighting and numbering mapped atoms, keyed by drawn-atom index.
  • depict_pair(mol1, mol2, mapping, opts=None, **kwargs): a side-by-side SVG of a mapping.
  • save_svg(svg_str, path): write SVG text to a file.
  • depict_mcs(mol1, mol2, *, tautomer_aware=False, timeout_ms=10000, size=(600, 300), highlight_color=(0.5, 0.8, 1.0)): an RDKit image of the MCS; highlight_color is deprecated, ignored, and warns when changed.
  • depict_substructure(query, target, *, timeout_ms=10000, size=(600, 300)): an RDKit image of a substructure match.
  • to_svg(mol_or_smiles, *, size=(300, 200)): deprecated RDKit SVG; use depict_svg.

The native SVG functions need no RDKit; keyword arguments set DepictOptions attributes, on opts when given. Defaults: bond_length and padding 30 px; line_width, bold_width, font_size and match_width 0 (automatic); width and height 0 (fitted to the molecule); bond_spacing and highlight_radius 0 (18% and 40% of bond_length); highlight_opacity 0.30; subscript_scale 0.70; show_carbon_labels and show_atom_indices False; show_map_numbers True; font_family "Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif".

docs.title: Further reading
docs.text: The user guide, Python package README, installation guide, C++ guide, Java guide and changelog.

docs.title: Python feature adapters and MCP
docs.text: The optional modules smsd.adapters, smsd.mcp_server and smsd.highlight leave the core API unchanged. They are part of smsd 8.1.0 (python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"). NumPy, PyTorch, scikit-learn and the MCP SDK are loaded only by the functions that need them.

docs.title: NumPy and PyTorch
docs.text:
The first Python block requires both NumPy and PyTorch, supplied by the torch extra. On macOS, use an OpenMP-free SMSD build or a compatible shared OpenMP runtime before running it; the source-build command below installs both extras. The adapters compute native molecular fingerprints and return a matrix with one molecule per row and one fingerprint position per column:

import smsd
from smsd.adapters import fingerprints_numpy, fingerprints_torch, to_numpy

molecules = ["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1O"]
features = fingerprints_numpy(molecules, kind="ecfp", fp_size=2048)
assert features.shape == (3, 2048)
assert str(features.dtype) == "uint8"

tensor = fingerprints_torch(molecules, kind="ecfp", fp_size=2048)
assert tuple(tensor.shape) == (3, 2048)

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", size=512, counts=True)
counts = fingerprints_numpy(molecules, options=options)
assert counts.shape == (3, 512)
assert str(counts.dtype) == "int64"

sparse = smsd.fingerprints(molecules, kind="path", fp_size=128)
assert to_numpy(sparse, fp_size=128).shape == (3, 128)

to_numpy and to_torch consume sparse fingerprint rows: set-bit positions, or (position, count) pairs with counts=True. They do not consume dense bit vectors. Empty batches have shape (0, fp_size); an empty row is a zero vector. Repeated count bins are summed. Positions outside the declared size, negative counts and counts that overflow the chosen dtype raise ValueError. An explicitly selected floating dtype can reduce integer precision.

Binary output defaults to NumPy uint8 or PyTorch uint8; count output defaults to int64. PyTorch defaults to the CPU and accepts dtype and device, such as device="cuda" for an NVIDIA GPU or device="mps" on Apple silicon; on macOS, PyTorch may need the OpenMP-free SMSD build described below. Its adapter does not require NumPy. Native fingerprint options, including structural keys and count fingerprints, determine the output size and count mode when supplied.

Packaged macOS OpenMP wheels may require an OpenMP-free SMSD build with PyTorch. Different bundled OpenMP runtimes can abort the process; the adapters conservatively raise ImportError before importing PyTorch or running their native batch when they detect this combination. A shared runtime or an OpenMP-free SMSD build is required. To build the latter from the release source:

python -m pip install ".[numpy,torch]" --config-settings=cmake.define.SMSD_BUILD_OPENMP=OFF

This is a source build requiring the documented C++ build dependencies. Import order and a single requested thread do not resolve distinct OpenMP runtimes. No duplicate-runtime environment override is used.

docs.title: scikit-learn
docs.text:
Install the sklearn extra. The transformer accepts an iterable of molecules or SMILES strings and participates in ordinary pipelines and parameter cloning:

from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from smsd.adapters import FingerprintTransformer

model = make_pipeline(
    FingerprintTransformer(kind="ecfp", fp_size=512),
    KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=1),
)
model.fit(["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1", "c1ccccc1O"], [0, 0, 1, 1])
assert model.predict(["CCO"]).tolist() == [0]

The transformer is stateless: fit records that it is fitted, and transform computes the fingerprints. Its counts=True mode supports ECFP, FCFP, path and torsion fingerprints. A scalar SMILES string must be wrapped in a list; the adapter will not treat its characters as separate molecules.

docs.title: MCP over standard input/output
docs.text:
The optional smsd[mcp] extra uses the official Python SDK over standard input/output. Run smsd-mcp or python -m smsd.mcp_server in the environment that has the extra installed.

The eight tools are find_mcs, find_substructure, search_smarts, molecular_fingerprint, molecular_similarity, screen_molecules, standardise_molecule and depict_mcs. They accept bounded molecular text, not paths, commands or network requests. Native proof/status remains distinct from fingerprint scores and from whether a witness was found. Default standardisation changes representation only; chemical transformations require explicit options and the optional backend.

See MCP tools and function definitions for signatures, finite budgets, original-JSON validation, result pages, timing boundaries, SVG scope, function-definition formats, lazy framework adapters and the local-wheel container/demo recipes. Exporting definitions makes no model request.

docs.title: MCS SVG highlight
docs.text:
The native SVG helper renders an existing result without running another search or importing an optional drawing toolkit:

import smsd
from smsd.highlight import mcs_svg

query, target = "c1ccccc1O", "c1ccccc1N"
result = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_timeout(1000).match(target)
svg = mcs_svg(query, target, result, width=600, height=300)
assert "<svg " in svg

Use the same molecules and numbering as the search. The SVG title and data-search-status, data-optimal and data-complete attributes retain the result's proof status. The pair renderer highlights mapped atoms and bonds joining them. If an MCES result omits a bond between mapped atoms, the helper raises rather than highlighting that extra bond; render smsd.depict_svg(result.best.to_graph(query)) to draw the selected common graph in that case.

docs.title: MCP fingerprint limits
docs.text: MCP inputs are limited to 16,384 text characters. The fingerprint tool accepts at most 1,024 parsed atoms, 65,536 fingerprint positions, radius 8 and path length 8. Path and torsion requests are also checked against a conservative 2,000,000-walk expansion bound before enumeration. Larger requests raise ValueError; these service limits do not change the native fingerprint APIs. Fingerprinting has no hard wall-clock deadline. Search budgets apply after parsing, as described above.

docs.title: SciPy sparse features
docs.text:
Install smsd[scipy]. to_scipy accepts the same sparse positions or position/count pairs as to_numpy, and fingerprints_scipy computes native fingerprints first. Both return a canonical CSR matrix with sorted columns, combined duplicates and no stored zero counts. They never allocate the full dense feature matrix. Binary values default to uint8; counts default to int64. Only boolean/integer dtypes are accepted. Counts are combined as Python integers before checking the selected dtype; overflow raises rather than wrapping or rounding.

from smsd.adapters import to_scipy, fingerprints_scipy

counts = to_scipy([[], [(1, 2), (1, 3)]], fp_size=4, counts=True)
assert counts.toarray().tolist() == [[0, 0, 0, 0], [0, 5, 0, 0]]
assert fingerprints_scipy(["CCO", "CCN"], fp_size=64).shape == (2, 64)

docs.title: pandas and Polars molecule columns
docs.text:
Install smsd[pandas] or smsd[polars]. molecules_pandas and molecules_polars return a DataFrame with molecule and fingerprint columns, in input order. Inputs must be native MolGraph objects or explicit SMILES strings. SMILES are parsed; native molecule references are retained. Other objects, missing values and scalar strings supplied as a batch raise. These functions do not stringify arbitrary objects or convert external molecule types implicitly.

pandas uses object columns with immutable fingerprint tuples. Polars uses an explicit Object column for molecules and typed lists of uint64 positions. With count options, its fingerprint rows are lists of [position, count] pairs, each value checked against uint64. Neither frame is a copy of the native molecules. Polars Object molecules cannot be exported as Arrow molecular data; export the fingerprint features separately.

from smsd.adapters import molecules_pandas, molecules_polars

pandas_frame = molecules_pandas(["CCO", "CCN"], fp_size=64)
polars_frame = molecules_polars(["CCO", "CCN"], fp_size=64)
assert pandas_frame["molecule"].iloc[0].n == 3
assert polars_frame["molecule"][0].n == 3

Both functions accept the ordinary native fingerprint arguments, including options for count mode, and num_threads. Empty batches retain both columns and their declared types.

docs.title: Arrow fingerprint buffers
docs.text:
Install smsd[arrow]. to_arrow exports one fingerprint column as an Arrow fixed-size list of integer values. Sparse inputs are expanded once into an owned dense NumPy matrix. A native-endian, C-contiguous two-dimensional integer NumPy matrix can instead share its value buffer without copying. Boolean NumPy storage needs conversion to byte values, since Arrow boolean storage is bit-packed. Other layouts and byte orders also need a copy. Floating values are rejected, including in count mode.

import numpy as np
from smsd.adapters import to_arrow

features = np.array([[0, 1, 0, 1]], dtype=np.uint8)
table = to_arrow(features, fp_size=4, zero_copy_only=True)
assert table.schema.metadata[b"smsd.zero_copy"] == b"true"
assert table.column("fingerprint").to_pylist() == [[0, 1, 0, 1]]

Arrow retains the NumPy buffer owner after the caller drops its reference. Shared values still alias the original array: do not mutate that array while using the exported table. Use copy=True for isolation. zero_copy_only=True rejects any required copy and cannot be combined with copy=True.

Schema metadata records smsd.fp_size, smsd.counts, smsd.zero_copy, smsd.copy_reason and smsd.ownership. A false zero-copy flag means copying from the original input was necessary, even though Arrow subsequently retains the prepared NumPy buffer. dtype is an optional integer dtype for sparse expansion only; an existing matrix retains its dtype. This is a feature-table export, not molecular graph serialisation or a GPU transfer.

docs.title: Similarity features in scikit-learn pipelines
docs.text:
The sklearn extra also supplies SimilarityTransformer. fit snapshots binary native fingerprints for its reference molecules, retaining order and duplicates. transform returns a dense float64 matrix of Tanimoto values, one column per fitted reference. It computes intersection/union of native set-bit positions; two empty fingerprints have similarity one. It does not fit an approximate index, execute MCS, or infer molecular identity from a fingerprint. The output matrix requires memory proportional to queries times references.

from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from smsd.adapters import SimilarityTransformer

model = make_pipeline(
    SimilarityTransformer(kind="ecfp", fp_size=128),
    KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=1),
)
model.fit(["CCO", "c1ccccc1"], [0, 1])
assert model.predict(["CCO"]).tolist() == [0]

fit_transform consumes an input iterator once. Empty query batches produce zero rows; an empty reference fit raises. Changing fingerprint parameters after fitting requires a refit. Native molecule objects and SMILES are the accepted input types, as for the DataFrame adapters.

docs.title: PyTorch Geometric molecular graphs
docs.text:
Install smsd[pyg]. to_pyg returns a PyTorch Geometric Data object, using the same macOS OpenMP guard as the existing PyTorch adapter. It defaults to CPU; an explicitly selected tensor device does not move molecular parsing or fingerprint generation to a GPU.

from smsd.adapters import to_pyg

graph = to_pyg("CCO")
assert tuple(graph.x.shape) == (3, 7)
assert tuple(graph.edge_index.shape) == (2, 4)
assert graph.atom_id.tolist() == [0, 1, 2]

All feature tensors are int64. Atom rows preserve native atom numbering; atom_id records it explicitly, and num_nodes retains isolated atoms. The seven x columns are atomic number, formal charge, mass number, recorded hydrogen count, degree, aromatic flag and ring flag. These are the native graph's recorded values, not newly inferred descriptors.

Every unique bond produces both directed edges, ordered by its native endpoint pair and then forward/reverse. The three edge_attr columns are recorded bond order, aromatic flag and ring flag. Empty graphs have shapes (0, 7), (2, 0) and (0, 3). No coordinates, stereo labels, training targets or one-hot encodings are invented. Stereo and coordinates are not encoded by this feature schema, so it is not a lossless molecular file format. Add task-specific features explicitly before model training.

The external data structures follow the official SciPy CSR interface, Arrow fixed-size-list interface and PyTorch Geometric Data interface.

docs.title: Jupyter and Colab notebook
docs.text:
The feature-search notebook combines MCS-to-SMARTS search, SVG highlighting, native fingerprint features, a small scikit-learn pipeline and a temporary packed corpus. Its example labels are illustrative, not a predictive-performance evaluation.

Use a local kernel with SMSD 8.1.0, NumPy and scikit-learn already installed. The setup cell detects an actual Colab shell; ordinary local execution performs no upload or installation. Upload the notebook file to Colab and select a fresh Linux x86_64 runtime. There, the cell prompts for one user-uploaded SMSD 8.1.0 core wheel. The distribution name, version, CPython ABI and compatible Linux x86_64 platform tags are checked before installation with sys.executable -m pip --no-index --no-deps --force-reinstall. The imported version is then checked. No CUDA package is needed.

Download the matching trusted wheel beforehand from PyPI or the GitHub releases page; the notebook does not download packages. NumPy and scikit-learn must already be available; they are checked but are not installed by this cell. Run the upload setup before importing SMSD, and restart the Colab runtime before repeating it. A native wheel executes code when loaded.

docs.title: SMSD Pro 8.1.0
docs.text: SMSD Pro 8.1.0 adds Python data and machine-learning adapters, local MCP tools, packed fingerprint corpora, corpus threshold searches and SMARTS export of MCS results, and corrects the C++ RDKit adapter. The deprecated 8.x APIs remain available and supported throughout the 8.x line. The Java library and command-line tool stay at 8.0.3 on Maven Central. The CPU Docker images carry the 8.1.0 command-line tool; otherwise the Java changes below are available only from a source build. The changelog lists every change.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• Python adapters give fingerprints as NumPy, PyTorch, SciPy CSR, Arrow, pandas and Polars data, add scikit-learn fingerprint and similarity transformers, and build PyTorch Geometric graphs with native atom numbering and no coordinates or stereo. The PyTorch adapters refuse a conflicting bundled OpenMP runtime; use a shared runtime or build SMSD with SMSD_BUILD_OPENMP=OFF.
  • smsd-mcp serves eight local molecular tools over MCP for MCS, substructure and SMARTS search, fingerprints, similarity, screening, standardisation and depiction; the registry also exports function definitions and optional LangChain and LlamaIndex tools. Results are JSON with search status and limits; no tool contacts a model provider.
  • A consolidated API reference, an llms.txt index and a guide to connecting AI assistants make the interfaces and local tools easier to find. New Python examples cover NVIDIA screening checked against the CPU, an offline chain of the molecular tools and an MCP client.
  • The MCP container recipe and Hugging Face demonstration source use supplied wheelhouses. They are source examples, not deployed services or published images. Native SVG helpers highlight existing MCS results.
  • Packed fingerprint corpora are read-only memory-mapped files for threshold and exact top-k scans, Butina clustering and MaxMin selection. The CPU is the default; backend="cuda" computes exact integer intersections on the GPU, and "auto" does so when a supported GPU is available. Clustering decisions stay on the CPU, and cuda_calls counts completed CUDA calls. All-pairs work is quadratic.
  • smsd-cuda adds smsd_cuda.preload(), retained device workspaces for prepared corpora, opt-in CUDA Graph replay (SMSD_CUDA_GRAPHS=1) and on-device top-k selection.
  • stream_screen_smiles and stream_screen_many_smiles screen target iterables in bounded chunks, and warm_start prepares a corpus and returns a first screen, with the usual TargetCorpus GPU dispatch and CPU fallback.
  • Substructure.match_corpus and MCS.match_corpus (C++ matchCorpus) decide, in target order, whether each target contains the query or shares at least a given number of atoms; a stopped search leaves the answer open. Matching runs on the CPU; gpu_prefilter=True lets an available GPU pre-screen targets.
  • SMARTS export writes MCS matches in C++, Java and Python; matchWithSmarts (Python match_with_smarts) returns the result and SMARTS together, and Java SmartsWriter writes whole graphs. Stereo, tautomer, complete-ring and strict ring-fusion options are rejected. A pattern carries neither the induced MCIS objective nor the search status.
  • Relevant cycles can be counted without listing them: computeRelevantCycleFamilies (Python compute_relevant_cycle_families) groups them into families, each with one member and its exact number of members, and two further functions find the family of a ring or list members up to a given limit. The grouping into families can depend on the input atom order.
  • The C++ RDKit adapter (fromRDKit, fromSmiles) keeps each atom's hydrogen count and specified double-bond E/Z configuration. Aromatic N–H atoms, as in pyrrole, previously lost their hydrogen.
  • SMILES writers and the C++ and Python SMARTS writer reuse ring-closure numbers and raise an error beyond 99 open closures; SMILES writers also write long chains without exhausting the stack. Compiled SMARTS evaluate distinct recursive predicates separately, and bond edits refresh cached rings and topology. Worker errors in TargetCorpus.prewarm, CPU corpus screening, C++ path-fingerprint batchFingerprint and batchFingerprintScreen now reach the caller instead of ending the process.
  • Conda recipes build the CPU package and the Linux CUDA package; the conda guide gives the conda, mamba and Pixi install routes.
  • NOTICE now carries licence notices for the RDKit MACCS key definitions and pybind11. The smsd-cuda package now ships the CUB and CCCL licences, and its NOTICE points to them.

docs.title: Upgrading from 8.0.3
docs.text:
SMSD Pro 8.1.0 supports CPython 3.12–3.15. On Python 3.10 and 3.11, pip continues to install 8.0.3.

Ring perception works within one fixed, deterministic work limit, the same in C++, Java and Python and independent of time, thread count and hardware. Very large fused-ring systems, such as synthetic cages, can reach it. Some ring systems that 8.0.3 left incomplete now complete, and their ring-dependent results can change. Where rings stay incomplete, values computed without the missing rings stay exact; where 8.0.3 computed the rest from incomplete rings, searches now report LimitReached and other calls raise an error naming the cause, with the zero-based input index in C++ and Python batch calls. That error is the new RingBasisUnavailable (Java RingBasisUnavailableException), which existing std::runtime_error, RuntimeError and IllegalStateException handlers still catch. A longer timeout does not change this; see Results and budgets.

Complete-ring matching uses all relevant cycles, and the new relevantCyclesTruncated (Python relevant_cycles_truncated) reports when their enumeration is incomplete. A relevant cycle outside the smallest set of smallest rings now counts as a complete ring, so a completeRingsOnly result that 8.0.3 reported as proved, sometimes empty, can now be larger. With completeRingsOnly, Java substructure matching now rejects matches that cover only part of a ring, as C++ and Python do. ringsTruncated keeps its meaning. Per-atom ring counts, and with them strict ring-fusion results, can differ from 8.0.3.

SMARTS R<n> (n > 0) uses the same minimum cycle basis in C++ and Java. If ring perception cannot complete it, an R<n> search that cannot be decided without it returns LimitReached without matches, which does not prove absence; other functions that need the basis raise an error, and computeSSSR and computeRings may return incomplete rings with truncation flags. R and R0 are unaffected. Ring-size and double-bond stereo fingerprint terms, aromatic-ring keys (as in MACCS) and SMARTS keys whose search needs the basis also raise an error then. Java now uses the same basis as C++ and Python for R<n> and these terms, so a Java result from a different minimum basis of equal size can change.

SMARTS parsing in C++ and Python now rejects a pattern ending in a bond, such as CC-, as Java already did; 8.0.3 C++ and Python accepted it after dropping the bond.

C++ and Python MCIS search (the default MCS objective) has changed: when 8.0.3 or 8.1.0 stops a search at its node or time limit, including the default time limit, the two results can differ, and a result of the same size can come with a different atom mapping. Java does not have this change, so a stopped search can return a different result in Java than in C++ and Python.

MCS.consensus always reports optimal as false; complete means the computation finished, not that no larger common graph exists. Searches on graphs from the C++ RDKit adapter can now differ. MCS searches reject graphs with inconsistent bond properties.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
SMSD Pro 8.1.0 is available from PyPI and GitHub. Install it with python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0", adding "smsd-cuda==8.1.0" (matching smsd) for GPU screening on Linux x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU. Python wheels cover CPython 3.12–3.15 on Linux x86_64 and aarch64, Windows x86_64 and macOS arm64 (macOS 14 or later). For Java, use 8.0.3: the library com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd:8.0.3 and the command-line tool com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli:8.0.3 on Maven Central, and the CLI files and installers of the 8.0.3 release. The CPU Docker images below carry the 8.1.0 command-line tool. Multi-GPU screening and native Windows CUDA wheels are not provided. See the installation guide for requirements, its Docker section for the Docker images and the GitHub releases page for the files and SHA256SUMS:

docs.title: SMSD Pro 8.0.3
docs.text: SMSD Pro 8.0.3 corrects complete-ring MCS matching, the status of MCS results that depend on truncated ring perception, and the built-in named SMARTS predicates. It adds opt-in Metal fingerprint screening for C++ source builds on macOS and a Python call that fingerprints many molecules at once. The changelog lists every change.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text:
• C++ and Java MCIS searches with stereochemistry find the largest mapping that keeps the configuration of mapped stereocentres and double bonds.
  • C++ MCIS searches return the maximum mapping whatever the atom and bond order of the target.
  • Complete-ring MCS matching recognises rings in graphs built without ring flags.
  • With complete rings or strict ring fusion, MCS keeps its mappings but no longer reports them as proved when it depends on truncated ring perception.
  • GPU similarity-bound screening returns the same hits as the CPU screen, including scores at the threshold and molecules with very large atom counts. The float-valued Metal similarity API is unchanged.
  • Metal fingerprint screening for C++ source builds on macOS returns the same hits, in the same order, as the CPU screen. It runs only when requested explicitly. The C++ guide gives its requirements and CPU fallback. The Python wheels use the CPU for screening on macOS.
  • The built-in named SMARTS predicates have corrected definitions, shared by C++ and Java and listed in the Java guide. isKetone and isEster now mark the carbonyl carbon.
  • Python fingerprints computes the fingerprints of many molecules or SMILES strings in one call, each identical to fingerprint and in input order.

docs.title: Upgrading from 8.0.2
docs.text:
Patterns that use the built-in named predicates can match different atoms. Java expands names made of ASCII letters, digits and underscores, including inside recursive SMARTS; a registered name containing other characters is no longer expanded.

With complete rings or strict ring fusion, a search that depends on truncated ring perception now reports LimitReached, with optimal and complete false, instead of Completed. isMappingMaximal (Python is_mapping_maximal) then raises its proof-unavailable error rather than returning a value.

In C++ and Python, a single-result connected MCIS search without stereochemistry or ring options can return a different mapping of the same size when every atom of the target is bonded to every other.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text:
The installation guide lists the supported platforms and runtime requirements. Python CPU wheels target CPython 3.10–3.14 on macOS arm64, Linux x86_64 and aarch64, and Windows x86_64. The optional smsd-cuda package targets Linux x86_64 and must match the smsd version. The Java CLI is supplied as a portable distribution and as Windows x86_64 MSI, macOS arm64 DMG and Linux amd64 DEB installers that include Java 25. CPU Docker image archives target Linux amd64 and arm64; the GPU Docker image archive targets Linux amd64 and needs a compatible NVIDIA GPU and driver.

See the GitHub releases page for the files and SHA256SUMS. Install with python -m pip install "smsd==8.0.3", and add "smsd-cuda==8.0.3" for GPU screening with an NVIDIA GPU.

docs.title: SMSD Pro 8.0.2
docs.text: SMSD Pro 8.0.2 adds the optional smsd-cuda package and ordered batches of corpus screening queries. Matching runs on the CPU. The changelog lists the changes in full.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• TargetCorpus.screen_many screens ECFP4 Tanimoto similarity for each query; screen_targets_many screens the atom-count MCS similarity bound. Each result keeps query and target order.
  • The optional CUDA backend keeps corpus fingerprints on the device for reuse. Scores use the CPU expressions and hits keep target order.
  • CPU wheels cover CPython 3.10–3.14 on four platforms. CPU Docker images cover Linux amd64 and arm64; the separate GPU image targets Linux amd64.

docs.title: Downloads and installation
docs.text:
See the supported-platforms table for the Python, Java and C++ requirements, the Docker section for the Docker images and the GitHub releases page for files and SHA256SUMS. Install the Python package with python -m pip install "smsd==8.0.2"; the optional CUDA package must also be version 8.0.2.

The Python guide describes CUDA dispatch and CPU fallback behaviour. Native Windows CUDA wheels and macOS GPU support are not included. Windows GPU use is through the GPU Docker image under WSL2.

docs.title: Upgrading from 8.0.1
docs.text: Python now requires version 3.10 or later. Existing scalar screening calls and prepared search calls keep their signatures; the two corpus batch screens are additional methods.

docs.title: SMSD Pro 8.0.1
docs.text: SMSD Pro 8.0.1 corrects parsing, aromaticity, CIP descriptors and stereochemistry, gives fingerprint quality one definition in C++, Java and Python, and screens targets on every core in Python. The prepared-query API is unchanged. The changelog lists the changes in full.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• SMILES, SMARTS and V3000 MOL input outside the supported characters or ranges is rejected with the same error on every platform, and SMILES atoms joined by : ring bonds are aromatic, as RDKit reads them.
  • CIP R/S and E/Z labels that only the later sequence rules decide, and C++ SMARTS chirality, ring closures and MCES stereochemistry that match Java.
  • Python screen_targets takes num_threads and a prepared TargetCorpus, and rings_truncated reports when a bounded ring search is cut short.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text: File Requirements C++ headers: smsd-cpp-8.0.1-headers.tar.gz A C++17 compiler Java library: smsd-8.0.1.jar, with smsd-8.0.1-sources.jar and smsd-8.0.1-javadoc.jar Java 8 or later and CDK 2.13 Command-line tool: smsd-cli-8.0.1-jar-with-dependencies.jar and smsd-8.0.1-cli.tar.gz Java 8 or later Python source distribution: smsd-8.0.1.tar.gz Python 3.9 or later, a C++17 compiler and CMake 3.18 or later Python wheels for macOS arm64, Linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64 CPython 3.14, as for 8.0.0 SHA256SUMS Lists the SHA-256 checksum of each file

docs.title: Upgrading from 8.0.0
docs.text:
• expected_collision_rate (Python analyze_fp_quality, Java analyzeFpQuality) is now the estimated share of hashed features that fell on a bit already set, and Java suggestFingerprintSize returns larger sizes; review thresholds based on either.
  • In C++ and Python, rings written aromatic that are not, such as cyclobutadiene, are no longer aromatic.
  • A long fragment MCES search for one best mapping can return a different mapping of the same size.

docs.title: SMSD Pro 8.0.0
docs.text: SMSD Pro 8.0.0 provides substructure and maximum common substructure (MCS) search for C++, Java and Python through prepared MCS and Substructure queries. A query is prepared once and searches one or more targets; each result holds its matches with their atom and bond mappings, the search status and whether the optimum was proved. The changelog lists the changes in full.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• One search API in three languages: connected and disconnected maximum common induced subgraphs (MCIS), maximum common edge subgraphs (MCES), atom-weighted MCIS and substructure search, through match, matchAll and matchMany (Python match, match_all and match_many).
  • Constrained, consensus and R-group searches: MCS.matchConstrained, MCS.consensus and Substructure.decomposeRGroups (Python match_constrained, consensus and decompose_r_groups).
  • Results that report status, proved optimality and completeness separately from the matches, under timeouts, node limits and cancellation.
  • Daylight SMARTS semantics in C++ and Java through Substructure.smarts, documented SMARTS size limits in every language, and the OpenSMILES limits for SMILES bracket atoms in C++ and Python.
  • The same valence and tetrahedral-centre rules in C++, Java and Python, and CIP descriptors for R/S that follow the IUPAC 2013 Sequence Rules 1 to 5, with Rule 6 as proposed by Hanson et al. (2018).
  • Tautomer classes that do not depend on the atom order, pH-dependent tautomer weights and a tautomer confidence for the selected bonds of a match.
  • FingerprintOptions, one fingerprint specification for circular, path, torsion and structural-key fingerprints, including the 166 MACCS keys, with identical bits in C++, Java and Python.
  • The Java library com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd, which depends only on the CDK modules it uses, and the separate command-line tool com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli.

docs.title: Downloads
