docs.title: Pick a diverse subset with MaxMin
docs.text:
smsd.maxmin(corpus, count, seed=0) starts at row seed, then repeatedly takes the row whose closest already-picked row is the least similar, that is, the row with the largest minimum Tanimoto distance (1 − Tanimoto) to the selection. Equal distances go to the lower row, and no random numbers are used, so the same index, count and seed always give the same list. The list is in the order picked, and a shorter run is a prefix of a longer one: the first three rows of a pick of eight are exactly the pick of three.

The seed decides where the selection starts. Row 0 is the default, which makes the result depend on the input order. Choose a seed that means something, such as a reference compound or the centre of the largest Butina cluster, and record it.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533


def closest_pair(fingerprints, rows):
    """The highest Tanimoto similarity between any two of the given rows."""
    return max(smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(fingerprints[a], fingerprints[b])
               for a, b in itertools.combinations(rows, 2))


options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, smiles,
                                            options=options) as corpus:
        first = smsd.maxmin(corpus, 8)  # starts at row 0, diazepam
        phenol = smsd.maxmin(corpus, 8, seed=names.index("phenol"))
        assert smsd.maxmin(corpus, 3) == first[:3]  # a prefix of the longer pick
        assert smsd.maxmin(corpus, 0) == []
        fingerprints = [corpus.fingerprint(row) for row in range(len(corpus))]

print("from diazepam:", [names[row] for row in first])
print("from phenol:  ", [names[row] for row in phenol])
print(f"closest pair in the first pick: {closest_pair(fingerprints, first):.3f}")
print(f"closest pair in rows 0 to 7:    "
      f"{closest_pair(fingerprints, range(8)):.3f}")
assert [names[row] for row in first[:3]] == ["diazepam", "GEN-148", "caffeine"]
assert phenol[0] == names.index("phenol") and len(set(phenol)) == 8

The program prints:

from diazepam: ['diazepam', 'GEN-148', 'caffeine', 'GEN-175', 'paracetamol', 'GEN-219', 'naproxen', 'GEN-294']
from phenol:   ['phenol', 'flunitrazepam', 'caffeine', 'GEN-222', 'GEN-164', 'ibuprofen', 'GEN-077', 'GEN-167']
closest pair in the first pick: 0.113
closest pair in rows 0 to 7:    0.755

Eight rows picked by MaxMin share at most 0.113 with each other, whereas the first eight rows of the file, all benzodiazepines, include a pair at 0.755. Two seeds give different selections of similar quality, which is expected: MaxMin is a greedy pick, not a search for the most diverse subset of a given size. count may be any number from 0 to the row count; a seed past the last row raises IndexError, and a negative one ValueError.

MaxMin favours the edges of the library: its first picks are the molecules least like everything already chosen, which often includes outliers and oddities. To cover the populated regions instead, cluster first and take the Butina centres, or run MaxMin on an index built from the centres.

docs.title: Nearest neighbours and pairs
docs.text:
corpus.top_k_pairs(k, threshold=0.0) yields the k most similar other rows of every row as (row, neighbour, Tanimoto). The output is grouped by row in row order, best first within each row, and equal scores prefer the lower neighbour. threshold drops neighbours below it, so a row with no neighbour at or above the threshold yields nothing: that is a direct way to find outliers. include_self=False leaves out each row's pairing with itself, and k is reduced to the number of other rows when it is larger. The method is a generator, so consume it as it streams when the library is large.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, smiles,
                                            options=options) as corpus:
        # The three nearest neighbours of the first two rows.
        nearest = [pair for pair in corpus.top_k_pairs(3) if pair[0] < 2]
        # Rows whose nearest neighbour has an identical fingerprint.
        twins = sum(score == 1.0 for _, _, score in corpus.top_k_pairs(1))
        # Rows with no neighbour at 0.4 or above.
        close = {row for row, _, _ in corpus.top_k_pairs(1, threshold=0.4)}

for row, neighbour, score in nearest:
    print(f"{names[row]:<11} -> {names[neighbour]:<11} {score:.3f}")
print("rows with an identical twin:", twins)
print("rows with no neighbour at 0.4:",
      [names[row] for row in range(len(names)) if row not in close])
assert len(nearest) == 6 and twins == 504 and len(close) == 526

The program prints:

diazepam    -> temazepam   0.582
diazepam    -> tetrazepam  0.542
diazepam    -> nordazepam  0.528
nordazepam  -> oxazepam    0.558
nordazepam  -> diazepam    0.528
nordazepam  -> bromazepam  0.519
rows with an identical twin: 504
rows with no neighbour at 0.4: ['aspirin', 'salicylic acid', 'paracetamol', 'ibuprofen', 'naproxen', 'caffeine', 'phenol']

The 504 twins are the repeated generated benzenes; the seven rows with no close neighbour are the common drugs, which have no analogue in this library. Both findings are worth having before clustering: the first says the counts behind Butina centres are inflated by duplicates, and the second says which rows will end up as singletons at 0.4 or above.

top_k_pairs reports each relationship from both sides, as two directed pairs. When every pair above a similarity is wanted once, use corpus.threshold_pairs(threshold), which yields (first, second, Tanimoto) with first < second; Neighbours and pairs within the index shows it.

docs.title: Chunk size, determinism and cost
docs.text:
chunk_size sets how many rows are compared at a time. It changes the working memory, never the clusters, selections or neighbours. The default of 4096 rows is reduced automatically to keep each chunk's working arrays within about 64 MiB, so it rarely needs changing; lower it only to cut peak memory on a small machine. Results do not depend on the chunk size, the backend or the run, because every score is computed exactly and every tie goes to the lower row.

The comparison work is what limits library size:

  • Butina compares every pair once to count neighbours, about n²/2 comparisons, then makes one pass over the library for each cluster it forms. With reordering=True it also makes a pass for every row it assigns, which adds about n² comparisons. Doubling the library roughly quadruples the time.
  • MaxMin makes one pass over the library for each row it picks, n × count comparisons, so it grows linearly with the library for a fixed count.
  • top_k_pairs compares every row with every other row, about n² comparisons, because each row is ranked against the whole library.

Memory stays modest. Butina keeps two arrays of n entries, about 9 bytes per row, and MaxMin one array of 8 bytes per row; neither builds a similarity matrix or a neighbour list. The index file is memory-mapped, at ceil(fp_size / 8) bytes per row: 256 bytes for 2048 bits. The returned clusters and any pairs you keep are ordinary Python objects and come on top; collecting all of top_k_pairs needs n × k results, and all of threshold_pairs can need memory that grows with n². Time a representative sample on your own hardware before committing to a library size, as the notes of Screening a library advise.

docs.title: CPU and GPU backends
docs.text:
smsd.butina, smsd.maxmin, top_k_pairs and threshold_pairs take the same backend argument as the other searches of a packed index:

Backend Behaviour "cpu" The default. NumPy compares the packed rows on the CPU; the CUDA package is not loaded. "cuda" The comparisons run on an NVIDIA GPU. It needs the smsd-cuda package of the same version, a usable device and a little-endian host, and raises RuntimeError otherwise; fingerprints wider than 65,536 bits raise ValueError. "auto" Uses the GPU under the same conditions, for an index of any size, and the CPU otherwise.

The GPU takes only the fingerprint comparisons; the decisions stay on the CPU:

Call On the GPU On the CPU butina Exact integer intersection counts of one row against a tile of rows Tanimoto scores from those counts, threshold tests, neighbour counts, centre choice, membership and recounting maxmin Exact integer intersection counts of the last picked row against a tile of rows Tanimoto distances, minimum-distance updates and the choice of the next row top_k_pairs Intersection counts, the threshold test and the best k of each tile Tanimoto scores from those counts, and the merge of the tile lists into the final k with the same score and row-order tie break threshold_pairs Exact integer intersection counts Tanimoto scores and the inclusive threshold test

Both devices form each score from the same integer counts with the same double-precision division, and every tie is broken on the CPU by row order. The clusters, selections, neighbours and scores are therefore identical on either device; the GPU does not make any of these methods approximate. Each device call covers one tile of at most 1,048,576 row pairs, and a 64 MiB host-work estimate can make a tile smaller than chunk_size. The rows of a tile are sent to the device for that call and released afterwards, so the index is not kept on the GPU between calls, and a Butina run sends the library once for every pass it makes.

corpus.cuda_calls is the cumulative number of packed CUDA calls that the corpus has completed, clustering passes included. Read it before and after a call: an increase proves that the device did work for that call. It is not a count of queries, hits or kernels, and it says nothing about speed. Under "auto", the CPU is used only when the CUDA package or a device is unavailable, or the width is unsupported; once device work has started, an error is raised rather than the call being retried on the CPU. Setting SMSD_DISABLE_GPU to any value other than 0 keeps these calls on the CPU, and on a Mac they always run on the CPU.

The program below runs on any machine. It checks that the chunk size and the "auto" backend leave every result unchanged, and, where backend="cuda" can run, that the GPU gives the same results:

import itertools
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

try:
    import smsd_cuda
except ImportError:
    smsd_cuda = None

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533


def cuda_usable():
    """Whether backend="cuda" can run here."""
    return (smsd_cuda is not None and sys.byteorder == "little"
            and os.environ.get("SMSD_DISABLE_GPU", "") in ("", "0")
            and smsd_cuda.__version__ == smsd.__version__
            and smsd_cuda.is_available())


def results(corpus, **controls):
    """Butina clusters, a MaxMin pick and the two nearest neighbours of each row."""
    return (smsd.butina(corpus, threshold=0.5, **controls),
            smsd.maxmin(corpus, 8, **controls),
            list(corpus.top_k_pairs(2, **controls)))


options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, smiles,
                                            options=options) as corpus:
        reference = results(corpus)  # backend="cpu", chunk_size=4096
        print("CUDA calls after the CPU run:", corpus.cuda_calls)
        assert corpus.cuda_calls == 0
        for chunk_size in (7, 100):
            assert results(corpus, chunk_size=chunk_size) == reference
        print("chunk sizes 7, 100 and 4096: identical results")

        # "auto" may run on either device, so check its results, not where.
        assert results(corpus, backend="auto") == reference
        print("backend='auto': identical results")

        if cuda_usable():
            before = corpus.cuda_calls
            assert results(corpus, backend="cuda") == reference
            assert corpus.cuda_calls > before  # the device did the comparisons

The program prints:

CUDA calls after the CPU run: 0
chunk sizes 7, 100 and 4096: identical results
backend='auto': identical results

On a machine without a usable GPU the "auto" run takes the CPU path and the branch under if cuda_usable(): is skipped. On a machine with smsd-cuda and a supported NVIDIA GPU, the "auto" and "cuda" runs do their comparisons on the device, corpus.cuda_calls rises, and the program prints the same lines. CPU and GPU screening covers installation of the CUDA package and how to time the two devices fairly.

docs.title: smsd.butina
docs.text:
smsd.butina(corpus, threshold=0.7, *, reordering=False, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu") returns a list of tuples of row indices, each with its centre first and its other members in row order.

Name Type Default Meaning corpus FingerprintCorpus required An open packed index; anything else raises TypeError, a closed one ValueError threshold float 0.7 Inclusive Tanimoto similarity a member must reach with its centre; finite and from 0 to 1 reordering bool False True recounts unassigned neighbours after each cluster; must be a bool chunk_size int 4096 Rows compared at a time; at least 1, reduced to keep each chunk within about 64 MiB backend str "cpu" "cpu", "cuda" or "auto"; any other value raises ValueError

docs.title: smsd.maxmin
docs.text:
smsd.maxmin(corpus, count, *, seed=0, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu") returns a list of count distinct row indices in the order picked.

Name Type Default Meaning corpus FingerprintCorpus required An open packed index count int required Rows to pick, from 0 to the row count; outside that range raises ValueError seed int 0 The first row picked; a row past the last raises IndexError, a negative one ValueError chunk_size int 4096 As for butina backend str "cpu" As for butina

docs.title: FingerprintCorpus.top_k_pairs
docs.text:
corpus.top_k_pairs(k, *, threshold=0.0, include_self=False, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu") yields (row, neighbour, Tanimoto) tuples.

Name Type Default Meaning k int required Neighbours per row, at least 0; reduced to the number of candidate rows; 0 yields nothing threshold float 0.0 Inclusive lower bound on the reported Tanimoto similarity include_self bool False True lets a row be its own neighbour, with a score of 1 chunk_size int 4096 As for butina backend str "cpu" As for butina; with "cuda" or "auto", a loaded CUDA package must also provide its top-k operation, or RuntimeError is raised

Integer arguments reject booleans and floats with TypeError. A threshold outside 0 to 1, or one that is not finite, raises ValueError.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A Butina cluster is defined by its centre. Two members of one cluster can be less similar to each other than the threshold, and a row joins the first cluster whose centre reaches it, not necessarily the closest centre.
  • Butina centres depend on the neighbour counts, so duplicates and the choice of reordering change them. Apart from the row that seed=0 names, changing the row order changes only how equal counts and equal distances are resolved.
  • MaxMin is greedy. It gives a well-spread selection quickly, but a different seed gives a different, equally valid selection.
  • The scores are Tanimoto similarities on binary fingerprints. Count fingerprints cannot be stored in a packed index.
  • These tools rank fingerprints, not structures. Confirm a series or a near-duplicate that matters with an exact search; see Maximum common substructure and Substructure search.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Packed fingerprint index: building, reopening and searching the index these tools read.
  • Screening a library: preparing a library and removing duplicates.
  • CPU and GPU screening: installing the CUDA package and checking where work ran.
  • Fingerprints and similarity: fingerprint families and FingerprintOptions.
  • Packed fingerprint corpora: the reference contract, including CPU and CUDA backends and ordering, work and memory.
  • The MCS to a small library search notebook runs Butina clustering and MaxMin selection.

docs.title: Command line and containers
docs.text: The command-line tool smsd runs one substructure, SMARTS or maximum common substructure (MCS) search between a query and a target, exports the atom mappings, and searches every record of an SDF file, reporting the results as JSON and through its exit status. This chapter covers the tool, the Docker images that carry it, and the local molecular tools server. Fingerprints and similarity screening are not available on the command line; the limitations section says where to find them.

docs.title: Get the command-line tool
docs.text:
The 8.1.0 tool comes from a Java source build or from the CPU Docker images. Maven Central and the 8.0.3 release carry the 8.0.3 tool, which the installation guide describes. To build 8.1.0, use a JDK (Java 25 LTS preferred) and Maven 3.9 or later, and from the repository root run:

mvn -f java/pom.xml clean package
export PATH="$PWD/java/cli/src/scripts:$PATH"
smsd --version

The build runs the default tests and writes java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar, which holds the tool and all its dependencies and runs on Java 8 or later, also as java -jar smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar. The launcher script java/cli/src/scripts/smsd runs the newest such JAR in java/cli/target, or one next to the script; smsd.bat and smsd.ps1 in the same folder do the same on Windows. The examples in this chapter call the tool as smsd.

Variable Effect SMSD_JAR The JAR to run, instead of the newest one found (smsd and smsd.bat) JAVA_HOME Run $JAVA_HOME/bin/java instead of the java on the path (smsd and smsd.bat) JAVA_OPTS Options for the Java virtual machine, such as -Xmx2g (all three launchers)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text:
smsd --Q TYPE --q QUERY --T TYPE --t TARGET [--mode sub|mcs] [options]

--Q and --T name the input types, and --q and --t give a SMILES or SMARTS string or a file path:

Type --q or --t holds Query Target SMI One SMILES string Yes Yes SIG One SMARTS string Yes, in substructure mode No MOL The path of an MDL MOL file Yes Yes ML2 The path of a Mol2 file Yes Yes PDB The path of a PDB file with one model Yes Yes CML The path of a CML file with one molecule Yes Yes SDF The path of an SDF file of up to 100,000 records No Yes, as a batch

Type names and the mode ignore case. Each molecule is standardised first (atom types, implicit hydrogens, rings and aromaticity); a molecule that cannot be standardised is used as read. Without --json the tool writes no report and answers only through its exit status; --json - writes the report to standard output. The first lines of smsd --help list every option:

smsd --help | head -5

The command prints:

Usage: smsd [-ahmrV] [--benchmark] [--fragments] [--induced] [--json-pretty]
            [--map-pretty] [--json=<jsonOut>] [--map-format=<mapFormat>]
            [--map-out=<mapOut>] [--mode=<mode>] [-o=<mcsFragmentOut>]
            [--objective=<objective>] --q=<q> --Q=<qType> --t=<t> --T=<tType>
            [--threads=<numThreads>] [--timeout=<timeoutMs>]

docs.title: Substructure search
docs.text:
Substructure mode is the default. Every report carries two effort figures, nodes_visited and elapsed_ms, that change from run to run, so the examples in this chapter delete them with sed; leave the filter out to see them. This search looks for benzene in phenol:

smsd --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "Oc1ccccc1" --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'

The command prints the following, and smsd exits with status 0:

{"query":"c1ccccc1","target":"Oc1ccccc1","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":true,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":6.0,"bonds":[{"query":[0,1],"target":[2,3]},{"query":[0,5],"target":[1,2]},{"query":[1,2],"target":[3,4]},{"query":[2,3],"target":[4,5]},{"query":[3,4],"target":[5,6]},{"query":[4,5],"target":[1,6]}],"fragments":[[0,1,2,3,4,5]]}

exists answers the question, and status, optimal and complete say whether the answer is proved, as described under reading a result. bonds pairs each query bond with its target bond, by atom indices in input order.

A SMARTS query uses the type SIG. The first search finds a carbonyl group in acetic acid and exits with status 0; the second finds none in ethanol and exits with status 1:

smsd --Q SIG --q "C=O" --T SMI --t "CC(=O)O" --json - --json-pretty \
  | sed -E '/"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)"/d'
smsd --Q SIG --q "C=O" --T SMI --t "CCO" --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'

The commands print:

{
  "query" : "C=O",
  "target" : "CC(=O)O",
  "mode" : "sub",
  "timeout_ms" : 10000,
  "exists" : true,
  "status" : "Completed",
  "optimal" : true,
  "complete" : true,
  "score" : 2.0,
  "bonds" : [ {
    "query" : [ 0, 1 ],
    "target" : [ 1, 2 ]
  } ],
  "fragments" : [ [ 0, 1 ] ]
}
{"query":"C=O","target":"CCO","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":false,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":0.0}

docs.title: MCS
docs.text:
--mode mcs finds a connected maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS) by default. For N-methylacetamide and propanamide:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CC(=O)NC" --T SMI --t "CCC(=O)N" --mode mcs \
  --json - --json-pretty \
  | sed -E '/"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)"/d'

The command prints the following, and smsd exits with status 0:

{
  "query" : "CC(=O)NC",
  "target" : "CCC(=O)N",
  "mode" : "mcs",
  "timeout_ms" : 10000,
  "status" : "Completed",
  "optimal" : true,
  "complete" : true,
  "score" : 4.0,
  "bonds" : [ {
    "query" : [ 0, 1 ],
    "target" : [ 1, 2 ]
  }, {
    "query" : [ 1, 2 ],
    "target" : [ 2, 3 ]
  }, {
    "query" : [ 1, 3 ],
    "target" : [ 2, 4 ]
  } ],
  "fragments" : [ [ 0, 1, 2, 3 ] ],
  "objective" : "MCIS",
  "mcs_size" : 4,
  "pairs" : [ [ 0, 1 ], [ 1, 2 ], [ 2, 3 ], [ 3, 4 ] ],
  "query_atoms" : [ 0, 1, 2, 3 ],
  "target_atoms" : [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ],
  "tanimoto" : 0.6666666666666666,
  "similarity_upper_bound" : 1.0,
  "mcs_smiles" : "C(C)(N)=O"
}

mcs_size counts the common atoms and pairs lists them as query and target indices. tanimoto is the MCS similarity 4 / (5 + 5 − 4), not a fingerprint similarity. --objective MCES maximises common bonds instead, and --fragments allows a disconnected result, here the two ethyl groups of diethyl ether and diethylamine:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CCOCC" --T SMI --t "CCNCC" \
  --mode mcs --objective MCES --fragments --timeout 1000 --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'

The command prints:

{"query":"CCOCC","target":"CCNCC","mode":"mcs","timeout_ms":1000,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":2.0,"bonds":[{"query":[0,1],"target":[0,1]},{"query":[3,4],"target":[3,4]}],"fragments":[[0,1],[3,4]],"objective":"MCES","mcs_size":4,"pairs":[[0,0],[1,1],[3,3],[4,4]],"query_atoms":[0,1,3,4],"target_atoms":[0,1,3,4],"tanimoto":0.3333333333333333,"similarity_upper_bound":1.0,"mcs_smiles":"CC.CC"}

For MCES, score and tanimoto count bonds, while mcs_size still counts atoms. -o writes the common graph as SMILES, to a file or, with -, to standard output, and writes nothing when there is no common graph:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CC(=O)NC" --T SMI --t "CCC(=O)N" --mode mcs -o -

The command prints:

C(C)(N)=O

docs.title: SDF batch search
docs.text:
With --T SDF, the query is searched against every record of the file. To follow the examples, write a small file with the Python package:

python - <<'EOF'
import smsd

library = {"phenol": "Oc1ccccc1", "cyclohexanol": "OC1CCCCC1",
           "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", "ethanol": "CCO",
           "toluene": "Cc1ccccc1"}
graphs = []
for name, smiles in library.items():
    graph = smsd.parse_smiles(smiles)
    graph.name = name
    graphs.append(graph)
smsd.write_sdf(graphs, "targets.sdf")
EOF

The report has one row per record under results, in file order. A row carries the record's position as target_index but not its title, so read the titles from the file when you need them. These commands run a substructure batch and an MCS batch, each on two threads, and print one line per record:

smsd --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SDF --t targets.sdf --threads 2 --json benzene.json
smsd --Q SMI --q "Oc1ccccc1" --T SDF --t targets.sdf --mode mcs --threads 2 --json phenol.json
python - <<'EOF'
import json
import smsd

names = [graph.name for graph in smsd.read_sdf("targets.sdf")]
with open("benzene.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    embeddings = json.load(handle)["results"]
with open("phenol.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    common = json.load(handle)["results"]
for row, mcs in zip(embeddings, common):
    print(names[row["target_index"]], row["exists"], mcs["mcs_size"], round(mcs["tanimoto"], 3))
EOF

The commands print:

phenol True 7 1.0
cyclohexanol True 7 1.0
aspirin True 7 0.538
ethanol False 3 0.429
toluene True 6 0.75

Benzene is found in cyclohexanol because of the fixed default chemistry; see limitations. An MCS row has mcs_size, pairs and tanimoto but no mcs_smiles. --threads 0, the default, uses every processor, so set --threads on a shared machine. The whole file is read into memory before the search starts.

docs.title: Mapping export
docs.text:
In substructure mode, -m enumerates up to 10,000 embeddings and reports them under mappings in place of exists. Methanol embeds in methanediol in two ways:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CO" --T SMI --t "OCO" -m --json - --json-pretty \
  | sed -E '/"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)"/d'

The command prints:

{
  "query" : "CO",
  "target" : "OCO",
  "mode" : "sub",
  "timeout_ms" : 10000,
  "status" : "Completed",
  "optimal" : true,
  "complete" : true,
  "score" : 2.0,
  "bonds" : [ {
    "query" : [ 0, 1 ],
    "target" : [ 0, 1 ]
  } ],
  "fragments" : [ [ 0, 1 ] ],
  "mappings" : [ {
    "index" : 0,
    "pairs" : [ [ 0, 1 ], [ 1, 0 ] ],
    "query_atoms" : [ 0, 1 ],
    "target_atoms" : [ 1, 0 ]
  }, {
    "index" : 1,
    "pairs" : [ [ 0, 1 ], [ 1, 2 ] ],
    "query_atoms" : [ 0, 1 ],
    "target_atoms" : [ 1, 2 ]
  } ],
  "tanimoto" : 0.6666666666666666
}

--map-out writes the mappings of a single-pair search in the format chosen by --map-format. In substructure mode it needs -m and otherwise writes nothing; in MCS mode it works on its own. The smiles format writes, for each mapping, the query and the target as SMILES with matching atom-map numbers, separated by a tab:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CO" --T SMI --t "OCO" -m --map-out - --map-format smiles
smsd --Q SMI --q "CC(=O)NC" --T SMI --t "CCC(=O)N" --mode mcs \
  --map-out - --map-format smiles

The commands print:

[CH3:1][OH:2]   [CH2:1]([OH:2])O
[CH3:1][OH:2]   [CH2:1](O)[OH:2]
[C:2]([CH3:1])([NH:4]C)=[O:3]   [C:2]([CH2:1]C)([NH2:4])=[O:3]

The formats are:

  • json (the default): an object with query_size, target_size and mappings, written without a final newline; --map-pretty indents it.
  • smiles or smi: atom-mapped SMILES, as above. smarts writes the same text.
  • mdl, mol or sdf: MOL blocks with generated two-dimensional coordinates; in MCS mode the common graph of the first match, and in substructure mode the matched target atoms of each mapping. The second header line of each block carries a time stamp to the minute, so the output changes between runs.

When --map-out - and --json - both write to standard output, the export comes first; a json export has no final newline and runs straight into the report, so send them to separate files. An SDF batch ignores -m, --map-out and -o.

docs.title: Hydrogens and induced matching
docs.text:
--induced requires an induced embedding: query atoms that are not bonded may not map to bonded target atoms. Propane embeds in cyclopropane as a path, but not as an induced subgraph:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CCC" --T SMI --t "C1CC1" --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'
smsd --Q SMI --q "CCC" --T SMI --t "C1CC1" --induced --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'

The commands print the following, and smsd exits with status 0 and then 1:

{"query":"CCC","target":"C1CC1","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":true,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":3.0,"bonds":[{"query":[0,1],"target":[0,1]},{"query":[1,2],"target":[0,2]}],"fragments":[[0,1,2]]}
{"query":"CCC","target":"C1CC1","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":false,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":0.0}

Explicit hydrogens are atoms of the graph. A query with an explicit hydrogen, such as [H]OC, finds no match in methanol written without one, unless -r removes the explicit hydrogens first. -a adds explicit hydrogens to both molecules, so methane must then match a carbon with four hydrogens, which methanol does not have:

smsd --Q SMI --q "[H]OC" --T SMI --t "CO" --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'
smsd --Q SMI --q "[H]OC" --T SMI --t "CO" -r --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'
smsd --Q SMI --q "C" --T SMI --t "CO" -a --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'

The commands print:

{"query":"[H]OC","target":"CO","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":false,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":0.0}
{"query":"[H]OC","target":"CO","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":true,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":2.0,"bonds":[{"query":[0,1],"target":[0,1]}],"fragments":[[0,1]]}
{"query":"C","target":"CO","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":false,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":0.0}

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text:
Status Single pair SDF batch 0 The search completed with a match At least one match, and every search completed 1 The search completed without a match No match, and every search completed 2 Invalid input, an unknown mode, an error, or a search stopped as TimedOut, LimitReached or Cancelled Any target that failed or stopped

A stopped search whose report says "exists": false proves nothing, which is why it exits with status 2. --timeout 0 always stops at once, and reaching the limit of 10,000 mappings with -m also counts as stopped. The exit status is enough for a script, even without --json:

smsd --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "Oc1ccccc1"; echo "exit status $?"
smsd --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "CCO"; echo "exit status $?"
smsd --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "Oc1ccccc1" --timeout 0; echo "exit status $?"
smsd --Q SMI --q "C1CC" --T SMI --t "CCC" 2> /dev/null; echo "exit status $?"

The commands print:

exit status 0
exit status 1
exit status 2
exit status 2

The third search timed out and the fourth query is not valid SMILES.

docs.title: JSON report
docs.text:
A single-pair report has these keys:

Key When Value query, target Always The --q and --t values as given mode Always The mode as typed timeout_ms Always The time limit for the pair status Always Completed, TimedOut, Cancelled or LimitReached optimal, complete Always Whether the answer is proved, and whether the search ran to its end score Always Substructure: the query atoms when found, otherwise 0.0; MCIS: atoms; MCES: bonds nodes_visited, elapsed_ms Always Effort figures that vary between runs bonds, fragments A match was found The bond pairs and the connected query atom sets of the first match exists Substructure mode without -m Whether an embedding was found mappings -m Each embedding: index, pairs, query_atoms and target_atoms objective MCS mode MCIS or MCES mcs_size, pairs, query_atoms, target_atoms MCS mode The common atoms of the first match tanimoto MCS mode or -m MCS similarity: common atoms / (query atoms + target atoms − common atoms), or the same count of bonds for MCES similarity_upper_bound MCS mode An upper bound on that similarity mcs_smiles MCS mode with a match The common graph as SMILES

An SDF batch report has query, target_file, target_count, threads_used, mode and results. Each row has target_index, the outcome keys from status to elapsed_ms, bonds and fragments when it matched, and then exists in substructure mode, or mcs_size, pairs and tanimoto in MCS mode. A row whose target could not be searched has an error message instead.

The tanimoto key compares atom or bond counts of the MCS. It is not a fingerprint Tanimoto coefficient: for phenol and aspirin it is 0.538, whereas the ECFP4 Tanimoto coefficient of the pair is 0.020.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Usage errors, such as a missing option, an unknown mode, a lower-case objective or a SMARTS query in MCS mode, print a message and the usage text on standard error:

smsd --Q SMI --q "CC" --T SMI --t "CCC" --mode foo 2>&1 | head -1
smsd --Q SMI --q "CCO" --T SMI --t "CCN" --mode mcs --objective mces 2>&1 | head -1
smsd --Q SIG --q "C=O" --T SMI --t "CC=O" --mode mcs 2>&1 | head -1

The commands print:

Unknown mode: foo
Invalid value for option '--objective': expected one of [MCIS, MCES] (case-sensitive) but was 'mces'
SMARTS queries require substructure mode

Other errors, such as SMILES that cannot be parsed, an unsupported file type, an unknown --map-format or a missing file, print a Java stack trace on standard error. In every case standard output stays empty and the exit status is 2. The Mol2 reader also prints warning lines on standard error for valid files, so redirect standard error when a program reads the report from standard output.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Value Default Meaning --Q Type Required Query type: SMI, SIG, MOL, ML2, PDB or CML --q Text or path Required Query SMILES or SMARTS, or a file path --T Type Required Target type: SMI, MOL, ML2, PDB, CML or SDF --t Text or path Required Target SMILES, or a file path --mode sub or mcs sub Substructure or MCS search --objective MCIS or MCES MCIS MCS objective; upper case only --fragments Flag Off Allow a disconnected MCS --induced Flag Off Require an induced embedding (substructure mode) -m, --mappings Flag Off Enumerate up to 10,000 embeddings (substructure mode) --timeout Milliseconds 10,000 Time limit for each query and target pair, in both modes; 0 stops at once -a, --add-hydrogens Flag Off Add explicit hydrogens to both molecules first -r, --remove-hydrogens Flag Off Remove explicit hydrogens from both molecules first --json Path or - None Write the JSON report; without it nothing is printed --json-pretty Flag Off Indent the JSON report --map-out Path or - None Write the mapping export of a single pair --map-format json, smiles, smi, smarts, mdl, mol or sdf json Mapping export format --map-pretty Flag Off Indent the JSON mapping export -o, --output Path or - None Write the MCS as SMILES (single-pair MCS mode) --benchmark Flag Off Run the substructure and MCS searches of one pair repeatedly and print their average times, which depend on the machine --threads Integer 0 Worker threads for an SDF batch; 0 uses every processor -h, --help Print the usage and exit -V, --version Print the version and exit

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• There are no fingerprint, similarity or index commands. Use the Python, C++ or Java library for those; see screening a library and C++ and Java.
  • The chemistry is always the default one: aromatic bonds also match single and double bonds, and formal charges are not compared. No option changes it, so benzene is found in cyclohexanol, as below. The libraries can switch to stricter chemistry.
  • SMI takes one SMILES string, not a file. A dotted SMILES is one disconnected molecule. To search many SMILES, convert them to an SDF file first.
  • An SDF file may hold up to 100,000 records and is read into memory first. Report rows give target_index but not the record title.
  • PDB and CML files must hold exactly one molecule or model.
  • The time limit is 10,000 ms per pair in both modes, whereas the libraries give an MCS a limit that grows with the size of the molecules.
smsd --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "OC1CCCCC1" --json - \
  | sed -E 's/,"(nodes_visited|elapsed_ms)":[0-9]+//g'

The command prints:

{"query":"c1ccccc1","target":"OC1CCCCC1","mode":"sub","timeout_ms":10000,"exists":true,"status":"Completed","optimal":true,"complete":true,"score":6.0,"bonds":[{"query":[0,1],"target":[2,3]},{"query":[0,5],"target":[1,2]},{"query":[1,2],"target":[3,4]},{"query":[2,3],"target":[4,5]},{"query":[3,4],"target":[5,6]},{"query":[4,5],"target":[1,6]}],"fragments":[[0,1,2,3,4,5]]}

docs.title: Docker images
docs.text:
The release provides three image archives:

Image Archive Platform Entry point Contents smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-amd64.tar.xz linux/amd64 The command-line tool Java 25 runtime, CPython 3.14.9 and the smsd package smsd:8.1.0-cpu-arm64 smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-arm64.tar.xz linux/arm64 The command-line tool As for amd64 smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8 smsd-8.1.0-cuda-linux-amd64.tar.xz linux/amd64 python CPython 3.14.9, smsd, smsd-cuda and the CUDA 12 runtime; no Java

Load a CPU image and pass the tool's options after the image name; use --entrypoint python for Python:

docker load --input smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-amd64.tar.xz
docker run --rm smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 --version
docker run --rm smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 \
  --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SMI --t "Oc1ccccc1" --json -
docker run --rm --entrypoint python smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 \
  -c "import smsd; assert smsd.Substructure.find('CC').match('CCC').found"

Without options, the CPU image prints the tool's help. The container runs as the user smsd in the working directory /work. If docker load stops with exec: "xz": executable file not found in $PATH, the engine cannot decompress the archive; decompress it on the host instead:

xz --decompress --stdout smsd-8.1.0-cpu-linux-amd64.tar.xz | docker load

The tool in the container reads only the files it is given. To search the file of the SDF batch search, mount the current directory on /work and run as yourself, so the report belongs to you:

docker run --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD:/work" smsd:8.1.0-cpu-amd64 \
  --Q SMI --q "c1ccccc1" --T SDF --t targets.sdf --threads 2 --json benzene.json

The Python in each image holds only the SMSD packages, and in the GPU image the CUDA runtime: there is no NumPy, pandas, RDKit or mcp. Packed fingerprint indexes, butina and maxmin clustering, the data-frame and array adapters and the molecular tools server therefore need an image built on top that adds those packages.

The GPU image runs Python on an NVIDIA host with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and a compatible driver:

docker load --input smsd-8.1.0-cuda-linux-amd64.tar.xz
docker run --rm --gpus all smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8 \
  -c "import smsd; print(smsd.__version__); print(smsd.gpu_device_info())"

As shipped, it serves prepared TargetCorpus screens, streamed screens and match_corpus(..., gpu_prefilter=True); a packed index on the GPU also needs NumPy. That a backend is available does not prove that a call used the GPU; the CPU and GPU screening chapter explains how to check. The installation guide describes building the images from source.

docs.title: Molecular tools server
docs.text: smsd-mcp, installed with python -m pip install "smsd[mcp]==8.1.0", serves eight molecular tools over standard input and output, with no network listener. Without the extra it exits with status 1 after a Python traceback that ends with ImportError: The MCP server requires the official SDK; install smsd[mcp]. The molecular tools guide lists the tools and their limits.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:

docs.title: CPU and GPU screening
docs.text: Graph matching in SMSD Pro, which covers every substructure, SMARTS and MCS search, always runs on the CPU. An NVIDIA GPU can take over screening steps: the ECFP4 screens of a prepared TargetCorpus, the pre-screen of a corpus search and the scans of a packed fingerprint index. Hits, scores and search decisions are identical on either device. Every Python program on this page runs on a CPU-only machine; the GPU branches run only where a device is ready.

docs.title: What runs where
docs.text:
Operation CPU NVIDIA GPU (smsd-cuda) How it is chosen Substructure, SMARTS and MCS matching Always Never Not applicable Fingerprints, batch_similarity and similarity coefficients Always Never Not applicable screen_targets, TargetCorpus.screen_targets_many, and Substructure.match_many on a TargetCorpus Always Never with smsd-cuda 8.1.0 Not applicable ECFP4 screens of a prepared TargetCorpus: screen, screen_many, warm_start, stream_screen_smiles and stream_screen_many_smiles Below the device rule, without a usable device, or after a device failure A Tesla T4 for 100,000 targets or more, or any supported device from SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS targets Automatically, for each screen Pre-screen of Substructure.match_corpus and MCS.match_corpus gpu_prefilter=False (the default), or without a usable device gpu_prefilter=True with an attached device By the caller, with CPU fallback Packed FingerprintCorpus scans, butina and maxmin backend="cpu" (the default), or "auto" without a usable device backend="cuda", or "auto" with a usable device By the caller; "cuda" raises without a device

The searches that follow a pre-screen, and every match, match_all and match_many call, use the CPU. Python never uses Metal; see Metal and C++.

The smsd package looks for smsd-cuda once per process, the first time a prepared screen, warm_start, a gpu_prefilter=True search, gpu_is_available() or gpu_device_info() needs it. Importing smsd does not load the CUDA runtime, so the first such call carries the device start-up cost; smsd_cuda.preload() moves that cost to a point the program chooses.

docs.title: Check the backend
docs.text:
smsd.gpu_is_available() returns True when an attached smsd-cuda package has found a usable device. smsd.gpu_device_info() describes the backend: on a CPU-only machine it starts with CPU: and names the OpenMP version and thread count; with an attached device it starts with GPU:, followed by the device name, its compute capability, its memory and, in brackets, the CPU threading. Both report what is available, not which device a call used.

The cuda_status() helper below is the one in the GPU screening example. It decides whether backend="cuda" can be used and gives the reason when it cannot.

import os

import smsd

try:
    import smsd_cuda
except ImportError:
    smsd_cuda = None


def cuda_status():
    """Return whether backend="cuda" can be used here, and the reason when it cannot."""
    if os.environ.get("SMSD_DISABLE_GPU", "") not in ("", "0"):
        return False, "disabled by SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"
    if smsd_cuda is None:
        return False, "smsd-cuda is not installed"
    if smsd_cuda.__version__ != smsd.__version__:
        return False, (f"smsd-cuda {smsd_cuda.__version__} does not match "
                       f"smsd {smsd.__version__}")
    reason = smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason()
    return reason is None, reason


ready, reason = cuda_status()
print("CUDA screening:", "ready" if ready else f"unavailable ({reason})")
assert ready or reason

available = smsd.gpu_is_available()
print("GPU available:", available)
assert isinstance(available, bool)

# 'CPU: ...' without a device; 'GPU: <device>  [...]' once smsd-cuda is attached.
backend = smsd.gpu_device_info()
assert isinstance(backend, str) and backend

if ready:
    smsd_cuda.preload()  # initialise the device and load its kernels now
    assert "compute" in smsd_cuda.device_info()

On a machine without smsd-cuda, the program prints:

CUDA screening: unavailable (smsd-cuda is not installed)
GPU available: False

With smsd-cuda and a usable device, the program prints CUDA screening: ready and GPU available: True. Otherwise smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason() explains why, for example no CUDA device was found, or a reason that names a device below compute capability 7.5.

docs.title: Install the CUDA package
docs.text:
The smsd-cuda package adds NVIDIA screening to smsd on Linux x86_64. Install it with the same version of smsd:

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0"

Packed indexes and clustering also need NumPy, which neither package installs:

python -m pip install "smsd[numpy]==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0"
  • The package needs Linux x86_64 and CPython 3.12–3.15; the supported-platforms table gives the C library version.
  • The device must be an NVIDIA GPU of compute capability 7.5 or later, with a driver compatible with the CUDA 12 runtime. The runtime is installed as a dependency; the CUDA toolkit is not needed.
  • The versions must match exactly. smsd-cuda 8.1.0 requires smsd 8.1.0, and smsd does not attach a package built for another version.
  • No smsd-cuda wheel is published for Windows or macOS. On Windows, the GPU container runs through WSL2; see Containers.

Prepared screens, the stream functions and match_corpus need no NumPy.

docs.title: Automatic use in prepared screens
docs.text:
Prepared ECFP4 screens choose their device automatically. TargetCorpus.screen and screen_many after prewarm(), warm_start, and the stream functions stream_screen_smiles and stream_screen_many_smiles use the GPU when smsd-cuda is attached and the corpus is large enough. Otherwise, and whenever device work fails, they run on the CPU with the same hits. The code is the same on every machine.

By default the GPU is used only on a Tesla T4 (compute capability 7.5), and only for a prepared corpus of at least 100,000 targets. Setting SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS to a positive whole number N lets any supported device take corpora of N targets or more; on a Tesla T4, N replaces 100,000. The stream functions apply the rule to each chunk of targets (4,096 by default), so they use the device only when a chunk is large enough.

import os

import smsd
from smsd.corpus import stream_screen_smiles

benzodiazepines = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
}
names = list(benzodiazepines)
library = list(benzodiazepines.values())
queries = [benzodiazepines["diazepam"], benzodiazepines["alprazolam"]]

# The same calls on every machine; each screen chooses its device.
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library)
corpus.prewarm()
hits = corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4)
for query, found in zip(("diazepam", "alprazolam"), hits):
    print(f"{query}:", ", ".join(names[index] for index in found))
assert hits == [[0, 1, 2, 9, 13], [10, 11, 12]]

# warm_start prepares the corpus it is given; streams prepare one chunk at a time.
fresh = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library)
assert smsd.warm_start(fresh, queries[0], 0.4) == hits[0]
streamed = list(stream_screen_smiles(queries[0], iter(library), 0.4, chunk_size=5))
assert streamed == hits[0]

# Let any supported GPU take corpora of one target or more; the CPU ignores it.
os.environ["SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS"] = "1"
same = corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4) == hits
print("same hits with SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS=1:", same)
assert same

The program prints:

diazepam: diazepam, nordazepam, temazepam, tetrazepam, clobazam
alprazolam: alprazolam, triazolam, midazolam
same hits with SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS=1: True

A CPU-only machine ignores SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS. No public record shows which device ran a prepared screen; the hits are the same either way.

docs.title: Request the GPU for a corpus pre-screen
docs.text:
Substructure.match_corpus and MCS.match_corpus rule out, with a proof, the targets that cannot contain the query or cannot share minimum_atoms atoms with it, and search the remaining targets on the CPU. With gpu_prefilter=True they ask an attached device to run that pre-screen, whatever the corpus size. Without a usable device, or if device work fails, the CPU pre-screen runs instead. Decisions, bounds and matches are identical either way, and no prewarm() is needed.

SMARTS queries, and searches with match_atom_type=False, a node limit, an immediate timeout or a cancellation token, search every target on the CPU without a pre-screen. MCS searches do the same for MCES, atom weights and excluded target atoms.

import smsd

benzodiazepines = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
}
names = list(benzodiazepines)
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(list(benzodiazepines.values()))


def decisions(results):
    """Each target's decision, atom bound and matches, leaving out timings."""
    return [(item.target_index, item.atom_upper_bound, item.threshold_reached,
             item.proven_below_threshold, None if item.result is None else
             (item.result.status, item.result.optimal, item.result.complete,
              item.result.matches))
            for item in results]


# 5-phenyl-1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one core
core = smsd.Substructure.find("O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2N1")
on_cpu = core.match_corpus(corpus)
requested = core.match_corpus(corpus, gpu_prefilter=True)
assert decisions(requested) == decisions(on_cpu)
found = [names[item.target_index] for item in on_cpu if item.threshold_reached]
ruled_out = [names[item.target_index] for item in on_cpu if item.result is None]
print("core found in", len(found), "targets")
print("ruled out before matching:", ", ".join(ruled_out))
assert len(found) == 9
assert ruled_out == ["alprazolam", "triazolam", "midazolam", "clobazam"]

# Targets that share all 22 atoms of alprazolam
mcs = smsd.MCS.find(benzodiazepines["alprazolam"])
on_cpu = mcs.match_corpus(corpus, 22)
requested = mcs.match_corpus(corpus, 22, gpu_prefilter=True)
assert decisions(requested) == decisions(on_cpu)
shared = [names[item.target_index] for item in on_cpu if item.threshold_reached]
print("all 22 atoms shared:", ", ".join(shared))
assert shared == ["alprazolam", "triazolam"]

The program prints:

core found in 9 targets
ruled out before matching: alprazolam, triazolam, midazolam, clobazam
all 22 atoms shared: alprazolam, triazolam

A target that was ruled out has result set to None and proven_below_threshold set to True. The other CorpusSearchResult fields are described in Screening a library.

docs.title: Choose a backend for packed indexes
docs.text:
The searches of a packed FingerprintCorpus (similarities, screen_many, threshold_pairs and top_k_pairs) and the clustering functions butina and maxmin take a backend argument:

Backend Behaviour "cpu" The default. The scan runs on the CPU and does not load smsd-cuda. "cuda" The scan runs on the GPU. It raises RuntimeError when no device is usable and ValueError for fingerprints wider than 65,536 bits. "auto" The scan runs on the GPU whenever a device is usable and the width is supported, for an index of any size, and on the CPU otherwise.

Hits, scores, their order, clusters and selections are identical for all three. Once device work has started, an error is raised rather than retried on the CPU, under "auto" as well. A packed index needs NumPy; see Packed fingerprint index for building and reopening one.

import os
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd
from smsd.clustering import butina, maxmin
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus

try:
    import smsd_cuda
except ImportError:
    smsd_cuda = None


def cuda_status():
    """Return whether backend="cuda" can be used here, and the reason when it cannot."""
    if os.environ.get("SMSD_DISABLE_GPU", "") not in ("", "0"):
        return False, "disabled by SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"
    if smsd_cuda is None:
        return False, "smsd-cuda is not installed"
    if smsd_cuda.__version__ != smsd.__version__:
        return False, (f"smsd-cuda {smsd_cuda.__version__} does not match "
                       f"smsd {smsd.__version__}")
    reason = smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason()
    return reason is None, reason


benzodiazepines = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
}
names = list(benzodiazepines)
options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
ready, reason = cuda_status()

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "benzodiazepines.fp"
    with FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, list(benzodiazepines.values()),
                                       options=options) as corpus:
        query = smsd.fingerprint(benzodiazepines["diazepam"], options=options)
        hits = list(corpus.similarities(query, threshold=0.4, backend="cpu"))
        named = [(names[index], round(score, 3)) for index, score in hits]
        for name, score in named:
            print(f"{name:<11} {score:.3f}")
        assert named == [("diazepam", 1.0), ("nordazepam", 0.528),
                         ("temazepam", 0.582), ("tetrazepam", 0.542),
                         ("clobazam", 0.5)]
        print("CUDA calls after the CPU scan:", corpus.cuda_calls)
        assert corpus.cuda_calls == 0

        # "auto" may run on either device, so check its results, not where it ran.
        automatic = list(corpus.similarities(query, threshold=0.4, backend="auto"))
        assert automatic == hits
        clusters = butina(corpus, threshold=0.4, backend="auto")
        assert clusters == butina(corpus, threshold=0.4, backend="cpu")
        picked = maxmin(corpus, count=3, backend="auto")
        assert picked == maxmin(corpus, count=3, backend="cpu")

        if ready:
            before = corpus.cuda_calls
            on_gpu = list(corpus.similarities(query, threshold=0.4, backend="cuda"))
            assert on_gpu == hits
            assert corpus.cuda_calls > before  # the device completed the scan
            assert butina(corpus, threshold=0.4, backend="cuda") == clusters
            assert maxmin(corpus, count=3, backend="cuda") == picked

The program prints:

diazepam    1.000
nordazepam  0.528
temazepam   0.582
tetrazepam  0.542
clobazam    0.500
CUDA calls after the CPU scan: 0

The branch under if ready: runs only where backend="cuda" can be used; on any other machine the program prints the same lines.

docs.title: Keep work on the CPU
docs.text:
Three switches keep work on the CPU:

  • SMSD_DISABLE_GPU, set to any value other than an empty string or 0, disables every GPU route in the process. Prepared screens and pre-screens run on the CPU, "auto" uses the CPU and backend="cuda" raises. The variable is read at each call, so a program can set and remove it as it runs. It is the only switch for prepared screens.
  • gpu_prefilter=False, the default, keeps a corpus pre-screen on the CPU.
  • backend="cpu", the default, keeps a packed scan or clustering run on the CPU.
import os
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus

os.environ["SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"] = "1"
available = smsd.gpu_is_available()
print("GPU available:", available)
assert available is False
marked = smsd.gpu_device_info().endswith("[GPU disabled]")
print("backend string ends with [GPU disabled]:", marked)
assert marked

# Prepared screens and pre-screens run on the CPU with their usual results.
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(["CCO", "CCN", "c1ccccc1O"])
corpus.prewarm()
assert corpus.screen("CCO", 1.0) == [0]
search = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1O")
assert search.match_corpus(corpus, gpu_prefilter=True)[2].threshold_reached

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    with FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "bits.fp", [[1], [1, 2], [3]],
                                  fp_size=8) as packed:
        hits = list(packed.similarities([1], threshold=0.5, backend="auto"))
        print("auto:", hits, "| CUDA calls:", packed.cuda_calls)
        assert hits == [(0, 1.0), (1, 0.5)] and packed.cuda_calls == 0

# The variable is read at each call, so removing it allows the GPU again.
del os.environ["SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"]
marked = smsd.gpu_device_info().endswith("[GPU disabled]")
print("after removing the variable:", marked)
assert not marked

The program prints:

GPU available: False
backend string ends with [GPU disabled]: True
auto: [(0, 1.0), (1, 0.5)] | CUDA calls: 0
after removing the variable: False

docs.title: Fallback and errors
docs.text:
The routes treat a missing or failing device differently:

Route No usable device Error during device work Prepared screens, warm_start and the stream functions The CPU The CPU, silently, with the same hits match_corpus(..., gpu_prefilter=True) The CPU pre-screen The CPU pre-screen, with the same decisions Packed backend="auto" The CPU The error is raised Packed backend="cuda" RuntimeError The error is raised

The packed searches are generators. A backend="cuda" request that cannot be met raises when the first item is requested, not when the method is called, so keep the iteration inside the try block. The program below sets SMSD_DISABLE_GPU so that its output is the same on every machine.

import os
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus

# Make the device unusable, so that every machine prints the same lines.
os.environ["SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"] = "1"

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    with FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "bits.fp", [[1], [1, 2], [3]],
                                  fp_size=8) as corpus:
        pending = corpus.similarities([1], threshold=0.5, backend="cuda")
        print("the call returns a", type(pending).__name__)
        assert type(pending).__name__ == "generator"
        try:
            next(pending)
        except RuntimeError as error:
            message = str(error)
        else:
            raise AssertionError("backend='cuda' should fail without a device")
        print("first item:", message)
        assert message.endswith("CUDA screening is disabled by SMSD_DISABLE_GPU")

    # Fingerprints wider than 65,536 bits stay on the CPU under "auto".
    with FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "wide.fp", [[1], [70000]],
                                  fp_size=70001) as wide:
        hits = list(wide.similarities([70000], threshold=0.5, backend="auto"))
        print("auto, 70,001 bits:", hits)
        assert hits == [(1, 1.0)]
        try:
            list(wide.similarities([70000], threshold=0.5, backend="cuda"))
        except ValueError as error:
            message = str(error)
        else:
            raise AssertionError("backend='cuda' should refuse 70,001 bits")
        print("cuda, 70,001 bits:", message)
        assert message == "CUDA packed screening supports at most 65536 bits"

# Argument errors are raised at once, whatever the machine.
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(["CCO", "CCN"])
try:
    smsd.Substructure.find("CO").match_corpus(corpus, gpu_prefilter=1)
except TypeError as error:
    message = str(error)
print("gpu_prefilter=1:", message)
assert message == "GPU prefilter flag must be a bool"

The program prints:

the call returns a generator
first item: The requested CUDA packed-screening backend is unavailable: CUDA screening is disabled by SMSD_DISABLE_GPU
auto, 70,001 bits: [(1, 1.0)]
cuda, 70,001 bits: CUDA packed screening supports at most 65536 bits
gpu_prefilter=1: GPU prefilter flag must be a bool

The RuntimeError message gives the cause after the colon: No module named 'smsd_cuda' when the package is missing, smsd and smsd-cuda must have the same version for a version mismatch, no CUDA device was found, or a reason that names a device below compute capability 7.5. A backend value other than "cpu", "cuda" or "auto" raises ValueError.

If the installed smsd-cuda serves another version of smsd, the first call that looks for it issues one RuntimeWarning. The warning names both versions, asks for smsd-cuda==8.1.0 and says that screening runs on the CPU; prepared screens and pre-screens then stay on the CPU.

docs.title: Prove that the GPU ran
docs.text:
gpu_is_available() and gpu_device_info() report what is available, not what any call used. The only public evidence that work ran on the device is FingerprintCorpus.cuda_calls: the number of packed CUDA calls, including clustering passes, that the corpus has completed. Read it before and after a call, as the packed-index example does; an increase proves that the device ran. It is not a count of queries, hits or kernels, and it says nothing about speed.

Prepared screens and gpu_prefilter=True searches have no public counter and do not change cuda_calls. Their results are identical on either device, so compare results rather than devices.

docs.title: Time and compare CPU and GPU
docs.text:
Timings depend on the device, the processor, the corpus, the thread count and the load on the machine. Measure on the hardware and data that matter, and treat any figure as specific to that set-up. A fair comparison:

  • calls smsd_cuda.preload() first, so that device start-up is not timed;
  • prepares the corpus and runs each call once before timing, so that the first transfer to the device is not timed;
  • times with time.perf_counter() and keeps the best of several runs;
  • asserts that the GPU results equal the CPU results.

The harness below writes its timings to standard error and prints only results that agree on every machine. It holds the prepared screen on the CPU with SMSD_DISABLE_GPU, then allows the GPU for the 2,000-target corpus with SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS.

import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus

try:
    import smsd_cuda
except ImportError:
    smsd_cuda = None


def cuda_status():
    """Return whether backend="cuda" can be used here, and the reason when it cannot."""
    if os.environ.get("SMSD_DISABLE_GPU", "") not in ("", "0"):
        return False, "disabled by SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"
    if smsd_cuda is None:
        return False, "smsd-cuda is not installed"
    if smsd_cuda.__version__ != smsd.__version__:
        return False, (f"smsd-cuda {smsd_cuda.__version__} does not match "
                       f"smsd {smsd.__version__}")
    reason = smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason()
    return reason is None, reason


def timed(label, work, repeats=3):
    """Run once to warm up, then write the best of several timed runs to stderr."""
    result = work()
    best = float("inf")
    for _ in range(repeats):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        assert work() == result
        best = min(best, time.perf_counter() - started)
    print(f"{label}: {best:.4f} s", file=sys.stderr)
    return result


# Substituted rings with chains of 0 to 49 carbons: 5 x 8 x 50 = 2,000 molecules.
rings = ["c1ccccc1", "c1ccncc1", "C1CCCCC1", "c1ccoc1", "c1ccsc1"]
groups = ["O", "N", "Cl", "C(=O)O", "OC", "C#N", "F", "CC"]
library = [ring + group + "C" * length
           for ring in rings for group in groups for length in range(50)]
queries = ["c1ccccc1O", "c1ccncc1Cl", "C1CCCCC1C(=O)O"]
ready, reason = cuda_status()
if ready:
    smsd_cuda.preload()  # keep device start-up out of the timings

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library)
corpus.prewarm()
os.environ["SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"] = "1"
cpu_hits = timed("prepared screen, CPU", lambda: corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4))
del os.environ["SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"]
if ready:
    os.environ["SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS"] = str(len(library))
    gpu_hits = timed("prepared screen, GPU allowed",
                     lambda: corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4))
    assert gpu_hits == cpu_hits
counts = [len(found) for found in cpu_hits]
print("targets:", len(library), "| hits per query:", counts)
assert len(library) == 2000 and counts == [2, 9, 2]

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    with FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, library) as packed:
        probes = [packed.fingerprint(index) for index in (0, 450, 1600)]
        cpu_rows = timed("packed scan, CPU", lambda: list(
            packed.screen_many(probes, threshold=0.4, backend="cpu")))
        if ready:
            before = packed.cuda_calls
            gpu_rows = timed("packed scan, GPU", lambda: list(
                packed.screen_many(probes, threshold=0.4, backend="cuda")))
            assert gpu_rows == cpu_rows and packed.cuda_calls > before
        print("packed hits:", len(cpu_rows))
        assert len(cpu_rows) == 12

The program prints:

targets: 2000 | hits per query: [2, 9, 2]
packed hits: 12

A prepared screen gives no public record of the device it used, so the harness labels its second timing "GPU allowed". The packed timing is backed by the cuda_calls assertion.

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
The GPU image smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8 (linux/amd64) contains smsd, the matching smsd-cuda and the CUDA 12 runtime, with Python as its entry point. It has no Java command-line tool, no CUDA toolkit and no NumPy. As shipped, it supports prepared screens, warm_start, the stream functions and match_corpus(..., gpu_prefilter=True); packed indexes and clustering need NumPy added in an image built from it. The image needs the NVIDIA Container Toolkit and a compatible host driver, including under WSL2 on Windows.

After loading the image archive from the release:

docker run --rm --gpus all smsd:8.1.0-cuda12.8 \
  -c "import smsd; print(smsd.__version__); print(smsd.gpu_device_info())"

As elsewhere, the backend string shows availability, not use. Command line and containers describes the CPU images, and the installation guide covers loading and building every image.

docs.title: Metal and C++
docs.text: Python never screens on Metal, and the published wheels include neither Metal nor native CUDA support. A Python source build with Metal or CUDA switched on changes only what gpu_is_available() and gpu_device_info() report. In C++, a program built from source can link the Metal library and request Metal fingerprint screening explicitly; see Optional Metal fingerprint screening. Matching stays on the CPU there as well.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Name Used by Type Default Meaning gpu_prefilter Substructure.match_corpus, MCS.match_corpus bool False True asks an attached device to run the pre-screen; a value that is not a bool raises TypeError backend FingerprintCorpus.similarities, screen_many, threshold_pairs, top_k_pairs; butina, maxmin str "cpu" "cpu", "cuda" or "auto"; any other value raises ValueError num_threads TargetCorpus.prewarm, screen, screen_many; warm_start; the stream functions; match_corpus int 0 CPU threads; 0 uses the OpenMP default threshold warm_start float 0.0 Inclusive ECFP4 Tanimoto threshold; the default returns every target, so pass one Function or attribute Returns Meaning smsd.gpu_is_available() bool Whether a GPU backend is available smsd.gpu_device_info() str A description of the backend, such as CPU: ... or GPU: ... smsd.warm_start(corpus, query, threshold=0.0, *, num_threads=0) list[int] Prepares the corpus when needed and screens one query FingerprintCorpus.cuda_calls int Packed CUDA calls completed by this corpus smsd_cuda.is_available() bool Whether a device of compute capability 7.5 or later is present smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason() str or None Why no device can be used, or None smsd_cuda.device_info() str Device name, compute capability and memory; raises RuntimeError without a usable device smsd_cuda.preload() None Initialises the device and loads the screening kernels, without uploading data or changing automatic use smsd_cuda.__version__ str Must equal smsd.__version__ Limit Value Compute capability 7.5 or later Automatic device rule A Tesla T4 and 100,000 targets, unless SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS is set Packed fingerprint width on the GPU 65,536 bits; wider indexes use the CPU under "auto" and raise ValueError under "cuda" Queries in one packed screen_many call 32, on either device Byte order for packed GPU scans Little-endian host

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Effect SMSD_DISABLE_GPU Unset Unset, empty or 0 allows the GPU. Any other value keeps every route on the CPU and makes backend="cuda" raise. Read at each call. SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS Unset A positive whole number N, written in decimal digits only, lets automatic prepared screens use any supported device for corpora of N targets or more; on a Tesla T4 it replaces 100,000. Signs, spaces, exponents, 0 and values too large for 64 bits are ignored. Read at each screen. It does not affect gpu_prefilter or backend. OMP_NUM_THREADS Unset The CPU threads used when num_threads is 0; when unset, OpenMP chooses.

SMSD_CUDA_POOL and SMSD_CUDA_GRAPHS tune the device workspace; see Retained workspace and graph replay.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Graph matching never runs on the GPU. A GPU screens or pre-screens, and every reported match comes from a CPU search.
  • Prepared screens need prewarm() after construction and after every addition; without it, screen and screen_many return no hits rather than raising. warm_start prepares the corpus when needed. See Screening a library.
  • A prepared corpus keeps its fingerprints on the device between screens. Adding targets drops that copy, and the next screen transfers them again.
  • Results do not depend on the device or the thread count, and thresholds are inclusive on both devices.
  • cuda_calls counts packed calls only; it stays at 0 for CPU and fallback work.
  • The automatic rule is narrow by default, so a small demonstration corpus stays on the CPU unless SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS is set.
