docs.title: Fingerprints and similarity
docs.text:
SMSD computes hashed fingerprints, substructure-key fingerprints and the coefficients that compare them. A binary fingerprint is a sorted list of the positions of its set bits. A count fingerprint is a list of (position, count) pairs for the bins that are not zero. Both are plain Python lists, so they can be stored, compared and turned into arrays without any further package.

This chapter starts with one molecule, then covers each family, count fingerprints, configurable specifications, substructure keys, batch generation, the similarity coefficients, encodings and NumPy arrays. The Options section lists every signature with its defaults. Each Python block is a complete program: run it as it stands with SMSD 8.1.0 and it prints the output shown below it. The block under NumPy arrays also needs NumPy.

Compare fingerprints only when they were made with the same family, radius or path length, size and switches. Nothing in a fingerprint records how it was made, so a mismatch gives a meaningless score without an error.

docs.title: Fingerprint one molecule
docs.text:
smsd.fingerprint takes a SMILES string, an SMSD MolGraph or an RDKit molecule and returns the sorted set positions. The kind argument chooses the family. The default kind differs between entry points: fingerprint uses the labelled path fingerprint "mcs", while fingerprint_from_smiles uses ECFP. Name the kind, or pass a FingerprintOptions, whenever the fingerprints will be compared with others.

import smsd

aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # aspirin

default = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin)                  # kind="mcs"
from_smiles = smsd.fingerprint_from_smiles(aspirin)  # mode="ecfp"
ecfp4 = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, kind="ecfp")       # radius 2, 2048 bits

print("fingerprint() set bits:", len(default))
print("fingerprint_from_smiles() set bits:", len(from_smiles))
print("fingerprint_from_smiles() equals kind='ecfp':", from_smiles == ecfp4)
print("first five ECFP4 positions:", ecfp4[:5])
assert len(default) == 127 and default == smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, kind="mcs")
assert len(from_smiles) == 36 and from_smiles == ecfp4
assert ecfp4[:5] == [23, 44, 61, 101, 172]

The program prints:

fingerprint() set bits: 127
fingerprint_from_smiles() set bits: 36
fingerprint_from_smiles() equals kind='ecfp': True
first five ECFP4 positions: [23, 44, 61, 101, 172]

The default fingerprint of each entry point:

Entry point Default fingerprint fingerprint, fingerprints kind="mcs" smsd.adapters.fingerprints_numpy, fingerprints_torch kind="mcs" fingerprint_from_smiles mode="ecfp" FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles kind="ecfp" smsd.adapters.fingerprints_scipy, molecules_pandas, molecules_polars, FingerprintTransformer, SimilarityTransformer kind="ecfp" batch_similarity ECFP with radius=2 and fp_size=2048, both adjustable TargetCorpus.screen and screen_many, warm_start, stream_screen_smiles, stream_screen_many_smiles Fixed: binary ECFP, radius 2, 2,048 bits

docs.title: Families
docs.text:
Each kind has a fixed function that computes it from a parsed molecule:

Kind What it hashes Fixed function Fixed function takes SMILES "ecfp" (also "circular") Circular atom environments: element, degree, valence, formal charge, isotope, hydrogen count, tautomer class, aromaticity, bond order and ring membership circular_fingerprint(graph, radius, fp_size) No "fcfp" Circular environments of pharmacophore classes, with degree, bond order and ring membership circular_fingerprint(graph, radius, fp_size, mode="fcfp") No "path" Heavy-atom paths of up to path_length bonds, by atomic number only; bonds are not hashed path_fingerprint(graph, path_length, fp_size) No "mcs" Heavy-atom paths of up to path_length bonds, labelled by element, ring membership, aromaticity, tautomer class and degree, and by bond order, ring and aromatic flags mcs_fingerprint(graph, path_length, fp_size) No "torsion" Linear four-atom paths, typed by element, heavy-atom degree, pi electrons and ring membership topological_torsion(mol, fp_size) Yes keys Substructure keys, including the 166 MACCS keys; set through FingerprintOptions only fingerprint(mol, options=FingerprintOptions.maccs()) Yes

The functions that take a graph accept an SMSD MolGraph only, so pass smsd.parse_smiles(smiles); a SMILES string raises TypeError. fingerprint, fingerprints, fingerprint_from_smiles and topological_torsion also take SMILES strings and RDKit molecules. Each kind gives exactly the bits of its fixed function, and the classic FingerprintOptions of the ECFP, FCFP, path and torsion families give them again:

import smsd

aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # aspirin
graph = smsd.parse_smiles(aspirin)

fixed = {
    "ecfp": smsd.circular_fingerprint(graph, radius=2, fp_size=2048),
    "fcfp": smsd.circular_fingerprint(graph, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="fcfp"),
    "path": smsd.path_fingerprint(graph, path_length=7, fp_size=2048),
    "mcs": smsd.mcs_fingerprint(graph, path_length=7, fp_size=2048),
    "torsion": smsd.topological_torsion(graph, fp_size=2048),
}
classic = {
    "ecfp": smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(),
    "fcfp": smsd.FingerprintOptions.fcfp(),
    "path": smsd.FingerprintOptions.path(),
    "torsion": smsd.FingerprintOptions.torsion(),
}
for kind, bits in fixed.items():
    assert smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, kind=kind) == bits
    if kind in classic:
        assert smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=classic[kind]) == bits
    print(f"{kind:8} {len(bits):3d} set bits")
maccs = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs())
print(f"{'maccs':8} {len(maccs):3d} set bits")
assert [len(bits) for bits in fixed.values()] == [36, 29, 29, 127, 16]
assert len(maccs) == 21

try:
    smsd.circular_fingerprint(aspirin)
except TypeError:
    print("circular_fingerprint() needs a MolGraph")
else:
    raise AssertionError("a SMILES string was accepted")

try:
    smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, kind="maccs")
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)
    assert str(error).startswith("Unknown fingerprint kind: 'maccs'")
else:
    raise AssertionError("an unknown kind was accepted")

The program prints:

ecfp      36 set bits
fcfp      29 set bits
path      29 set bits
mcs      127 set bits
torsion   16 set bits
maccs     21 set bits
circular_fingerprint() needs a MolGraph
Unknown fingerprint kind: 'maccs'. Use 'path', 'mcs', 'ecfp', 'circular', 'fcfp', or 'torsion'.

MACCS keys are not a kind; they come from FingerprintOptions.maccs(), as shown under Substructure keys and MACCS.

The FCFP pharmacophore class of each atom is available on its own. classify_pharmacophore(graph, atom_index) returns a bit mask: 1 for a hydrogen-bond donor, 2 for an acceptor, 4 for a positive ionisable atom, 8 for a negative ionisable atom, 16 for an aromatic atom and 32 for a hydrophobic atom.

import smsd

paracetamol = smsd.parse_smiles("CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1")  # paracetamol
classes = [smsd.classify_pharmacophore(paracetamol, atom)
           for atom in range(paracetamol.n)]
print(classes)
assert classes == [32, 0, 2, 3, 16, 16, 16, 16, 3, 16, 16]

The program prints:

[32, 0, 2, 3, 16, 16, 16, 16, 3, 16, 16]

docs.title: Count fingerprints
docs.text:
A count fingerprint records how often each folded bin is hit. Its positions are the set positions of the binary fingerprint of the same specification. circular_fingerprint_counts and topological_torsion_counts compute counts from a graph; for any family, FingerprintOptions(..., counts=True) does the same through fingerprint and fingerprints.

import smsd

hexane = smsd.parse_smiles("CCCCCC")  # hexane
counts = smsd.circular_fingerprint_counts(hexane, radius=2, fp_size=2048)
print("ECFP4 counts:", counts)
assert len(counts) == 8 and counts[0] == (592, 2) and counts[-1] == (1861, 4)
assert [position for position, _ in counts] == smsd.circular_fingerprint(hexane)
counted = smsd.FingerprintOptions("ecfp", counts=True)
assert smsd.fingerprint("CCCCCC", options=counted) == counts

path = smsd.FingerprintOptions("path", counts=True)
path_counts = smsd.fingerprint("CCCCCC", options=path)
print("path counts:", path_counts)
assert all(count == 1 for _, count in path_counts)

aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # aspirin
maccs = smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs()
bits = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=maccs)
maccs.counts = True
key_counts = dict(smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=maccs))
print("MACCS key 125 count:", key_counts[124], "| bit set:", 124 in bits)
assert key_counts[124] == 1 and 124 not in bits

The program prints:

ECFP4 counts: [(592, 2), (906, 2), (1015, 2), (1147, 2), (1512, 2), (1702, 2), (1828, 2), (1861, 4)]
path counts: [(145, 1), (273, 1), (277, 1), (401, 1), (405, 1), (533, 1)]
MACCS key 125 count: 1 | bit set: False

Path counts are always 1. Key counts are the raw number of matches and do not apply a key's minimum: MACCS key 125 needs two aromatic rings, so aspirin reports a count of 1 for it while the binary bit stays clear.

docs.title: Configurable fingerprints
docs.text:
FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", **switches) describes a fingerprint completely. It starts from the classic configuration of the family, which gives the bits of the fixed function, and each keyword then switches a hashed term on or off. The class methods ecfp, fcfp, path, torsion and maccs build the classic configurations. Pass the value as options to fingerprint, fingerprints, fingerprint_from_smiles, FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles or the NumPy, PyTorch, SciPy, pandas and Polars adapters; the same options give the same bits in C++ and Java.

Stereo and ring terms are off in the classic configurations:

import smsd

fcfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.fcfp()
print(fcfp4)
assert repr(fcfp4).endswith("terms=[degree, bond_order, ring_membership])")

first, second = "C[C@H](N)C(=O)O", "C[C@@H](N)C(=O)O"  # alanine enantiomers
classic = smsd.FingerprintOptions()
stereo = smsd.FingerprintOptions(cip_atoms=True)
same = smsd.fingerprint(first, options=classic) == smsd.fingerprint(
    second, options=classic)
apart = smsd.fingerprint(first, options=stereo) != smsd.fingerprint(
    second, options=stereo)
print("classic ECFP4 separates the enantiomers:", not same)
print("cip_atoms separates them:", apart)
assert same and apart

e_butene, z_butene = "C/C=C/C", "C/C=C\\C"  # E- and Z-2-butene
geometry = smsd.FingerprintOptions(cip_bonds=True)
apart = smsd.fingerprint(e_butene, options=geometry) != smsd.fingerprint(
    z_butene, options=geometry)
print("cip_bonds separates E and Z:", apart)
assert apart

cyclohexane = "C1CCCCC1"  # cyclohexane
ring = smsd.FingerprintOptions(ring_size=True)
changed = smsd.fingerprint(cyclohexane, options=ring) != smsd.fingerprint(
    cyclohexane, options=classic)
print("ring_size changes the bits:", changed)
assert changed

The program prints:

FingerprintOptions(family='fcfp', size=2048, radius=2, terms=[degree, bond_order, ring_membership])
classic ECFP4 separates the enantiomers: False
cip_atoms separates them: True
cip_bonds separates E and Z: True
ring_size changes the bits: True

The scaffold, fragments and radius keywords change what part of the molecule is fingerprinted. scaffold="murcko" fingerprints the ring framework with its linkers. fragments="largest" keeps the component with the most heavy atoms, which removes counter-ions, and "per_fragment" tags each atom term with its component. A radius of -1 grows each environment to the whole component.

import smsd

ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions()

murcko = smsd.FingerprintOptions(scaffold="murcko")
toluene = smsd.fingerprint("Cc1ccccc1", options=murcko)  # toluene
benzene = smsd.fingerprint("c1ccccc1", options=ecfp4)    # benzene
print("Murcko framework of toluene equals benzene:", toluene == benzene)
assert toluene == benzene

salt = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O.[Na+].[Cl-]"  # aspirin with sodium chloride
parent = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=ecfp4)  # aspirin
whole = smsd.fingerprint(salt, options=ecfp4)
largest = smsd.fingerprint(salt, options=smsd.FingerprintOptions(fragments="largest"))
print("whole salt equals aspirin:", whole == parent)
print("largest fragment equals aspirin:", largest == parent)
assert whole != parent and largest == parent

decane = "CCCCCCCCCC"  # decane
full = smsd.fingerprint(decane, options=smsd.FingerprintOptions(radius=-1))
print("decane set bits, radius -1 and radius 2:",
      len(full), len(smsd.fingerprint(decane, options=ecfp4)))
assert len(full) == 44 and len(smsd.fingerprint(decane, options=ecfp4)) == 9

The program prints:

Murcko framework of toluene equals benzene: True
whole salt equals aspirin: False
largest fragment equals aspirin: True
decane set bits, radius -1 and radius 2: 44 9

Assigning family after construction keeps the current switches, so ECFP options changed to "fcfp" are not classic FCFP; build FingerprintOptions("fcfp") or FingerprintOptions.fcfp() instead. Switch values must be True or False, and an unknown keyword raises TypeError. Values that are out of range raise ValueError when the fingerprint is computed. Some messages use the C++ field names, such as ringSizeCap for ring_size_cap and pathLength for path_length.

import smsd

aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # aspirin
changed = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp()
changed.family = "fcfp"  # keeps the ECFP switches
classic = smsd.FingerprintOptions.fcfp()
same = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=changed) == smsd.fingerprint(
    aspirin, options=classic)
print("assigned family gives classic FCFP:", same)
assert not same

expected = {
    "radius=-2": "radius must be >= -1 (use -1 for unlimited)",
    "ring_size_cap=2": "ringSizeCap must be at least 3",
}
cases = {
    "radius=-2": smsd.FingerprintOptions(radius=-2),
    "ring_size_cap=2": smsd.FingerprintOptions(ring_size=True, ring_size_cap=2),
}
for label, options in cases.items():
    try:
        smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=options)
    except ValueError as error:
        print(f"{label}: {error}")
        assert str(error) == expected[label]
    else:
        raise AssertionError(f"{label} was accepted")

try:
    smsd.FingerprintOptions(element=1)
except TypeError as error:
    print(f"element=1: {error}")
    assert str(error) == "element must be True or False"
else:
    raise AssertionError("a non-boolean switch was accepted")

The program prints:

assigned family gives classic FCFP: False
radius=-2: radius must be >= -1 (use -1 for unlimited)
ring_size_cap=2: ringSizeCap must be at least 3
element=1: element must be True or False

docs.title: Substructure keys and MACCS
docs.text:
The "keys" family sets one bit per substructure key, in the order given. A key is a SMARTS string, a (smarts, minimum) pair or a FingerprintKey(smarts, minimum=1); its bit is set when at least minimum distinct atom sets match. The size of a key fingerprint is the number of keys.

FingerprintOptions.maccs() gives the 166 MACCS keys. Key k is at position k − 1, so add 1 to a position to read the key number. maccs_keys() lists the definitions as FingerprintKey values with smarts, minimum and kind; kind is "smarts" for most keys and "isotope", "aromatic_rings" or "fragments" for the few keys that count something else.

import smsd

keys = smsd.FingerprintOptions("keys", keys=[
    "[#8]",                                   # key 0: an oxygen atom
    ("[#8]", 3),                              # key 1: three or more oxygens
    smsd.FingerprintKey("c1ccccc1"),          # key 2: a benzene ring
    smsd.FingerprintKey("[NX3]", minimum=2),  # key 3: two trivalent nitrogens or more
])
aspirin = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=keys)  # aspirin
paracetamol = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1", options=keys)  # paracetamol
print("size:", keys.size)
print("aspirin:", aspirin)
print("paracetamol:", paracetamol)
assert keys.size == 4 and aspirin == [0, 1, 2] and paracetamol == [0, 2]

maccs = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
                         options=smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs())
key_numbers = [position + 1 for position in maccs]
print("MACCS keys set for aspirin:", key_numbers)
assert len(smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs_keys()) == 166
assert len(key_numbers) == 21
assert key_numbers[:3] == [89, 113, 123] and key_numbers[-1] == 165

The program prints:

size: 4
aspirin: [0, 1, 2]
paracetamol: [0, 2]
MACCS keys set for aspirin: [89, 113, 123, 126, 127, 136, 139, 140, 143, 144, 146, 150, 152, 154, 157, 159, 160, 162, 163, 164, 165]

Each key search has fixed time and embedding limits. A key that cannot be decided within them raises RuntimeError instead of returning a bit that could depend on the machine.

docs.title: Many molecules at once
docs.text:
fingerprints(mols, ...) computes the fingerprint of every molecule in one native call. It takes the same kind, path_length, fp_size, radius and options arguments as fingerprint, and returns the results in input order. The results equal one-at-a-time results whatever the thread count. num_threads=0 uses the OpenMP default, which OMP_NUM_THREADS controls. The input may mix SMILES strings, MolGraph objects and RDKit molecules.

import smsd

names = ["aspirin", "salicylic acid", "paracetamol", "ibuprofen", "naproxen",
         "caffeine", "phenol"]
library = ["CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
           "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O", "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
           "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C", "Oc1ccccc1"]
ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)

batch = smsd.fingerprints(library, options=ecfp4, num_threads=2)
assert batch == [smsd.fingerprint(smiles, options=ecfp4) for smiles in library]
assert batch == smsd.fingerprints(library, options=ecfp4, num_threads=1)
mixed = [library[0], smsd.parse_smiles(library[1])]
assert smsd.fingerprints(mixed, options=ecfp4) == batch[:2]

for name, bits in zip(names, batch):
    print(f"{name:15} {len(bits):3d} set bits")
assert [len(bits) for bits in batch] == [36, 28, 24, 32, 46, 33, 14]

try:
    smsd.fingerprints(["CCO", "C1CC"], options=ecfp4)
except ValueError as error:
    print("ValueError:", error)
    assert str(error) == "Unclosed ring(s): 1"
else:
    raise AssertionError("an invalid SMILES string was accepted")

The program prints:

aspirin          36 set bits
salicylic acid   28 set bits
paracetamol      24 set bits
ibuprofen        32 set bits
naproxen         46 set bits
caffeine         33 set bits
phenol           14 set bits
ValueError: Unclosed ring(s): 1

The first molecule that fails raises its own error, as fingerprint would. A parse error does not name the input position; a ring-perception or key-search refusal adds the zero-based input index to its message.

docs.title: Similarity coefficients
docs.text:
The binary coefficients compare set positions A and B:

  • tanimoto_coefficient: |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|.
  • dice: 2|A ∩ B| / (|A| + |B|).
  • cosine: |A ∩ B| / √(|A| |B|).
  • overlap_coefficient: |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|), which is 1.0 when one fingerprint is contained in the other.
  • soergel: 1 − Tanimoto, a distance rather than a similarity.

dice, cosine and soergel take the fingerprint width as fp_size (default 2048) and ignore positions at or above it; always pass the real width. tanimoto_coefficient and overlap_coefficient do not read fp_size.

import smsd

ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
a = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=ecfp4)  # aspirin
b = smsd.fingerprint("OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", options=ecfp4)        # salicylic acid
print("set bits:", len(a), len(b), "| in common:", len(set(a) & set(b)))
assert (len(a), len(b), len(set(a) & set(b))) == (36, 28, 10)

scores = {
    "tanimoto_coefficient": smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(a, b),
    "dice": smsd.dice(a, b, fp_size=2048),
    "cosine": smsd.cosine(a, b, fp_size=2048),
    "overlap_coefficient": smsd.overlap_coefficient(a, b),
    "soergel": smsd.soergel(a, b, fp_size=2048),
}
for name, score in scores.items():
    print(f"{name:21} {score:.3f}")
rounded = [round(score, 3) for score in scores.values()]
assert rounded == [0.185, 0.312, 0.315, 0.357, 0.815]

The program prints:

set bits: 36 28 | in common: 10
tanimoto_coefficient  0.185
dice                  0.312
cosine                0.315
overlap_coefficient   0.357
soergel               0.815

The count coefficients compare count fingerprints a and b position by position:

  • count_tanimoto_coefficient: Σ min(a, b) / Σ max(a, b).
  • count_dice: 2 Σ min(a, b) / (Σ a + Σ b).
  • count_cosine: Σ ab / (√Σ a² √Σ b²).
  • count_overlap_coefficient: Σ min(a, b) / min(Σ a, Σ b).

Pass (position, count) pairs, as count fingerprints are returned. count_dice and count_cosine also take dense lists of equal length or {position: count} dictionaries. count_tanimoto_coefficient and count_overlap_coefficient read a dictionary by its keys only, as positions with a count of 1. The binary tanimoto_coefficient accepts count pairs but compares their positions only.

import smsd

counted = smsd.FingerprintOptions("ecfp", counts=True)
a = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=counted)  # aspirin
b = smsd.fingerprint("OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", options=counted)        # salicylic acid
scores = {
    "count_tanimoto_coefficient": smsd.count_tanimoto_coefficient(a, b),
    "count_dice": smsd.count_dice(a, b),
    "count_cosine": smsd.count_cosine(a, b),
    "count_overlap_coefficient": smsd.count_overlap_coefficient(a, b),
    "tanimoto_coefficient": smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(a, b),  # positions only
}
for name, score in scores.items():
    print(f"{name:27} {score:.3f}")
rounded = [round(score, 3) for score in scores.values()]
assert rounded == [0.211, 0.348, 0.462, 0.4, 0.185]

pairs = smsd.count_tanimoto_coefficient([(1, 2)], [(1, 1)])
mapping = smsd.count_tanimoto_coefficient({1: 2}, {1: 1})  # keys only
print("pairs:", pairs, "| dictionaries:", mapping)
assert pairs == 0.5 and mapping == 1.0

The program prints:

count_tanimoto_coefficient  0.211
count_dice                  0.348
count_cosine                0.462
count_overlap_coefficient   0.400
tanimoto_coefficient        0.185
pairs: 0.5 | dictionaries: 1.0

The width matters for dice, cosine and soergel. With 4,096-bit fingerprints, the default fp_size=2048 drops every position from 2,048 upwards and gives a different score without an error:

import smsd

wide = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=4096)
a = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", options=wide)  # aspirin
b = smsd.fingerprint("OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", options=wide)        # salicylic acid
right = smsd.dice(a, b, fp_size=4096)
wrong = smsd.dice(a, b)  # reads positions below 2048 only
print(f"dice with fp_size=4096: {right:.3f}")
print(f"dice with the default:  {wrong:.3f}")
assert round(right, 3) == 0.312 and round(wrong, 3) == 0.333
assert smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(a, b) == smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(
    a, b, fp_size=4096)

The program prints:

dice with fp_size=4096: 0.312
dice with the default:  0.333

SMSD has no Tversky function. The asymmetric Tversky index is a few lines over the set positions; with both weights 1 it equals Tanimoto, and with both weights 0.5 it equals Dice.

import smsd


def tversky(query, target, alpha=0.9, beta=0.1):
    q, t = set(query), set(target)
    common = len(q & t)
    denominator = common + alpha * len(q - t) + beta * len(t - q)
    return 1.0 if denominator == 0 else common / denominator


ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp()
phenol = smsd.fingerprint("Oc1ccccc1", options=ecfp4)                # phenol
paracetamol = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1", options=ecfp4)  # paracetamol
forward = tversky(phenol, paracetamol)
reverse = tversky(paracetamol, phenol)
print(f"phenol in paracetamol: {forward:.3f}")
print(f"paracetamol in phenol: {reverse:.3f}")
assert round(forward, 3) == 0.533 and round(reverse, 3) == 0.348
tanimoto = smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(phenol, paracetamol)
assert abs(tversky(phenol, paracetamol, 1, 1) - tanimoto) < 1e-12
dice = smsd.dice(phenol, paracetamol, fp_size=2048)
assert abs(tversky(phenol, paracetamol, 0.5, 0.5) - dice) < 1e-12

The program prints:

phenol in paracetamol: 0.533
paracetamol in phenol: 0.348

smsd.similarity(mol1, mol2) is not a fingerprint score. It is the same as similarity_upper_bound: an upper bound on the atom-count similarity of the maximum common substructure, described under MCS similarity.

import smsd

phenol, aspirin = "Oc1ccccc1", "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # phenol, aspirin
bound = smsd.similarity(phenol, aspirin)
ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp()
tanimoto = smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(smsd.fingerprint(phenol, options=ecfp4),
                                     smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=ecfp4))
print(f"smsd.similarity: {bound:.3f}")
print(f"ECFP4 Tanimoto:  {tanimoto:.3f}")
assert bound == smsd.similarity_upper_bound(phenol, aspirin)
assert round(bound, 3) == 0.538 and round(tanimoto, 3) == 0.020

The program prints:

smsd.similarity: 0.538
ECFP4 Tanimoto:  0.020

docs.title: Empty fingerprints
docs.text:
A molecule can have an empty fingerprint: methanol and ethanol, for example, have no four-atom torsion. The coefficients treat empty input as follows:

Coefficient Both empty One empty tanimoto_coefficient 1.0 0.0 overlap_coefficient 1.0 0.0 dice 0.0 0.0 cosine 0.0 0.0 soergel 0.0 1.0 count_tanimoto_coefficient, count_overlap_coefficient, count_dice, count_cosine 0.0 0.0

tanimoto_coefficient also returns 0.0 when either argument is None.

import smsd

rules = [
    ("tanimoto_coefficient", smsd.tanimoto_coefficient, [1], 1.0, 0.0),
    ("overlap_coefficient", smsd.overlap_coefficient, [1], 1.0, 0.0),
    ("dice", smsd.dice, [1], 0.0, 0.0),
    ("cosine", smsd.cosine, [1], 0.0, 0.0),
    ("soergel", smsd.soergel, [1], 0.0, 1.0),
    ("count_tanimoto_coefficient", smsd.count_tanimoto_coefficient,
     [(1, 1)], 0.0, 0.0),
    ("count_overlap_coefficient", smsd.count_overlap_coefficient,
     [(1, 1)], 0.0, 0.0),
    ("count_dice", smsd.count_dice, [(1, 1)], 0.0, 0.0),
    ("count_cosine", smsd.count_cosine, [(1, 1)], 0.0, 0.0),
]
for name, metric, one, both_empty, one_empty in rules:
    print(f"{name:27} {metric([], []):.1f} {metric([], one):.1f}")
    assert metric([], []) == both_empty and metric([], one) == one_empty

methanol = smsd.topological_torsion("CO")  # methanol
ethanol = smsd.topological_torsion("CCO")  # ethanol
score = smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(methanol, ethanol)
print("torsion bits:", methanol, ethanol, "| Tanimoto:", score)
assert methanol == [] and ethanol == [] and score == 1.0

The program prints:

tanimoto_coefficient        1.0 0.0
overlap_coefficient         1.0 0.0
dice                        0.0 0.0
cosine                      0.0 0.0
soergel                     0.0 1.0
count_tanimoto_coefficient  0.0 0.0
count_overlap_coefficient   0.0 0.0
count_dice                  0.0 0.0
count_cosine                0.0 0.0
torsion bits: [] [] | Tanimoto: 1.0

Two molecules too small for a family therefore score 1.0 by Tanimoto. Filter empty fingerprints out before ranking when that matters.

docs.title: Ranking a small set
docs.text:
batch_similarity(query, targets, fp_size=2048, radius=2) fingerprints the query and each target with ECFP of the given radius and width, and returns (index, Tanimoto) pairs from most to least similar. Targets with equal scores keep their input order. For other families, or for libraries that are screened repeatedly, see Similarity screen in memory and the packed fingerprint index.

import smsd

query = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # aspirin
library = [
    "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",               # salicylic acid
    "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",            # paracetamol
    "c1ccccc1",                      # benzene
    "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1",               # phenyl acetate
    "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)OC",        # methyl acetylsalicylate
    "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",  # caffeine
    "OC(=O)c1ccccc1",                # benzoic acid
]
ranking = smsd.batch_similarity(query, library, fp_size=2048, radius=2)
for index, score in ranking[:3]:
    print(f"{score:.3f} {library[index]}")
top = [(index, round(score, 3)) for index, score in ranking[:3]]
assert top == [(4, 0.63), (3, 0.439), (6, 0.256)]

ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
q = smsd.fingerprint(query, options=ecfp4)
scores = [smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(q, t)
          for t in smsd.fingerprints(library, options=ecfp4)]
by_hand = sorted(enumerate(scores), key=lambda pair: -pair[1])
assert by_hand == ranking

The program prints:

0.630 CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)OC
0.439 CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1
0.256 OC(=O)c1ccccc1

docs.title: Encodings
docs.text:
to_hex(fp, fp_size) writes a binary fingerprint as hexadecimal text and from_hex(text) reads it back. The text holds the fingerprint in 64-bit words in ascending order, each written as 16 lower-case hexadecimal digits with the most significant digit first, so bit 0 is the last digit of the first word. A width that is not a multiple of 64 is padded to whole words. from_hex also accepts upper case. This layout is not the byte layout of a packed fingerprint file.

to_binary_string(fp, fp_size) writes one character per bit, character i being bit i. counts_to_array(counts, fp_size) turns (position, count) pairs or a {position: count} dictionary into a dense list, ignoring positions outside the width.

import smsd

phenol = smsd.fingerprint("Oc1ccccc1", kind="ecfp")  # phenol
text = smsd.to_hex(phenol, fp_size=2048)
print("hex characters:", len(text))
print("round trip:", smsd.from_hex(text) == phenol)
assert len(text) == 512 and smsd.from_hex(text) == phenol

for positions, width in (([0], 64), ([63], 64), ([0], 8)):
    print(f"to_hex({positions}, {width}):", smsd.to_hex(positions, fp_size=width))
assert smsd.to_hex([0], fp_size=64) == "0000000000000001"
assert smsd.to_hex([63], fp_size=64) == "8000000000000000"
assert smsd.to_hex([0], fp_size=8) == "0000000000000001"
assert smsd.from_hex("8000000000000000".upper()) == [63]

bits = smsd.to_binary_string([0, 3], fp_size=8)
print("to_binary_string([0, 3], 8):", bits)
assert bits == "10010000"

dense = smsd.counts_to_array([(1, 2), (9, 5)], 4)
print("counts_to_array([(1, 2), (9, 5)], 4):", dense)
assert dense == [0, 2, 0, 0]

try:
    smsd.from_hex("0x01")
except ValueError as error:
    print("ValueError:", error)
    assert str(error) == "hex_str must contain only hexadecimal digits"
else:
    raise AssertionError("non-hexadecimal text was accepted")

The program prints:

hex characters: 512
round trip: True
to_hex([0], 64): 0000000000000001
to_hex([63], 64): 8000000000000000
to_hex([0], 8): 0000000000000001
to_binary_string([0, 3], 8): 10010000
counts_to_array([(1, 2), (9, 5)], 4): [0, 2, 0, 0]
ValueError: hex_str must contain only hexadecimal digits

docs.title: NumPy arrays
docs.text:
A fingerprint becomes a NumPy row by setting the listed positions to 1. smsd.adapters.fingerprints_numpy(molecules, ...) builds the whole matrix natively: one row per molecule, uint8 for bits and int64 for counts. Like fingerprints, it defaults to kind="mcs", so pass the kind or the options. A Tanimoto matrix then follows from one matrix product. These functions need NumPy (python -m pip install "smsd[numpy]==8.1.0").

import numpy as np
import smsd
from smsd.adapters import fingerprints_numpy

names = ["aspirin", "salicylic acid", "paracetamol", "phenol"]
smiles = ["CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O", "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
          "Oc1ccccc1"]
ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)

fps = smsd.fingerprints(smiles, options=ecfp4)
by_hand = np.zeros((len(fps), 2048), dtype=np.uint8)
for row, positions in enumerate(fps):
    by_hand[row, positions] = 1

matrix = fingerprints_numpy(smiles, options=ecfp4)
print("shape:", matrix.shape, "| dtype:", matrix.dtype)
assert matrix.shape == (4, 2048) and matrix.dtype == np.uint8
assert (matrix == by_hand).all()

a = matrix.astype(np.int32)
common = a @ a.T
sizes = a.sum(axis=1)
tanimoto = common / (sizes[:, None] + sizes[None, :] - common)
expected = [[smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(p, q) for q in fps] for p in fps]
assert np.allclose(tanimoto, expected)
for name, row in zip(names, tanimoto.round(3).tolist()):
    print(f"{name:15}", row)
assert tanimoto.round(3).tolist()[0] == [1.0, 0.185, 0.034, 0.02]

The program prints:

shape: (4, 2048) | dtype: uint8
aspirin         [1.0, 0.185, 0.034, 0.02]
salicylic acid  [0.185, 1.0, 0.13, 0.273]
paracetamol     [0.034, 0.13, 1.0, 0.267]
phenol          [0.02, 0.273, 0.267, 1.0]

SciPy sparse matrices, pandas and Polars columns, Arrow buffers, PyTorch tensors and scikit-learn transformers are covered in the Python feature adapters page.

docs.title: Fingerprint quality
docs.text:
analyze_fp_quality(fp, fp_size=2048) reports how full a binary fingerprint is: set_bits, fp_size, density, expected_collision_rate (the estimated share of hashed features that fell on a bit already set) and is_saturated (density above 0.75). A saturated fingerprint has lost most of its ability to separate molecules; use a larger width or a shorter path length.

import smsd

diazepam = "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21"  # diazepam
for size in (2048, 256, 64):
    bits = smsd.fingerprint(diazepam, kind="mcs", fp_size=size)
    quality = smsd.analyze_fp_quality(bits, fp_size=size)
    row = (quality["set_bits"], round(quality["density"], 3),
           round(quality["expected_collision_rate"], 3), quality["is_saturated"])
    print(f"fp_size {size}: set {row[0]}, density {row[1]}, "
          f"collision rate {row[2]}, saturated {row[3]}")
    assert row == {2048: (297, 0.145, 0.074, False),
                   256: (182, 0.711, 0.426, False),
                   64: (64, 1.0, 1.0, True)}[size]

The program prints:

fp_size 2048: set 297, density 0.145, collision rate 0.074, saturated False
fp_size 256: set 182, density 0.711, collision rate 0.426, saturated False
fp_size 64: set 64, density 1.0, collision rate 1.0, saturated True

fingerprint_subset(fp1, fp2) is true when every position of fp1 is set in fp2. Both lists must be sorted; unsorted input gives a wrong answer without an error. It compares two sets of positions and is not a substructure test: with the similarity fingerprints, a target that contains the query can fail it, and a target that passes it need not contain the query.

import smsd

ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
query = smsd.fingerprint("Oc1ccccc1", options=ecfp4)          # phenol
search = smsd.Substructure.find("Oc1ccccc1")
rows = []
for name, smiles in (("paracetamol", "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1"),   # paracetamol
                     ("caffeine", "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C")):  # caffeine
    subset = smsd.fingerprint_subset(query, smsd.fingerprint(smiles, options=ecfp4))
    found = search.match(smiles).found
    print(f"{name:12} ECFP4 subset {subset}, contains phenol {found}")
    rows.append((subset, found))
assert rows == [(False, True), (False, False)]
assert smsd.fingerprint_subset([1, 5], [1, 2, 5]) and not smsd.fingerprint_subset([1, 6], [1, 2, 5])

The program prints:

paracetamol  ECFP4 subset False, contains phenol True
caffeine     ECFP4 subset False, contains phenol False

For substructure screening of a library, use Substructure.match_corpus (see Search a prepared corpus), which rules out targets that cannot contain the query before matching, with a proof.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Fingerprint functions, with their defaults. "Graph" means an SMSD MolGraph only; "molecule" means a SMILES string, a MolGraph or an RDKit molecule.

Function Takes Returns fingerprint(mol, *, kind="mcs", path_length=7, fp_size=2048, radius=2, options=None) molecule Sorted positions, or (position, count) pairs when options.counts is true fingerprints(mols, *, kind="mcs", path_length=7, fp_size=2048, radius=2, options=None, num_threads=0) iterable of molecules One fingerprint per molecule, in input order fingerprint_from_smiles(smiles, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="ecfp", *, path_length=7, options=None) non-empty SMILES string As fingerprint circular_fingerprint(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="ecfp") graph Sorted positions; mode is "ecfp" or "fcfp" circular_fingerprint_counts(mol, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="ecfp") graph (position, count) pairs path_fingerprint(mol, path_length=7, fp_size=2048) graph Sorted positions mcs_fingerprint(mol, path_length=7, fp_size=2048, tautomer_aware=False) graph Sorted positions; tautomer_aware hashes atoms of a tautomeric group without their element and tautomer class topological_torsion(mol, fp_size=2048) molecule Sorted positions topological_torsion_counts(mol, fp_size=2048) graph (position, count) pairs classify_pharmacophore(mol, atom_index) graph Pharmacophore class bit mask of one atom tanimoto_coefficient(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048), overlap_coefficient(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048) positions or pairs float; fp_size is not read dice(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048), cosine(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048), soergel(fp1, fp2, fp_size=2048) positions float; positions at or above fp_size are ignored count_tanimoto_coefficient(fp1, fp2), count_overlap_coefficient(fp1, fp2) pairs or positions float count_dice(fp1, fp2), count_cosine(fp1, fp2) pairs, dictionaries or dense lists float; dense lists of unequal length give 0.0 batch_similarity(query, targets, fp_size=2048, radius=2) molecules (index, Tanimoto) pairs, most similar first to_hex(fp, fp_size=2048), from_hex(hex_str) positions; text Text; sorted positions to_binary_string(fp, fp_size=2048) positions Text of fp_size characters counts_to_array(counts_dict, fp_size) pairs or dictionary Dense list of length fp_size fingerprint_subset(fp1, fp2) sorted positions bool analyze_fp_quality(fp, fp_size=2048) positions dict smsd.adapters.fingerprints_numpy(molecules, *, kind="mcs", path_length=7, fp_size=2048, radius=2, options=None, num_threads=0, dtype=None) molecules NumPy matrix

When options is given, it defines the fingerprint completely and kind, path_length, fp_size and radius are not read. fp_size and path_length must be at least 1, and num_threads must not be negative. With kind, a radius of -1 means the whole component and a more negative radius is treated as -1, while FingerprintOptions raises ValueError for it.

FingerprintOptions(family="ecfp", **keywords) takes the family "ecfp" (or "circular"), "fcfp", "path", "torsion" or "keys", as a string in any case or as a FingerprintFamily value. The keywords, with their defaults for the classic ECFP, FCFP, path and torsion configurations (a dash marks a value the family does not read):

Keyword Type ECFP FCFP Path Torsion Meaning radius int 2 2 – – Circular radius; 2 gives ECFP4 or FCFP4, -1 the whole component path_length int – – 7 – Longest path, in bonds size int 2048 2048 2048 2048 Bits or bins; for keys, the number of keys counts bool False False False False Return (position, count) pairs element bool True False True True Atomic number degree bool True True False True Number of explicit neighbours valence bool True False False True Bond order sum; pi electrons for torsion formal_charge, isotope, hydrogen_count, tautomer_class, aromaticity bool True False False False The named atom property bond_order bool True True False False Bond order of neighbour or path bonds aromatic_bond, ring_bond bool False False False False Aromatic and ring flags of bonds ring_membership bool True True False True Whether the atom is in a ring ring_size bool False False False False Smallest ring through the atom ring_size_cap int 8 8 8 8 Rings of this size or more share a class; at least 3 cip_atoms bool False False False False R/S (and r/s) labels of stereocentres cip_bonds bool False False False False E/Z labels of double bonds fragments str or FragmentMode "whole" "whole" "whole" "whole" "whole", "largest" or "per_fragment" scaffold str or ScaffoldMode "none" "none" "none" "none" "none" or "murcko" keys sequence [] [] [] [] Keys of the "keys" family: SMARTS strings, (smarts, minimum) pairs or FingerprintKey values

Every keyword is also a readable and writable attribute, and copy() returns an independent copy. The class methods are ecfp(radius=2, size=2048), fcfp(radius=2, size=2048), path(path_length=7, size=2048), torsion(size=2048), maccs() and maccs_keys(). FingerprintKey(smarts, minimum=1) has the read-only attributes smarts, minimum and kind.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• FingerprintOptions calls the width size; the functions call it fp_size.
  • The FCFP pharmacophore class is always hashed and is not listed among the terms in the repr.
  • Stereo terms use whole-molecule CIP labels. Radius 0 does not separate stereoisomers, and double bonds in rings of fewer than eight atoms carry no E/Z term.
  • A whole-molecule fingerprint includes counter-ions and solvent; use fragments="largest" to fingerprint the parent.
  • mcs_fingerprint is not configurable through FingerprintOptions.
  • Ring-size terms, double-bond stereo terms, aromatic-ring keys and some SMARTS keys need a complete ring basis. When ring perception cannot complete it, they raise smsd.RingBasisUnavailable naming the cause.
  • Fingerprints are always computed on CPU threads. A GPU applies only to some comparison steps; see What runs where.
  • The same FingerprintOptions gives the same bits in C++ and Java. The C++ batchFingerprint is a different all-atom path fingerprint and does not match Python path_fingerprint.
  • overlapCoefficient and count_overlapCoefficient are deprecated aliases of overlap_coefficient and count_overlap_coefficient.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This chapter installs SMSD Pro 8.1.0, runs a first substructure search and a first maximum common substructure (MCS) search, and sets out the conventions that every other chapter relies on: what a result proves, how molecules are given and numbered, the default chemistry, and time limits and threads.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Install the Python package from PyPI:

python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"
python -c "import smsd; print(smsd.__version__); assert smsd.parse_smiles('CC').n == 2"

The package has no required dependencies. Searches, fingerprints, prepared target corpora, streamed screens and corpus searches all work without the optional packages. Extras add the packages that particular features need, for example python -m pip install "smsd[rdkit,numpy]==8.1.0":

Extra Installs Needed for rdkit rdkit RDKit molecules as input, and RDKit depiction numpy numpy Packed fingerprint indexes, butina and maxmin clustering, NumPy feature arrays pandas pandas Molecule columns in pandas data frames polars polars Molecule columns in Polars data frames scipy numpy, scipy Sparse fingerprint matrices sklearn numpy, scikit-learn Fingerprint features in scikit-learn pipelines torch numpy, torch Fingerprint tensors pyg torch, torch-geometric Molecular graphs for graph learning arrow numpy, pyarrow Arrow fingerprint columns mcp mcp The local molecular tools server, smsd-mcp

For NVIDIA GPU screening on Linux x86_64, add the optional CUDA package of the same version, python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0" "smsd-cuda==8.1.0"; the CPU and GPU screening chapter covers it. Interpreters and platforms are listed in the supported-platforms table, which also leads to the source builds.

docs.title: A first search
docs.text:
A prepared query is built once and then matched against any number of targets. This program finds phenol in 4-tert-butylphenol and the MCS of N-methylacetamide and propanamide:

import smsd

# Substructure: phenol in 4-tert-butylphenol
result = smsd.Substructure.find("Oc1ccccc1").match("CC(C)(C)c1ccc(O)cc1")
assert result.found and result.optimal and result.complete
assert result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED
mapping = dict(sorted(result.best.atom_mapping.items()))
assert mapping == {0: 8, 1: 7, 2: 6, 3: 5, 4: 4, 5: 10, 6: 9}
print("substructure:", result.found, result.status.name, result.optimal, result.complete)
print("atom mapping:", mapping)

# MCS: N-methylacetamide and propanamide
common = smsd.MCS.find("CC(=O)NC").with_timeout(1000).match("CCC(=O)N")
assert common.found and common.optimal and common.complete
assert common.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED
common_mapping = dict(sorted(common.best.atom_mapping.items()))
assert common.best.atom_count == 4 and common_mapping == {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 4}
assert common.best.to_smiles("CC(=O)NC") == "C(C)(N)=O"
print("MCS:", common.found, common.status.name, common.optimal, common.complete)
print("MCS atoms:", common.best.atom_count, common_mapping)
print("common graph:", common.best.to_smiles("CC(=O)NC"))

The program prints:

substructure: True COMPLETED True True
atom mapping: {0: 8, 1: 7, 2: 6, 3: 5, 4: 4, 5: 10, 6: 9}
MCS: True COMPLETED True True
MCS atoms: 4 {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 3, 3: 4}
common graph: C(C)(N)=O

The atom mapping runs from query atom to target atom: the phenol oxygen, atom 0 of the query, is atom 8 of the target. to_smiles(query) writes the matched part of the query as SMILES, with the cut valences capped.

docs.title: Reading a result
docs.text:
Each match and match_all call returns a SearchResult, and match_many and MCS.match_constrained return one per query or target. The other entry points wrap one or report their own fields:

  • match_corpus returns one CorpusSearchResult per target, holding a SearchResult, or None when the target is proved not to qualify (see Search a prepared corpus).
  • MCS.match_with_smarts returns a SmartsResult with the SearchResult and a SMARTS string (see Export the common graph).
  • Substructure.decompose_r_groups returns one dictionary per target, with the SearchResult under search.
  • MCS.consensus returns a ConsensusResult with its own status, optimal, complete and found fields, and optimal is always False (see Common graph of a series).

The fields of a SearchResult:

Field Type Meaning matches tuple of Match The matches found, at most one from match status SearchStatus COMPLETED, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED or LIMIT_REACHED optimal bool The answer is proved: for a substructure search, a match exists or a completed search proved absence; for an MCS, the maximum is proved complete bool The search, or the enumeration of match_all, ran to its end score float Substructure: the number of query atoms when found, otherwise 0.0; MCIS: atoms; MCES: bonds; weighted MCIS: the weight sum nodes_visited int Search effort, for diagnostics elapsed_ms int Elapsed milliseconds, which vary from run to run found bool Whether matches is not empty best Match or None The first match

A Match has a read-only atom_mapping from query atom to target atom, bond_mapping as (query_first, query_second, target_first, target_second) tuples, fragments (the components of the matched bonds, as query atoms), atom_count, bond_count, and the methods to_smiles(query), to_graph(query) and to_smarts(query).

The rule that the rest of the guide relies on:

  • Any match returned is a valid embedding or common subgraph, whatever the status.
  • An empty result proves absence only when status is COMPLETED and optimal is True.
  • An MCS is proved maximum only when optimal is True.
  • A search stopped by its time limit, node limit or cancellation token proves nothing about what it did not find.

A time limit of 0 stops a search at once, which shows the stopped state:

import smsd

anthracene = "c1ccc2cc3ccccc3cc2c1"                     # anthracene
benzene = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1")            # benzene

stopped = benzene.with_timeout(0).match(anthracene)
assert stopped.status == smsd.SearchStatus.TIMED_OUT
assert not (stopped.found or stopped.optimal or stopped.complete)
print(stopped.status.name, stopped.found, stopped.optimal, stopped.complete)

finished = benzene.match(anthracene)
assert finished.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED
assert finished.found and finished.optimal and finished.complete and finished.score == 6.0
print(finished.status.name, finished.found, finished.optimal, finished.complete, finished.score)

The program prints:

TIMED_OUT False False False
COMPLETED True True True 6.0

docs.title: Molecule input
docs.text:
Searches and most other functions accept a molecule in any of these forms; a few low-level functions, such as circular_fingerprint, take a MolGraph only.

  • A SMILES string. It is parsed on every call, so when a molecule is used repeatedly, parse it once with smsd.parse_smiles(smiles, *, lenient=False). lenient=True recovers from malformed text, such as an unclosed ring, that otherwise raises ValueError.
  • A MolGraph, from parse_smiles, read_mol_file, read_mol_block or read_sdf.
  • An RDKit molecule, when RDKit is installed.

read_sdf(filename) reads every record of a file at once and write_sdf(molecules, filename) writes V2000 records. Each MolGraph carries an editable name (the record title) and properties (the SD fields), and write_sdf writes both. A malformed record is read as an empty graph with no warning, so keep the graphs with n > 0; a missing file raises ValueError.

import smsd
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

aspirin = smsd.parse_smiles("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O")      # aspirin
aspirin.name = "aspirin"
aspirin.properties = {"SOURCE": "inline"}
paracetamol = smsd.parse_smiles("CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1")     # paracetamol
paracetamol.name = "paracetamol"
paracetamol.properties = {"SOURCE": "inline"}

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "drugs.sdf"
    smsd.write_sdf([aspirin, paracetamol], path)
    with path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:    # a damaged third record
        handle.write("damaged\nnot a MOL block\n\nM  END\n$$$$\n")
    records = smsd.read_sdf(path)

sizes = [graph.n for graph in records]
assert sizes == [13, 11, 0]
molecules = [graph for graph in records if graph.n > 0]
names = [graph.name for graph in molecules]
fields = dict(molecules[0].properties)
assert names == ["aspirin", "paracetamol"] and fields == {"SOURCE": "inline"}
print("atoms per record:", sizes)
print("kept:", names)
print("fields of the first:", fields)

The program prints:

atoms per record: [13, 11, 0]
kept: ['aspirin', 'paracetamol']
fields of the first: {'SOURCE': 'inline'}

A line of a SMILES file that carries a title, or even trailing whitespace, is not valid SMILES, so split off the first column before parsing. parse_smiles("") returns an empty graph, while searches, fingerprints and target corpora raise ValueError for an empty string:

import smsd

lines = ["CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O aspirin", "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1 paracetamol"]
try:
    smsd.parse_smiles(lines[0])
except ValueError as error:
    message = str(error)
assert message == "Unexpected character at position 21: ' '"
print("whole line:", message)

graphs = []
for line in lines:
    smiles, title = line.split(maxsplit=1)
    graph = smsd.parse_smiles(smiles)
    graph.name = title
    graphs.append(graph)
assert [(graph.name, graph.n) for graph in graphs] == [("aspirin", 13), ("paracetamol", 11)]
print("parsed:", [(graph.name, graph.n) for graph in graphs])

recovered = smsd.to_smiles(smsd.parse_smiles("C1CC", lenient=True))
assert recovered == "C(C)C"
print("lenient C1CC:", recovered)

The program prints:

whole line: Unexpected character at position 21: ' '
parsed: [('aspirin', 13), ('paracetamol', 11)]
lenient C1CC: C(C)C

Explicit hydrogens, such as [H] in SMILES or hydrogen atoms in a MOL block, are atoms of the graph, whereas bracket hydrogen counts are not. A molecule query with an explicit hydrogen therefore needs an explicit hydrogen in the target, and an explicit-hydrogen record gives different fingerprints from its hydrogen-suppressed form. Normalise hydrogens the same way for every molecule before comparing them.

docs.title: Atom numbering
docs.text:
Search results and atom weights use each input's own numbering, separately for the query and the target: parser order for SMILES, graph order for a MolGraph, and RDKit order for an RDKit molecule. Sort the items of atom_mapping before printing them, because their order is not sorted for RDKit input:

from rdkit import Chem
import smsd

target = Chem.MolFromSmiles("OCC1=CC=CC=C1")              # benzyl alcohol, RDKit order
result = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1CO").match(target)
mapping = dict(sorted(result.best.atom_mapping.items()))
assert mapping == {0: 3, 1: 4, 2: 5, 3: 6, 4: 7, 5: 2, 6: 1, 7: 0}
oxygen = target.GetAtomWithIdx(mapping[7]).GetSymbol()
assert oxygen == "O"
print("RDKit-numbered mapping:", mapping)
print("query atom 7 is target atom", mapping[7], oxygen)

The program prints:

RDKit-numbered mapping: {0: 3, 1: 4, 2: 5, 3: 6, 4: 7, 5: 2, 6: 1, 7: 0}
query atom 7 is target atom 0 O

The Python guide describes the RDKit index helpers.

docs.title: Default chemistry
docs.text:
Every search starts from the same chemistry options:

Option Default Effect match_atom_type True Elements must agree match_bond_order BondOrderMode.STRICT Bond orders must agree aromaticity_mode AromaticityMode.FLEXIBLE An aromatic bond also matches a single or double bond match_formal_charge, match_isotope False Charges and isotopes are not compared use_chirality, use_bond_stereo False Stereochemistry is not compared ring_matches_ring_only False Ring atoms may match chain atoms complete_rings_only False An MCS may include part of a ring ring_fusion_mode RingFusionMode.IGNORE Ring fusion is not compared tautomer_aware False Tautomeric forms are not treated as equivalent

Two consequences surprise new users:

  • Because aromatic bonds also match single and double bonds, benzene is found in cyclohexanol.
  • A molecule query does not compare hydrogen counts, so the phenol graph also embeds in the ester oxygen of aspirin. A SMARTS pattern such as c[OX2H] states the hydrogen and does not.
import smsd

benzene = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1")              # benzene
cyclohexanol = "OC1CCCCC1"                                 # cyclohexanol
aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"                          # aspirin
flexible = benzene.match(cyclohexanol).found
assert flexible
print("benzene in cyclohexanol:", flexible)

options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.chemistry.aromaticity_mode = smsd.AromaticityMode.STRICT
strict = benzene.with_options(options).match(cyclohexanol).found
assert not strict
print("with STRICT aromaticity:", strict)

molecule_query = smsd.Substructure.find("Oc1ccccc1").match(aspirin).found      # phenol
smarts_query = smsd.Substructure.smarts("c[OX2H]").match(aspirin).found
assert molecule_query and not smarts_query
print("phenol in aspirin:", molecule_query, "| c[OX2H] in aspirin:", smarts_query)

The program prints:

benzene in cyclohexanol: True
with STRICT aromaticity: False
phenol in aspirin: True | c[OX2H] in aspirin: False

The substructure chapter describes every option and the named profiles.

docs.title: Time limits and threads
docs.text:
Each search has its own limits, set on an options object:

  • timeout_ms, default -1, selects 10,000 ms per target for a substructure search, and 500 + 2 × query atoms × target atoms ms, at most 30,000 ms, for an MCS. A positive value applies to each query and target pair; 0 stops at once.
  • node_limit, default 0 (no cap): reaching it reports LIMIT_REACHED.
  • cancellation, default None: a CancellationToken whose cancel(), from any thread, stops the search with CANCELLED. A token stays cancelled, so use a new one for each request.

Options objects take no keyword arguments: create one and set its attributes. A misspelt attribute raises AttributeError. with_options and with_timeout return a new query with a copy of the options, apart from the cancellation token, which stays shared.

Batch calls such as match_many take num_threads; 0, the default, uses the OpenMP default, which follows the OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable. Results do not depend on the thread count. Pass a non-negative integer: TargetCorpus.screen and TargetCorpus.prewarm do not check it.

import smsd

anthracene = "c1ccc2cc3ccccc3cc2c1"                       # anthracene
benzene = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1")              # benzene

options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
assert (options.timeout_ms, options.node_limit, options.cancellation) == (-1, 0, None)
try:
    smsd.Substructure.Options(timeout_ms=2000)
except TypeError:
    print("keyword arguments: TypeError")
else:
    raise AssertionError("keyword arguments were accepted")
options.timeout_ms = 2000                                 # per target
options.node_limit = 3
capped = benzene.with_options(options).match(anthracene)
assert capped.status == smsd.SearchStatus.LIMIT_REACHED
assert not (capped.found or capped.complete)
print("node limit:", capped.status.name, capped.found, capped.complete)

token = smsd.CancellationToken()
options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.cancellation = token
cancellable = benzene.with_options(options)
token.cancel()                                            # the query shares the token
cancelled = cancellable.match(anthracene)
assert cancelled.status == smsd.SearchStatus.CANCELLED and not cancelled.found
print("cancelled:", cancelled.status.name, cancelled.found)

targets = ["Oc1ccccc1", "OC1CCCCC1", "CCO", "Cc1ccccc1"]   # phenol, cyclohexanol, ethanol, toluene
one_thread = [result.found for result in benzene.match_many(targets, num_threads=1)]
default = [result.found for result in benzene.match_many(targets)]
assert one_thread == default == [True, True, False, True]
print("match_many:", default)

The program prints:

keyword arguments: TypeError
node limit: LIMIT_REACHED False False
cancelled: CANCELLED False
match_many: [True, True, False, True]
