docs.title: C++ and Java
docs.text: The C++ headers and the Java library offer the substructure, MCS and fingerprint searches of the Python package, with the same default chemistry. This chapter shows one complete program in each language, how to build and run it, and where the languages differ. The C++ guide and the Java guide are the references for everything else.

docs.title: C++
docs.text:
The C++ library is header-only and needs a C++17 compiler: include smsd/smsd.hpp and add cpp/include to the include path. An installed CMake package provides the target smsd::smsd through find_package(smsd 8.1.0 CONFIG REQUIRED); the C++ module README shows the install and a minimal consumer project.

This program computes ECFP4 similarities of phenol to five molecules, screens a prepared TargetCorpus at a threshold of 0.5, and runs exact substructure and MCS searches over the same corpus:

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "smsd/smsd.hpp"

int main() {
    const std::vector<std::string> names = {"phenol", "cyclohexanol", "aspirin", "ethanol", "toluene"};
    const std::vector<std::string> smiles = {"Oc1ccccc1", "OC1CCCCC1", "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", "CCO",
                                             "Cc1ccccc1"};
    const double expected[] = {1.000, 0.000, 0.020, 0.000, 0.040};
    const auto query = smsd::parseSMILES("Oc1ccccc1");                             // phenol
    const auto queryFp = smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles("Oc1ccccc1", 2, 2048);  // ECFP4, 2,048 bits

    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(3);
    std::vector<smsd::MolGraph> targets;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < smiles.size(); ++i) {
        targets.push_back(smsd::parseSMILES(smiles[i]));
        const auto fp = smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles(smiles[i], 2, 2048);
        const double similarity = smsd::batch::fingerprintTanimoto(queryFp, fp);
        if (std::abs(similarity - expected[i]) > 0.0005) return 1;
        std::cout << names[i] << " ECFP4 Tanimoto " << similarity << '\n';
    }

    smsd::batch::TargetCorpus corpus;
    corpus.addTargets(targets);
    corpus.prewarm(2);  // computes the fingerprints that screen() needs
    const std::vector<int> similar = corpus.screen(query, 0.5, 2);

    // The targets each corpus search reached; a search that stopped fails the program.
    bool stopped = false;
    auto hits = [&](const std::vector<smsd::CorpusSearchResult>& rows) {
        std::vector<int> found;
        for (const auto& row : rows) {
            if (row.thresholdReached) found.push_back(static_cast<int>(row.targetIndex));
            else if (!row.provenBelowThreshold) stopped = true;
        }
        return found;
    };
    const auto embeddings = hits(smsd::Substructure::find(query).matchCorpus(corpus, false, 2));
    const auto common = hits(smsd::MCS::find(query).withTimeout(1000).matchCorpus(corpus, 6, false, 2));
    if (stopped || similar != std::vector<int>{0} || embeddings != std::vector<int>{0, 1, 2}
        || common != std::vector<int>{0, 1, 2, 4}) return 1;

    auto print = [&](const char* label, const std::vector<int>& indices) {
        std::cout << label;
        for (int index : indices) std::cout << ' ' << names[index];
        std::cout << '\n';
    };
    print("screen at 0.5:", similar);
    print("substructure hits:", embeddings);
    print("MCS of at least 6 atoms:", common);
}

The program prints:

phenol ECFP4 Tanimoto 1.000
cyclohexanol ECFP4 Tanimoto 0.000
aspirin ECFP4 Tanimoto 0.020
ethanol ECFP4 Tanimoto 0.000
toluene ECFP4 Tanimoto 0.040
screen at 0.5: phenol
substructure hits: phenol cyclohexanol aspirin
MCS of at least 6 atoms: phenol cyclohexanol aspirin toluene

Save it as screen.cpp and build it from the repository root:

c++ -std=c++17 -O2 -pthread -I cpp/include screen.cpp -o screen
./screen

The calls used are:

  • smsd::batch::fingerprintFromSmiles(smiles, radius = 2, fpSize = 2048): an ECFP fingerprint as 64-bit words, and fingerprintTanimoto(a, b) to compare two of them.
  • TargetCorpus::addTargets(graphs) and prewarm(numThreads = 0), which computes the ECFP4 fingerprints, radius 2 and 2,048 bits, that screen(query, threshold, numThreads = 0) compares. screen returns the targets whose similarity is at least the threshold, and nothing before prewarm.
  • Substructure::matchCorpus(corpus, gpuPrefilter = false, numThreads = 0) and MCS::matchCorpus(corpus, minimumAtoms, gpuPrefilter = false, numThreads = 0): one CorpusSearchResult per target, in corpus order. thresholdReached means a match, or a common substructure of at least minimumAtoms atoms, was found. provenBelowThreshold means the target is proved not to reach it, either by a completed search or because it was ruled out before matching. result holds the exact search result of every target that was searched. When neither flag is set, the search stopped.

Cyclohexanol is a substructure hit because the default chemistry lets aromatic bonds match single and double bonds; see default chemistry. Batch operations use OpenMP when the compiler enables it; the installation guide covers the CMake build and its options.

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
The Java library is com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd and the command-line tool com.bioinceptionlabs:smsd-cli. Maven Central has 8.0.3; for 8.1.0, run mvn -f java/pom.xml install from the repository root, which installs both in the local Maven repository (Gradle then needs mavenLocal()). The Java module README gives the Maven and Gradle dependencies, and the code runs on Java 8 or later.

This program computes the same ECFP4 similarities and runs exact substructure and MCS searches over the list on two threads:

import com.bioinception.smsd.core.FingerprintEngine;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.MCS;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.MolGraph;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.SearchResult;
import com.bioinception.smsd.core.Substructure;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Locale;
import org.openscience.cdk.silent.SilentChemObjectBuilder;
import org.openscience.cdk.smiles.SmilesParser;

/** ECFP4 similarity, then exact substructure and MCS searches, over a small list. */
public class ScreenExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        SmilesParser parser = new SmilesParser(SilentChemObjectBuilder.getInstance());
        String[] names = {"phenol", "cyclohexanol", "aspirin", "ethanol", "toluene"};
        String[] smiles = {"Oc1ccccc1", "OC1CCCCC1", "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", "CCO", "Cc1ccccc1"};
        double[] expectedSimilarity = {1.000, 0.000, 0.020, 0.000, 0.040};
        boolean[] expectedHit = {true, true, true, false, false};
        int[] expectedAtoms = {7, 7, 7, 3, 6};

        MolGraph query = FingerprintEngine.toMolGraph(parser.parseSmiles("Oc1ccccc1"));  // phenol
        long[] queryFp = FingerprintEngine.ecfp(query, 2, 2048);                           // ECFP4
        List<MolGraph> targets = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String text : smiles) targets.add(FingerprintEngine.toMolGraph(parser.parseSmiles(text)));

        List<SearchResult> embeddings = Substructure.find(query).matchMany(targets, 2);
        List<SearchResult> common = MCS.find(query).withTimeout(1000).matchMany(targets, 2);
        for (int i = 0; i < targets.size(); i++) {
            SearchResult embedding = embeddings.get(i);
            SearchResult mcs = common.get(i);
            double similarity = FingerprintEngine.tanimoto(queryFp, FingerprintEngine.ecfp(targets.get(i), 2, 2048));
            int atoms = mcs.found() ? mcs.matches().get(0).atomCount() : 0;
            if (!embedding.complete() || !mcs.optimal() || embedding.found() != expectedHit[i]
                || atoms != expectedAtoms[i] || Math.abs(similarity - expectedSimilarity[i]) > 0.0005)
                throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected result for " + names[i]);
            System.out.println(String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%-13s ECFP4 %.3f  substructure %-5s  MCS atoms %d",
                names[i], similarity, embedding.found(), atoms));
        }
    }
}

The program prints:

phenol        ECFP4 1.000  substructure true   MCS atoms 7
cyclohexanol  ECFP4 0.000  substructure true   MCS atoms 7
aspirin       ECFP4 0.020  substructure true   MCS atoms 7
ethanol       ECFP4 0.000  substructure false  MCS atoms 3
toluene       ECFP4 0.040  substructure false  MCS atoms 6

Save it as ScreenExample.java and compile it from the repository root against the self-contained JAR of the source build; on Windows, separate the class path entries with a semicolon:

javac --release 8 -cp java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar ScreenExample.java
java -cp "java/cli/target/smsd-cli-8.1.0-jar-with-dependencies.jar:." ScreenExample

With JDK 25, javac --release 8 warns that release 8 is obsolete; the class still compiles and runs on Java 8 or later.

The Java searches take CDK molecules or MolGraph graphs, and FingerprintEngine.toMolGraph standardises a CDK molecule into a graph. Java has no prepared target corpus, so it screens a list with matchMany and fingerprint comparisons, as above.

docs.title: Packed fingerprint index
docs.text:
A packed fingerprint index is a file of binary fingerprints that is built once, reopened in any later session and scanned exactly, without holding the library in memory. smsd.FingerprintCorpus (also smsd.corpus.FingerprintCorpus) builds and reads it; smsd.butina and smsd.maxmin cluster and select from it. Every operation on the index, including opening it, needs NumPy, which the numpy extra installs:

python -m pip install "smsd[numpy]==8.1.0"

The examples use the same inline library as Screening a library: 14 benzodiazepines, 7 common drugs and 512 generated trisubstituted benzenes. Each program writes its index in a temporary directory.

docs.title: Build an index
docs.text:
FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, molecules, options=...) fingerprints SMILES strings, MolGraph objects (for example from smsd.read_sdf) or RDKit molecules in bounded batches and writes the file. Any iterable works, including a generator over a large file. FingerprintCorpus.create(path, fingerprints, fp_size=...) writes fingerprints that already exist as lists of set bits; from_fingerprints is the same method under another name. Both return the new index, already open.

The file is written in full under a temporary name in the destination directory and then published, so a failed build leaves no file behind. An existing file is kept, and the build raises FileExistsError, unless overwrite=True replaces it. Without overwrite, the filesystem must support hard links. There is no append or merge: to change an index, build it again.

The file records the width and the row count only, not the fingerprint specification or any identifiers. Store those beside it, for example in a small JSON sidecar file:

import itertools
import json
import struct
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)  # ECFP4
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    index_path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(
            index_path, smiles, options=options, num_threads=2) as corpus:
        print("rows:", len(corpus), "| bits:", corpus.fp_size)
        print("set bits in row 0:", len(corpus.fingerprint(0)))
        assert len(corpus.fingerprint(0)) == 42

    # The file holds bits only: keep the specification and the names with it.
    spec = {"family": "ecfp", "radius": options.radius, "size": options.size,
            "names": names}
    index_path.with_suffix(".json").write_text(json.dumps(spec),
                                               encoding="utf-8")
    size = index_path.stat().st_size
    header = struct.unpack("<8sQQ", index_path.read_bytes()[:24])
    print(f"file size: {size:,} bytes | header: {header}")

    # An existing file is kept unless overwrite=True.
    try:
        smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(index_path, smiles[:21],
                                           options=options)
    except FileExistsError:
        print("library.fp already exists and is unchanged")
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(
            index_path, smiles[:21], options=options, overwrite=True) as corpus:
        print("replaced with", len(corpus), "rows")
        assert len(corpus) == 21

    # Bit lists from any source: MACCS keys, 166 bits wide.
    maccs = smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs()
    keys = smsd.fingerprints(smiles[:21], options=maccs)
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "maccs.fp", keys,
                                       fp_size=maccs.size) as corpus:
        print("MACCS index:", len(corpus), "rows of", corpus.fp_size, "bits")
        assert (len(corpus), corpus.fp_size) == (21, 166)
        assert corpus.fingerprint(16) == keys[16]

assert size == 24 + 533 * 256
assert header == (b"SMSDFP1\x00", 2048, 533)

The program prints:

rows: 533 | bits: 2048
set bits in row 0: 42
file size: 136,472 bytes | header: (b'SMSDFP1\x00', 2048, 533)
library.fp already exists and is unchanged
replaced with 21 rows
MACCS index: 21 rows of 166 bits

A 2048-bit row takes 256 bytes, so the 533-row file is 24 header bytes plus 533 rows of 256 bytes.

docs.title: Reopen an index
docs.text:
FingerprintCorpus(path) opens an existing file read-only. It checks the header and the file length and maps the rows into memory without reading them all. Use it as a context manager, or call close(); len(corpus) and corpus.fp_size still work after closing. corpus.fingerprint(i) returns the set bits of row i.

Queries must be made with the same specification as the index. A query made another way, for example with the default kind of smsd.fingerprint or with another width, still runs and returns scores, but they answer a different question and nothing reports the mismatch. Rebuild the options from the sidecar file:

import itertools
import json
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    index_path = Path(directory) / "library.fp"
    sidecar = Path(directory) / "library.json"

    # Session 1: build the index and record how it was built.
    build = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
    smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(index_path, smiles,
                                       options=build).close()
    sidecar.write_text(json.dumps({"family": "ecfp", "radius": 2, "size": 2048,
                                   "names": names}), encoding="utf-8")

    # Session 2: rebuild the options from the sidecar, then open the index.
    spec = json.loads(sidecar.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=spec["radius"],
                                           size=spec["size"])
    row_names = spec["names"]
    diazepam = NAMED["diazepam"]
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus(index_path) as corpus:
        assert corpus.fp_size == spec["size"] and len(corpus) == len(row_names)
        assert corpus.fingerprint(9) == smsd.fingerprint(smiles[9],
                                                         options=options)
        query = smsd.fingerprint(diazepam, options=options)
        right = [row_names[row]
                 for row, _ in corpus.similarities(query, threshold=0.5)]
        # Queries made another way still run, but answer a different question.
        default_kind = smsd.fingerprint(diazepam)  # kind "mcs"
        narrow = smsd.fingerprint(diazepam, kind="ecfp", fp_size=1024)
        wrong = [len(list(corpus.similarities(bits, threshold=0.5)))
                 for bits in (default_kind, narrow)]
    print("rows:", len(corpus), "| bits:", corpus.fp_size)
    print("same specification:", right)
    print("default kind, 1024-bit ECFP:", wrong, "rows")

assert right == ["diazepam", "nordazepam", "temazepam", "tetrazepam",
                 "clobazam"]
assert wrong == [0, 0]

The program prints:

rows: 533 | bits: 2048
same specification: ['diazepam', 'nordazepam', 'temazepam', 'tetrazepam', 'clobazam']
default kind, 1024-bit ECFP: [0, 0] rows

docs.title: Similarity search with a threshold
docs.text:
corpus.similarities(query, threshold=...) scans every row and yields (row, Tanimoto) for the rows whose score is at least the threshold, in row order. The scores are exactly those of smsd.tanimoto_coefficient on the same bits. An empty query scores 1.0 against an empty row and 0.0 against any other.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
query = smsd.fingerprint(NAMED["diazepam"], options=options)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(
            Path(directory) / "library.fp", smiles,
            options=options) as corpus:
        hits = list(corpus.similarities(query, threshold=0.5))
for row, score in hits:
    print(f"{row:3d}  {names[row]:<12} {score:.3f}")

# The scores are tanimoto_coefficient on the same bits ...
for row, score in hits:
    bits = smsd.fingerprint(smiles[row], options=options)
    assert score == smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(query, bits)
# ... and the rows are those of the in-memory ECFP4 screen.
targets = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles)
targets.prewarm(num_threads=2)
assert [row for row, _ in hits] == targets.screen(NAMED["diazepam"], 0.5,
                                                  num_threads=2)

The program prints:

  0  diazepam     1.000
  1  nordazepam   0.528
  2  temazepam    0.582
  9  tetrazepam   0.542
 13  clobazam     0.500

With ECFP radius 2 and 2048 bits, the rows are the same as those of TargetCorpus.screen at the same threshold.

docs.title: The N most similar
docs.text:
There is no top-N method for a query from outside the index. With the default threshold of 0, similarities yields every row, and heapq.nlargest keeps the best N while the scan streams past. The key (score, -row) makes equal scores prefer the lower row, so the result is repeatable.

import heapq
import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",

docs.title: Several queries in one pass
docs.text:
corpus.screen_many(queries, threshold=...) scans the file once for up to 32 queries and yields (query, row, Tanimoto). The output comes chunk by chunk, then by query, then by row: it is neither grouped by query nor ranked. Sort it when order matters. For more than 32 queries, call it again for each group of 32.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",

    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
queries = [smsd.fingerprint(NAMED[name], options=options)
           for name in ("diazepam", "alprazolam", "aspirin")]
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(
            Path(directory) / "library.fp", smiles, options=options) as corpus:
        # Small chunks show the order: by chunk, then query, then row.
        hits = list(corpus.screen_many(queries, threshold=0.5, chunk_size=4))
        whole = list(corpus.screen_many(queries, threshold=0.5))
        try:
            list(corpus.screen_many(queries * 11, threshold=0.5))
        except ValueError as error:
            message = str(error)
            print("33 queries:", message)
print("as yielded:", [(query, row) for query, row, _ in hits])
for query, row, score in sorted(hits):
    print(f"  query {query}  {names[row]:<12} {score:.3f}")

assert message == "screen_many supports at most 32 queries"
assert [(query, row) for query, row, _ in hits] == [
    (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 9), (1, 10), (1, 11), (0, 13), (1, 12), (2, 14)]
assert sorted(hits) == sorted(whole)

  query 0  diazepam     1.000

docs.title: Neighbours and pairs within the index
docs.text:
corpus.top_k_pairs(k) yields the k nearest neighbours of every row as (row, neighbour, Tanimoto), grouped by row and best first; equal scores prefer the lower neighbour. corpus.threshold_pairs(threshold) yields every pair of rows whose score is at least the threshold, once each, as (first, second, Tanimoto) with first < second. Both scan every pair exactly, so the work grows with the square of the row count, and neither builds a similarity matrix. Consume them as they stream: collecting every pair can need memory that grows with the square of the row count, and collecting all neighbours memory for n times k results.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",

    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",

    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    named = Path(directory) / "named.fp"
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(  # the 21 named drugs
            named, smiles[:21], options=options) as corpus:

for query, target, score in nearest[:4]:

print("pairs at 0.5 or above:")
for first, second, score in pairs:

assert len(nearest) == 21 and len(pairs) == 13
assert all(first < second for first, second, _ in pairs)

docs.title: Clustering and diverse selection
docs.text:
smsd.butina(corpus, threshold=0.7) groups rows around cluster centres and returns a list of tuples, each with its centre first and the other members in row order. Every member reaches the threshold with its centre, but not necessarily with the other members. reordering=True updates the neighbour counts after each cluster is taken. smsd.maxmin(corpus, count) picks count diverse rows: it starts at row seed (0 by default), then repeatedly takes the row that is least similar to its closest chosen row. Both are deterministic, and ties go to the lower row.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

options = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    named = Path(directory) / "named.fp"
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(  # the 21 named drugs
            named, smiles[:21], options=options) as corpus:
        clusters = smsd.butina(corpus, threshold=0.4)
        diverse = smsd.maxmin(corpus, 5)
print("Butina clusters at 0.4:", len(clusters))
for cluster in clusters:
    if len(cluster) > 1:
        print("  centre", names[cluster[0]], "with",
              [names[member] for member in cluster[1:]])
print("MaxMin, 5 diverse:", [names[row] for row in diverse])

docs.title: Substructure searches
docs.text: The index holds similarity fingerprints only, so it cannot answer a substructure question. Load the library into a TargetCorpus and use Substructure.match_corpus, which rules out targets that cannot contain the query before matching and confirms every other target exactly; see Substructure screen with exact confirmation.

docs.title: File format
docs.text:
Version 1 of the format is a 24-byte header followed by fixed-width rows:

Offset Size Content 0 8 bytes The magic bytes SMSDFP1 followed by a zero byte 8 8 bytes fp_size, the width in bits, an unsigned little-endian integer from 1 to 16,777,216 16 8 bytes The row count, an unsigned little-endian integer 24 rows times ceil(fp_size / 8) bytes One row per fingerprint, in input order

Bit p of a row is stored in byte p // 8 of that row, at bit p % 8, so bit 0 is the least significant bit of the first byte. Unused bits in the last byte of a row must be zero. The file length is exactly 24 bytes plus the rows. There is no other metadata and no version field beyond the magic bytes.

Opening a file checks the magic bytes, the width and the length; searches also reject non-zero padding bits. Any program can write the format. Within SMSD Pro, only the Python package reads it. The program below writes a 12-bit, three-row file by hand and opens it:

import struct
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

fp_size = 12                      # any width from 1 to 16,777,216 bits
rows = [[0, 3, 11], [3], []]
row_bytes = (fp_size + 7) // 8    # 2 bytes per row
payload = bytearray()
for bits in rows:
    packed = bytearray(row_bytes)
    for bit in bits:
        packed[bit // 8] |= 1 << (bit % 8)  # bit 0: lowest bit of byte 0
    payload += packed

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "by_hand.fp"
    header = struct.pack("<8sQQ", b"SMSDFP1\0", fp_size, len(rows))
    path.write_bytes(header + payload)
    data = path.read_bytes()
    print("bytes:", data.hex(" "))
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus(path) as corpus:
        stored = [corpus.fingerprint(row) for row in range(len(corpus))]
        print("rows read back:", stored)
        hits = list(corpus.similarities([3], threshold=0.3))
        print("similar to [3]:",
              [(row, round(score, 3)) for row, score in hits])

    # Bits past fp_size in the last byte of a row must be zero.
    broken = Path(directory) / "padding.fp"
    broken.write_bytes(data[:25] + bytes([data[25] | 0x80]) + data[26:])
    with smsd.FingerprintCorpus(broken) as corpus:
        try:
            list(corpus.similarities([3]))
        except ValueError as error:
            message = str(error)
            print("ValueError:", message)

assert len(data) == 24 + len(rows) * row_bytes
assert stored == rows
assert [(row, round(score, 3)) for row, score in hits] == [(0, 0.333), (1, 1.0)]
assert message == "fingerprint corpus contains non-zero padding bits"

The program prints:

bytes: 53 4d 53 44 46 50 31 00 0c 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 09 08 08 00 00 00
rows read back: [[0, 3, 11], [3], []]
similar to [3]: [(0, 0.333), (1, 1.0)]
ValueError: fingerprint corpus contains non-zero padding bits

docs.title: Build options
docs.text:
FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(path, molecules, *, kind="ecfp", fp_size=2048, radius=2, path_length=7, options=None, chunk_size=4096, num_threads=0, overwrite=False) and FingerprintCorpus.create(path, fingerprints, *, fp_size=2048, chunk_size=4096, overwrite=False) take these arguments:

Name Type Default Meaning path str or path required The file to create molecules iterable required from_smiles: SMILES strings, MolGraph objects or RDKit molecules fingerprints iterable of bit lists required create: set-bit positions, each from 0 to fp_size - 1; duplicates are folded, count pairs are rejected options FingerprintOptions or None None The full specification; when given, its size sets the width; count options are rejected kind str "ecfp" Used when options is None: "path", "mcs", "ecfp", "circular", "fcfp" or "torsion" fp_size int 2048 Width in bits, from 1 to 16,777,216 radius int 2 Circular radius, used when options is None path_length int 7 Path length, used when options is None chunk_size int 4096 Molecules or rows per batch; reduced when needed to keep each batch's arrays within about 64 MiB num_threads int 0 Fingerprinting threads; 0 uses the OpenMP default overwrite bool False True replaces an existing file; False raises FileExistsError

The default kind here is "ecfp", whereas smsd.fingerprint defaults to "mcs", so pass the same FingerprintOptions object to both.

docs.title: Search options
docs.text:
Method Arguments and defaults Yields similarities query, *, threshold=0.0, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu" (row, Tanimoto) in row order screen_many queries, *, threshold=0.0, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu" (query, row, Tanimoto) by chunk, then query, then row; at most 32 queries threshold_pairs threshold, *, include_self=False, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu" (first, second, Tanimoto) with first < second top_k_pairs k, *, threshold=0.0, include_self=False, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu" (row, neighbour, Tanimoto), at most k per row, best first iter_packed_chunks *, chunk_size=4096 (first_row, array): copies of the packed bytes as uint8 arrays smsd.butina corpus, threshold=0.7, *, reordering=False, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu" Returns a list of tuples, centre first smsd.maxmin corpus, count, *, seed=0, chunk_size=4096, backend="cpu" Returns a list of rows in selection order

Every threshold is inclusive and must be a finite number from 0 to 1; threshold=True raises TypeError and a value outside the range raises ValueError. A query bit outside 0 to fp_size - 1 raises ValueError. chunk_size changes how many rows are compared at a time, and so the working memory and the order of screen_many output, never the hits. backend is "cpu" (the default), "cuda" or "auto"; any other value raises ValueError. Choose a backend for packed indexes describes the GPU choices and corpus.cuda_calls.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The working arrays of a search or build are kept to about 64 MiB per chunk. Mapped pages, queries and the results you keep are additional; see Ordering, work and memory.
  • Keep the file unchanged while it is open. Opening checks only the header and the length.
  • After close(), reading a row raises ValueError, but len(corpus) still works. Arrays from iter_packed_chunks are copies and stay valid.
  • TargetCorpus, stream_screen_smiles, stream_screen_many_smiles and Substructure.match_corpus need no NumPy.
