docs.title: Screening a library
docs.text: Screening narrows a library down to the molecules worth a closer look. SMSD Pro offers these routes: a ranked list for a handful of molecules, a fingerprint threshold screen held in memory or streamed from a file, a saved packed index, an exact substructure screen and an MCS-similarity screen. This chapter shows which route suits which task, how to prepare the library, how to run each screen and how to save the hits. Every example uses the same inline library of 533 molecules: 14 benzodiazepines, 7 common drugs and 512 generated trisubstituted benzenes, so each program runs as it stands, with no data files.

docs.title: Choose a route
docs.text:
Task Use Fingerprint Prepare first Needs NumPy GPU Rank a small list batch_similarity ECFP; radius 2 and 2048 bits by default Nothing No No Threshold screen in memory TargetCorpus.screen or screen_many ECFP radius 2, 2048 bits, fixed prewarm() after every addition No With smsd-cuda, automatic on a Tesla T4 for 100,000 targets or more, or on any supported device from SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS targets; see the device rule Screen a large file once stream_screen_smiles or stream_screen_many_smiles ECFP radius 2, 2048 bits, fixed Nothing No As above, chunk by chunk Search a saved index many times FingerprintCorpus; see the packed index Any binary specification Build the file once Yes On request, with backend="cuda" or "auto" Exact substructure Substructure.match_corpus None: exact search A TargetCorpus No Optional pre-screen, with gpu_prefilter=True MCS similarity screen_targets, then MCS.match_many; or MCS.match_corpus None: an atom-count bound, then the exact MCS A list or a TargetCorpus No screen_targets runs on the CPU; MCS.match_corpus takes gpu_prefilter=True

The in-memory, streamed and packed-index screens give the same hits for the same query and threshold when the index is built with ECFP radius 2 and 2048 bits, because they then compare the same fingerprints. Graph matching always runs on the CPU, and every GPU route returns the same results as the CPU. CPU and GPU screening explains when a device is used.

docs.title: Prepare the library
docs.text:
A screen is only as consistent as its input. Four points matter before any corpus is built:

  • Malformed SD records. smsd.read_sdf reads the whole file and returns a malformed record as an empty graph, with no warning. An empty graph still takes part in a screen and passes one with a threshold of 0, so keep only graphs with graph.n > 0.
  • SMILES files. A line that holds a name after the SMILES does not parse as SMILES, so split off the first column. There is no SMILES-file reader; a generator over the lines serves, and keeps memory flat for the streamed screens.
  • Identifiers. A TargetCorpus or FingerprintCorpus stores no names and cannot be indexed or iterated. Keep the names in a list in the same order; every hit index refers to that list.
  • Hydrogens. Explicit hydrogens are graph atoms, so a record written with them has quite different fingerprints from the same molecule without them. Write or export every record in the same form, with implicit hydrogens.

The program below defines the library, writes it as an SD file with a title and a SOURCE field per record and as a SMILES file with SMILES name lines, adds a malformed record, then reads both files back:

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    sdf_path = Path(directory) / "library.sdf"
    smi_path = Path(directory) / "library.smi"

    # Write an SD file with a title and a SOURCE field per record ...
    graphs = []
    for name, text in library:
        graph = smsd.parse_smiles(text)
        graph.name = name
        graph.properties = {"SOURCE": "named" if name in NAMED else "generated"}
        graphs.append(graph)
    smsd.write_sdf(graphs, sdf_path)
    with sdf_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        stream.write("garbage\nnot a molfile\n\nM  END\n$$$$\n")  # malformed
    # ... and a SMILES file with "SMILES name" lines.
    smi_path.write_text("".join(f"{text} {name}\n" for name, text in library),
                        encoding="utf-8")

    # A malformed SD record comes back as an empty graph: drop it.
    records = smsd.read_sdf(sdf_path)
    kept = [graph for graph in records if graph.n > 0]
    print("SD records:", len(records), "| with atoms:", len(kept))
    print("first record:", kept[0].name, dict(kept[0].properties))

    # A SMILES line holds the SMILES first; the rest of the line is the name.
    lines = smi_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    rows = [line.split(maxsplit=1) for line in lines if line.strip()]
    file_smiles = [row[0] for row in rows]
    file_names = [row[1] if len(row) > 1 else "" for row in rows]
    print("SMILES lines:", len(rows), "| a name with a space:", file_names[15])

assert len(records) == 534 and len(kept) == 533
assert [graph.name for graph in kept] == names == file_names
assert dict(kept[0].properties) == {"SOURCE": "named"}
assert file_smiles == smiles

The program prints:

SD records: 534 | with atoms: 533
first record: diazepam {'SOURCE': 'named'}
SMILES lines: 533 | a name with a space: salicylic acid

Duplicates are common in assembled libraries. smsd.canonical_hash groups candidate duplicates quickly, but a hash is a screening key rather than proof of identity, so confirm each candidate with smsd.same_canonical_graph. The generated benzenes carry their three substituents in equivalent positions, so the 512 SMILES describe only 120 distinct structures, and the whole library holds 141:

import itertools

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

# Group records by canonical hash, then confirm each candidate with a graph
# comparison, because a hash alone is not proof of identity.
graphs = [smsd.parse_smiles(text) for text in smiles]
seen = {}
unique, repeats = [], []
for index, graph in enumerate(graphs):
    bucket = seen.setdefault(smsd.canonical_hash(graph), [])
    same = [kept for kept in bucket
            if smsd.same_canonical_graph(graphs[kept], graph)]
    if same:
        repeats.append((index, same[0]))
    else:
        bucket.append(index)
        unique.append(index)
print("records:", len(graphs), "| distinct structures:", len(unique))
print("first repeat:", names[repeats[0][0]], "is", names[repeats[0][1]])
assert len(unique) == 141 and len(repeats) == 392
assert [names[i] for i in repeats[0]] == ["GEN-008", "GEN-001"]

# Explicit hydrogens are graph atoms, so they change every fingerprint.
plain = smsd.parse_smiles(NAMED["paracetamol"])
explicit = smsd.parse_smiles(  # paracetamol with explicit hydrogens
    "[H]Oc1c([H])c([H])c(N([H])C(=O)C([H])([H])[H])c([H])c1[H]")
score = smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(smsd.fingerprint(plain, kind="ecfp"),
                                  smsd.fingerprint(explicit, kind="ecfp"))
print("paracetamol atoms:", plain.n, "and", explicit.n,
      "| ECFP4 Tanimoto:", f"{score:.3f}")
assert (plain.n, explicit.n) == (11, 20)
assert f"{score:.3f}" == "0.018"

The program prints:

records: 533 | distinct structures: 141
first repeat: GEN-008 is GEN-001
paracetamol atoms: 11 and 20 | ECFP4 Tanimoto: 0.018

The same paracetamol with and without explicit hydrogens shares almost no ECFP bits, which is why a library should be consistent before it is screened.

docs.title: Similarity screen in memory
docs.text:
TargetCorpus.from_smiles parses the library once and keeps it in memory. prewarm() computes an ECFP radius 2, 2048-bit fingerprint for every target; screen and screen_many then compare one or more queries with them and return the indices of the targets whose Tanimoto score is at least the threshold, in library order. They return indices only. For scores, use batch_similarity on the hits, as in Save the hits, or a packed index.

A screen run before prewarm(), or after any target is added, returns an empty list rather than raising, so call prewarm() again after every addition. smsd.warm_start(corpus, query, threshold) prepares the corpus when it needs it and then screens.

import itertools

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

diazepam = NAMED["diazepam"]
alprazolam = NAMED["alprazolam"]

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles[:21])  # the named drugs
corpus.prewarm(num_threads=2)
corpus.add_targets(smiles[21:])                      # then the generated set
# An addition clears the preparation, and an unprepared screen finds nothing.
assert not corpus.is_prewarmed
assert corpus.screen(diazepam, 0.5, num_threads=2) == []

corpus.prewarm(num_threads=2)
hits = corpus.screen(diazepam, 0.5, num_threads=2)
print("diazepam, at least 0.5:", [names[i] for i in hits])

per_query = corpus.screen_many([diazepam, alprazolam], 0.5, num_threads=2)
print("alprazolam, at least 0.5:", [names[i] for i in per_query[1]])

# The threshold is inclusive: 1.0 keeps identical fingerprints.
exact = corpus.screen(diazepam, 1.0, num_threads=2)
print("diazepam, at least 1.0:", [names[i] for i in exact])

# warm_start prepares a corpus when needed, then screens it.
fresh = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles)
assert smsd.warm_start(fresh, diazepam, 0.5, num_threads=2) == hits
assert fresh.is_prewarmed

assert [names[i] for i in hits] == [
    "diazepam", "nordazepam", "temazepam", "tetrazepam", "clobazam"]
assert per_query[0] == hits
assert [names[i] for i in per_query[1]] == [
    "alprazolam", "triazolam", "midazolam"]
assert exact == [0]

The program prints:

diazepam, at least 0.5: ['diazepam', 'nordazepam', 'temazepam', 'tetrazepam', 'clobazam']
alprazolam, at least 0.5: ['alprazolam', 'triazolam', 'midazolam']
diazepam, at least 1.0: ['diazepam']

screen and screen_many do not check the threshold: a value above 1 or a NaN returns no hits, and a negative value returns every target, so pass a number from 0 to 1. warm_start does check it, but defaults to 0.0, which returns every target; always pass a threshold. Thread counts must be non-negative integers; screen and prewarm do not check this either.

docs.title: Streamed similarity screen
docs.text:
A library that is screened once does not need to sit in memory. smsd.stream_screen_smiles(query, targets, threshold) takes any one-shot iterable of molecules, such as a generator over the lines of a file, builds one chunk of targets at a time, screens it with the same fixed ECFP radius 2, 2048-bit fingerprints and yields the input index of each hit, in input order. Only one chunk is held at a time, and NumPy is not needed.

smsd.stream_screen_many_smiles screens several queries in bounded tiles of queries by targets and yields (query_index, target_index) pairs. The pairs come tile by tile, then by query, then by target: they are neither grouped by query nor ranked, so sort them when order matters.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533


def smiles_column(path):
    """Yield the first column of a SMILES file, one line at a time."""
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as stream:
        for line in stream:
            if line.strip():
                yield line.split()[0]


diazepam = NAMED["diazepam"]
alprazolam = NAMED["alprazolam"]
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "library.smi"
    path.write_text("".join(f"{text} {name}\n" for name, text in library),
                    encoding="utf-8")

    hits = list(smsd.stream_screen_smiles(
        diazepam, smiles_column(path), 0.5, chunk_size=100, num_threads=2))
    print("diazepam, at least 0.5, input indices:", hits)

    pairs = list(smsd.stream_screen_many_smiles(
        [diazepam, alprazolam], smiles_column(path), 0.5,
        target_chunk_size=4, query_chunk_size=2, num_threads=2))
    print("(query, input index) as streamed:", pairs)
    print("(query, input index) sorted:", sorted(pairs))

assert [names[i] for i in hits] == [
    "diazepam", "nordazepam", "temazepam", "tetrazepam", "clobazam"]
assert pairs == [(0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 9), (1, 10), (1, 11), (0, 13),
                 (1, 12)]
assert [index for query, index in sorted(pairs) if query == 0] == hits

The program prints:

diazepam, at least 0.5, input indices: [0, 1, 2, 9, 13]
(query, input index) as streamed: [(0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 9), (1, 10), (1, 11), (0, 13), (1, 12)]
(query, input index) sorted: [(0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (0, 9), (0, 13), (1, 10), (1, 11), (1, 12)]

With tiles of four targets, the diazepam hit at index 13 arrives after the alprazolam hits at indices 10 and 11, because it lies in a later tile; the sorted pairs match the in-memory results. An invalid molecule later in the input raises ValueError after the hits of earlier chunks have been yielded, and the message does not name the failing input, so check a doubtful file before a long run.

docs.title: Substructure screen with exact confirmation
docs.text:
Substructure.match_corpus(corpus) searches a TargetCorpus and returns one CorpusSearchResult per target, in library order. Targets that cannot contain the query are ruled out before matching, with a proof; every other target is searched exactly on the CPU. The decisions are the same as those of match_many over the whole library, and no prewarm() is needed.

Field Meaning target_index The position of the target in the corpus threshold_reached The query was found; result holds the match proven_below_threshold The query is proved absent, before matching or by a completed search result The SearchResult of the search, or None for a target ruled out before matching atom_upper_bound Always None for a substructure search

When both flags are false the outcome is unknown, for example after a search that stopped at its time limit; that is not proof of absence.

import itertools

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles)
# The 5-phenyl-1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one core
core = smsd.Substructure.find("O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2N1")

decisions = core.match_corpus(corpus, num_threads=2)
found = [names[d.target_index] for d in decisions if d.threshold_reached]
ruled_out = sum(d.result is None for d in decisions)
absent = [names[d.target_index] for d in decisions
          if d.result is not None and d.proven_below_threshold]
unknown = sum(not d.threshold_reached and not d.proven_below_threshold
              for d in decisions)
print("contain the core:", found)
print("ruled out before matching:", ruled_out, "| searched and absent:",
      absent, "| unknown:", unknown)

# STRICT aromaticity: an aromatic query bond needs an aromatic target bond.
options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.chemistry = smsd.ChemOptions().with_aromaticity_mode(
    smsd.AromaticityMode.STRICT)
strict = core.with_options(options).match_corpus(corpus, num_threads=2)
strict_found = [names[d.target_index] for d in strict if d.threshold_reached]
print("STRICT drops:", sorted(set(found) - set(strict_found)))

# A SMARTS query searches every target.
pattern = smsd.Substructure.smarts("O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2N1")
by_smarts = pattern.match_corpus(corpus, num_threads=2)
print("SMARTS: ruled out", sum(d.result is None for d in by_smarts),
      "| found", sum(d.threshold_reached for d in by_smarts))

assert len(found) == 9 and len(strict_found) == 8
assert set(found) - set(strict_found) == {"tetrazepam"}
assert "bromazepam" not in found and absent == ["bromazepam"]
assert ruled_out + 10 == len(decisions) and unknown == 0
assert all(d.result is not None for d in by_smarts)
assert [d.threshold_reached for d in by_smarts] == [
    d.threshold_reached for d in strict]
assert [r.found for r in core.match_many(corpus, num_threads=2)] == [
    d.threshold_reached for d in decisions]

The program prints:

contain the core: ['diazepam', 'nordazepam', 'temazepam', 'oxazepam', 'lorazepam', 'clonazepam', 'nitrazepam', 'flunitrazepam', 'tetrazepam']
ruled out before matching: 523 | searched and absent: ['bromazepam'] | unknown: 0
STRICT drops: ['tetrazepam']
SMARTS: ruled out 0 | found 8

Bromazepam is searched and found not to contain the core, because its pyridine nitrogen sits where the core has a phenyl carbon. Tetrazepam contains the core under the default chemistry, because the default FLEXIBLE aromaticity lets an aromatic query bond match a single or double bond, so its cyclohexene ring stands in for the phenyl ring. STRICT aromaticity requires an aromatic bond and drops it. The SMARTS form of the same pattern behaves like STRICT here, because a lower-case c in SMARTS is an aromatic carbon.

SMARTS queries, and searches with a node limit, a cancellation token or an immediate time limit, search every target without ruling any out first. ECFP similarity bits cannot rule out a substructure, so do not filter a substructure screen by fingerprint similarity. With smsd-cuda installed, gpu_prefilter=True asks the GPU to rule targets out; the decisions are the same, and the step falls back to the CPU on any failure (see Request the GPU for a corpus pre-screen).

docs.title: MCS-similarity screen
docs.text:
MCS similarity here is the atom-count Tanimoto of the maximum common substructure: common / (query atoms + target atoms - common). Computing the MCS for every target is the expensive step, so screen first. smsd.screen_targets(query, targets, threshold) computes a fast upper bound on that score for every target and returns the indices that reach the threshold. Under the same chemistry options it never rejects a target that can reach the threshold. It needs no prewarm(). The bound can keep targets that fall short, so run the exact MCS on the survivors and keep the results that are optimal and reach the threshold.

MCS.match_corpus(corpus, minimum_atoms) answers a related question for each target: whether the MCS with the query has at least minimum_atoms atoms. It returns the same CorpusSearchResult fields as the substructure screen, with atom_upper_bound holding an upper bound on the MCS atom count where one was computed.

import itertools

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles)
query = smsd.parse_smiles(NAMED["diazepam"])

# 1. A fast upper bound that never drops a target able to reach 0.8.
candidates = smsd.screen_targets(query, corpus, 0.8, num_threads=2)

# 2. The exact MCS on the survivors, scored as an atom-count Tanimoto.
search = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_timeout(1000)
results = search.match_many([smiles[i] for i in candidates], num_threads=2)
confirmed = []
for index, result in zip(candidates, results):
    target_atoms = smsd.parse_smiles(smiles[index]).n
    common = result.best.atom_count if result.found else 0
    score = common / (query.n + target_atoms - common)
    if result.optimal and score >= 0.8:
        confirmed.append((names[index], common, f"{score:.3f}"))
print("bound kept:", [names[i] for i in candidates])
print("exact MCS, at least 0.8:")
for name, common, score in confirmed:
    print(f"  {name:<12} {common} common atoms  {score}")

# 3. Or one atom-count decision per target: an MCS of at least 18 atoms.
decisions = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_timeout(1000).match_corpus(
    corpus, 18, num_threads=2)
print("MCS of 18 atoms or more:",
      [names[d.target_index] for d in decisions if d.threshold_reached])

# Default chemistry lets an aromatic query bond pair with a single or double
# bond, so the cyclohexene ring of tetrazepam stands in for the phenyl ring.
strict = smsd.MCS.Options()
strict.chemistry = smsd.ChemOptions().with_aromaticity_mode(
    smsd.AromaticityMode.STRICT)
strict.timeout_ms = 1000
result = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_options(strict).match(NAMED["tetrazepam"])
target_atoms = smsd.parse_smiles(NAMED["tetrazepam"]).n
common = result.best.atom_count
score = common / (query.n + target_atoms - common)
print("tetrazepam with STRICT aromaticity:", common, "common atoms",
      f"{score:.3f}")

assert result.optimal and (common, f"{score:.3f}") == (14, "0.538")
assert len(candidates) == 9 and len(confirmed) == 7
assert ("tetrazepam", 20, "1.000") in confirmed
assert sum(d.threshold_reached for d in decisions) == 12
assert not any(not d.threshold_reached and not d.proven_below_threshold
               for d in decisions)

The program prints:

bound kept: ['diazepam', 'nordazepam', 'temazepam', 'oxazepam', 'lorazepam', 'clonazepam', 'tetrazepam', 'alprazolam', 'clobazam']
exact MCS, at least 0.8:
  diazepam     20 common atoms  1.000
  nordazepam   19 common atoms  0.950
  temazepam    20 common atoms  0.952
  oxazepam     19 common atoms  0.905
  lorazepam    19 common atoms  0.864
  tetrazepam   20 common atoms  1.000
  alprazolam   19 common atoms  0.826
MCS of 18 atoms or more: ['diazepam', 'nordazepam', 'temazepam', 'oxazepam', 'lorazepam', 'clonazepam', 'nitrazepam', 'flunitrazepam', 'tetrazepam', 'alprazolam', 'triazolam', 'midazolam']
tetrazepam with STRICT aromaticity: 14 common atoms 0.538

The bound kept nine targets, and the exact MCS confirmed seven: clonazepam and clobazam fall short of 0.8. Tetrazepam reaches 1.000 for the same reason as in the substructure screen; with STRICT aromaticity it shares 14 atoms with diazepam. The guarantee of screen_targets holds for the atom-count Tanimoto only, not for bond counts, MCES or weighted scores, and only when the exact search uses the same ChemOptions. A result that is not optimal, because its search stopped at the time limit, gives a lower bound on the common atoms.

docs.title: Save the hits
docs.text:
MolGraph.name and MolGraph.properties can be set on any graph, and smsd.write_sdf writes the name as the record title and every property as an SD field. batch_similarity uses the same ECFP radius 2, 2048-bit fingerprints as TargetCorpus.screen, so it supplies the scores for the hits. Format scores as strings with three decimal places.

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

diazepam = NAMED["diazepam"]
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles)
corpus.prewarm(num_threads=2)
hits = corpus.screen(diazepam, 0.5, num_threads=2)  # indices, no scores

# batch_similarity uses the same ECFP4 bits and returns the scores.
scored = smsd.batch_similarity(diazepam, [smiles[i] for i in hits])
graphs = []
for position, score in scored:  # most similar first
    graph = smsd.parse_smiles(smiles[hits[position]])
    graph.name = names[hits[position]]
    graph.properties = {"TANIMOTO": f"{score:.3f}"}
    graphs.append(graph)

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "hits.sdf"
    smsd.write_sdf(graphs, path)
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    saved = smsd.read_sdf(path)
for graph in saved:
    print(f"{graph.name:<12} TANIMOTO {graph.properties['TANIMOTO']}")

assert "> <TANIMOTO>" in text
assert hits == [index for index, score in
                sorted(smsd.batch_similarity(diazepam, smiles)) if score >= 0.5]
assert scored[-1][1] == 0.5  # clobazam: kept, as the threshold is inclusive
assert [graph.name for graph in saved] == [
    "diazepam", "temazepam", "tetrazepam", "nordazepam", "clobazam"]
assert all(float(graph.properties["TANIMOTO"]) >= 0.5 for graph in saved)

The program prints:

diazepam     TANIMOTO 1.000
temazepam    TANIMOTO 0.582
tetrazepam   TANIMOTO 0.542
nordazepam   TANIMOTO 0.528
clobazam     TANIMOTO 0.500

Clobazam scores exactly 0.500 and is kept, because the threshold is inclusive.

docs.title: End-to-end example
docs.text:
The program below runs the similarity, substructure and MCS-similarity screens over the library and writes the molecules that pass all three to an SD file, with both scores as fields:

import itertools
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

NAMED = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "aspirin": "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "salicylic acid": "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
    "paracetamol": "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "ibuprofen": "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "naproxen": "COc1ccc2cc(ccc2c1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "caffeine": "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "phenol": "Oc1ccccc1",
}
GROUPS = ["C", "CC", "OC", "N", "O", "F", "Cl", "C(=O)O"]
library = list(NAMED.items()) + [
    (f"GEN-{number:03d}", f"c1c({a})cc({b})cc1{c}")
    for number, (a, b, c) in enumerate(itertools.product(GROUPS, repeat=3))
]
names = [name for name, _ in library]
smiles = [text for _, text in library]
assert len(library) == 533

QUERY = NAMED["diazepam"]
CORE = "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2N1"  # benzodiazepinone core

# 1. Prepare the library once; keep the names beside it.
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(smiles)
corpus.prewarm(num_threads=2)

# 2. Similarity: ECFP4 Tanimoto of at least 0.5.
similar = corpus.screen(QUERY, 0.5, num_threads=2)

# 3. Substructure: exact decisions for the core.
decisions = smsd.Substructure.find(CORE).match_corpus(corpus, num_threads=2)
with_core = [d.target_index for d in decisions if d.threshold_reached]

# 4. MCS similarity: bound first, then the exact MCS on the survivors.
query = smsd.parse_smiles(QUERY)
candidates = smsd.screen_targets(query, corpus, 0.8, num_threads=2)
results = smsd.MCS.find(query).with_timeout(1000).match_many(
    [smiles[i] for i in candidates], num_threads=2)
mcs_scores = {}
for index, result in zip(candidates, results):
    common = result.best.atom_count if result.found else 0
    score = common / (query.n + smsd.parse_smiles(smiles[index]).n - common)
    if result.optimal and score >= 0.8:
        mcs_scores[index] = score

# 5. Write the molecules that pass all three screens, with their scores.
fingerprint_scores = dict(smsd.batch_similarity(QUERY, smiles))
selected = [i for i in similar if i in with_core and i in mcs_scores]
graphs = []
for index in selected:
    graph = smsd.parse_smiles(smiles[index])
    graph.name = names[index]
    graph.properties = {"TANIMOTO": f"{fingerprint_scores[index]:.3f}",
                        "MCS_TANIMOTO": f"{mcs_scores[index]:.3f}"}
    graphs.append(graph)
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "hits.sdf"
    smsd.write_sdf(graphs, path)
    saved = smsd.read_sdf(path)

print("similar:", len(similar), "| core:", len(with_core),
      "| MCS:", len(mcs_scores), "| all three:", len(saved))
for graph in saved:
    print(f"  {graph.name:<12} TANIMOTO {graph.properties['TANIMOTO']}"
          f"  MCS_TANIMOTO {graph.properties['MCS_TANIMOTO']}")

counts = (len(similar), len(with_core), len(mcs_scores), len(saved))
assert counts == (5, 9, 7, 4)
assert [graph.name for graph in saved] == [names[i] for i in selected]
assert names[selected[0]] == "diazepam"

The program prints:

similar: 5 | core: 9 | MCS: 7 | all three: 4
  diazepam     TANIMOTO 1.000  MCS_TANIMOTO 1.000
  nordazepam   TANIMOTO 0.528  MCS_TANIMOTO 0.950
  temazepam    TANIMOTO 0.582  MCS_TANIMOTO 0.952
  tetrazepam   TANIMOTO 0.542  MCS_TANIMOTO 1.000

Clobazam passes the fingerprint screen but has neither the core nor an MCS similarity of 0.8; oxazepam and lorazepam have the core and a high MCS similarity, but their fingerprints fall below 0.5. The library screening notebook runs the same steps cell by cell, with a packed index and clustering.

docs.title: TargetCorpus
docs.text:
Member Returns Meaning TargetCorpus.from_smiles(targets) TargetCorpus Captures SMILES strings, MolGraph objects or RDKit molecules from any iterable add_target(target), add_targets(targets) None Adds targets; the corpus then needs prewarm() again prewarm(*, num_threads=0) None Computes the screening fingerprints and graph invariants is_prewarmed bool Whether prewarm() has run since the last addition len(corpus) int The number of targets screen(query, threshold, *, num_threads=0) list[int] ECFP radius 2, 2048-bit Tanimoto hits, at least threshold, in target order screen_many(queries, threshold, *, num_threads=0) list[list[int]] One hit list per query, in query order screen_targets_many(queries, threshold, chemistry=None, *, num_threads=0) list[list[int]] The MCS-similarity bound for each query; no prewarm() needed smsd.warm_start(corpus, query, threshold=0.0, *, num_threads=0) list[int] Prepares the corpus if needed, then screens; the threshold is checked

A TargetCorpus cannot be saved or pickled. num_threads=0 uses the OpenMP default, which OMP_NUM_THREADS sets.

docs.title: Streamed screens
docs.text:
stream_screen_smiles(query, targets, threshold, *, chunk_size=4096, num_threads=0) and stream_screen_many_smiles(queries, targets, threshold, *, target_chunk_size=4096, query_chunk_size=64, max_queries=4096, num_threads=0) take these arguments:

Name Type Default Meaning query, queries molecule, iterable of molecules required SMILES strings, MolGraph objects or RDKit molecules targets iterable required Read once; a generator is suitable threshold float required Inclusive; finite and from 0 to 1, otherwise ValueError chunk_size int 4096 Targets per chunk; values above 1,048,576 are reduced to 1,048,576 target_chunk_size int 4096 Targets per tile, from 1 to 1,048,576 query_chunk_size int 64 Queries per tile, from 1 to 1,048,576; a tile may hold at most 1,048,576 query and target pairs max_queries int 4096 Most queries accepted, from 1 to 1,048,576; more raise ValueError num_threads int 0 Threads per chunk; 0 uses the OpenMP default

With no queries, stream_screen_many_smiles yields nothing and does not read the targets.

docs.title: screen_targets
docs.text:
smsd.screen_targets(query, targets, threshold, chemistry=None, *, num_threads=0) returns the indices of the targets whose bound reaches the threshold, in target order.

Name Type Default Meaning query molecule required SMILES string, MolGraph or RDKit molecule targets list or TargetCorpus required A TargetCorpus is converted once and reused threshold float required Inclusive atom-count Tanimoto threshold; not checked chemistry ChemOptions or None None None means ChemOptions(); use the options of the exact search num_threads int 0 Non-negative; 0 uses the OpenMP default

docs.title: batch_similarity
docs.text:
smsd.batch_similarity(query, targets, fp_size=2048, radius=2) returns (index, Tanimoto) pairs, most similar first; equal scores keep their input order.

Name Type Default Meaning query molecule required SMILES string or MolGraph targets list required Every target is fingerprinted on each call, so keep the list small fp_size int 2048 Fingerprint width in bits radius int 2 ECFP radius

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Hits do not depend on the thread count or the chunk sizes. Only the order of the pairs from stream_screen_many_smiles and FingerprintCorpus.screen_many depends on the tile sizes.
  • smsd.similarity(a, b) is the MCS-similarity bound of screen_targets, the same value as smsd.similarity_upper_bound, not a fingerprint score.
  • smsd.prewarm(mol) caches the invariants of a molecule that is searched many times, such as a query run against several libraries.
  • A parse error in TargetCorpus.from_smiles, the streamed screens or FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles does not name the failing input.
  • smsd.to_smiles raises ValueError for the few stereo records it cannot write; keep those records in SD form. smsd.canonical_smiles is a deprecated alias of smsd.to_smiles.
  • A substructure or MCS screen needs the whole TargetCorpus in memory; only the fingerprint screens stream.
  • Speed depends on the data, the hardware and the thread count. Time a representative sample on your own machine, and compare the results as well as the times.

docs.title: SMARTS queries
docs.text: A SMARTS pattern describes the atoms and bonds a match must have, rather than a whole molecule. SMSD patterns follow standard SMARTS semantics. This chapter lists the primitives and operators SMSD accepts, shows each with a target it matches and one it does not, and covers recursion, components, stereochemistry, the chemistry options that apply, limits, error messages and common traps. Searching with a pattern works as described in Substructure search.

docs.title: Compile and run a pattern
docs.text:
Substructure.smarts(pattern) compiles a pattern once. The compiled query offers the same calls as a molecule query: match, match_all and match_many. An empty or non-string pattern, or one that does not parse, raises ValueError with the parser's message.

import smsd

hydroxyl = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[OX2H]")   # hydroxyl oxygen
targets = ["CCO",       # ethanol
           "COC",       # dimethyl ether
           "CC(=O)O"]   # acetic acid

print("ethanol:", hydroxyl.match("CCO").found)
assert hydroxyl.match("CCO").found
found = [result.found for result in hydroxyl.match_many(targets, num_threads=1)]
print("ethanol, dimethyl ether, acetic acid:", found)
assert found == [True, False, True]

every = hydroxyl.with_timeout(1000).match_all("OCCO", limit=10)   # ethylene glycol
print("ethylene glycol:", len(every.matches), every.status.name)
assert len(every.matches) == 2 and every.complete

errors = {"": "SMARTS must be a non-empty string",
          "CC-": "Trailing bond in SMARTS",
          "[C": "Expected ']' in bracket atom at pos 2",
          "C(": "Unmatched '(' in SMARTS"}
for pattern, message in errors.items():
    try:
        smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
    except ValueError as error:
        print(f"{pattern!r:6} -> {error}")
        assert str(error) == message
    else:
        raise AssertionError(pattern)

The program prints:

ethanol: True
ethanol, dimethyl ether, acetic acid: [True, False, True]
ethylene glycol: 2 COMPLETED
''     -> SMARTS must be a non-empty string
'CC-'  -> Trailing bond in SMARTS
'[C'   -> Expected ']' in bracket atom at pos 2
'C('   -> Unmatched '(' in SMARTS

docs.title: Atom primitives
docs.text:
Inside square brackets, an atom is described by one or more primitives. An element symbol outside brackets, such as C, c or Cl, is the same as the symbol in brackets.

Primitive Meaning Example Matches Does not match * Any atom C*O CCO CO #n Atomic number, aromatic or not [#7] c1ccncc1 c1ccccc1 Upper-case symbol Aliphatic atom of that element [C] CC c1ccccc1 Lower-case symbol Aromatic atom of that element [c] c1ccccc1 C1CCCCC1 a Aromatic atom [a] c1ccncc1 C1CCCCC1 A Aliphatic atom [N;A] CN c1ccncc1 D<n> Explicit connections, counting explicit hydrogen atoms [D3] CC(C)C CCCC X<n> Total connections, implicit hydrogens included [CX4] CC C=C d<n> Heavy-atom neighbours [C;d3] CC(C)C CCC v<n> Valence, counting bond orders and hydrogens [Cv4] CC [CH3] H<n> Attached hydrogens [CH3] CC C=C R In a ring [R] C1CC1 CC R<n> Number of rings that contain the atom; R0 is not in a ring [R2] c1ccc2ccccc2c1 c1ccccc1 r<n> The smallest ring that contains the atom has n atoms [c;r5] c1ccoc1 c1ccccc1 x<n> Ring bonds [Cx2] C1CCCCC1 CCC z<n> Neighbours that are neither carbon nor hydrogen [Cz2] OC(N)C OCC Z<n> Aliphatic neighbours that are neither carbon nor hydrogen [Z1] CCO Cc1ccccn1 ^<n> Hybridisation: 0 to 5 for s, sp, sp2, sp3, sp3d and sp3d2 [C^1] CC#N CC=C +, -, +<n>, -<n> Formal charge [#7;+] C[N+](C)(C)C CN Mass number Isotope [13C] [13CH4] C [H] A hydrogen atom, not a hydrogen count [H] [H]C C :n Atom class; a label that does not restrict the match [C:1]O CO CN

Recursive SMARTS, $(...), and the chirality primitives @, @@, @? and @@? are described below. The program below checks every row of the table.

import smsd

rows = [
    ("C*O", "CCO", "CO"),
    ("[#7]", "c1ccncc1", "c1ccccc1"),
    ("[C]", "CC", "c1ccccc1"),
    ("[c]", "c1ccccc1", "C1CCCCC1"),
    ("[a]", "c1ccncc1", "C1CCCCC1"),
    ("[N;A]", "CN", "c1ccncc1"),
    ("[D3]", "CC(C)C", "CCCC"),
    ("[CX4]", "CC", "C=C"),
    ("[C;d3]", "CC(C)C", "CCC"),
    ("[Cv4]", "CC", "[CH3]"),
    ("[CH3]", "CC", "C=C"),
    ("[R]", "C1CC1", "CC"),
    ("[R2]", "c1ccc2ccccc2c1", "c1ccccc1"),
    ("[c;r5]", "c1ccoc1", "c1ccccc1"),
    ("[Cx2]", "C1CCCCC1", "CCC"),
    ("[Cz2]", "OC(N)C", "OCC"),
    ("[Z1]", "CCO", "Cc1ccccn1"),
    ("[C^1]", "CC#N", "CC=C"),
    ("[#7;+]", "C[N+](C)(C)C", "CN"),
    ("[13C]", "[13CH4]", "C"),
    ("[H]", "[H]C", "C"),
    ("[C:1]O", "CO", "CN"),
]
for pattern, hit, miss in rows:
    query = smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
    outcome = (query.match(hit).found, query.match(miss).found)
    print(f"{pattern:8} {hit:15} {outcome[0]!s:5} {miss:10} {outcome[1]}")
    assert outcome == (True, False)

The program prints:

C*O      CCO             True  CO         False
[#7]     c1ccncc1        True  c1ccccc1   False
[C]      CC              True  c1ccccc1   False
[c]      c1ccccc1        True  C1CCCCC1   False
[a]      c1ccncc1        True  C1CCCCC1   False
[N;A]    CN              True  c1ccncc1   False
[D3]     CC(C)C          True  CCCC       False
[CX4]    CC              True  C=C        False
[C;d3]   CC(C)C          True  CCC        False
[Cv4]    CC              True  [CH3]      False
[CH3]    CC              True  C=C        False
[R]      C1CC1           True  CC         False
[R2]     c1ccc2ccccc2c1  True  c1ccccc1   False
[c;r5]   c1ccoc1         True  c1ccccc1   False
[Cx2]    C1CCCCC1        True  CCC        False
[Cz2]    OC(N)C          True  OCC        False
[Z1]     CCO             True  Cc1ccccn1  False
[C^1]    CC#N            True  CC=C       False
[#7;+]   C[N+](C)(C)C    True  CN         False
[13C]    [13CH4]         True  C          False
[H]      [H]C            True  C          False
[C:1]O   CO              True  CN         False

docs.title: Bond primitives and operators
docs.text:
Bond Meaning Example Matches Does not match - Single C-C CC C=C = Double C=O CC=O CCO # Triple C#N CC#N CC=N : Aromatic [#6]:[#7] c1ccncc1 Nc1ccccc1 ~ Any bond [#6]~[#7] CC#N CCO @ Ring bond C@C C1CCCCC1 CCCCCC Unwritten Single or aromatic CC CC C=C /, \ Double-bond configuration See Stereochemistry /?, \? That configuration or none See Stereochemistry

Operators combine primitives in atom and bond expressions. In order of precedence, from the highest:

Operator Meaning Example Matches Does not match ! Not [!#6;!#1] CCO CC & or nothing And [N,O&H1] CN(C)C CC , Or [C,N]=O CN=O CS=O ; And, with low precedence [N,O;H1] CNC CN(C)C

[N,O&H1] reads as nitrogen, or oxygen with one hydrogen, so it matches the nitrogen of trimethylamine. [N,O;H1] reads as nitrogen or oxygen, with one hydrogen, so it does not.

import smsd

rows = [
    ("C-C", "CC", "C=C"),
    ("C=O", "CC=O", "CCO"),
    ("C#N", "CC#N", "CC=N"),
    ("[#6]:[#7]", "c1ccncc1", "Nc1ccccc1"),
    ("[#6]~[#7]", "CC#N", "CCO"),
    ("C@C", "C1CCCCC1", "CCCCCC"),
    ("CC", "CC", "C=C"),
    ("[!#6;!#1]", "CCO", "CC"),
    ("[N,O&H1]", "CN(C)C", "CC"),
    ("[C,N]=O", "CN=O", "CS=O"),
    ("[N,O;H1]", "CNC", "CN(C)C"),
]
for pattern, hit, miss in rows:
    query = smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
    outcome = (query.match(hit).found, query.match(miss).found)
    print(f"{pattern:10} {hit:9} {outcome[0]!s:5} {miss:10} {outcome[1]}")
    assert outcome == (True, False)

The program prints:

C-C        CC        True  C=C        False
C=O        CC=O      True  CCO        False
C#N        CC#N      True  CC=N       False
[#6]:[#7]  c1ccncc1  True  Nc1ccccc1  False
[#6]~[#7]  CC#N      True  CCO        False
C@C        C1CCCCC1  True  CCCCCC     False
CC         CC        True  C=C        False
[!#6;!#1]  CCO       True  CC         False
[N,O&H1]   CN(C)C    True  CC         False
[C,N]=O    CN=O      True  CS=O       False
[N,O;H1]   CNC       True  CN(C)C     False

docs.title: Recursive SMARTS
docs.text:
$(...) matches an atom that is the first atom of the enclosed pattern, so it tests the atom's surroundings without adding them to the match. Alternatives are joined with ,. Recursive patterns may be nested up to 20 levels deep; Python cannot change this limit, and a deeper pattern raises ValueError.

import smsd

# The nitrogen of an amide: bonded to a carbon that bears a double-bonded oxygen
amide_n = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[$(C=O)]N")
print("acetamide:", amide_n.match("CC(=O)N").found,
      "ethylamine:", amide_n.match("CCN").found)
assert amide_n.match("CC(=O)N").found and not amide_n.match("CCN").found

# A carboxyl carbon or a nitrile carbon
either = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[$(C(=O)O),$(C#N)]")
names = {"CC(=O)O": "acetic acid", "CC#N": "acetonitrile", "CC=O": "acetaldehyde"}
found = {name: either.match(smiles).found for smiles, name in names.items()}
print(found)
assert found == {"acetic acid": True, "acetonitrile": True, "acetaldehyde": False}


def nested(depth):
    pattern = "C"
    for _ in range(depth):
        pattern = f"[$({pattern})]"
    return pattern


deepest = smsd.Substructure.smarts(nested(20)).match("C").found
print("depth 20:", deepest)
assert deepest
try:
    smsd.Substructure.smarts(nested(21))
except ValueError as error:
    print("depth 21:", error)
    assert "maximum depth of 20" in str(error)

The program prints:

acetamide: True ethylamine: False
{'acetic acid': True, 'acetonitrile': True, 'acetaldehyde': False}
depth 20: True
depth 21: Recursive SMARTS nesting exceeds maximum depth of 20

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
A dot separates pattern components. Each component may match anywhere, with no shared atoms. Parentheses around the whole pattern or around components group them by target component:

  • (C.C) requires both atoms in the same target component.
  • (C).(C) requires them in different target components.
import smsd

rows = [("C.C", ["CC", "C.C"], [True, True]),
        ("(C.C)", ["CC.CC", "C.C"], [True, False]),
        ("(C).(C)", ["CC", "C.C"], [False, True])]
for pattern, targets, expected in rows:
    query = smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
    found = [query.match(target).found for target in targets]
    print(f"{pattern:8}", dict(zip(targets, found)))
    assert found == expected

The program prints:

C.C      {'CC': True, 'C.C': True}
(C.C)    {'CC.CC': True, 'C.C': False}
(C).(C)  {'CC': False, 'C.C': True}

docs.title: Stereochemistry
docs.text:
Stereochemistry written in a pattern is always enforced; use_chirality and use_bond_stereo are not needed. A pattern with a configuration does not match a target that leaves it unspecified, unless the pattern uses @?, @@?, /? or \?, which also accept no configuration. A double bond with a direction written on one side only places no constraint.

A tetrahedral tag is read relative to the written order of the neighbours, as in SMILES. To compare a pattern with a target, write both with the neighbours in the same order.

import smsd

trans = smsd.Substructure.smarts("F/C=C/F")
targets = {"trans": "F/C=C/F", "cis": "F/C=C\\F", "unspecified": "FC=CF"}
found = {name: trans.match(smiles).found for name, smiles in targets.items()}
print("F/C=C/F:", found)
assert found == {"trans": True, "cis": False, "unspecified": False}

either = smsd.Substructure.smarts("F/C=C/?F")
found = {name: either.match(smiles).found for name, smiles in targets.items()}
print("F/C=C/?F:", found)
assert found == {"trans": True, "cis": False, "unspecified": True}

one_side = smsd.Substructure.smarts("F/C=CF")
found = {name: one_side.match(smiles).found for name, smiles in targets.items()}
print("F/C=CF:", found)
assert found == {"trans": True, "cis": True, "unspecified": True}

centres = {"@": "[C@H](F)(Cl)Br", "@@": "[C@@H](F)(Cl)Br", "none": "C(F)(Cl)Br"}
for pattern in ("[C@H](F)(Cl)Br", "[C@?H](F)(Cl)Br"):
    query = smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
    found = {name: query.match(smiles).found for name, smiles in centres.items()}
    print(f"{pattern}:", found)
    assert found["@"] and not found["@@"] and found["none"] == ("?" in pattern)

The program prints:

F/C=C/F: {'trans': True, 'cis': False, 'unspecified': False}
F/C=C/?F: {'trans': True, 'cis': False, 'unspecified': True}
F/C=CF: {'trans': True, 'cis': True, 'unspecified': True}
[C@H](F)(Cl)Br: {'@': True, '@@': False, 'none': False}
[C@?H](F)(Cl)Br: {'@': True, '@@': False, 'none': True}

docs.title: Which options apply
docs.text:
A pattern states its own element, charge, hydrogen count, aromaticity, bond order and stereochemistry. Of the chemistry options, a SMARTS query therefore reads only complete_rings_only, together with Substructure.Options.induced. The other options have no effect on a pattern: put such constraints into the pattern itself. The time limit, node limit and cancellation token apply as usual.

import smsd


def found(pattern, target, induced=False, **fields):
    options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
    options.induced = induced
    for name, value in fields.items():
        setattr(options.chemistry, name, value)
    return smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern).with_options(options).match(target).found


rows = [
    ("C-C in ethene", "C-C", "C=C",
     dict(match_bond_order=smsd.BondOrderMode.ANY), (False, False)),
    ("C[N] in methylammonium", "C[N]", "C[NH3+]",
     dict(match_formal_charge=True), (True, True)),
    ("CCC in cyclohexane", "CCC", "C1CCCCC1",
     dict(ring_matches_ring_only=True), (True, True)),
    ("CCC in cyclohexane", "CCC", "C1CCCCC1",
     dict(complete_rings_only=True), (True, False)),
    ("CCC in cyclopropane", "CCC", "C1CC1", dict(induced=True), (True, False)),
]
for label, pattern, target, fields, expected in rows:
    outcome = (found(pattern, target), found(pattern, target, **fields))
    setting = ", ".join(fields)
    print(f"{label:23} {setting:23} {outcome[0]!s:5} -> {outcome[1]}")
    assert outcome == expected

The program prints:

C-C in ethene           match_bond_order        False -> False
C[N] in methylammonium  match_formal_charge     True  -> True
CCC in cyclohexane      ring_matches_ring_only  True  -> True
CCC in cyclohexane      complete_rings_only     True  -> False
CCC in cyclopropane     induced                 True  -> False

docs.title: Writing SMARTS from a molecule
docs.text:
smsd.to_smarts(molecule, ...) writes a molecule as SMARTS. Its switches choose which properties the pattern fixes:

Argument Default Adds include_aromaticity True a or A on each atom include_charge True The formal charge of each charged atom include_ring_member False R or !R on each atom include_h_count False H<n> on each atom include_isotope False The mass number of each labelled atom

Match.to_smarts(query, chemistry=None) writes only the matched atoms and bonds of a result. The pattern encodes the matching rules of chemistry, or of the default options when it is omitted, and a rule that SMARTS cannot express, such as tautomer matching, raises ValueError. An MCS can be turned into a pattern in one step with MCS.match_with_smarts; see Maximum common substructure and SMARTS export.

import smsd

phenol = "c1ccccc1O"
written = [
    (smsd.to_smarts(phenol),
     "[#6;a]:1(:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:1)-[#8;A]"),
    (smsd.to_smarts(phenol, include_ring_member=True),
     "[#6;a;R]:1(:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:1)-[#8;A;!R]"),
    (smsd.to_smarts("C[NH3+]"), "[#6;A]-[#7;A;+]"),
    (smsd.to_smarts("C[NH3+]", include_charge=False), "[#6;A]-[#7;A]"),
    (smsd.to_smarts("[13CH4]"), "[#6;A]"),
    (smsd.to_smarts("[13CH4]", include_isotope=True), "[13#6;A]"),
]
for text, expected in written:
    print(text)
    assert text == expected

# Acetaldehyde found in propanoic acid, written as SMARTS
result = smsd.Substructure.find("CC=O").match("CCC(=O)O")
pattern = result.best.to_smarts("CC=O")
print(pattern)
assert pattern == "[#6]-,:[#6]=,:[#8]"
assert smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern).match("CCC(=O)O").found

The program prints:

[#6;a]:1(:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:[#6;a]:1)-[#8;A]
[#6;a;R]:1(:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:[#6;a;R]:1)-[#8;A;!R]
[#6;A]-[#7;A;+]
[#6;A]-[#7;A]
[#6;A]
[13#6;A]
[#6]-,:[#6]=,:[#8]

Under the default flexible aromaticity, aromatic bonds also match single or double bonds, so the exported bonds read -,: and =,:. To fix hydrogen counts, see Hydrogen counts.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Limit Value Pattern length, in characters 100,000 Atoms, counting those inside recursive SMARTS 10,000 Expression nodes in the whole pattern 100,000 Expression nodes in one atom or bond expression 10,000 Nesting depth of recursive SMARTS 20

A pattern beyond a limit raises ValueError, for example SMARTS exceeds the maximum length of 100000 characters.

docs.title: Unsupported syntax
docs.text:
• The implicit-hydrogen primitive h is not supported. [Ch2] raises ValueError ("Unknown aromatic element in SMARTS: h"); write H<n> or X<n> instead.
  • Named predicates such as $isHalogen are not accepted in Python. Write the definition as SMARTS, using $(...) where it describes an atom's surroundings. The C++ and Java libraries can expand named predicates; see C++ SMARTS and Java prepared searches.
import smsd

errors = {"[Ch2]": "Unknown aromatic element in SMARTS: h",
          "[$isHalogen]": "Expected '(' after '$' in recursive SMARTS"}
for pattern, message in errors.items():
    try:
        smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
    except ValueError as error:
        print(f"{pattern:13} -> {error}")
        assert str(error) == message
    else:
        raise AssertionError(pattern)

halogen = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[F,Cl,Br,I]")
found = [halogen.match(smiles).found for smiles in ("CCl", "CBr", "CO")]
print("halogen in chloromethane, bromomethane, methanol:", found)
assert found == [True, True, False]

The program prints:

[Ch2]         -> Unknown aromatic element in SMARTS: h
[$isHalogen]  -> Expected '(' after '$' in recursive SMARTS
halogen in chloromethane, bromomethane, methanol: [True, True, False]

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• SMARTS C is an aliphatic carbon. SMSD perceives aromaticity when it reads a molecule, so Kekulé input can become aromatic: caffeine written as CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C has aromatic carbonyl carbons, and C(=O)[NX3] misses them. Write [#6] when aromaticity should not matter.
  • Inside brackets, a two-letter element symbol takes precedence: [Cd3] is read as cadmium, not as carbon with d3. Write [C;d3] for a carbon with three heavy-atom neighbours.
  • A molecule written as SMARTS is stricter than the same molecule used as a query. The pattern's lower-case atoms must be aromatic, while a molecule query with the default flexible aromaticity also matches non-aromatic rings.
  • D<n> counts explicit hydrogen atoms, such as those written [H], while d<n> counts heavy atoms only.

The program below shows the first and third notes on shared example data.

import smsd

caffeine = "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C"
print("read as:", smsd.to_smiles(caffeine))
assert smsd.to_smiles(caffeine) == "Cn1c2c(c(n(C)c1=O)=O)n(C)cn2"
aliphatic = smsd.Substructure.smarts("C(=O)[NX3]").match(caffeine).found
any_carbon = smsd.Substructure.smarts("[#6](=O)[#7X3]").match(caffeine).found
print("C(=O)[NX3]:", aliphatic, "[#6](=O)[#7X3]:", any_carbon)
assert not aliphatic and any_carbon

benzodiazepines = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
}
core = "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2N1"   # 5-phenyl-1,4-benzodiazepin-2-one
names, targets = list(benzodiazepines), list(benzodiazepines.values())
hits = {}
for label, query in (("molecule query", smsd.Substructure.find(core)),
                     ("SMARTS", smsd.Substructure.smarts(core))):
    results = query.match_many(targets, num_threads=1)
    assert all(result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED for result in results)
    hits[label] = [name for name, result in zip(names, results) if result.found]
    print(f"{label}: {len(hits[label])} hits")
missing = sorted(set(hits["molecule query"]) - set(hits["SMARTS"]))
print("found only by the molecule query:", missing)
assert len(hits["molecule query"]) == 9 and missing == ["tetrazepam"]

The program prints:

read as: Cn1c2c(c(n(C)c1=O)=O)n(C)cn2
C(=O)[NX3]: False [#6](=O)[#7X3]: True
molecule query: 9 hits
SMARTS: 8 hits
found only by the molecule query: ['tetrazepam']
