docs.title: Substructure search
docs.text:
A substructure search asks whether a query occurs whole inside a target, and where. SMSD prepares the query once and then searches one target, every embedding in one target, a list of targets or a captured corpus. Every call returns a SearchResult that holds the matches together with the reason the search ended, so an empty result proves absence only when its status is COMPLETED and optimal is true.

This chapter covers molecule queries in Python. The SMARTS syntax is described in SMARTS queries, and the exhaustive API list is in the Python guide.

docs.title: Prepare a query
docs.text:
• Substructure.find(query) prepares a molecule query from a SMILES string, a MolGraph or an RDKit molecule. The query graph is copied, so later changes to the input do not reach it.
  • Substructure.smarts(pattern) compiles a SMARTS pattern once.

A prepared query is immutable. with_options, with_timeout and with_induced return a new query with a copy of the options and leave the original unchanged. Searches release the global interpreter lock, so several threads can share one prepared query.

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import smsd

# The same phenol query, prepared from SMILES, from a MolGraph and as SMARTS
queries = {
    "SMILES": smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1O"),
    "MolGraph": smsd.Substructure.find(smsd.parse_smiles("c1ccccc1O")),
    "SMARTS": smsd.Substructure.smarts("c1ccccc1[OX2H]"),
}
bounded = queries["SMILES"].with_timeout(500)
assert bounded is not queries["SMILES"]

targets = ["CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",          # paracetamol
           "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",  # ibuprofen
           "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O"]             # salicylic acid

# One prepared query serves several threads at once
with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
    for name, query in queries.items():
        found = [result.found for result in pool.map(query.match, targets)]
        print(f"{name:8}", found)
        assert found == [True, False, True]

The program prints:

SMILES   [True, False, True]
MolGraph [True, False, True]
SMARTS   [True, False, True]

docs.title: Find one embedding
docs.text:
match(target) returns at most one embedding. atom_mapping maps each query atom index to a target atom index, in each input's own numbering (see Getting started). score is the number of query atoms when a match is found and 0.0 otherwise.

import smsd

query = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1O")   # phenol
result = query.match("CC(C)(C)c1ccc(O)cc1")   # 4-tert-butylphenol

print("found:", result.found)
print("status:", result.status.name, "optimal:", result.optimal,
      "complete:", result.complete)
print("score:", result.score)
print("mapping:", sorted(result.best.atom_mapping.items()))
print("matched query atoms as SMILES:", result.best.to_smiles("c1ccccc1O"))
assert result.found and result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED
assert result.optimal and result.complete and result.score == 7.0
assert sorted(result.best.atom_mapping.items()) == [
    (0, 6), (1, 5), (2, 4), (3, 10), (4, 9), (5, 7), (6, 8)]
assert result.best.to_smiles("c1ccccc1O") == "c1(ccccc1)O"

# A completed search that finds nothing proves absence
absent = query.match("Nc1ccccc1")             # aniline
print("aniline:", absent.found, absent.status.name, absent.optimal,
      absent.complete)
assert not absent.found and absent.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED
assert absent.optimal and absent.complete

The program prints:

found: True
status: COMPLETED optimal: True complete: True
score: 7.0
mapping: [(0, 6), (1, 5), (2, 4), (3, 10), (4, 9), (5, 7), (6, 8)]
matched query atoms as SMILES: c1(ccccc1)O
aniline: False COMPLETED True True

docs.title: Enumerate embeddings
docs.text:
match_all(target, limit=1000) lists every embedding up to limit. Symmetry-related embeddings are listed separately: benzene sits in toluene in twelve ways, all on the same six ring atoms. To count occurrences, collect the target atom sets with frozenset.

When the limit is reached, the status is LIMIT_REACHED and complete is false; optimal stays true, because a found embedding already proves that the query occurs. A limit that is not a positive integer raises ValueError. Give every enumeration on a large target both a limit and a time limit.

import smsd

benzene = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1").with_timeout(1000)
toluene = "Cc1ccccc1"

every = benzene.match_all(toluene, limit=100)
occurrences = {frozenset(match.atom_mapping.values()) for match in every.matches}
print("embeddings:", len(every.matches), every.status.name,
      "complete:", every.complete)
print("distinct ring occurrences:", len(occurrences))
assert len(every.matches) == 12 and every.complete and len(occurrences) == 1

capped = benzene.match_all(toluene, limit=5)
print("limit 5:", len(capped.matches), capped.status.name,
      "optimal:", capped.optimal, "complete:", capped.complete)
assert capped.status == smsd.SearchStatus.LIMIT_REACHED
assert capped.optimal and not capped.complete

# Two carbonyl groups in aspirin
carbonyl = smsd.Substructure.smarts("C=O").with_timeout(1000)
groups = carbonyl.match_all("CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O", limit=100)
atoms = sorted(sorted(match.atom_mapping.values()) for match in groups.matches)
print("carbonyl atoms in aspirin:", atoms)
assert atoms == [[1, 2], [10, 11]]

try:
    benzene.match_all(toluene, limit=0)
except ValueError as error:
    print("limit 0:", error)
    assert str(error) == "Match limit must be positive"

The program prints:

embeddings: 12 COMPLETED complete: True
distinct ring occurrences: 1
limit 5: 5 LIMIT_REACHED optimal: True complete: False
carbonyl atoms in aspirin: [[1, 2], [10, 11]]
limit 0: Match limit must be positive

docs.title: Search many targets
docs.text:
match_many(targets, *, num_threads=0) searches each target independently and returns one SearchResult per target, in input order. SMILES strings, MolGraph objects and RDKit molecules can be mixed in one list. Each target gets its own time limit and keeps its own atom numbering. num_threads=0 uses the OpenMP default, which OMP_NUM_THREADS sets.

match_many keeps at most one embedding per target. To count occurrences in each target, call match_all on that target.

import smsd

acid = smsd.Substructure.smarts("C(=O)[OX2H1]")      # carboxylic acid
targets = ["CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",                  # aspirin
           smsd.parse_smiles("CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1"),  # paracetamol
           "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O"]             # ibuprofen
results = acid.match_many(targets, num_threads=2)
found = [result.found for result in results]
completed = all(result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED for result in results)
print("carboxylic acid:", found, "all completed:", completed)
assert found == [True, False, True] and completed

benzene = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1").with_timeout(1000)
pair = ["Cc1ccccc1", "c1ccc2ccccc2c1"]               # toluene, naphthalene
kept = [len(result.matches) for result in benzene.match_many(pair, num_threads=2)]
listed = [len(benzene.match_all(target, limit=100).matches) for target in pair]
print("match_many keeps:", kept, "match_all lists:", listed)
assert kept == [1, 1] and listed == [12, 24]

The program prints:

carboxylic acid: [True, False, True] all completed: True
match_many keeps: [1, 1] match_all lists: [12, 24]

docs.title: Search a prepared corpus
docs.text:
TargetCorpus.from_smiles(targets) captures a library once, with each target's atom numbering, so that many queries can search it. A substructure search needs no prewarm and no NumPy. match_many accepts a corpus in place of a list.

match_corpus(corpus, *, gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0) returns one CorpusSearchResult for each corpus slot, in order. Targets that cannot contain the query are ruled out before matching, with a proof; every other target is searched as usual.

Field Meaning target_index The slot in the corpus atom_upper_bound Always None for a substructure search proven_below_threshold True when the query is proved absent threshold_reached True when an embedding was found result The SearchResult, or None for a slot ruled out before matching

When both flags are false, the outcome is unknown, for example after a search was stopped. Every slot is searched, with no slot ruled out, for a SMARTS query, with match_atom_type=False, with a node_limit other than 0, with timeout_ms set to 0 or with a cancellation token. With gpu_prefilter=True, an attached device runs the step that rules targets out, and the CPU runs it when no device is usable; the decisions are the same either way. See CPU and GPU screening.

import smsd

names = ["aspirin", "paracetamol", "ibuprofen", "caffeine", "salicylic acid"]
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles([
    "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O",
    "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1",
    "CC(C)Cc1ccc(cc1)C(C)C(=O)O",
    "CN1C=NC2=C1C(=O)N(C(=O)N2C)C",
    "OC(=O)c1ccccc1O",
])

searches = [("benzene ring", smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1"),
             ["aspirin", "paracetamol", "ibuprofen", "salicylic acid"]),
            ("aromatic hydroxyl", smsd.Substructure.smarts("c[OX2H]"),
             ["paracetamol", "salicylic acid"])]
for label, query, expected in searches:
    results = query.match_many(corpus, num_threads=2)
    hits = [name for name, result in zip(names, results) if result.found]
    print(f"{label}:", hits)
    assert all(result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED for result in results)
    assert hits == expected

decisions = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1O").match_corpus(corpus, num_threads=2)
outcomes = []
for name, decision in zip(names, decisions):
    if decision.result is None:
        outcome = "ruled out before matching"
    elif decision.threshold_reached:
        outcome = "found"
    elif decision.proven_below_threshold:
        outcome = "searched, proved absent"
    else:
        outcome = "unknown"
    print(f"{name:15}", outcome)
    assert decision.atom_upper_bound is None
    outcomes.append(outcome)
assert outcomes == ["found", "found", "searched, proved absent",
                    "ruled out before matching", "found"]

The program prints:

benzene ring: ['aspirin', 'paracetamol', 'ibuprofen', 'salicylic acid']
aromatic hydroxyl: ['paracetamol', 'salicylic acid']
aspirin         found
paracetamol     found
ibuprofen       searched, proved absent
caffeine        ruled out before matching
salicylic acid  found

docs.title: Induced matching
docs.text:
By default a search is non-induced: query bonds must map to target bonds, but two query atoms that are not bonded may map to target atoms that are. with_induced() also requires every pair of unbonded query atoms to map to unbonded target atoms. Propane is then no longer found in cyclopropane, while cyclohexane is still found in decalin.

import smsd

pairs = [("CCC", "C1CC1", "propane in cyclopropane"),
         ("C1CCCCC1", "C1CCC2CCCCC2C1", "cyclohexane in decalin")]
for query, target, label in pairs:
    plain = smsd.Substructure.find(query).match(target).found
    induced = smsd.Substructure.find(query).with_induced().match(target).found
    print(f"{label:24} default: {plain!s:5} induced: {induced}")
    assert plain and induced == (target != "C1CC1")

The program prints:

propane in cyclopropane  default: True  induced: False
cyclohexane in decalin   default: True  induced: True

docs.title: Chemistry options
docs.text:
options.chemistry is a ChemOptions object that decides which atoms and bonds may match. For a SMARTS query, the pattern itself states charge, hydrogen count, aromaticity, bond order and stereochemistry, so only complete_rings_only applies (see SMARTS queries).

Attribute Default Effect on a molecule query SMARTS match_atom_type True Matched atoms have the same element No match_formal_charge False Matched atoms have the same formal charge No match_isotope False Matched atoms have the same mass number where both atoms state one No use_chirality False A tagged query centre needs the same configuration in the target; an untagged query centre matches any; an untagged target centre does not satisfy a tagged query No use_bond_stereo False The same rule for double-bond configuration No ring_matches_ring_only False Ring atoms and bonds match only ring atoms and bonds No complete_rings_only False Matched ring atoms and bonds lie in fully matched rings of the target Yes ring_fusion_mode RingFusionMode.IGNORE STRICT requires the same number of rings on each matched atom; PERMISSIVE behaves as IGNORE No match_bond_order BondOrderMode.STRICT Bond orders agree; LOOSE and ANY both accept any order and give identical results No aromaticity_mode AromaticityMode.FLEXIBLE Aromatic atoms and bonds may also match non-aromatic ones; STRICT requires agreement No tautomer_aware False Recognised tautomeric bonds may match; usually combined with a relaxed bond order No pH, solvent 7.4, Solvent.AQUEOUS Used only by MCS.compute_tautomer_confidence No

LOOSE and ANY still respect aromaticity_mode=STRICT and ring_matches_ring_only. Options objects take no keyword arguments, so set each field as an attribute. The program below shows the effect of each option on a small pair of molecules.

import smsd


def found(query, target, **fields):
    options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
    for name, value in fields.items():
        setattr(options.chemistry, name, value)
    return smsd.Substructure.find(query).with_options(options).match(target).found


BOND = smsd.BondOrderMode
AROMATIC = smsd.AromaticityMode
FUSION = smsd.RingFusionMode
rows = [
    ("C=C in ethane", "C=C", "CC", dict(match_bond_order=BOND.ANY)),
    ("C=C in ethane", "C=C", "CC", dict(match_bond_order=BOND.LOOSE)),
    ("phenol in cyclohexanol", "c1ccccc1O", "OC1CCCCC1",
     dict(aromaticity_mode=AROMATIC.STRICT)),
    ("C[NH3+] in methylamine", "C[NH3+]", "CN", dict(match_formal_charge=True)),
    ("[13CH4] in methane", "[13CH4]", "C", dict(match_isotope=True)),
    ("methanol in methylamine", "CO", "CN", dict(match_atom_type=False)),
    ("L-alanine in D-alanine", "N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O", "N[C@H](C)C(=O)O",
     dict(use_chirality=True)),
    ("L-alanine in racemic alanine", "N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O", "NC(C)C(=O)O",
     dict(use_chirality=True)),
    ("racemic alanine in L-alanine", "NC(C)C(=O)O", "N[C@@H](C)C(=O)O",
     dict(use_chirality=True)),
    ("F/C=C/F in F/C=C\\F", "F/C=C/F", "F/C=C\\F", dict(use_bond_stereo=True)),
    ("propane in cyclohexane", "CCC", "C1CCCCC1",
     dict(ring_matches_ring_only=True)),
    ("propane in cyclohexane", "CCC", "C1CCCCC1", dict(complete_rings_only=True)),
    ("propane in propylcyclohexane", "CCC", "CCCC1CCCCC1",
     dict(complete_rings_only=True)),
    ("cyclohexane in decalin", "C1CCCCC1", "C1CCC2CCCCC2C1",
     dict(ring_fusion_mode=FUSION.STRICT)),
    ("acetone in its enol", "CC(=O)C", "CC(O)=C", dict(tautomer_aware=True)),
    ("acetone in its enol", "CC(=O)C", "CC(O)=C",
     dict(tautomer_aware=True, match_bond_order=BOND.ANY)),
]
expected = [(False, True), (False, True), (True, False), (True, False),
            (True, True), (False, True), (True, False), (True, False),
            (True, True), (True, False), (True, False), (True, False),
            (True, True), (True, False), (False, False), (False, True)]
for (label, query, target, fields), outcome in zip(rows, expected):
    setting = ", ".join(f"{name}={getattr(value, 'name', value)}"
                        for name, value in fields.items())
    default, changed = found(query, target), found(query, target, **fields)
    print(f"{label:29} {setting:40} {default!s:5} -> {changed}")
    assert (default, changed) == outcome

The program prints:

C=C in ethane                 match_bond_order=ANY                     False -> True
C=C in ethane                 match_bond_order=LOOSE                   False -> True
phenol in cyclohexanol        aromaticity_mode=STRICT                  True  -> False
C[NH3+] in methylamine        match_formal_charge=True                 True  -> False
[13CH4] in methane            match_isotope=True                       True  -> True
methanol in methylamine       match_atom_type=False                    False -> True
L-alanine in D-alanine        use_chirality=True                       True  -> False
L-alanine in racemic alanine  use_chirality=True                       True  -> False
racemic alanine in L-alanine  use_chirality=True                       True  -> True
F/C=C/F in F/C=C\F            use_bond_stereo=True                     True  -> False
propane in cyclohexane        ring_matches_ring_only=True              True  -> False
propane in cyclohexane        complete_rings_only=True                 True  -> False
propane in propylcyclohexane  complete_rings_only=True                 True  -> True
cyclohexane in decalin        ring_fusion_mode=STRICT                  True  -> False
acetone in its enol           tautomer_aware=True                      False -> False
acetone in its enol           tautomer_aware=True, match_bond_order=ANY False -> True

Three rows deserve attention. Under the default FLEXIBLE mode, phenol is found in cyclohexanol; STRICT aromaticity prevents this. match_isotope compares mass numbers only where both atoms state one, so the labelled query still matches unlabelled methane. Tautomer matching usually also needs a relaxed bond order.

ChemOptions.profile(name) returns a named set of options, and the name is not case-sensitive. Each profile starts from the defaults and changes only the fields shown below. strict changes only the aromaticity mode, so charge and isotope matching still need match_formal_charge or match_isotope. An unknown name raises ValueError.

import smsd

FIELDS = ("match_atom_type", "match_formal_charge", "match_isotope",
          "use_chirality", "use_bond_stereo", "ring_matches_ring_only",
          "complete_rings_only", "ring_fusion_mode", "match_bond_order",
          "aromaticity_mode", "tautomer_aware")
default = smsd.ChemOptions()


def changes(chemistry):
    changed = []
    for name in FIELDS:
        value = getattr(chemistry, name)
        if value != getattr(default, name):
            changed.append(f"{name}={getattr(value, 'name', value)}")
    return changed


expected = {
    "default": [],
    "strict": ["aromaticity_mode=STRICT"],
    "pharma": ["match_formal_charge=True", "ring_matches_ring_only=True",
               "complete_rings_only=True"],
    "reaction": ["match_bond_order=LOOSE"],
    "compat-fmcs": ["match_bond_order=LOOSE"],
    "compat-substruct": ["match_bond_order=LOOSE"],
}
for name, fields in expected.items():
    print(f"{name:17}", changes(smsd.ChemOptions.profile(name)))
    assert changes(smsd.ChemOptions.profile(name.upper())) == fields
tautomer = changes(smsd.ChemOptions.tautomer_profile())
print(f"{'tautomer_profile':17}", tautomer)
assert tautomer == ["match_bond_order=LOOSE", "tautomer_aware=True"]

try:
    smsd.ChemOptions.profile("fast")
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)
    assert str(error) == "Unknown ChemOptions profile: fast"

The program prints:

default           []
strict            ['aromaticity_mode=STRICT']
pharma            ['match_formal_charge=True', 'ring_matches_ring_only=True', 'complete_rings_only=True']
reaction          ['match_bond_order=LOOSE']
compat-fmcs       ['match_bond_order=LOOSE']
compat-substruct  ['match_bond_order=LOOSE']
tautomer_profile  ['match_bond_order=LOOSE', 'tautomer_aware=True']
Unknown ChemOptions profile: fast

docs.title: Hydrogen counts
docs.text:
A molecule query does not compare hydrogen counts. Phenol as a molecule query therefore matches aspirin, whose ester oxygen bears no hydrogen. When hydrogen counts matter, write SMARTS with an H primitive, such as c[OX2H], or turn the drawn query into SMARTS with to_smarts(..., include_h_count=True). The second route fixes the hydrogen count of every atom, including the ring positions, so the pattern below matches unsubstituted phenol only.

import smsd

aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"
phenol = "Oc1ccccc1"
butylphenol = "CC(C)(C)c1ccc(O)cc1"   # 4-tert-butylphenol

molecule = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1O").match(aspirin).found
hydroxyl = smsd.Substructure.smarts("c[OX2H]").match(aspirin).found
print("phenol as a molecule query, in aspirin:", molecule)
print("c[OX2H] in aspirin:", hydroxyl)
assert molecule and not hydroxyl

pattern = smsd.to_smarts("c1ccccc1O", include_h_count=True)
print(pattern)
assert pattern.endswith("-[#8;A;H1]") and pattern.count("H1") == 6
fixed = smsd.Substructure.smarts(pattern)
outcome = [fixed.match(target).found for target in (aspirin, phenol, butylphenol)]
print("aspirin, phenol, 4-tert-butylphenol:", outcome)
assert outcome == [False, True, False]

The program prints:

phenol as a molecule query, in aspirin: True
c[OX2H] in aspirin: False
[#6;a;H0]:1(:[#6;a;H1]:[#6;a;H1]:[#6;a;H1]:[#6;a;H1]:[#6;a;H1]:1)-[#8;A;H1]
aspirin, phenol, 4-tert-butylphenol: [False, True, False]

docs.title: Time limits, node limits and cancellation
docs.text:
Each search stops at the first of these limits:

  • timeout_ms: the time limit per target in milliseconds. The default -1 selects 10,000 ms for a substructure search; 0 stops at once.
  • node_limit: the number of search nodes. The default 0 sets no limit; reaching one gives LIMIT_REACHED.
  • cancellation: a CancellationToken. Calling cancel() from any thread stops the search with CANCELLED.

A stopped search with no matches proves nothing: optimal and complete are both false. A token stays cancelled and is shared by every options object and prepared query that holds it, so use a new token for each request.

import smsd

query = smsd.Substructure.find("c1ccccc1O")   # phenol
target = "CC(C)(C)c1ccc(O)cc1"                # 4-tert-butylphenol


def report(label, result):
    print(f"{label:14}", result.status.name, "found:", result.found,
          "optimal:", result.optimal, "complete:", result.complete)


stopped = query.with_timeout(0).match(target)
report("timeout 0", stopped)
assert stopped.status == smsd.SearchStatus.TIMED_OUT and not stopped.optimal

options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.node_limit = 3
capped = query.with_options(options).match(target)
report("node limit 3", capped)
assert capped.status == smsd.SearchStatus.LIMIT_REACHED and not capped.complete

token = smsd.CancellationToken()
options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.cancellation = token
options.timeout_ms = 1000
cancellable = query.with_options(options)
before = cancellable.match(target)
report("before cancel", before)
assert before.found and before.status == smsd.SearchStatus.COMPLETED
token.cancel()
cancelled = cancellable.match(target)
report("after cancel", cancelled)
assert cancelled.status == smsd.SearchStatus.CANCELLED and token.is_cancelled

The program prints:

timeout 0      TIMED_OUT found: False optimal: False complete: False
node limit 3   LIMIT_REACHED found: False optimal: False complete: False
before cancel  COMPLETED found: True optimal: True complete: True
after cancel   CANCELLED found: False optimal: False complete: False

To stop a long search from another thread, raise the token there. Keep a limit and a time limit as a safety net. The number of embeddings found before the stop depends on timing, so the program below does not print it.

import threading

import smsd

# A carbon ladder of 181 atoms holds a very large number of 20-carbon chains
ladder = ("".join(f"C%{ring}" for ring in range(10, 100)) + "C"
          + "".join(f"C%{ring}" for ring in range(99, 9, -1)))
chain = smsd.Substructure.find("C" * 20)

token = smsd.CancellationToken()
options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
options.cancellation = token
options.timeout_ms = 5000                     # safety net
timer = threading.Timer(0.1, token.cancel)
timer.start()
result = chain.with_options(options).match_all(ladder, limit=1_000_000)
timer.join()

print("status:", result.status.name, "complete:", result.complete)
assert result.status == smsd.SearchStatus.CANCELLED and not result.complete

The program prints:

status: CANCELLED complete: False

docs.title: Draw a hit
docs.text:
depict_mapping(molecule, mapping) draws a molecule natively, with no RDKit, and highlights the atoms in mapping. Its keys are atoms of the drawn molecule, so invert the search mapping to draw the target. This route works for molecule and SMARTS queries alike.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd

paracetamol = "CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1"
hit = smsd.Substructure.smarts("c[OX2H]").match(paracetamol)
assert hit.found

highlight = {target: query for query, target in hit.best.atom_mapping.items()}
print("highlighted target atoms:", sorted(highlight.items()))
assert highlight == {7: 0, 8: 1}

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:

highlighted target atoms: [(7, 0), (8, 1)]
SVG written: True

With RDKit installed, depict_substructure(query, target, *, timeout_ms=10000, size=(600, 300)) runs its own molecule-query search and returns an RDKit image of the query and the target with the matched atoms highlighted. It does not accept SMARTS and reports no search status: when the search stops without a match, it draws the pair without a highlight.

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from rdkit import Chem
import smsd

query = Chem.MolFromSmiles("c1ccccc1O")              # phenol
target = Chem.MolFromSmiles("CC(C)(C)c1ccc(O)cc1")   # 4-tert-butylphenol
image = smsd.depict_substructure(query, target)
print("image size:", image.size)
assert image.size == (600, 300)

with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "phenol_hit.png"
    image.save(path)
    assert path.stat().st_size > 0

image size: (600, 300)

docs.title: R-group decomposition
docs.text:
Substructure.decompose_r_groups(core, targets, options=None) searches each target for the core and returns a dictionary with the matched core graph, the substituents as rgroups (R1, R2 and so on) and the search result. The core keeps its original hydrogen counts, so its attachment atoms are written as bracket atoms.

import smsd

targets = ["Cc1ccccc1O",   # 2-methylphenol
           "CCN"]          # ethylamine
parts = smsd.Substructure.decompose_r_groups("c1ccccc1", targets)   # benzene core
summary = []
for target, part in zip(targets, parts):
    found = part["search"].found
    core = smsd.to_smiles(part["core"]) if found else None
    groups = {name: smsd.to_smiles(graph) for name, graph in part["rgroups"].items()}
    print(f"{target:11}", "found:", found, "core:", core, "R-groups:", groups)
    summary.append((found, core, groups))
assert summary == [(True, "[c]1[c]cccc1", {"R1": "[CH3]", "R2": "[OH]"}),
                   (False, None, {})]

The program prints:

Cc1ccccc1O  found: True core: [c]1[c]cccc1 R-groups: {'R1': '[CH3]', 'R2': '[OH]'}
CCN         found: False core: None R-groups: {}

docs.text:
Method Default Meaning Substructure.find(query) Prepare a molecule query from SMILES, a MolGraph or an RDKit molecule Substructure.smarts(pattern) Compile a SMARTS pattern; an empty or non-string pattern raises ValueError with_options(options) A new query with a copy of options with_timeout(milliseconds) A new query with timeout_ms set with_induced(enabled=True) enabled=True A new query with induced matching on or off match(target) One embedding, with its status match_all(target, limit=1000) limit=1000 Every embedding up to limit; limit must be a positive integer match_many(targets, *, num_threads=0) num_threads=0 One result per target, in order; num_threads must be a non-negative integer match_corpus(corpus, *, gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0) gpu_prefilter=False, num_threads=0 One decision per corpus slot; corpus must be a TargetCorpus Substructure.decompose_r_groups(core, targets, options=None) options=None (default options) Core, R-groups and search result for each target

Substructure.Options() holds these fields. Copy one with Substructure.Options(other).

Field Type Default Meaning chemistry ChemOptions ChemOptions() Matching rules (see Chemistry options) timeout_ms int -1 Time limit per target; a negative value selects 10,000 ms; 0 stops at once node_limit int 0 Search node limit; 0 sets no limit cancellation CancellationToken or None None A token that stops the search when cancelled induced bool False Require an induced embedding

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Substructure.Options and ChemOptions take no keyword arguments. Set each field as an attribute; a misspelt attribute raises AttributeError. options.chemistry can be edited in place.
  • with_options copies the options object, so later edits do not reach the query. A CancellationToken held in the options is shared, not copied.
  • A query with several components, such as C.O, maps each component to distinct target atoms: C.O is found in ethanol, O.O is not.
  • An empty SMILES string raises ValueError. An empty MolGraph query, from parse_smiles(""), is found in every target with one empty match.
  • Match.atom_mapping is read-only, and Match and SearchResult are frozen.
  • elapsed_ms is in whole milliseconds and nodes_visited measures effort; both vary between runs and builds.
  • match and match_all count the time spent building Python results towards the time limit. match_many stops building results only when cancelled.
  • A molecule query with an explicit [H] atom needs an explicit hydrogen atom in the target; a bracket hydrogen count is not an atom (see Input atom numbering).
  • num_threads=0 means the OpenMP default in Python and one thread per processor in C++. In Java, matchMany(targets) without a thread count runs on one thread.
  • The substructure tools of the local molecular tools server (smsd-mcp) use their own defaults: a time limit of 1,000 ms and a node limit of 100,000; see Molecular tools server.

import os
import re
import time

from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

import smsd
from smsd.clustering import butina, maxmin
from smsd.corpus import FingerprintCorpus, stream_screen_smiles

_release = re.match(r"(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)", smsd.__version__)
if _release is None or tuple(int(part) for part in _release.groups()) < (8, 1, 0):
    raise RuntimeError(f"This notebook needs SMSD 8.1.0 or later; found {smsd.__version__}")
print("SMSD", smsd.__version__)

try:
    import numpy
except ImportError:
    numpy = None
    print("NumPy is not installed; the packed-index steps are skipped.")

try:
    import smsd_cuda
except ImportError:
    smsd_cuda = None


def cuda_status():
    """Return whether backend="cuda" can be used here, and the reason when it cannot."""
    if os.environ.get("SMSD_DISABLE_GPU", "") not in ("", "0"):
        return False, "disabled by SMSD_DISABLE_GPU"
    if smsd_cuda is None:
        return False, "smsd-cuda is not installed"
    if smsd_cuda.__version__ != smsd.__version__:
        return False, f"smsd-cuda {smsd_cuda.__version__} does not match smsd {smsd.__version__}"
    reason = smsd_cuda.unavailable_reason()
    return reason is None, reason


@contextmanager
def environment(name, value):
    """Set an environment variable inside a with block, then restore its previous state."""
    previous = os.environ.get(name)
    os.environ[name] = value
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        if previous is None:
            os.environ.pop(name, None)
        else:
            os.environ[name] = previous


ready, reason = cuda_status()
print("CUDA screening:", "ready" if ready else f"unavailable ({reason})")

# A generated library: 5 rings x 8 groups x chains of 0 to 49 carbons = 2,000 molecules.
rings = ["c1ccccc1", "c1ccncc1", "C1CCCCC1", "c1ccoc1", "c1ccsc1"]
groups = ["O", "N", "Cl", "C(=O)O", "OC", "C#N", "F", "CC"]
library = [ring + group + "C" * length
           for ring in rings for group in groups for length in range(50)]
queries = ["c1ccccc1O", "c1ccncc1Cl", "C1CCCCC1C(=O)O"]

# Prepared ECFP4 screens choose their device for each call. By default the GPU is used
# only on a Tesla T4 for 100,000 targets or more, so this 2,000-target corpus stays on
# the CPU unless SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS lowers that size.
corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library)
corpus.prewarm()
hits = corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4)
print("Targets:", len(corpus), "| hits per query:", [len(found) for found in hits])

# warm_start prepares the corpus it is given; the stream screens one chunk at a time.
assert smsd.warm_start(smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(library), queries[0], 0.4) == hits[0]
assert list(stream_screen_smiles(queries[0], iter(library), 0.4)) == hits[0]
print("warm_start and stream_screen_smiles give the same hits")

if ready:
    # Let any supported device take corpora of one target or more.
    with environment("SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS", "1"):
        assert corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4) == hits
    print("The hits with the GPU allowed equal the CPU hits")

if numpy is None:
    print("NumPy is not installed; skipping the packed-index errors.")
else:
    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        with FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "bits.fp", [[1], [1, 2], [3]],
                                      fp_size=8) as small:
            # Packed searches are generators: a failed backend="cuda" request raises
            # when the first item is requested, not when the method is called.
            pending = small.similarities([1], threshold=0.5, backend="cuda")
            print("The call returns a", type(pending).__name__)
            if ready:
                cpu = list(small.similarities([1], threshold=0.5, backend="cpu"))
                assert list(pending) == cpu
                print("backend='cuda' ran on the device with the CPU hits")
            else:
                try:
                    next(pending)
                except RuntimeError as error:
                    print("First item:", error)
                else:
                    raise AssertionError("backend='cuda' should fail without a usable device")

        # Wider than 65,536 bits: "auto" stays on the CPU and "cuda" is refused.
        with FingerprintCorpus.create(Path(directory) / "wide.fp", [[1], [70000]],
                                      fp_size=70001) as wide:
            print("auto, 70,001 bits:",
                  list(wide.similarities([70000], threshold=0.5, backend="auto")))
            try:
                list(wide.similarities([70000], threshold=0.5, backend="cuda"))
            except ValueError as error:
                print("cuda, 70,001 bits:", error)
            else:
                raise AssertionError("backend='cuda' should refuse 70,001 bits")

def timed(label, work, repeats=3):
    """Run once to warm up, then print the best of several timed runs."""
    result = work()
    best = float("inf")
    for _ in range(repeats):
        started = time.perf_counter()
        assert work() == result
        best = min(best, time.perf_counter() - started)
    print(f"{label:<30} {best:8.4f} s")
    return result


with environment("SMSD_DISABLE_GPU", "1"):
    cpu_hits = timed("prepared screen, CPU", lambda: corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4))
if ready:
    with environment("SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS", str(len(library))):
        gpu_hits = timed("prepared screen, GPU allowed",
                         lambda: corpus.screen_many(queries, 0.4))
    assert gpu_hits == cpu_hits
print("Hits per query:", [len(found) for found in cpu_hits])

if numpy is None:

else:

        with FingerprintCorpus.from_smiles(Path(directory) / "library.fp", library) as packed:
            probes = [packed.fingerprint(index) for index in (0, 450, 1600)]
            cpu_rows = timed("packed scan, CPU", lambda: list(
                packed.screen_many(probes, threshold=0.4, backend="cpu")))
            if ready:

                    packed.screen_many(probes, threshold=0.4, backend="cuda")))
                assert gpu_rows == cpu_rows and packed.cuda_calls > before
            print("Packed hits:", len(cpu_rows))

docs.title: CPU and GPU screening¶
docs.text:
This notebook shows where SMSD 8.1.0 work runs. Graph matching, which covers every substructure, SMARTS and MCS search, always runs on the CPU. With the optional smsd-cuda package and an NVIDIA GPU of compute capability 7.5 or later, prepared ECFP4 screens, corpus pre-screens and packed fingerprint scans can run on the GPU, and their hits, scores and decisions are identical to the CPU results. Every cell also runs on a machine without a GPU: the GPU steps check for a usable device first. NumPy is optional and needed only for the packed-index steps, which report when it is missing.

The notebook performs no downloads and writes files only to temporary directories. In local Jupyter, select a kernel with SMSD 8.1.0 or later installed. For Colab, copy the setup cell of feature_search.ipynb to the top of this notebook and run it first; it installs an uploaded SMSD core wheel. No cell needs the CUDA package.

docs.title: Time CPU and GPU work¶
docs.text:
The next cell times the same screens on the CPU and, where a device is ready, on the GPU. In that case an earlier cell has already initialised the device with smsd_cuda.preload(). Each call runs once before it is measured, the best of three runs measured with time.perf_counter() is kept, and the GPU results are asserted equal to the CPU results. The prepared screen is held on the CPU with SMSD_DISABLE_GPU and then allowed on the GPU with SMSD_CUDA_MIN_TARGETS; only the packed scan proves device use, through cuda_calls.

Timings depend on the device, the processor, the corpus, the thread count and the load on the machine. They describe this run only and are not benchmarks. Without a usable device, only the CPU lines appear.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text: Every route that ran gave the same hits, scores and decisions as the CPU. With a usable device, the packed scans also proved device use through cuda_calls; prepared screens and pre-screens keep no public record of the device they used. The CPU and GPU screening chapter covers installation, the fallback rules and the environment variables, and gpu_screening.py shows the same pattern as a script.

docs.title: MCS to a small library search¶
docs.text: This notebook uses SMSD 8.1.0 to turn a common graph into a SMARTS query, search a small molecular library, and explore fingerprint neighbours and clustering. Search results retain their completion and proof status. NumPy and scikit-learn are optional; the cells that need them report when they are missing.

docs.title: Setup: local Jupyter or Colab¶
docs.text:
In local Jupyter, select a kernel with SMSD 8.1.0, NumPy and scikit-learn already installed. The setup cell uses that package and performs no upload or installation.

Upload this notebook file to Colab and start a fresh Linux x86_64 runtime. Run the setup cell first and upload exactly one trusted SMSD 8.1.0 core wheel matching its CPython version and ABI. Download the wheel beforehand from PyPI or the GitHub releases page; this notebook does not download packages. The filename and compatible Linux x86_64 tags are checked before installation, followed by an exact imported-version check. The optional CUDA wheel is not needed.

Colab normally supplies NumPy and scikit-learn. The setup cell checks their availability but does not install dependencies. It installs only the uploaded core wheel with this kernel's sys.executable, --no-index, --no-deps and --force-reinstall. Restart the runtime before repeating the upload setup after importing SMSD. Uploaded wheels contain native code; use a trusted matching artefact.

docs.title: Find the common graph and export SMARTS¶
docs.text: The search below maximises common induced atoms under the default chemistry rules. Both the time and node limits are explicit. A found candidate is usable as a pattern even if stopped, but it is described as a maximum only when optimal is true. SMARTS export raises for matching rules that cannot be represented, rather than dropping those rules.

docs.title: Optional fingerprint features¶
docs.text: The feature adapter returns one native fingerprint per row. Binary features default to uint8; count features default to int64. The classifier below is a small pipeline demonstration with example labels, not an estimate of predictive performance.

docs.title: Packed corpus, top-k neighbours and clustering¶
docs.text: The file stores packed binary fingerprints and is opened read-only through a memory map. Pair scans are exact and quadratic; thresholds or top-k limit the returned data. Butina groups molecules near each cluster centre, while MaxMin selects diverse rows. This example uses a temporary file that is removed on completion.

# Every fingerprint family on aspirin. Each kind of fingerprint() gives the
# bits of its fixed function, and the classic FingerprintOptions give them again.
aspirin = "CC(=O)Oc1ccccc1C(=O)O"  # aspirin
graph = smsd.parse_smiles(aspirin)

fixed = {
    "ecfp": smsd.circular_fingerprint(graph, radius=2, fp_size=2048),
    "fcfp": smsd.circular_fingerprint(graph, radius=2, fp_size=2048, mode="fcfp"),
    "path": smsd.path_fingerprint(graph, path_length=7, fp_size=2048),
    "mcs": smsd.mcs_fingerprint(graph, path_length=7, fp_size=2048),
    "torsion": smsd.topological_torsion(graph, fp_size=2048),
}
classic = {
    "ecfp": smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(),
    "fcfp": smsd.FingerprintOptions.fcfp(),
    "path": smsd.FingerprintOptions.path(),
    "torsion": smsd.FingerprintOptions.torsion(),
}
for kind, bits in fixed.items():
    assert smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, kind=kind) == bits
    if kind in classic:
        assert smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=classic[kind]) == bits
    print(f"{kind:8} {len(bits):3d} set bits, first five {bits[:5]}")
maccs_bits = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin, options=smsd.FingerprintOptions.maccs())
print(f"{'maccs':8} {len(maccs_bits):3d} set bits")
assert [len(bits) for bits in fixed.values()] == [36, 29, 29, 127, 16]
assert len(maccs_bits) == 21

# The default kind differs between entry points.
default = smsd.fingerprint(aspirin)
from_smiles = smsd.fingerprint_from_smiles(aspirin)
print("fingerprint() default equals kind='mcs':", default == fixed["mcs"])
print("fingerprint_from_smiles() default equals ECFP4:", from_smiles == fixed["ecfp"])
assert default == fixed["mcs"] and from_smiles == fixed["ecfp"]

# SMSD has no Tversky function; it is a few lines over the set positions.
def tversky(query, target, alpha=0.9, beta=0.1):
    q, t = set(query), set(target)
    common = len(q & t)
    denominator = common + alpha * len(q - t) + beta * len(t - q)
    return 1.0 if denominator == 0 else common / denominator


ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp()
phenol = smsd.fingerprint("Oc1ccccc1", options=ecfp4)                # phenol
paracetamol = smsd.fingerprint("CC(=O)Nc1ccc(O)cc1", options=ecfp4)  # paracetamol
forward, reverse = tversky(phenol, paracetamol), tversky(paracetamol, phenol)
print(f"phenol in paracetamol: {forward:.3f}")
print(f"paracetamol in phenol: {reverse:.3f}")
assert round(forward, 3) == 0.533 and round(reverse, 3) == 0.348
assert abs(tversky(phenol, paracetamol, 1, 1) - smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(phenol, paracetamol)) < 1e-12
dice = smsd.dice(phenol, paracetamol, fp_size=2048)
assert abs(tversky(phenol, paracetamol, 0.5, 0.5) - dice) < 1e-12

# An ECFP4 Tanimoto matrix of the benzodiazepines.
benzodiazepines = {
    "diazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "nordazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2N1",
    "temazepam": "CN1C(=O)C(O)N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "oxazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "lorazepam": "OC1N=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc(Cl)ccc2NC1=O",
    "clonazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2Cl)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "nitrazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccc2)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc2N1",
    "flunitrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(c2ccccc2F)c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc21",
    "bromazepam": "O=C1CN=C(c2ccccn2)c2cc(Br)ccc2N1",
    "tetrazepam": "CN1C(=O)CN=C(C2=CCCCC2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
    "alprazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1)=NC2",
    "triazolam": "Cc1nnc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1Cl)=NC2",
    "midazolam": "Cc1ncc2n1-c1ccc(Cl)cc1C(c1ccccc1F)=NC2",
    "clobazam": "CN1C(=O)CC(=O)N(c2ccccc2)c2cc(Cl)ccc21",
}
names, smiles = list(benzodiazepines), list(benzodiazepines.values())
ecfp4 = smsd.FingerprintOptions.ecfp(radius=2, size=2048)
fps = smsd.fingerprints(smiles, options=ecfp4)
by_coefficient = [[smsd.tanimoto_coefficient(p, q) for q in fps] for p in fps]

if np is not None:
    A = np.zeros((len(fps), 2048), dtype=np.int32)
    for row, positions in enumerate(fps):
        A[row, positions] = 1
    common = A @ A.T
    sizes = A.sum(axis=1)
    matrix = common / (sizes[:, None] + sizes[None, :] - common)
    assert np.allclose(matrix, by_coefficient)
    rows = matrix.round(2).tolist()
else:
    rows = [[round(score, 2) for score in row] for row in by_coefficient]

labels = [name[:4] for name in names]  # short column labels
assert len(set(labels)) == len(names)
if pd is not None:
    print(pd.DataFrame(rows, index=names, columns=labels).to_string())
else:
    for name, row in zip(names, rows):
        print(f"{name:14}", row)

# The nearest neighbour of each molecule, other than itself.
nearest = {}
for i, name in enumerate(names):

    print(f"{name:14} nearest {names[j]:14} {by_coefficient[i][j]:.3f}")
assert all(by_coefficient[i][i] == 1.0 for i in range(len(names)))

common) assert np.allclose(matrix, by_coefficient) rows = matrix.round(2).tolist() else: rows = [[round(score, 2) for score in row] for row in by_coefficient] labels = [name[:4] for name in names] # short column labels assert len(set(labels)) == len(names) if pd is not None: print(pd.DataFrame(rows, index=names, columns=labels).to_string()) else: for name, row in zip(names, rows): print(f"{name:14}", row) # The nearest neighbour of each molecule, other than itself. nearest = {} for i, name in enumerate(names): j = max((k for k in range(len(names)) if k != i), key=lambda k: by_coefficient[i][k]) nearest[name] = (names[j], round(by_coefficient[i][j], 3)) print(f"{name:14} nearest {names[j]:14} {by_coefficient[i][j]:.3f}") assert all(by_coefficient[i][i] == 1.0 for i in range(len(names))) assert nearest["diazepam"] == ("temazepam", 0.582) assert nearest["oxazepam"] == ("lorazepam", 0.755) assert nearest["alprazolam"] == ("triazolam", 0.76)

docs.title: Fingerprints and similarity¶
docs.text: This notebook uses SMSD 8.1.0 to compute each fingerprint family for a few common drugs, compare fingerprints with every binary and count coefficient, configure a fingerprint with stereo, scaffold and fragment switches, and rank a series of benzodiazepines by similarity. Each value the notebook prints is checked by an assertion in the same cell. NumPy and pandas are optional: without them, the matrix cell uses plain lists and the setup cell reports what is missing.

docs.title: Setup¶
docs.text:
Select a kernel with SMSD 8.1.0 or later installed (python -m pip install "smsd==8.1.0"); NumPy and pandas are used when present. The notebook downloads nothing and writes no files.

To run it in Colab, copy the setup cell of feature_search.ipynb to the top of this notebook and run it first. That cell installs a trusted SMSD 8.1.0 core wheel that you upload, after checking its name and platform tags.

docs.title: Where next¶
docs.text: Fingerprints made with different families, radii, path lengths, widths or switches cannot be compared, and nothing in a fingerprint records how it was made, so keep one specification per comparison. The fingerprints chapter of the user guide covers every function and option shown here, with the defaults. Screening a library and the packed fingerprint index apply these fingerprints to larger libraries, and the Python feature adapters page turns them into NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Polars, Arrow and PyTorch data.

def version_tuple(text):
    """The first three numeric parts of a version string."""
    parts = []

        parts.append(int(digits or 0))
    return tuple(parts + [0] * (3 - len(parts)))

The fingerprint screens return the same hits whichever route runs them, and the substructure decisions carry a proof for every target ruled out before matching. The screening chapter explains each route, its options and its limits, and the packed index chapter covers building, reopening and searching a saved index.

docs.title: Screening a library end to end¶
docs.text:
This notebook uses SMSD 8.1.0 to screen a small library five ways: a fingerprint screen held in memory, a saved packed index, a streamed screen of a SMILES file, an exact substructure screen and an MCS-similarity screen. It then clusters the index and saves the hits to an SD file. The library is built inside the notebook: 14 benzodiazepines, 7 common drugs and 512 generated trisubstituted benzenes. The files it writes go to a temporary directory that the last cell removes.

NumPy is needed only for the packed index and the clustering cells, and pandas only to print one table; cells that need a missing package say so and carry on. Select a kernel with SMSD 8.1.0 or later installed. This notebook has no upload cell: to run it in Colab, first copy the setup cell of feature_search.ipynb into a new first cell and run it, as the setup section of that notebook describes.

docs.title: Similarity screens¶
docs.text:
A TargetCorpus keeps the parsed library in memory. prewarm() computes an ECFP radius 2, 2048-bit fingerprint for every target, and screen returns the indices of the targets whose Tanimoto score is at least the threshold, in library order. A screen run before prewarm(), or after targets are added, returns an empty list rather than raising.

The packed index stores the same kind of fingerprints in a file that a later session can reopen. The file holds bits only, so a small JSON sidecar keeps the fingerprint specification and the names. The streamed screen reads the SMILES file one chunk at a time. All three give the same hits here.

docs.title: Substructure and MCS-similarity screens¶
docs.text:
Substructure.match_corpus rules out targets that cannot contain the query before matching, with a proof, and searches every other target exactly. Each decision says whether the query was found, proved absent or left unknown, for example by a search that stopped at its time limit. The default FLEXIBLE aromaticity lets an aromatic query bond match a single or double bond, so tetrazepam, with a cyclohexene ring in place of the phenyl ring, contains the core; STRICT aromaticity drops it.

screen_targets computes a fast upper bound on the atom-count MCS Tanimoto, common / (query atoms + target atoms - common), and never drops a target that can reach the threshold under the same chemistry options. The exact MCS then runs on the survivors only.

def common_graph(first, second, **fields):
    options = smsd.MCS.Options()
    options.timeout_ms = 1000
    for name, value in fields.items():
        setattr(options.chemistry, name, value)
    found = smsd.MCS.find(first).with_options(options).match(second)
    if not found.found:
        return 0, "(none)"
    return found.best.atom_count, found.best.to_smiles(first)

docs.title: Maximum common substructure¶
docs.text:
This notebook uses SMSD 8.1.0 or later to find the maximum common substructure (MCS) of small drug-like molecules. It compares the two objectives, shows what a stopped search returns, changes the chemistry rules, computes MCS similarity, exports a SMARTS pattern and finds a common graph across a short series. Every result keeps its status, so a proved maximum is never confused with a partial answer. All molecules are written inline; nothing is downloaded.

IPython and pandas are optional. Without IPython, drawings are summarised as text; without pandas, the similarity table is printed row by row.

To run the notebook in Colab, copy the setup cell of feature_search.ipynb to the top of this notebook and run it first; it installs an uploaded SMSD wheel.

docs.title: Objectives and fragments¶
docs.text: The default objective, MCIS, maximises common atoms and keeps every bond and non-bond between them. MCES maximises common bonds and may leave out a bond between two mapped atoms. The score counts atoms for MCIS and bonds for MCES, so compare scores only within one objective. with_fragments() allows a disconnected common graph; MCIS fragments can include isolated atoms.

docs.title: Partial results¶
docs.text: A node limit, a time limit or a cancellation token can stop a search early. The common graph found so far is still valid, but it is described as the maximum only when optimal is true. Do not rely on the exact mapping of a stopped search.

docs.title: Chemistry rules¶
docs.text: options.chemistry decides which atoms and bonds may correspond. Bond order, aromaticity and the three ring options each change the common graph in a different way.

docs.title: MCS similarity¶
docs.text: The MCS similarity is common atoms divided by query atoms plus target atoms minus common atoms, computed here from best.atom_count. similarity_upper_bound is a fast upper bound on it, and screen_targets keeps every target whose bound reaches a threshold, so the targets it keeps are confirmed with an MCS search.

docs.title: A common graph across a series¶
docs.text: MCS.consensus looks for a graph shared by all inputs, or by a fraction of them set with threshold. The result is an approximate common graph, not proved optimal, so optimal is always false.

docs.title: Further reading¶
docs.text: The MCS chapter of the user guide covers every option shown here, with atom weights, reserved atoms, validation, tautomers and the full options tables. Screening a library by MCS similarity is covered in Screening a library.

def found(query, target, **fields):
    options = smsd.Substructure.Options()
    for name, value in fields.items():
        setattr(options.chemistry, name, value)
    return smsd.Substructure.find(query).with_options(options).match(target).found

# One decision per slot: targets that cannot contain the core are ruled out
# before matching, with a proof; the rest are searched as usual.
library_corpus = smsd.TargetCorpus.from_smiles(list(library.values()))
decisions = smsd.Substructure.find(core).match_corpus(library_corpus, num_threads=2)
counts = {}
for name, decision in zip(library, decisions):
    if decision.result is None:
        outcome = "ruled out before matching"
    elif decision.threshold_reached:
        outcome = "found"
    elif decision.proven_below_threshold:
        outcome = "searched, proved absent"
    else:
        outcome = "unknown (search stopped)"
    counts[outcome] = counts.get(outcome, 0) + 1
    print(f"{name:15} {outcome}")
print(counts)

docs.title: Substructure and SMARTS search¶
docs.text: This notebook uses SMSD 8.1.0 to search a small inline library of common drugs and benzodiazepines with molecule queries and SMARTS patterns. It covers a first search, hydrogen counts, functional-group flags, enumeration, chemistry options, limits, corpus decisions and drawing a hit. Every result keeps its status, so a search that stopped early is never read as an absence. pandas is optional: without it, the table is printed as plain rows.

docs.title: Setup¶
docs.text:
Select a local Jupyter kernel with SMSD 8.1.0 or later installed (see Installation). The setup cell checks the version; it installs and downloads nothing, and no cell writes a file.

To use Colab, copy the setup cell of feature_search.ipynb to the top of this notebook and run it first. That cell installs an uploaded SMSD 8.1.0 core wheel; for a later wheel, change the version checks in the copy to match. Ignore its notice about NumPy and scikit-learn, which this notebook does not use.

docs.title: Hydrogen counts¶
docs.text: A molecule query does not compare hydrogen counts, so phenol as a molecule query also matches the ester oxygen of aspirin. A SMARTS H primitive, as in c[OX2H], fixes the count. to_smarts(..., include_h_count=True) fixes the count on every atom, ring positions included, so its pattern matches unsubstituted phenol only.

docs.title: Chemistry options¶
docs.text: options.chemistry decides which atoms and bonds may match. The default FLEXIBLE aromaticity lets aromatic atoms and bonds of the query match non-aromatic ones, so the benzodiazepine core below also finds tetrazepam, whose phenyl ring is replaced by a cyclohexenyl ring. STRICT aromaticity excludes it. The last two rows show formal-charge and ring-membership matching on small molecules. Options objects take no keyword arguments: set each field as an attribute.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
Molecule queries and SMARTS patterns share one prepared-query interface, and every result states whether the search completed. Check the status before reading a missing match as an absence, give enumerations a limit and a time limit, and use SMARTS H primitives when hydrogen counts matter.

For the full reference, see the Substructure search and SMARTS queries chapters of the user guide.
